Retain ONE code copy and extract role-specific values into a DATA PACK (role-config file / env var set / capability descriptor / feature-flag bundle) consumed by the one code to instantiate either role.
  - DETECTION: reviewer or mechanical scan finds a byte-identical fork when `diff` shows every difference is a config value (hostname/port/flag/label/env/credential-ref), not behavioral; common git-history ancestor; > 90% byte identity (threshold is per-§11.4.35 DATA).
  - EXTRACTION: (1) identify the configuration surface; (2) extract to a data pack per role; (3) refactor the single code copy to consume it at instantiation (constructor injection/factory/config-loader-at-startup); (4) delete one fork; (5) verify per §11.4.5 that both role instantiations produce the same observable behavior their forks produced (§11.4.243 characterization before refactor); (6) commit the extraction per §11.4.124 with git-history evidence.
  - LEGITIMATE FORKS: temporary migration (tracked §11.4.197 end date), experimental/A-B (bounded end date), truly divergent behavior (algorithm/protocol/data-model differs, not just config).
  - Reference case: a SonarQube factory launcher byte-for-byte the caching-proxy launcher; fix = role-real acceptance test and "roles become data-only packs you reference, never repos you fork". Classification universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-251-PROPAGATION, CM-NO-BYTE-IDENTICAL-FORK (plus paired §1.1 mutation)
- **No escape hatch:** --fork-for-role-OK, --skip-data-pack-extraction, --copy-and-modify-config, --duplicate-code-per-environment, --near-identical-forks-are-fine
- **Honest boundary:** Extraction-source offset citation un-resolvable per §11.4.239 CITATION NOTE; resolves to module 35 taxonomy row 8 (module_35:127/130/132).
- **Composes:** §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.28, §11.4.35, §11.4.124, §11.4.177, §11.4.194, §11.4.197, §11.4.243, §1.1

#### §11.4.276 — Review-round budget: every independently-reviewed work item converges within a declared budget of at most 7 rounds (5-7, consumer-declared), by front-loading ground truth, class-exhaustive enumeration, real-path tests and a declared threat boundary, with a binding methodology change at round 3 (User mandate, 2026-10-05)
- **Source:** Constitution.md (constitution tip a71b1767) lines 11928-11966 (this anchor is in no groups/*.md file at this tip, see pin-upstream-findings.md)
- **Rules:**
  - Verbatim operator mandate (2026-10-05, CRITICAL): "Make sure we never ever get to such extremely high never ending review rounds count! Determine exact causes of issues we are facing with deep planning and exhaustive analisys so all work ALWAYS gets done with 5 to 7 reviews max! This MUST BE mandatory part of the constitution!!! Reasonable reviews rounds count with fully deterministically validated and verified working results produced!"
  - Forensic FACTS (genericised): one reference consuming project ran four independently-reviewed work items to 7, 10+, 30 and 39+ rounds in one week; the recorded findings show five avoidable mechanisms: (1) wrong-model ground truth (a build-configuration fix and its verifying gate both built on a simplified model of an external build tool's inheritance mechanism, the gate running the real tool on a hand-simplified fixture and so reporting GREEN on a fix that could never work); (2) instance-at-a-time closure of a known class (a command-shadowing gate hardened one command name per round across consecutive rounds; a 'close the whole class' instruction met by fixing a syntactic proxy token, the same defect family returning in four consecutive rounds); (3) fixer-authored tests that never drive the real code (re-implemented or text-extracted logic, so the reviewer's mutations of the real code survived); (4) non-binding escalation signals (the heuristic-tower anchor §11.4.250 invoked about thirty times, the stall anchor §11.4.267 having no declared retry bound, a reviewer-recommended structural fix deferred in two successive rounds while in-file point hardening continued); (5) scope drift (an out-of-scope tangent absorbed by a review loop while the round counter kept accruing against the original item). Genuinely new findings legitimately needing another round also occurred; iteration as such is not the defect, rounds spent re-discovering what one front-loaded investigation would have found are.
  - Boundary stated first (§11.4.227): §11.4.134 governs the GO bar and the obligation to re-run until met; §11.4.267 the attempt record and an undeclared stall bound N; §11.4.250 the heuristic-tower signal; none bounds the review loop's LENGTH or binds a concrete action to a round NUMBER. §11.4.276 adds exactly that: (A) the ceiling, (E) the round-3 checkpoint and the ceiling escalation. (B)-(D) add no new substantive duty, they fix WHEN existing duties are discharged ((B) binds §11.4.6/§11.4.99/§11.4.102 phase 1/§11.4.199/§11.4.226 to a recorded artifact before the first fix; (C) binds §11.4.250/§11.4.201(7)(b) to the round that first meets a nameable class; (D) binds §11.4.224(A)/§11.4.194(6)(d)/§11.4.115(F)/§11.4.235(D) to every remediation round's regression set).
  - (A) DECLARED ROUND BUDGET, HARD CEILING 7: every work item through the §11.4.125/§11.4.134/§11.4.142/§11.4.194 review loop carries a round budget R_max declared by the consumer as DATA (§11.4.35) in the closed range 5 <= R_max <= 7; an absent declaration resolves to 5 (conservative, escalation fires earliest, §11.4.101). The ceiling is a constitutional literal because the operator supplied it verbatim (same pattern as §11.4.246); the consumer's R_max within it IS its §11.4.267 N for the review loop and remains consumer DATA. A round = one independent review verdict on the item (uncommitted or already-pushed work), counted from the first review and recorded with the item's review record; a review that never received its brief, or crashed without a verdict, is recorded but not counted. Splitting, renaming or re-filing the item does NOT reset the count unless (E)(3) applies. A tracked item created from a finding raised during a budgeted item's review inherits its consumed round count, except a finding outside a scope/threat boundary declared before round 1 under (E)(2), which starts a fresh budget; recurrence identity follows §11.4.214 (link, never mint).
  - (B) GROUND TRUTH BEFORE THE FIRST FIX: for any change or finding whose correctness depends on a system the author does not own (build tool, compiler, interpreter or shell semantics, kernel, runtime, third-party library, protocol) the author MUST, before the first fix attempt, record a ground-truth probe: (1) the authoritative source of the behaviour (the tool's own source or normative specification, cited by file and line, not a summary or memory); (2) a minimal fixture executed on the REAL tool through its REAL composition path (the actual inheritance, sourcing, linking or dispatch mechanism the product uses; a hand-simplified approximation does not count); (3) the recorded behavioural model the fix relies on. The fix's own verifying gate or test MUST exercise the same real path; a gate verified on a simplified model is wrong-layer evidence (§11.4.226) and cannot support a GO.
  - (C) CLASS-EXHAUSTIVE ENUMERATION ON FIRST INSTANCE: when a finding is an instance of a class (bypass via name resolution, unguarded external command, masked character, mutation-surviving test, missed parse case) the round that fixes it MUST (1) name the class; (2) enumerate every member across the item's whole scope with a mechanical instrument whose null result is control-needle-proven (§11.4.201(7)(b)) and record that inventory; (3) close every member or scope one out explicitly with a reason and a tracked item (§11.4.197). Fixing only the reported instance when the class is nameable is a §11.4.276(C) violation. If the enumeration needs a tool that does not exist (e.g. a decision-path vs display-only call classifier), building it IS the remediation work; 'no classifier yet' is not a reason to fall back to instance-by-instance fixes. A claim a class is closed MUST cite the inventory artifact; a fix that closes a syntactic proxy instead of the class is an unclosed finding (§11.4.250).
  - (D) REAL-PATH TESTS AND REVIEWER MUTATIONS ADOPTED VERBATIM: every regression test added in a remediation round MUST drive the real shipped artifact through its real invocation path (§11.4.224(A)); a test re-implementing the guarded logic inline, or running extracted source text outside the artifact's own process, guards nothing and is a source-defect finding under §11.4.235(D). Every mutation a reviewer reported as surviving is added to the item's mutation set verbatim and must FAIL the suite before the next review is requested (§11.4.194(6)(d), §11.4.115(F)). The fixer runs the item's full regression set and the reviewer's previous attacks against the fix before requesting review; the dispatch seam REFUSES to start a review when that record is absent (never counted, never dispatched). A review that WAS dispatched and returned a verdict always counts as a round, even if its triggering record was later found deficient.
  - (E) BINDING METHODOLOGY CHANGE AT ROUND 3 AND THE CEILING ESCALATION: (1) at round 3 and every later round the round's fixer MUST first record a convergence assessment classifying every finding so far as new-class / same-class-as-earlier / regression-introduced-by-a-fix / wrong-layer-evidence. If two or more findings share a defect class named under (C) (not merely a shared §11.4.235(D) finding layer) with at least one non-MINOR finding in that class, any finding reappeared after being reported fixed, or any finding was wrong-layer evidence, the next round MUST be a structural round: a fresh fixer instance that did not author rounds 1-2 (the reviewer remains structurally separate throughout, §11.4.240), re-deriving (B) from first principles, re-running the (C) enumeration over the whole scope, and replacing the approach rather than adding a layer (§11.4.250). A structural fix a reviewer recommended may not be deferred past this point without a recorded operator decision (§11.4.66). (2) Every review declares, before round 1, its scope and acceptance boundary (and for adversarial/security reviews the threat model: which actor capabilities are in scope and the seam at which the defence lives) so a zero-finding GO under §11.4.134 is reachable; findings outside it are tracked items, not loop-extending findings; the boundary is fixed at round 1 and changes only by recorded operator decision, narrowing it mid-loop to reach GO is a §11.4.6 fabrication. (3) If round R_max returns anything but GO the item MUST NOT run round R_max+1 under the same approach: it stops and goes to a recorded operator decision (§11.4.66) carrying the finding classification, the evidence of which of (B)-(D) was skipped or failed, and the options (re-scope into smaller slices per §11.4.148; replace the approach with the structural design as a new item; or accept residual LOW findings only through a §11.4.271 waiver). Only a recorded operator decision opens a new budget. The escalated item is parked per §11.4.101/§11.4.267(F), parking only that work unit while the autonomous loop (§11.4.126) continues all other work and the pending decision is surfaced in every §11.4.97 progress report. Every breach is also recorded as a process escape and audited for which of (B)-(D) would have prevented it (§11.4.238(C) pattern).
  - (F) NOTHING HERE LOWERS THE BAR: the budget bounds the NUMBER of rounds, never what a round must establish; §11.4.134's zero-finding zero-warning GO bar is unchanged and its re-run obligation is bounded per approach by R_max, after which (E)(3) governs; §11.4.209's substrate, §11.4.235(D)'s finding layers and §11.4.262's machine evidence are unchanged. Reaching R_max without GO never produces a GO, a 'good enough' or a silent close: the item stays open until a recorded operator decision.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); the consumer supplies R_max (5-7), its review-record location, and its probe and inventory artifact paths as DATA (§11.4.35).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-276-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.276 as a block-start, exactly once per governance file, lockstep content-hash equality per §11.4.227(B); implemented upstream in scripts/gates/cm_covenant_114_276_propagation.sh with its paired mutation test), CM-REVIEW-ROUND-BUDGET (every reviewed item has a declared R_max in 5-7 or the default 5 and a round count from its review record; a round R_max+1 dispatched with no recorded operator decision FAILs; an item closed without GO FAILs), CM-REVIEW-ROUND3-CONVERGENCE-ASSESSMENT (every round >= 3 carries a convergence classification; a non-structural round after an assessment that triggered (E)(1) FAILs; an adversarial review with no pre-round-1 threat boundary FAILs), CM-FIX-GROUND-TRUTH-AND-CLASS-INVENTORY (a fix touching a declared external-system surface with no ground-truth probe record, or a class finding fixed with no inventory artifact, FAILs); the three mechanism gates are registered upstream as tracked deferrals OWED-GATE-111..113 (gate-code is a separate work item, NOT claimed shipped); paired §1.1 mutations (dispatch round 8 with no decision record; delete the round-3 classification or follow a same-class trigger with a point-fix round; strip the probe record or mark a class closed with no inventory; strip the literal); golden-FALSE per §11.4.201(1): an item reaching GO at round 4 with a round-3 assessment showing only new-class findings, a recorded probe and an inventory for its one class finding fires no gate
- **No escape hatch:** --unbounded-review-rounds, --fix-instance-not-class, --defer-ground-truth-probe, --narrow-threat-model-to-reach-go, --reset-round-count-on-refile, --defer-structural-fix-past-round-3
- **Honest boundary:** the anchor does not promise every item converges within R_max rounds; some problems are hard and a determined adversarial reviewer can keep finding real defects in an in-process defence whose threat boundary is wider than its design. It removes the avoidable round inflation (wrong external-system model, one member of a known class, tests that never drove the real code, an un-actioned stall signal, an unrelated tangent accruing against the wrong item); when a problem is genuinely hard (E)(3) turns an open-ended loop into a bounded evidence-backed operator decision. The cap counts rounds, not effort, and licenses no shallower review. The operator's wording ('5 to 7 reviews max') is read as a ceiling with a mandatory escalation at that ceiling, not a guarantee every item closes within it; that reading was recorded in canon and surfaced to the operator at landing per §11.4.66.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.66, §11.4.101, §11.4.102, §11.4.125, §11.4.134, §11.4.142, §11.4.148, §11.4.194(6)(d), §11.4.197, §11.4.201(7)(b), §11.4.209, §11.4.214, §11.4.224(A), §11.4.226, §11.4.235(D), §11.4.238(C), §11.4.240, §11.4.250, §11.4.267, §11.4.271, §1.1

### Design system and UI (11 anchors)

#### §11.4.162 — OpenDesign UI design system mandate
- **Source:** design-system-and-ui.md:3-29
- **Rules:**
  - Every project producing user-facing interfaces (web, desktop, mobile, TUI, or other surface classes per §11.4.25) MUST use OpenDesign (https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design) as the mandatory UI design-and-refinement system; NOT ad-hoc CSS, one-off design tools, improvised inline styles, or a different token system.
  - OpenDesign is consumed as a project dependency (npm package or stack equivalent), never vendored or forked.
  - MUST use OpenDesign tokens/themes for (1) all color palette definitions supporting BOTH light and dark themes from the project's brand colors extracted from canonical brand assets (logo, style guides, brand guidelines per §11.4.35); color tokens are defined in OpenDesign's token format, never duplicated in CSS custom properties or inline styles.
  - (2) Typography scale and spacing (typefaces, sizes, line heights, letter spacing, margin/padding tokens) defined in OpenDesign and consumed by every component, never scattered across component files.
  - (3) Component-level tokens for every reusable component (buttons, cards, dialogs, inputs, navigation, tables, modals, etc.): border radius, shadow, hover/active/focus states, animation timing defined in OpenDesign, not component-specific stylesheets.
  - Extend, never reimplement: if a UI pattern (component, theme variant, token type, rendering target) is unsupported, MUST extend OpenDesign upstream per §11.4.74 (submit a PR); working around it with ad-hoc CSS or another tool is a violation.
  - Every UI component MUST ship BOTH light and dark variants with palette from canonical brand assets; a component correct in only one theme is a violation; surfaces MUST be usable in both modes on any platform supporting theme switching.
  - Layout regression prohibition: UI elements MUST NOT overlap, fonts MUST NOT collide with other elements/text, labels MUST NOT overlay labels; any layout regression (clipped text, overlapping controls, misaligned grids, overflow-hidden content, wrong z-ordering) is a violation regardless of the token change's intent; OpenDesign token-diff comparison (before/after) is the primary regression-detection tool, correlated with visual regression tests.
  - All UI changes MUST be covered by the project's standard test types including visual regression tests (§11.4.4(b) layer 3) capturing before/after screenshots of every changed component/token with per-pixel or perceptual-diff PASS/FAIL.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies OpenDesign package path, brand-asset location, token definitions file, component registry, visual regression harness per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-162-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.162), CM-OPENDESIGN-UI-SYSTEM (OpenDesign installed; tokens/themes for all colors light+dark, typography, spacing, component tokens; upstream extension for unsupported patterns; no ad-hoc CSS-only UI; visual regression covers every UI change); paired section 1.1 mutations (token-driven style -> inline CSS FAILs; light-only component FAILs; non-OpenDesign color tool FAILs); gate-code = separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-opendesign, --ad-hoc-css-OK, --light-only-OK, --no-token-system, --no-visual-regression-tests
- **Honest boundary:** OpenDesign governs tokens and themes; it does NOT replace functional testing (§11.4.27), accessibility/WCAG contrast verification (§11.4.107), or §11.4.48/§11.4.49 UI-driven and dual-approach testing. Using OpenDesign tokens while shipping broken components is still a violation.
- **Composes:** §11.4.74, §11.4.25, §11.4.27, §11.4.4(b), §11.4.107, §11.4.48, §11.4.49, §11.4.35, §11.4.6, §11.4.69, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.170 — Device-independent host-side rendered-UI visual-proof mandate
- **Source:** design-system-and-ui.md:31
- **Rules:**
  - Every change to any user-facing UI surface (screen/component/view/widget/layout/theme on any platform: Android-Compose, iOS SwiftUI/UIKit, web, desktop, TUI) MUST be proven by device-independent host-side RENDERED PIXELS before it may be claimed correct: the real component rendered to an image ON THE HOST (no device, no emulator, no running app) via a host-render harness (Compose -> Roborazzi/Paparazzi on JVM; web -> Playwright/Storybook snapshot; SwiftUI -> snapshot-testing; equivalent per stack), for EVERY relevant screen x state x {light,dark} theme combination.
  - Each produced PNG MUST be validated by BOTH (i) image-diff against an approved golden (per-pixel or perceptual-diff PASS/FAIL) AND (ii) an OCR/vision oracle reading rendered text, labels and control bounds to assert legibility and NO element overlap, NO label-over-label, NO clipping, NO off-screen control, NO collapsed-or-giant unbounded widget (the §11.4.162 layout invariants proven on real pixels, not asserted on tokens).
  - Forbidden bluff: value-equality / token-equality / property-assertion UI tests (hex string, sp/dp integer, token field equals constant) are FORBIDDEN as the proof a UI is correct; they may SUPPLEMENT (confirm token wiring) but NEVER SUBSTITUTE for rendered-pixel proof; a green UI suite with no rendered-pixel artefact for the changed surface is a PASS-bluff at the visual layer.
  - (1) Rendered-pixel proof per screen x state x theme, device-independent, runnable in CI on EVERY commit with zero hardware; not subject to device availability.
  - (2) Dual oracle: golden image-diff AND OCR/vision content+layout oracle, both required; each PASS cites the captured PNG + diff artefact path per §11.4.5/§11.4.69.
  - (3) Value-only UI claims FORBIDDEN as proof; a UI change with no rendered-pixel artefact for its surface is a finding (§11.4.4 test-interrupt -> render -> fix -> re-render GREEN).
  - (4) Self-validated analyzer: the image-diff + OCR oracle is golden-good/golden-bad calibrated per §11.4.107(10) (a golden-bad fixture seeded with overlapping labels / clipped control / unbounded button MUST FAIL, else the analyzer is a bluff gate); thresholds calibrated on the project's OWN fixtures, not hardcoded from literature (§11.4.6).
  - (5) "Device offline" is NEVER a valid skip; an honest §11.4.3 SKIP applies ONLY where the platform genuinely has no host-render harness (a tracked migration item, never a silent gap or value-only fallback).
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies host-render harness, golden corpus, screen x state x theme matrix, OCR/vision thresholds per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-170-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.170), CM-HOST-RENDERED-UI-VISUAL-PROOF (every changed UI surface carries a device-independent host-rendered PNG per screen x state x theme, dual-oracle-validated, run on every commit; UI change proven only by value/token-equality FAILs); paired section 1.1 mutations (strip literal; accept value-equality-only proof / golden-bad overlapping-label fixture that PASSes -> gate FAILs); gate-code = separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --value-assertion-proves-ui, --skip-rendered-pixel-proof, --token-equality-suffices, --device-offline-skip-visual, --single-theme-only, --unvalidated-image-diff-OK, --no-ocr-layout-oracle
- **Honest boundary:** Host-render proves the COMPONENT renders correctly device-independently on every commit; it does NOT prove the running app on real hardware (§11.4.153/.158/.159/.160 live-device recording remains mandatory; the two layers complement), does NOT replace §11.4.162 token governance, and is distinct from §11.4.168 exported-document validation.
- **Composes:** §11.4.3, §11.4.5, §11.4.27, §11.4.40, §11.4.69, §11.4.107, §11.4.108, §11.4.117, §11.4.153, §11.4.158, §11.4.159, §11.4.160, §11.4.162, §11.4.163, §11.4.168, §11.4.169, §1.1, §11.4.4, §11.4.6, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.190 — Website engineering-quality mandate (responsive, SEO, OpenDesign-unique, enterprise quality, all PROVEN)
- **Source:** design-system-and-ui.md:41
- **Rules:**
  - Every website / web-UI surface a project ships, INCLUDING the project's own website, MUST satisfy AND PROVE with captured physical evidence (§11.4.5/.69/.107/.170; never a bare claim, §11.4.6) ALL of (A)-(E).
  - (A) FULL RESPONSIVENESS: correct usable rendering across ALL major browser engines (Chromium/Firefox/WebKit), all operating systems, all device classes (desktop/laptop/tablet/phone/large-display), full range of screen sizes/orientations/pixel-densities; NO broken layout/overflow/clipping/overlap/off-screen/unusable control at ANY breakpoint.
  - (B) COMPLETE SEO: semantic HTML + correct document outline; per-page unique title + meta description; Open Graph + Twitter cards; canonical URLs; structured data (schema.org / JSON-LD); robots + XML sitemap; crawlable/indexable markup; WCAG AA accessibility + Core Web Vitals performance.
  - (C) UNIQUE OpenDesign-AUTHORED templates/layouts: EVERY layout/template designed FROM the OpenDesign token system (§11.4.162), NOT generic/off-the-shelf/templated; visually unique, innovative, creative, brand-distinct.
  - (D) BLEEDING-EDGE ENTERPRISE VISUAL QUALITY: stunning, polished, professional look-and-feel in BOTH light AND dark themes (§11.4.162 tokens).
  - (E) ANTI-BLUFF PROOF: none of (A)-(D) may be CLAIMED without captured evidence: responsiveness by device-independent host-rendered screenshots across the real breakpoint x engine matrix + OCR/vision layout oracle (no overlap/label-over-label/clip/overflow/off-screen); SEO by automated audit (Lighthouse SEO + structured-data validation + meta/OG/sitemap/robots presence) meeting a defined score floor; visual quality by §11.4.170 host-rendered pixel proof per screen x state x {light,dark}; uniqueness by OpenDesign-token provenance.
  - A website reported responsive/SEO-optimized/unique/enterprise-quality WITHOUT these proofs is a PASS-bluff at the web-UI layer.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies breakpoint x engine matrix, SEO score floor, OpenDesign token set per §11.4.35. Strict web-quality expansion of §11.4.162; sibling of §11.4.168 at web-UI layer.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-190-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.190), CM-WEBSITE-RESPONSIVE-PROVEN, CM-WEBSITE-SEO-OPTIMIZED, CM-WEBSITE-OPENDESIGN-UNIQUE; paired section 1.1 mutation (claim without proof, generic non-OpenDesign template, or skipped light/dark host-render proof -> recommended gate FAILs; strip literal -> propagation FAILs); gate-code = separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-responsive-proof, --seo-optional, --generic-template-OK, --visual-quality-later, --claim-without-render
- **Honest boundary:** none stated beyond the proof requirement (references no project-specific hardware; concrete matrix/floor/tokens are consumer data).
- **Composes:** §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.69, §11.4.107, §11.4.162, §11.4.168, §11.4.170, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.216 — Canonical machine-readable design-token source (one CSS custom-property file, generated bindings elsewhere)
- **Source:** design-system-and-ui.md:43-55
- **Rules:**
  - Every project shipping user-facing interfaces MUST maintain design tokens as ONE canonical machine-readable source; everything else MUST derive from it.
  - (1) Canonical file shape: CSS custom properties, light values in `:root {}`, dark values via the `[data-theme="dark"]` override pattern, composing the project's sanctioned dark-mode mechanisms (`@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` system default, explicit `data-theme` attribute, framework-compat class); never duplicate hand-kept light/dark palettes.
  - (2) Generated bindings only: every consuming surface (web CSS, native mobile, desktop, TUI, design tools, rendered doc artifacts) binds either directly via `var(--...)` or through a GENERATED binding produced by codegen FROM the canonical file; a hand-copied or hand-restated token value anywhere (inline hex restating a token, hand-kept per-platform palette) is a violation.
  - (3) No invented values (§11.4.6 applied to design): every color/size/duration traceable to captured evidence: brand colors to a recorded eyedrop/measurement of the canonical brand asset, accent pairs to a MEASURED WCAG contrast ratio against their PAIRED background, structural values to the documented shared-system scale; a hex in any design artifact resolving to no token is a violation: flag it and use the nearest existing token, never mint an ad-hoc value.
  - (4) The token source is the white-label seam: per-brand/per-account re-theming swaps token VALUES within the §11.4.217 closed override set, never component structure.
  - Not-yet-built codegen bridges are `[OPEN]`-registered gaps (§11.4.223), never claimed working (§11.4.197 wiring honesty).
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies token-file path, brand-asset evidence, platform fan-out list, codegen bridges per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-216-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.216), CM-DESIGN-TOKEN-SINGLE-SOURCE (canonical token file with `:root {}` + `[data-theme="dark"]` blocks; tracked design artifacts bind via var() not inline token hex; every declared platform names its generated-binding artifact or its [OPEN] id); paired section 1.1 mutation (hand-restate token hex -> FAILs; strip dark override block -> FAILs; strip literal -> propagation FAILs); gate-code = separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --hand-copied-palette-OK, --inline-hex-OK, --invent-token-value, --light-only-tokens, --platform-keeps-own-palette
- **Honest boundary:** One canonical source proves consistency of DEFINITION, not correctness of USE (role discipline is §11.4.217; rendered-pixel proof is §11.4.170). A codegen bridge that does not exist is an [OPEN] gap, never claimed.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.162, §11.4.170, §11.4.190, §11.4.197, §11.4.217, §11.4.223, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.217 — OpenDesign brand contract (9-section DESIGN.md + tokens.css twin, disjoint color roles, AA-pinned accents, locked attribution footer)
- **Source:** design-system-and-ui.md:57-69
- **Rules:**
  - Every product shipping user-facing interfaces MUST carry an OpenDesign brand contract under its design area (`design/opendesign/` or declared equivalent per §11.4.35) consisting of (1)-(5).
  - (1) `DESIGN.md` in the verified 9-section schema: H1 product title with the `> Category:` blockquote IMMEDIATELY after the H1; nine numbered sections (parser matches number prefix, not heading text); a "Font labels for catalog extraction" block (`Display:` / `Body:` / `Mono:` lines) in the typography section; real hex codes; CSS variables wrapped in `:root {}` (never bare) with dark tokens via the `[data-theme="dark"]` override; real component CSS with `prefers-reduced-motion` targeting specific elements (never a global `*`); `:focus-visible` on every interactive component. Format claims verified against the tool's CURRENT source per §11.4.99, never from memory.
  - (2) The `tokens.css` machine-readable twin: the §11.4.216 canonical token file (or a compiled view of it) following the tool's token schema; prose and tokens never diverge.
  - (3) Disjoint color roles by contract: brand is DECORATIVE only (never body text); accent is INTERACTIVE and AA-PINNED (each accent/on-accent pair carries a measured >= 4.5:1 ratio against its paired background, both modes); semantic (success/warn/danger) is STATE and is NEVER overridden by a brand (a brand color can never mask an error signal).
  - (4) White-label closed override set, server-validated: per-account branding may swap decorative brand tokens, the accent pair, logo, slogan; accent overrides SERVER-VALIDATED to WCAG AA >= 4.5:1 or REJECTED (rejection carries the measured ratio + an AA-passing suggestion); structural tokens, neutral surfaces, semantic tokens NOT account-overridable (advanced neutral overrides gate behind full AA re-validation).
  - (5) Locked attribution footer: the organization's attribution footer ships on every surface and is NEVER removed, even fully white-labeled.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies brand values, category line, white-label storage/API bindings, attribution string per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-217-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.217), CM-OPENDESIGN-BRAND-CONTRACT (DESIGN.md with 9 numbered sections + category blockquote + font-labels block + `:root {}` + `[data-theme="dark"]` + targeted reduced-motion; tokens.css twin present and consistent; accent pairs carry measured ratios; attribution footer token/lockup present and not account-overridable); paired section 1.1 mutation (drop font-labels block, let brand token override --danger, or mark footer overridable -> FAILs; strip literal -> propagation FAILs); gate-code = separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-brand-contract, --prose-only-design-md, --brand-as-text-OK, --unvalidated-accent-override, --remove-attribution-footer, --semantic-tokens-brandable
- **Honest boundary:** The contract governs DEFINITION and roles; it does not prove rendered correctness (§11.4.170/§11.4.190) nor replace §11.4.162's token-system, test-coverage, extend-don't-reimplement obligations. Schema-version drift between local tool checkout and doc is recorded as fact and re-verified at integration.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.99, §11.4.162, §11.4.190, §11.4.216, §11.4.220, §11.4.223, §11.4.17, §11.4.35, §11.4.170

#### §11.4.218 — Living design-library catalogue + cross-platform reusability matrix with per-cell provenance
- **Source:** design-system-and-ui.md:71-83
- **Rules:**
  - Every project shipping user-facing interfaces MUST maintain a LIVING design-library catalogue.
  - (1) Complete component x state x theme rendering: every component of the design system in every declared state (default/hover/focus-visible/disabled/loading/error/empty/skeleton as applicable), auditable in BOTH light and dark from one artifact; a component or state in the spec but not the catalogue is a coverage gap tracked per §11.4.223.
  - (2) Self-contained artifacts: renders with ZERO external requests (no CDNs, no external fonts - self-hosted or system-stack fallback stated honestly, vendored libraries inlined); a catalogue needing the network is not auditable offline and violates the CSP/offline posture.
  - (3) Real behaviors, token-bound: interactive exhibits real (real dialog, sort, toggle), every color/size binds to the §11.4.216 token source, all motion honors `prefers-reduced-motion` per §11.4.221.
  - (4) Cross-platform reusability matrix with per-cell provenance: components x platforms matrix where EVERY cell is marked from the closed provenance set VERIFIED (reproduced from source and re-checked at source, with check date) / PROPOSED (a `[DEFAULT - adjustable]` design pending review) / ASSUMED (inference labeled as such); an unmarked cell reads as ASSUMED. The matrix is read BEFORE implementing any component on any platform; scaffolds are named scaffolds; a scaffold cell claiming VERIFIED is a PASS-bluff at the design-planning layer.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies component set, state vocabulary, platform list, matrix location per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-218-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.218), CM-DESIGN-LIBRARY-LIVING-CATALOGUE (catalogue exists, self-contained with zero external URL references, covers every spec'd component x state in both themes or tracks the gap, matrix has closed-set provenance marker in every cell); paired section 1.1 mutation (CDN reference -> FAILs; blank a cell marker or claim VERIFIED on a scaffold row -> FAILs; strip literal -> propagation FAILs); gate-code = separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --cdn-in-catalogue, --single-theme-catalogue, --mocked-behaviors-OK, --unmarked-matrix-cell, --scaffold-claims-verified
- **Honest boundary:** The catalogue proves the DESIGN renders and behaves as specified in a browser-class runtime; it does not prove any platform IMPLEMENTATION (matrix provenance + each platform's §11.4.170 proof). PROPOSED components are named proposals pending upstream-vs-project split decision, never silently promoted to shipped.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.162, §11.4.170, §11.4.216, §11.4.221, §11.4.223, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.219 — Per-app screen catalogues: full-IA coverage, per-platform chrome variants, honesty markers
- **Source:** design-system-and-ui.md:85-97
- **Rules:**
  - Every application/surface a governed project ships MUST have a screen catalogue.
  - (1) Full-IA coverage: covers EVERY node of the surface's information architecture (every screen of the wireframe/IA contract); an IA screen absent from the catalogue is a coverage gap tracked per §11.4.223, never silently skipped.
  - (2) Per-platform chrome variants: where one design serves several host platforms, render the platform chrome variants (mobile OS chrome toggle, per-OS window chrome, terminal-width constraints), not one chrome pretending to fit all; ports not yet designed are tracked, not faked.
  - (3) Self-contained, token-bound, both themes: each screen is a self-contained artifact binding §11.4.216 tokens, rendered light + dark, populated with REALISTIC product data (never lorem-ipsum for load-bearing content), carrying its per-screen state contract (loading/empty/error/populated declared).
  - (4) Honesty markers for unbuilt behavior: where the backing backend, contract, or product decision does not exist, the screen MUST say so with a `[GAP: id]` / `[OPEN: id]` marker (registered per §11.4.223), a labelled placeholder, inline note, or disabled control; NEVER a designed-as-if-real fake flow; designing a flow for an undecided behavior and presenting it as settled is a PASS-bluff at the product-design layer.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies surface list, IA contract, chrome-variant matrix, realistic-data corpus per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-219-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.219), CM-SCREEN-CATALOGUE-FULL-IA (every IA node maps to a catalogue screen or registered [OPEN] id; every screen renders both themes; every screen with absent backing contract carries its honesty marker); paired section 1.1 mutation (remove a screen without registering the gap -> FAILs; strip an honesty marker from an unbacked flow -> FAILs; strip literal -> propagation FAILs); gate-code = separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --partial-ia-coverage, --one-chrome-fits-all, --fake-flow-OK, --lorem-ipsum-content, --single-theme-screens
- **Honest boundary:** A screen catalogue is the DESIGN contract, not the implementation; implementation correctness stays with §11.4.170 pixel proof, §11.4.190 web-quality proof, and the §11.4.185 manual-QA final gate.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.162, §11.4.170, §11.4.185, §11.4.190, §11.4.216, §11.4.218, §11.4.223, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.220 — Open-first design tooling (self-hosted PenPot via submodule; proprietary tools import/export only; in-repo open formats)
- **Source:** design-system-and-ui.md:99-111
- **Rules:**
  - (1) Self-hosted open platform primary: the collaborative design platform is open-source and self-hostable (PenPot the standing default), run SELF-HOSTED; with the §11.4.162 OpenDesign engine it forms the primary design toolchain.
  - (2) Consumption ONLY via the PenPot submodule: ALL PenPot mechanisms/utilities (deployment recipe, RPC client utilities, access-token minting, import tooling, browser-hydration automation, MCP wiring) live in the dedicated reusable PenPot submodule (working name `vasic-digital/PenPot`; final repo name UNCONFIRMED; generic referent "the PenPot submodule" is normative until it lands), inherited BY REFERENCE per §11.4.28; the submodule itself consumes the Containers submodule (§11.4.76, rootless §11.4.161) and DECLARES that dependency in its §11.4.31 `helix-deps.yaml`. Projects MUST NOT hand-roll PenPot deployment or client code outside the submodule; missing capability is extended UPSTREAM per §11.4.74. The submodule carries MECHANISMS/UTILITIES ONLY, never project design content.
  - (3) Proprietary tools (Figma or equivalent) are optional import/export/review bridges via documented bridge kits, NEVER the source of truth; NO design value may exist ONLY inside a proprietary tool or its cloud; canonical form lands in-repo the moment a decision lands.
  - (4) In-repo open formats: design sources versioned in the repo as open diffable formats: SVG (vector masters), CSS (tokens per §11.4.216), JSON (manifests, IR captures, variables payloads), Lottie JSON (motion per §11.4.221), self-contained HTML (screens/library per §11.4.218/.219); binary proprietary formats are derived artifacts at most, never sources (§11.4.215 applied to design).
  - (5) Runtime-probed capability claims: every tooling claim ("daemon runs", "CLI exports", "import works") established by a runtime probe recorded as evidence (§11.4.201; §11.4.99 for format contracts), with an explicit headless-vs-operator-interactive matrix and an HONEST-LIMITS section; a cloud push claimed without a real credentialed run is a fabrication of PASS-bluff severity.
  - (6) PenPot automation operational rules (research-verified): (a) the HEADLESS write path is the token-authenticated RPC API; access tokens (minted under the backend's `enable-access-tokens` flag, handled per §11.4.10) are the MANDATED auth for all automation; interactive OAuth relays / session-cookie scraping are FORBIDDEN as automation auth; (b) API-created PenPot files REQUIRE a browser hydration pass before handoff (thumbnails and text layout materialized by the browser runtime, not the write API); handing off an unhydrated API-created file as render-ready is a PASS-bluff; hydration is automated via the PenPot submodule's browser-hydration utility and its execution recorded as evidence (§11.4.69).
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies platform choice within open-first constraint, PenPot-submodule pointer + config (instance URL, token env-var NAMES per §11.4.10), bridge kits, probe scripts per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-220-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.220), CM-OPEN-DESIGN-TOOLING-PRIMARY (self-hosted open platform declared and consumed via PenPot submodule with no hand-rolled PenPot code in project tree; submodule helix-deps.yaml declares Containers dependency; automation authenticates via access tokens never OAuth relay; every API-created file handed off carries a recorded hydration-pass run; every design source referenced resolves to an in-repo open-format file; every capability claim cites a recorded probe; no design artifact exists only as a proprietary-cloud reference); paired section 1.1 mutation (hand-rolled PenPot RPC client, proprietary tool as source of truth, or hand-off with no hydration record -> FAILs; claim with no probe -> FAILs; strip literal -> propagation FAILs); gate-code = separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --figma-is-source-of-truth, --cloud-only-design, --proprietary-format-source, --hand-rolled-penpot-stack, --oauth-relay-automation, --skip-hydration-pass, --unprobed-tooling-claim, --rootful-design-stack
- **Honest boundary:** Open-first governs WHERE truth lives and WHICH tool is primary; operators may still use proprietary tools for review/hand-off; missing bridges (PenPot/Lottie export, proprietary-file creation) are [OPEN]-registered work per §11.4.223/§11.4.197; citations use the generic referent until the PenPot submodule's final name is confirmed.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.10, §11.4.28, §11.4.31, §11.4.69, §11.4.74, §11.4.76, §11.4.99, §11.4.161, §11.4.162, §11.4.201, §11.4.215, §11.4.216, §11.4.223, §11.4.221, §11.4.218, §11.4.219, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.221 — Motion discipline (token-bound timing, manifest, reduced-motion static fallbacks)
- **Source:** design-system-and-ui.md:113-125
- **Rules:**
  - (1) Token-bound timing: every duration and easing binds to the §11.4.216 motion tokens (shared base durations + easing curves); documented choreography MAY extend them, but an animation timed by an ad-hoc literal bypassing the token layer is a violation (§11.4.6 no-invented-values).
  - (2) Reduced-motion fallback per animation: every playable animation ships a STATIC fallback derived from its own keyframes (poster frame for looping animations, final frame for one-shots), delivered as an open-format asset; where correct reduced-motion behavior is intentionally something else (instant cut, no artwork) that is recorded EXPLICITLY in the manifest with its reason; a missing fallback is a gap, a silent missing fallback is a violation.
  - (3) Machine-readable manifest: a versioned motion manifest enumerates every animation with id, loop mode, poster frame, reduced-motion mode, fallback reference; runtimes consume the MANIFEST, not folklore.
  - (4) `prefers-reduced-motion` honored everywhere: every surface (web, library, screens, previews, implementations) gates motion on `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` with TARGETED component-level gates (never a global `*` kill-switch, per the §11.4.217 review lens), swapping in the manifest-named fallback.
  - (5) Render-validated, honestly bounded: no animation claimed working without a real render in a real runtime (§11.4.107(10) analyzer discipline applied to motion: parse + structure + rendered geometry with progression assertions); runtimes not yet exercised are named [OPEN] items, never assumed.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies animation inventory, motion tokens, manifest path, runtime list per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-221-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.221), CM-MOTION-TOKEN-BOUND-REDUCED-FALLBACK (every animation's timing resolves to tokens; manifest enumerates every playable animation; every entry names a fallback or an explicit recorded null-with-reason; every animation carries its parse/structure/render validation record); paired section 1.1 mutation (ad-hoc literal duration -> FAILs; drop a fallback reference without recorded reason -> FAILs; strip literal -> propagation FAILs); gate-code = separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --ad-hoc-duration, --no-reduced-motion-fallback, --global-star-motion-kill, --manifest-optional, --unrendered-animation-claimed-working
- **Honest boundary:** Manifest + fallbacks prove reduced-motion COVERAGE, not physical-display fidelity (a pixel A/B of statics against frozen frames on a real display remains a tracked item); jsdom/headless renders do not certify mobile runtimes.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.107(10), §11.4.162, §11.4.170, §11.4.216, §11.4.218, §11.4.223, §11.4.217, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.222 — Design-completion export wave
- **Source:** design-system-and-ui.md:127-139
- **Rules:**
  - A design (system, brand, screen set, or change wave) is NOT done until its EXPORT WAVE has run and outputs are verified: (1)-(5).
  - (1) Per-platform token codegen: the §11.4.216 generated bindings are (re)generated from the canonical token source, or their absence is [OPEN]-tracked.
  - (2) Full icon/asset raster matrix via an honest-output pipeline: the per-platform pixel/format matrix (every OS surface) documented, locked 1:1 to a generator script, produced by a pipeline that (a) PROBE-TESTS every candidate renderer with a real content-verified probe render before trusting it (§11.4.201: presence is not correctness), (b) falls through to the next candidate on probe failure, (c) SKIPs-with-note any step whose tool is genuinely absent (§11.4.3/§11.4.69), (d) NEVER writes a placeholder, blank, or faked output; every produced raster verified non-degenerate (size floor + non-blank content check; multi-resolution bundles verified to contain declared members per §11.4.38).
  - (3) Both-theme screen renders + bound design book: every catalogue screen rendered in light AND dark at the declared scale with deterministic theme forcing, each render verified non-blank, set bound into the portable design book.
  - (4) Hand-off bundles: open-platform and proprietary-bridge bundles (§11.4.220) built with per-leg HONEST statuses: produced / deferred-operator-only / impossible-with-reason.
  - (5) Doc twins regenerated: the design area's §11.4.65/§11.4.73 export siblings regenerated so no reader gets a divergent view.
  - A design wave reported complete without its export wave, or with any faked/unverified export output, is a PASS-bluff at the design-delivery layer.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies raster matrix, generator, renderer candidates, book builder, bundle targets per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-222-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.222), CM-DESIGN-EXPORT-WAVE-COMPLETE (raster generator probe-tests renderers and content-verifies outputs; matrix doc and generator agree 1:1; every screen has both-theme verified renders or a tracked gap; every bundle leg has an honest status; doc twins in sync); paired section 1.1 mutation (renderer skips probe, or writes placeholder PNG on renderer absence -> FAILs; wave reported complete with stale doc twin -> FAILs; strip literal -> propagation FAILs); gate-code = separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-export-wave, --unprobed-renderer, --placeholder-raster-OK, --single-theme-renders, --fake-bundle-status, --stale-doc-twins
- **Honest boundary:** The export wave proves artifacts exist, are real and non-degenerate; it does not prove visual correctness on physical displays (§11.4.170/.190/.185 own that). A wave rendered before later additions is stamped with its coverage boundary; regeneration lands as a tracked downstream pass, never claimed retroactively.
- **Composes:** §11.4.3, §11.4.6, §11.4.38, §11.4.65, §11.4.69, §11.4.73, §11.4.201, §11.4.216, §11.4.219, §11.4.220, §11.4.17, §11.4.35, §11.4.170, §11.4.190, §11.4.185

#### §11.4.223 — Provenance-marker discipline for design documentation + central open-item registry
- **Source:** design-system-and-ui.md:141-153
- **Rules:**
  - (1) Mandatory marker vocabulary: a closed, project-declared marker set whose minimum core is `[VERIFIED]` (established from source/runtime/measurement, with evidence or check date), `[OPERATOR]` (an operator decision), `[DEFAULT - adjustable]` (proposed default pending review), `[OPEN: id]` (unresolved item with stable id); projects extend (`[RESEARCH]`, `[ASSUMED]`, `[BUILD-NEW]`, `[GAP: id]`, `[IN-HOUSE: ...]`, `[CONSTITUTION §x]`) per §11.4.35. A load-bearing claim with no marker reads as UNVERIFIED; presenting an assumption as verified is a §11.4.6 violation of PASS-bluff severity at the design-documentation layer.
  - (2) Every unresolved decision is an `[OPEN: id]` with a stable never-renumbered id (§11.4.54 discipline), owned by a named file, never papered over with an invented answer.
  - (3) Central registry in the area index: the design area's index maintains the SINGLE canonical open-item registry: every `[OPEN: id]` in the tree appears in it, every registry row names its owning file(s) and state; TREE-VERIFIED in both directions on every consolidation pass (id in tree missing from registry, or registry ghost with no tree presence, is a violation; §11.4.186 applied to design opens); closures cite the closing revision; narrowed items record exactly what closed and what remains.
  - (4) Opens map to tracked work: registry items map to workable-item tracking (§11.4.15/§11.4.54/§11.4.93) so §11.4.197 applies; a design open is driven to closed-with-evidence or explicitly-closed-with-reason, never silently abandoned.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies marker-set extensions, id families, area-index path, tracker binding per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-223-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.223), CM-DESIGN-DOC-PROVENANCE-MARKERS (every design doc declares/uses the marker vocabulary; area index registry exists; tree-grep of open-item ids equals the registry set in both directions; every registry row names owner + state); paired section 1.1 mutation (add [OPEN: id] without registering -> FAILs; delete a registered id from tree while registry lists it open -> FAILs; strip literal -> propagation FAILs); gate-code = separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --unmarked-claims-OK, --assumption-as-verified, --unregistered-open-item, --registry-optional, --silently-abandon-open
- **Honest boundary:** Markers prove the EPISTEMIC STATUS of each claim, not its truth ([VERIFIED] is only as good as its evidence, §11.4.123); the registry proves open-item ACCOUNTING, not progress (§11.4.197 owns completion).
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.15, §11.4.44, §11.4.54, §11.4.61, §11.4.93, §11.4.123, §11.4.186, §11.4.197, §11.4.212, §11.4.17, §11.4.35


### Documentation and export (27 anchors)

#### §11.4.12 — Auto-generated docs sync mandate
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:3-14
- **Rules:**
  - Every auto-generated document (Issues_Summary, API reference, build manifest, etc.) MUST be regenerated in the same commit as any edit to its source.
  - Stale auto-generated docs are PASS-bluffs in document form.
  - All file types MUST stay in sync at all times: Markdown source + HTML export + PDF export (or equivalent multi-format output the project ships).
  - Enforced by a pre-build gate that checks mtime ordering and content hash agreement.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4

#### §11.4.18 — Script documentation mandate
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:16-75
- **Rules:**
  - Every Bash/shell/POSIX-sh script ANYWHERE in a project (scripts/, bin/, tests/, library dirs, Upstreams/, deployment hooks, CI helpers; depth-N recursive) MUST carry an in-source documentation block at the top of the file.
  - The in-source block MUST contain: Purpose (one sentence); Usage (full invocation syntax with all flags, env vars, positional args, examples); Inputs (env vars, files read, args, stdin); Outputs (files written, stdout/stderr behaviour, exit codes); Side-effects (anything changing system state outside the script's scratch dir); Dependencies (required commands and how to install them, required system state such as "must be run as root" / "must run from project root"); Cross-references (companion guides under docs/).
  - Every such script MUST also have an external user guide at docs/scripts/<script-name>.md with required sections: Overview; Prerequisites; Usage examples (copy-paste recipes); Edge cases; Internal behaviour (step-by-step); Related scripts; Last verified version / date.
  - Whenever script source is modified, the in-source block AND the external guide MUST be updated in the SAME commit; a commit touching a script but leaving docs unchanged or drifting is a violation.
  - Pre-build gate walks every *.sh and *.bash under scripts/ (or equivalent), verifies companion docs/scripts/<name>.md exists AND was modified in the same commit (SHA cross-reference, or mtime >= script mtime as softer floor). Paired mutation strips the doc-sync invariant and asserts the gate FAILs.
  - No documentation ever can be out of sync with its codebase.
- **Gates:** CM-SCRIPT-DOCS-SYNC
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.11, §11.4.12

#### §11.4.19 — Fixed-document column-alignment mandate
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:77-178
- **Rules:**
  - Every project maintaining an Issues/open-work tracker AND a Fixed/closed-archive tracker MUST keep them structurally aligned along at least Status and Type.
  - (1) Per-entry annotation: every heading in the Fixed archive MUST carry, within 8 non-blank lines of the heading, a **Status:** line and a **Type:** line as §11.4.15 + §11.4.16 require for Issues.
  - Fixed Status closure-set values: `Fixed (→ Fixed.md)` (fully verified on device with captured evidence per §11.4.5); `Fixed — pending device verification` (source fix landed, regression gate wired, awaiting next build+flash+cycle); `Fixed — RECLASSIFIED` (reclassified during investigation: test-side defect, environment-only, etc.).
  - Type values per §11.4.16: Bug | Feature | Task. Default on missing annotation: Task.
  - (2) A Fixed_Summary.md MUST exist alongside Fixed.md, regenerated by an automation script (e.g. generate_fixed_summary.sh), mirroring Issues_Summary.md columns exactly: `| # | Level | Status | Type | One-line description |`.
  - The Level column uses the ORIGINAL severity the item had when open; same deterministic classification (REAL PRODUCT DEFECT / PARTIAL-or-WORKSTREAM-or-DEEP-DIVE / everything-else mapping to C / M / L).
  - (3) All three file types (.md, .html, .pdf) for BOTH Fixed and Fixed_Summary MUST stay in sync always, using the same export pipeline as §11.4.12; the single-shot sync wrapper (e.g. sync_issues_docs.sh) MUST invoke the Fixed_Summary generator AND export all five variants (Issues, Issues_Summary, Fixed, Fixed_Summary, CONTINUATION) in one operation so they carry the same mtime.
  - (4) Cross-lifecycle: a status `Fixed (→ Fixed.md)` in Issues.md is a migration marker; on resolution the entry MUST be moved to Fixed.md in the same commit, disappear from Issues_Summary (open items only) and appear in Fixed_Summary (closed items).
  - The migrated Fixed.md entry MUST carry: closure cycle, closure commit SHA, captured-evidence pointer, regression-protection gate name + paired mutation reference.
  - Pre-build gate invariants (5+): docs/Fixed_Summary.md exists; its table header contains both Status and Type columns; mtime(Fixed_Summary.md) >= mtime(Fixed.md); generator script exists (generate_fixed_summary.sh or equivalent branch in generate_issues_summary.sh); sync wrapper invokes the Fixed_Summary generator; HTML + PDF exports for both Fixed and Fixed_Summary exist (docs/Fixed.html, Fixed.pdf, Fixed_Summary.html, Fixed_Summary.pdf).
  - Paired mutation: strip the Status column from the Fixed_Summary header (or rename generator) -> gate FAILs; enforced by meta_test_false_positive_proof.sh.
  - Universal rule (§11.4.17); propagation gate enforces presence in every covenant file.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker regardless of context.
- **Gates:** CM-FIXED-COLUMN-ALIGNMENT, CM-COVENANT-114-19-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated as: no escape hatch, non-compliance is a release blocker)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.4, §11.4.5, §11.4.12, §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.22 — Document-sync commit discipline
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:180-271
- **Rules:**
  - Universal (§11.4.17). Every project shipping a status-tracking doc set MUST provide a lightweight commit path distinct from the full-repo commit wrapper, which stages, commits and pushes ONLY the status-tracking doc set.
  - Doc set: (1) active issue tracker (docs/Issues.md or equivalent) + HTML + PDF exports; (2) docs/Issues_Summary.md + exports; (3) docs/Fixed.md + exports; (4) docs/Fixed_Summary.md + exports; (5) docs/CONTINUATION.md (per §12.10) + exports; (6) any auto-generated audit artifact (docs/audit/anti_bluff_audit.md or equivalent) pairing with the above.
  - The wrapper MUST auto-invoke the project's export-regeneration pipeline first so MD+HTML+PDF are synchronised before push (skipped only with explicit --no-sync AND the operator just ran the pipeline manually).
  - The wrapper MUST stage ONLY the doc-set files via an explicit file list; NEVER `git add -A`.
  - The wrapper MUST use a separate flock disjoint from the full-tree commit wrapper's lock.
  - The wrapper MUST push to every parent-repo remote (reusing the project's push-all driver where available).
  - Exit codes: 0 success, 1 validation failure, 2 lock contention, 3 nothing-to-commit (informational, not an error).
  - The wrapper MUST be invocable standalone OR via a flag on the full-tree wrapper (e.g. commit_all.sh --docs-only).
  - §9 preflight inheritance: if meta_test_* is mid-mutation or *.mut.bak files exist, the wrapper refuses to run, same as the full-tree wrapper.
  - Recommended gate CM-COMMIT-DOCS-EXISTS: lightweight wrapper exists + executable, its external guide (per §11.4.18) exists, the full-tree wrapper advertises the delegation flag, wrapper's doc-set enumeration lists >= N entries (project-dependent; a consuming project's set is 15). Paired mutation strips the doc-set array -> gate FAILs.
  - Operators who cannot run the lightweight wrapper MUST run the full-tree wrapper; doc-status drift is non-negotiable.
- **Gates:** CM-COMMIT-DOCS-EXISTS
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated as: no escape hatch)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.4, §11.4.12, §11.4.15, §11.4.17, §11.4.18, §12.10, §9

#### §11.4.23 — Visual-cue & grouping mandate for Issues docs
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:275-371
- **Rules:**
  - Classification mixed: discipline universal; implementation (CSS, HTML post-processor, weasyprint) project-specific.
  - Every project shipping tracked-item docs (per §11.4.15) MUST apply visual-cue coloring AND status grouping to the HTML + PDF exports; the Markdown source stays free of color noise; exports enriched in a post-processing stage.
  - Type cell base colors: Bug pale red (#FFE5E5 or equivalent ~5% red saturation); Task pale blue (#E5F0FF); Feature pale yellow (#FFF8DC).
  - Status cell colors: Queued no color (transparent), type cell keeps base; In progress pale green #D4F1D4; Ready for testing pale green-blue #C6EAEF; In testing pale green-yellow #E7F4D6; Reopened pale red #FFCCCC; Fixed pale green #A8E6A8 and ALSO turns the Type cell pale green; Operator-blocked/Blocker vibrant red #FF4444 with white text for readability. In all non-Fixed cases the Type cell keeps its base color.
  - Status grouping: rendered table MUST group items by Status, with an H3-class heading per group showing item count. Order: 1 Operator-blocked/Blocker, 2 In testing, 3 Ready for testing, 4 In progress, 5 Reopened, 6 Queued, 7 Fixed.
  - Print-fidelity: CSS MUST declare `print-color-adjust: exact` (or renderer equivalent) so PDFs preserve backgrounds; HTML and PDF MUST be visually equivalent; a color-stripped PDF is an export-drift defect.
  - Recommended gate CM-DOC-COLOR-GROUPING-DISCIPLINE: CSS carries the type+status class set, post-processor exists and is executable, sync wrapper invokes it, AND after sync the rendered HTML carries grouping headings + per-cell color classes (captured-evidence proof against stub post-processors). Paired mutation strips a Status class literal from CSS -> gate FAILs.
  - Color cues are not optional polish.
- **Gates:** CM-DOC-COLOR-GROUPING-DISCIPLINE
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated as: no escape hatch)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.12, §11.4.15, §11.4.17, §11.4.19, §11.4.22

#### §11.4.44 — Document Revision Header Mandate
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:375-475
- **Rules:**
  - Every IN-scope tracked Markdown document MUST carry a header block directly below the H1 with two MANDATORY fields: `**Revision:** N` (monotonic positive integer; never decremented, never reset on rewrite; new docs start at 1) and `**Last modified:** YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` (ISO 8601 UTC).
  - Optional encouraged fields: Description, Authority, Maintainer, Scope, Auto-generated-from (auto-generated docs only), Status (plan docs only).
  - Canonical format: H1 title, then bold-label lines (Revision, Last modified, Description, Authority, Maintainer), then content.
  - YAML front-matter and HTML-comment headers are FORBIDDEN (invisible to humans scrolling raw Markdown).
  - IN scope: docs/Issues.md, Issues_Summary.md, Fixed.md, Fixed_Summary.md, CONTINUATION.md, docs/guides/**/*.md, docs/research/**/*.md, docs/scripts/**/*.md, docs/changelogs/**/*.md, docs/superpowers/plans/**/*.md, docs/hardware/**/*.md, and every other tracked Markdown under docs/.
  - OUT of scope: CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md (every layer; version-tracked via VERSION + inheritance pointer per §11.4.35); README.md / CONTRIBUTING.md / LICENSE / NOTICE / VERSION / OWNERS; rendered HTML/PDF (revision inherited from source MD); auto-generated docs already carrying an embedded generation-time stamp.
  - Auto-bump tooling: scripts/doc_revision_bump.sh <file> (manual, idempotent, no-op if Last-modified within 5 s of `date -u`); .git/hooks/pre-commit (walks staged IN-scope docs, bumps, re-stages); scripts/testing/sync_issues_docs.sh composes the bump for Issues_Summary + Fixed_Summary after regeneration; scripts/commit_docs.sh calls the bump before staging.
  - §12.10 composition: CONTINUATION.md adds `**Revision:** N` under H1 and reuses its existing `Last updated:` line as `Last modified:` (one source of truth).
  - §11.4.12 composition: Issues_Summary/Fixed_Summary inherit the revision number of their source MD at generation time; NOT incremented independently.
  - §11.4.23 composition: HTML colorizer preserves the revision header (only Issues-table rows are mutated).
  - Gates: CM-DOC-REVISION-HEADER-PRESENT asserts both fields appear within 15 lines below the H1 in IN-scope docs; CM-COVENANT-114-44-PROPAGATION asserts the anchor literal in every covenant file. Paired mutations strip the Revision line OR the anchor literal -> gates FAIL.
  - Universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-DOC-REVISION-HEADER-PRESENT, CM-COVENANT-114-44-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-revision-bump, --no-header, --allow-missing-revision
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.12, §11.4.17, §11.4.23, §11.4.35, §12.10

#### §11.4.45 — Integration-Status-Doc Maintenance Mandate
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:477-574
- **Rules:**
  - Generic form of §12.10 applied to every non-trivial domain integration (e.g. Dolby/Arvus, NanoKVM, Firebase, Widevine, Netflix, Cuttlefish, Chromecast, Sonos, etc.). Universal (§11.4.17).
  - Every integration-status doc at docs/<domain>/<integration>/Status.md MUST satisfy ALL 10 sub-points:
  - (1) MUST exist when a domain integration is non-trivial (more than one fix/test/gate landing).
  - (2) MUST carry the §11.4.44 revision header directly below H1 (Revision + Last modified + Description + Authority + Maintainer + Scope).
  - (3) MUST be auto-synced (HTML + PDF) on every related-test-cycle completion AND every fix touching the integration; manual regeneration as the sole path is forbidden.
  - (4) MUST be auto-colorized per §11.4.23 (Status cells by lifecycle state, Type cells by Type, operator-blocked rows distinct).
  - (5) MUST have a sync wrapper invocable as `bash scripts/testing/sync_integration_status.sh <Status.md>` OR a per-integration thin shell delegating to the generic wrapper.
  - (6) MUST live under docs/<domain>/<integration>/.
  - (7) MUST include a captured-evidence-driven status table per §11.4.5: every status claim cites the test log path, recording path or sink-probe report; claims without evidence are PASS-bluffs.
  - (8) MUST use the closed status vocabulary per §11.4.6/§11.4.7: PASS / FAIL / SKIP / PENDING_FORENSICS / OPERATOR-BLOCKED; no implicit values.
  - (9) MUST list operator-blocked items at the top (just below the revision header).
  - (10) MUST be referenced from docs/CONTINUATION.md section 3 (Active work) when any item is non-terminal (Queued / In progress / Reopened / Operator-blocked).
  - Paired meta-test mutations: propagation strip -> propagation gate FAILs; delete **Revision:** from a Status.md -> status-docs gate FAILs; touch Status.md without re-syncing -> mtime mismatch FAILs; inject `likely` outside an UNCONFIRMED: block -> CM-NO-GUESSING-MANDATE catches it.
  - Gate CM-AF-INTEGRATION-STATUS-DOCS: discovers all docs/**/Status.md via glob, verifies §11.4.44 header, sync wrapper, HTML+PDF mtime-current vs source, colorization applied (cell-status class in colorized HTML).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-45-PROPAGATION, CM-AF-INTEGRATION-STATUS-DOCS, CM-NO-GUESSING-MANDATE
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-status-sync, --no-revision-bump-on-status, --allow-stale-html
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.7, §11.4.12, §11.4.13, §11.4.15, §11.4.22, §11.4.23, §11.4.44, §12.10

#### §11.4.53 — Fixed_Summary parity mandate
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:576-714
- **Rules:**
  - docs/Fixed_Summary.md is the symmetric short-form summary of docs/Fixed.md; it MUST be regenerated whenever Fixed.md changes; its HTML + PDF exports MUST travel with the markdown (identical mtimes within sync_issues_docs.sh granularity). Stale exports are violations even if the .md is correct. Same discipline as §11.4.12 applied to Fixed.md. Universal (§11.4.17).
  - Generator: scripts/testing/generate_fixed_summary.sh is canonical; MUST exist, be executable and emit a markdown table whose header includes Status and Type (per §11.4.19) mirroring Issues_Summary.md.
  - Auto-sync wrapper: scripts/testing/sync_issues_docs.sh is the single operator entry point; it regenerates BOTH Issues_Summary AND Fixed_Summary (stages 1a+1b), exports HTML+PDF (stage 2), colorizes per §11.4.23 (stage 3), re-renders PDFs from colorized HTML (stage 3b). MUST be invoked after any edit to Fixed.md. An --issues-only-style flag is FORBIDDEN; the wrapper has none and §11.4.53 prohibits adding one.
  - Sort order: by closure date DESC (most-recent Fixed first), with section-letter / Fix-# secondary sort; documented at top of generated file.
  - HTML + PDF travel together: the three file types MUST always have identical mtimes within wrapper granularity.
  - Composition duties: edits to Issues.md or Fixed.md trigger regeneration of BOTH summaries via the same wrapper; on closure (Fixed / Implemented / Completed (→ Fixed.md) per §11.4.33) the entry moves atomically from Issues.md to Fixed.md and sync_issues_docs.sh runs; colorizer post-processes both Issues_Summary.html AND Fixed_Summary.html (stale Fixed_Summary.html with pre-§11.4.23 styling is itself a violation); Fixed_Summary MUST emit the three terminal values (`Fixed (→ Fixed.md)`, `Implemented (→ Fixed.md)`, `Completed (→ Fixed.md)`) literally in the Status column; §11.4.44 revision header applies to Fixed_Summary.md.
  - Pre-build gate CM-FIXED-SUMMARY-SYNC (6 invariants): (1) docs/Fixed_Summary.md exists; (2) Fixed_Summary.html exists with mtime >= .md; (3) Fixed_Summary.pdf exists with mtime >= .md; (4) Fixed_Summary.md mtime >= Fixed.md mtime; (5) generate_fixed_summary.sh exists + executable; (6) sync_issues_docs.sh invokes the generator. Pre-build FAILs on any violation. Overlaps CM-FIXED-COLUMN-ALIGNMENT and CM-DOCS-EXPORT-SYNC.
  - Gate CM-COVENANT-114-53-PROPAGATION: anchor literal present across all 5 canonical files (constitution/Constitution.md, constitution/CLAUDE.md, constitution/AGENTS.md, parent consumer CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md).
  - Paired mutations: strip literal from constitution/CLAUDE.md -> propagation gate FAILs; move generate_fixed_summary.sh aside -> CM-FIXED-SUMMARY-SYNC FAILs; touch Fixed_Summary.md older than Fixed.md -> CM-FIXED-SUMMARY-SYNC FAILs.
  - Scope: every project maintaining an Issues.md/Fixed.md split; projects with no Fixed.md are NOT_APPLICABLE; all others MUST land both gates and mutations within one cycle of adopting this Constitution version.
- **Gates:** CM-FIXED-SUMMARY-SYNC, CM-COVENANT-114-53-PROPAGATION, CM-FIXED-COLUMN-ALIGNMENT, CM-DOCS-EXPORT-SYNC, CM-COVENANT-114-51-PROPAGATION, CM-COVENANT-114-52-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-fixed-summary-sync, --issues-only, --summary-not-applicable
- **Honest boundary:** NOT_APPLICABLE for projects without a Fixed.md (e.g. single-binary throwaway prototypes).
- **Composes:** §11.4.12, §11.4.15, §11.4.17, §11.4.19, §11.4.23, §11.4.33, §11.4.44, §12.10, §1.1, §11.4
- **Review addendum:** CM-COVENANT-114-51-PROPAGATION and CM-COVENANT-114-52-PROPAGATION are sibling propagation patterns, and CM-FIXED-COLUMN-ALIGNMENT and CM-DOCS-EXPORT-SYNC partially overlap; this anchor owns CM-FIXED-SUMMARY-SYNC and CM-COVENANT-114-53-PROPAGATION.

#### §11.4.56 — Status_Summary parity + two-audience format
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:718-814
- **Rules:**
  - For every docs/<domain>/<integration>/Status.md satisfying §11.4.45, a companion Status_Summary.md MUST exist in the same directory, always derived from Status.md so the two cannot diverge. Universal (§11.4.17); applies wherever §11.4.45 applies.
  - (1) Revision header per §11.4.44.
  - (2) Page 1 - "For the <team>" (audience heading; team derived from domain, e.g. audio team for docs/dolby/*, video team for docs/video/*): plain-language summary of current state (1-3 paragraphs); What works (1-3 bullets, end-user-visible); What's broken or pending (1-3 bullets); Operator/team actions if any; NO code references, NO section-letter jargon, NO captured-evidence file paths, NO gate/mutation names.
  - (3) Page 2 - "For software engineers": same content density as Status.md but condensed; section-letter references, gate names, commit hashes, captured-evidence file paths; cross-references to Issues.md/Fixed.md items by ATM-NNN (§11.4.54).
  - (4) HTML + PDF exports travel with the markdown (identical mtimes within sync wrapper granularity).
  - (5) Auto-generation: canonical helper scripts/testing/generate_status_summary.sh <Status.md path> produces both pages; MUST be invoked from a sync wrapper (e.g. scripts/testing/sync_integration_status.sh per §11.4.45) every time the source Status.md is updated.
  - Page-1 audience derivation: the generator maps domain -> audience via a project-controlled mapping table (e.g. audio -> Audio team, video -> Video team, network -> Network team, drm -> DRM / streaming team); unmapped domains default to `Project team`; the table lives in the project's generator config, NOT in the Constitution.
  - Status_Summary COMPLEMENTS, never replaces, Status.md; follows the §11.4.12 + §11.4.53 regeneration / HTML+PDF / mtime pattern; §11.4.23 colorizer applies if tracked-item references are embedded.
  - Gates: CM-STATUS-SUMMARY-EXISTS-FOR-EVERY-STATUS (every docs/**/Status.md has sibling Status_Summary.md + HTML + PDF with mtime >= Status.md mtime minus tolerance); CM-STATUS-SUMMARY-TWO-AUDIENCE (both `Page 1 — For the <team>` and `Page 2 — For software engineers` headings present); CM-STATUS-SUMMARY-REVISION-HEADER; CM-COVENANT-114-56-PROPAGATION.
  - Paired mutations: delete a Status_Summary.md -> EXISTS gate FAILs; remove Page 1 heading -> TWO-AUDIENCE gate FAILs; strip §11.4.56 literal from constitution/CLAUDE.md -> propagation gate FAILs.
- **Gates:** CM-STATUS-SUMMARY-EXISTS-FOR-EVERY-STATUS, CM-STATUS-SUMMARY-TWO-AUDIENCE, CM-STATUS-SUMMARY-REVISION-HEADER, CM-COVENANT-114-56-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-status-summary, --engineer-only, --no-audience-split
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.12, §11.4.17, §11.4.23, §11.4.44, §11.4.45, §11.4.53, §11.4.54, §12.10, §1.1

#### §11.4.57 — README.md doc-link section + revision metadata
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:818-917
- **Rules:**
  - Every project's top-level README.md MUST contain a section whose heading contains the literal `Tracked-Items` (title `Tracked-Items + Status Documents` or localized equivalent), as a markdown table with columns: Document (human-readable name), Last modified (ISO 8601 UTC from the doc's §11.4.44 header), Revision (integer from same header), Markdown (relative link to .md), HTML (relative link to .html), PDF (relative link to .pdf).
  - The section MUST link to: (1) Issues.md, Issues_Summary.md; (2) Fixed.md, Fixed_Summary.md; (3) CONTINUATION.md; (4) EVERY docs/**/Status.md and its Status_Summary.md pair (auto-discovered via `find docs -name 'Status.md'`).
  - Generator: scripts/testing/update_readme_doc_links.sh scans canonical doc paths, extracts Revision + Last modified from each §11.4.44 header, renders the table, and replaces the section between explicit markers `<!-- doc-link-section:begin -->` and `<!-- doc-link-section:end -->`.
  - The generator MUST be invoked from sync_issues_docs.sh AND from sync_integration_status.sh.
  - Gates: CM-README-DOC-LINK-SECTION-PRESENT (literal Tracked-Items heading AND both markers); CM-README-DOC-LINK-ROWS-COMPLETE (every canonical doc incl. every Status.md + Status_Summary.md appears as a row); CM-README-DOC-LINK-FRESHNESS (row Last modified matches the doc's header within sync-wrapper tolerance); CM-COVENANT-114-57-PROPAGATION.
  - Paired mutations: strip markers -> SECTION-PRESENT FAILs; remove CONTINUATION row -> ROWS-COMPLETE FAILs; backdate a Last modified -> FRESHNESS FAILs; strip §11.4.57 literal -> propagation FAILs.
  - Universal (§11.4.17); applies to every project with any of §11.4.15 / §11.4.45 / §11.4.53 in scope.
- **Gates:** CM-README-DOC-LINK-SECTION-PRESENT, CM-README-DOC-LINK-ROWS-COMPLETE, CM-README-DOC-LINK-FRESHNESS, CM-COVENANT-114-57-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-readme-doc-links, --collapse-status-rows, --no-freshness-check
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.12, §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.17, §11.4.19, §11.4.44, §11.4.45, §11.4.53, §11.4.56, §12.10

#### §11.4.59 — README always-sync mandate
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:921-997
- **Rules:**
  - README.md at the project root is a §11.4.12-class always-sync document. Universal (§11.4.17).
  - (1) MUST be reviewed and updated whenever new docs / integrations / Status.md entries appear, new submodules land, applied-fixes count changes, or canonical paths shift.
  - (2) MUST be kept in lockstep with docs/CONTINUATION.md (§12.10) and the Issues / Issues_Summary / Fixed / Fixed_Summary set (§11.4.12, §11.4.53).
  - (3) MUST be exported to .html and .pdf on every update, via helper scripts/testing/sync_readme_export.sh (pandoc + weasyprint), auto-invoked by scripts/testing/sync_issues_docs.sh so one doc-sync run refreshes the whole doc surface.
  - (4) MUST carry a §11.4.44 revision header (Revision N + Last modified ISO timestamp) at top.
  - (5) MUST contain a Documentation Map section linking every Status.md + Status_Summary.md + spec + plan + guide + script-companion doc + changelog + the constitution submodule, plus per-audience navigation (end user / developer / QA / agent).
  - (6) MUST be self-contained: no hyperlinks to ephemeral external systems as the only source of truth.
  - Stale exports are violations even if README.md is correct.
  - Pre-build gate CM-README-EXPORT-SYNC locks four invariants: (a) README.md exists, (b) README.html exists, (c) README.html mtime >= README.md mtime, (d) README.pdf mtime >= README.md mtime (skipped gracefully if weasyprint unavailable on host, enforced when PDF present). Paired mutation backdates README.html + README.pdf -> gate FAILs.
  - Doc-sync helper, pandoc + weasyprint deps and gate name are universal; Documentation Map contents are consumer-side.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-README-EXPORT-SYNC
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-readme-sync, --no-readme-export, --readme-stale-OK
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.12, §11.4.17, §11.4.18, §11.4.23, §11.4.44, §11.4.45, §11.4.53, §11.4.56, §11.4.57, §12.10

#### §11.4.60 — Documentation always-sync composite covenant
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:999-1100
- **Rules:**
  - Eight documentation classes constitute the project's living state surface and MUST be in sync at all times across .md + .html + .pdf: (1) docs/Issues.md; (2) docs/Issues_Summary.md; (3) docs/Fixed.md; (4) docs/Fixed_Summary.md; (5) docs/CONTINUATION.md; (6) README.md; (7) every docs/**/Status.md; (8) every docs/**/Status_Summary.md.
  - Mandatory composite pre-build gate CM-DOCS-COMPOSITE-SYNC: for every doc-class instance with .md present, .html mtime >= .md mtime AND .pdf mtime >= .md mtime; for every Status.md also sibling Status_Summary.md mtime >= Status.md mtime (if summary exists); walks docs/ recursively for Status.md (fleet not enumerated statically).
  - The composite gate FAILs the build if ANY single instance fails. Per-class gates (CM-ISSUES-SUMMARY-SYNC, CM-DOCS-EXPORT-SYNC, CM-FIXED-SUMMARY-SYNC, CM-CONTINUATION-DOC-INSYNC, CM-README-EXPORT-SYNC) remain in place; §11.4.60 is the belt-and-suspenders layer.
  - Paired mutation: meta_test_false_positive_proof.sh backdates docs/Issues.html to year 2000 (touch -t 200001010000.00) and asserts CM-DOCS-COMPOSITE-SYNC FAILs.
  - Revision-header coupling: each of the 8 classes carries the §11.4.44 Revision + Last modified header under the H1; the composite gate does NOT re-check it (covered by CM-DOC-REVISION-HEADER-PRESENT); composite gate is artefact-mtime only.
  - Wrapper contract unchanged: Issues/Fixed edits flow through sync_issues_docs.sh (§11.4.12); Status.md edits through sync_integration_status.sh <Status.md> (§11.4.45); README edits through sync_readme_export.sh (§11.4.59); §11.4.60 catches wrapper bypass (markdown committed without regenerated exports).
