  - Propagation gate CM-COVENANT-114-60-PROPAGATION enforces the anchor literal in every CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md across parent + 10 owned submodules + HelixQA deps; propagation gate is OPTIONAL for initial landing - only the composite gate + paired mutation are mandatory.
  - Universal (§11.4.17); composite gate logic universal, doc-class instance paths consumer-side. Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-DOCS-COMPOSITE-SYNC, CM-ISSUES-SUMMARY-SYNC, CM-DOCS-EXPORT-SYNC, CM-FIXED-SUMMARY-SYNC, CM-CONTINUATION-DOC-INSYNC, CM-README-EXPORT-SYNC, CM-DOC-REVISION-HEADER-PRESENT, CM-COVENANT-114-60-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-composite-doc-sync, --allow-stale-html, --summary-not-applicable
- **Honest boundary:** Composite gate is artefact-mtime only, by design narrow; propagation gate optional for initial landing.
- **Composes:** §11.4.12, §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.17, §11.4.19, §11.4.23, §11.4.33, §11.4.44, §11.4.45, §11.4.53, §11.4.56, §11.4.57, §11.4.59, §12.10, §1.1

#### §11.4.61 — Mandatory Markdown metadata table + structured-doc ToC
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:1102-1235
- **Rules:**
  - Adds two content disciplines alongside (not replacing) §11.4.65: metadata display at the top, and ToC kept in lockstep with heading structure. §11.4.65 governs .html/.pdf existence/freshness; §11.4.61 governs the Markdown source content.
  - (A) Canonical metadata TABLE supersedes the §11.4.44 bold-line header: a Markdown table immediately after the H1 (and following blank line). Pre-existing bold-line headers remain historically valid but MUST migrate to the table at the next substantive edit.
  - MANDATORY rows: Revision (positive integer; starts at 1, monotonic, never reset); Created (ISO 8601 date, first commit touching file); Last modified (ISO 8601 date, most recent commit touching file); Status (one of active / draft / deprecated / superseded).
  - ENCOURAGED rows (REQUIRED when the doc tracks workable items or has a known continuation; render `—`/`none` when N/A): Status summary (one-line hook); Issues (comma-separated workable-item IDs); Issues summary; Fixed (IDs of resolved items); Fixed summary; Continuation (next action or linked CONTINUATION.md anchor). Additional project-specific rows allowed if mandatory rows present.
  - (B) Any tracked *.md with two or more H2 sections MUST include a `## Table of contents` section immediately after the metadata table, listing every H2 and H3 in document order with anchor links, regenerated on every structural change (heading added/removed/renamed/reordered). A stale ToC is a PASS-bluff.
  - IN scope: every tracked *.md in the §11.4.65 INCLUDED set (project-root *.md, docs/**/*.md, scripts/**/*.md companion docs, owned-submodule trees, constitution/**/*.md, owned HelixQA deps). The §11.4.44 exclusions for CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / README.md are SUPERSEDED here.
  - NOT in scope: same EXCLUDED set as §11.4.65 (external/**, prebuilts/**, out/**, build/**, application-internal *.md shipped with source, non-owned third-party submodule trees) plus LICENSE, LICENSE.md, NOTICE, VERSION, OWNERS, machine-generated CHANGELOG.md.
  - PDF + HTML siblings deferred to §11.4.65 (CM-UNIVERSAL-MARKDOWN-EXPORT-SYNC); a metadata/ToC change is a .md modification which transitively triggers regeneration.
  - Planned gates: CM-MD-METADATA-PRESENT (every tracked *.md minus exemptions: H1 present; within 25 lines below H1 a table contains rows `| Revision |`, `| Created |`, `| Last modified |`, `| Status |`); CM-MD-TOC-PARITY (every *.md with >= 2 H2 has `## Table of contents` whose anchor slugs match live H2/H3 set in order).
  - Planned paired mutations: strip `| Revision |` row -> CM-MD-METADATA-PRESENT FAILs; rename an H2 without updating ToC -> CM-MD-TOC-PARITY FAILs.
  - §11.4.44 stays authoritative for the fact that docs carry revision metadata; §11.4.61 changes format (bold-lines -> table) and scope (docs/**/*.md -> every tracked *.md per §11.4.65 INCLUDED). Consumer gates grepping `**Revision:**` MUST also accept the table form. Migration period: 30 days from §11.4.61 landing.
  - Universal (§11.4.17); per-project tracker IDs and doc paths are consumer-side. Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-MD-METADATA-PRESENT, CM-MD-TOC-PARITY, CM-UNIVERSAL-MARKDOWN-EXPORT-SYNC
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-md-metadata, --no-metadata-table, --toc-stale-OK, --allow-missing-revision
- **Honest boundary:** Gates and mutations are stated as planned; export freshness is deferred to §11.4.65 (no duplicate enforcement).
- **Composes:** §11.4.17, §11.4.44, §11.4.45, §11.4.59, §11.4.60, §11.4.65, §11.4

#### §11.4.63 — Workable-items procedure docs as single source of truth
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:1237-1329
- **Rules:**
  - Every workable-item action (opening, updating, closing, reopening, migrating Issues.md <-> Fixed.md) MUST follow the canonical procedure document at docs/procedures/issues/<Action>.md. The five procedure docs are MANDATORY references; no agent or operator may invent ad-hoc procedures.
  - Closed set: Creation.md (opening a new item: Bug / Feature / Task); Updating.md (non-closure, non-reopen edits: status transitions, evidence append, type re-classification); Resolution.md (atomic Issues.md -> Fixed.md close: Bug->Fixed, Feature->Implemented, Task->Completed per §11.4.33); Reopening.md (atomic Fixed.md -> Issues.md reopen with §11.4.34 source attribution + §11.4.55 reopens-history); Migration.md (bidirectional atomic-move mechanics + sync_issues_docs.sh internals, consumed by Resolution + Reopening).
  - Each procedure doc carries the §11.4.44 revision header + HTML + PDF exports synchronised to its .md. Helper scripts/testing/sync_procedure_docs_export.sh walks the procedures dir and emits .html + .pdf per .md; invoked as the final stage of scripts/testing/sync_issues_docs.sh.
  - Universality of scope: ALL work (new features, behavioural changes, tasks such as refactor/doc/infra/gate/audit/cleanup, bug fixes, investigation, documentation) MUST flow through these procedures; the "I'll just tweak this one file" escape is forbidden.
  - Pre-build gate CM-PROCEDURES-DOCS-PRESENT: (1) all 5 docs exist at docs/procedures/issues/{Creation,Updating,Resolution,Reopening,Migration}.md; (2) each carries §11.4.44 header; (3) each has .html + .pdf with mtime >= .md; (4) scripts/testing/sync_procedure_docs_export.sh exists + executable; (5) scripts/testing/sync_issues_docs.sh invokes it. Paired mutation: rename one procedure doc -> gate FAILs.
  - Propagation gate CM-COVENANT-114-63-PROPAGATION enforces the anchor literal in every CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md across parent + 10 owned submodules + nested submodules + HelixQA deps; paired mutation strips literal -> FAILs.
  - Universal (§11.4.17); closed set of five docs and sync composition universal; per-procedure examples consumer-side. Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-PROCEDURES-DOCS-PRESENT, CM-COVENANT-114-63-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** --ad-hoc-procedure, --skip-procedure-doc, --procedure-not-applicable
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.7, §11.4.11, §11.4.12, §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.17, §11.4.19, §11.4.23, §11.4.33, §11.4.34, §11.4.44, §11.4.53, §11.4.54, §11.4.55, §11.4.60

#### §11.4.65 — Universal Markdown export mandate
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:1331-1461
- **Rules:**
  - Every Markdown document in the project that is not part of an application/service source-code tree MUST be exported (available) as .html and .pdf; already-existing such docs lacking or out of sync with exports MUST have them (re)generated; every modification MUST regenerate its HTML and PDF; Markdown, HTML and PDF MUST be in sync at all times. This is the catch-all generalising the per-class always-sync anchors §11.4.12/.18/.44/.45/.53/.56/.57/.59/.60/.63/.64.
  - INCLUDED scope (closed set): project-root *.md (README.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, etc.); docs/**/*.md (guides, research, plans, changelogs, procedures, hardware notes); scripts/**/*.md (script-companion docs, NOT shebang scripts); owned-submodule trees at device/rockchip/atmosphere/<submodule>/ (top-level README.md / CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / CHANGELOG.md and docs/**/*.md); constitution/**/*.md; tools/helixqa/<helixqa-submodule>/ top-level README/CLAUDE/AGENTS and docs/**/*.md (owned HelixQA deps).
  - EXCLUDED scope (closed set; application/service source or third-party trees): external/**; prebuilts/**; packages/modules/**; kernel-5.10/**; out/**; build/**; application/service source-code trees (module-internal *.md shipped with library code, READMEs inside source-only third-party gradle module dirs); any third-party submodule NOT in the owned set (presenter, vlc-player, nova-player, mpv-player, gramophone-player, rhythm-player, strep-player, smarttube-player, torrserve, lampa) or the HelixQA-owned set (Challenges, Containers, DocProcessor, LLMOrchestrator, LLMProvider, VisionEngine).
  - Mandatory protection 1: every INCLUDED .md has .html and .pdf siblings; a missing export is a violation regardless of when the markdown was last touched.
  - Protection 2: .html and .pdf mtime >= .md mtime (within same sync-wrapper granularity); stale exports are violations even if .md is correct.
  - Protection 3: every modification triggers regeneration, via the sync wrapper (sync_all_markdown_exports.sh), a git pre-commit hook on staged .md, or the per-class wrappers (sync_issues_docs.sh, script-docs sync, sync_readme_export.sh, etc.) all delegating the universal export path to the same canonical helper.
  - Protection 4: pre-build gate CM-UNIVERSAL-MARKDOWN-EXPORT-SYNC walks the INCLUDED scope, verifies .html + .pdf siblings with mtime >= .md, and FAILs the build if any missing or stale.
  - Protection 5: no escape hatch for files inside the INCLUDED scope; the EXCLUDED scope is the only legitimate opt-out and is closed-set.
  - Canonical helper scripts/testing/sync_all_markdown_exports.sh: walks INCLUDED scope; pandoc (HTML) + weasyprint (PDF) with `timeout 60` each (graceful per-file degradation); uses docs/_progress-style.css; supports --check-only (exit nonzero if out-of-sync, print list) and --regenerate-all (force); caps at 500 candidates with explicit abort+list if scope unexpectedly large; idempotent.
  - Gate CM-UNIVERSAL-MARKDOWN-EXPORT-SYNC invariants: (a) sync_all_markdown_exports.sh exists + executable; (b) running it in --check-only returns 0.
  - Gate CM-COVENANT-114-65-PROPAGATION: anchor literal 11.4.65 in every CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md across canonical-root + parent + 10 owned submodules + nested submodules + HelixQA deps (42-file fleet, same as §11.4.58). Paired meta-test mutations: strip the gate's enforcement literal; strip the anchor literal from a sentinel propagation file; both assert the gate FAILs.
  - Universal (§11.4.17); specific INCLUDED/EXCLUDED path lists are consumer-side. Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-UNIVERSAL-MARKDOWN-EXPORT-SYNC, CM-COVENANT-114-65-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-md-exports, --no-pdf-only, --md-export-not-applicable, --application-internal-doc
- **Honest boundary:** Scope path lists are consumer-side; exclusion only via the closed EXCLUDED set.
- **Composes:** §11.4.12, §11.4.18, §11.4.23, §11.4.44, §11.4.45, §11.4.53, §11.4.56, §11.4.57, §11.4.58, §11.4.59, §11.4.60, §11.4.63, §11.4.64, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.73 — Main-specification document versioning + revision discipline
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:1465-1497
- **Rules:**
  - Scope condition: applies ONLY when a project recognises a main specification document (canonical "what this system does" reference, typically docs/specs/**/specification*.md); projects with none (small libraries, internal tooling) or only per-feature specs/ADRs are exempt unless they elect the pattern. Universal (§11.4.17), conditionally applicable.
  - (1) Every additive operator requirement, refinement or accepted recommendation MUST be applied to the spec before, or as part of, the work that implements it; the spec is the source of truth.
  - (2) Two version axes: Primary (V1/V2/V3...) bumps for major rewrites (substantial architecture changes, foundational scope shifts, deprecating large sections, replacing the tech stack), triggered explicitly by operator decision, old primaries move to archive/ per §11.4.61; Secondary = the §11.4.61 metadata-table Revision integer, bumped for every other change (section additions, mandate landings, structural reorganisation, polish, type-contract refinements), monotonic per §11.4.44.
  - (3) Spec metadata table MUST stay current: Revision bumps in lockstep with the change; Last modified updated; Status summary describes the bump; Fixed and Fixed summary reference relevant work IDs.
  - (4) Cross-document propagation: propagated copies of the spec-change rule (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, project constitution file) MUST reference the active spec file (specification.V<primary>.md), not a stale archived version.
  - (5) Archive: on primary bump the old specification.V<n>.md moves to <spec-dir>/archive/specification.V<n>.md, gains Status: superseded with a Continuation pointer to the new active file; archived .html/.pdf siblings travel with it per §11.4.65.
  - Planned gate CM-SPEC-VERSION-DISCIPLINE: if the project advertises a main spec (via [project].main_spec_path = "docs/specs/.../specification.V<n>.md" in a canonical config file), assert the file exists; its metadata Revision >= highest Revision referenced elsewhere (Issues.md, Fixed.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md); FAIL if commits touch the spec since last Revision bump (operator forgot to bump).
  - Paired §1.1 mutation: backdate the Last modified row while leaving real-content edits -> gate FAILs.
  - Non-compliance (forgetting to bump, or letting the spec drift behind operator-mandated requirements) is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-SPEC-VERSION-DISCIPLINE
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** Applies only where a main spec is recognised; gate stated as planned.
- **Composes:** §11.4.44, §11.4.59, §11.4.61, §11.4.65, §11.4.17, §1.1

#### §11.4.86 — Roster/corpus-backed Status-doc auto-sync mandate
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:1499-1520
- **Rules:**
  - Status docs (§11.4.45) backed by a tracked roster (set of installed apps/components) or tracked asset corpus (directory of test/media assets) MUST be brought back into sync out of the box, mechanically, when a member changes: the Status doc, its Status_Summary, and their HTML + PDF exports.
  - (1) Drift-proof signal: a content fingerprint (sha256 of the sorted member list, NOT mtime, which git checkout resets) persisted in a sidecar next to the Status doc; adding/removing/modifying a member changes it deterministically.
  - (2) Sync helper: regenerates the fingerprint and re-exports HTML + PDF (composing with the §11.4.65 universal exporter); invocable standalone AND wired so sync happens automatically (commit path and/or pre-build).
  - (3) Enforcement gate: a pre-build gate recomputes the live fingerprint and FAILs when it differs from the persisted one, forcing the Status doc update; mirrors §11.4.12 CM-ISSUES-SUMMARY-SYNC + §11.4.45 sync_integration_status.
  - (4) Paired §1.1 mutation: corrupt the fingerprint (drift without doc update) and assert the gate FAILs.
  - Universal (§11.4.17); consuming project supplies specific docs, roster/corpus sources, helper and gate name in its own CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / QWEN.md per §11.4.35. Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-ISSUES-SUMMARY-SYNC
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-roster-sync, --allow-status-drift, --roster-sync-not-applicable
- **Honest boundary:** The fingerprint is FACT, not a guess about freshness; gate name is consumer-supplied.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.12, §11.4.17, §11.4.35, §11.4.45, §11.4.53, §11.4.56, §11.4.57, §11.4.59, §11.4.60, §11.4.65
- **Review addendum:** Gate name is consumer-supplied; the pattern mirrors §11.4.12 CM-ISSUES-SUMMARY-SYNC.

#### §11.4.99 — Latest-Source Documentation Cross-Reference Mandate
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:1522-1570
- **Rules:**
  - Every operator-facing instruction, guide, manual, troubleshooting cookbook or setup walkthrough MUST be cross-referenced against the LATEST official online documentation of the service/library being documented BEFORE it is committed (reason: a stale first-draft guide recommended VoIP numbers and omitted a mandatory pre-login email step, contradicting official docs and risking permanent account bans).
  - (A) Before committing any document with operator-actionable steps (setup walkthroughs, integration guides, API how-tos, credential acquisition, security configs, troubleshooting cookbooks, billing-policy docs, ToS summaries, any external-service interaction guide), the author MUST: (1) fetch the latest official online docs via WebFetch, direct browsing, the service's own MCP server, or equivalent real-time source, NOT training data/memory/prior assumptions/older committed docs; (2) cross-reference each instruction, verifying the service still supports the action, form fields/parameters/endpoints are unchanged, and any new constraints/deprecations/warnings since last verification; (3) seek secondary authoritative sources where official docs are sparse/silent (maintainer guides such as submodules/<lib>/README.md, SUPPORT.md, SECURITY.md; official blog/changelog; official support channels; community-vetted FAQs); (4) cite source URL + date checked at the bottom in a `## Sources verified` section (e.g. `Sources verified 2026-05-28: <urls>`); a doc without it is NOT verified; (5) include a `Sources verified <date>: <urls>` footer line in the commit message.
  - (B) Negative-finding documentation required: if the official source is silent/contradictory/outdated on a question the doc must answer, the doc MUST explicitly note that gap so absence of contradiction is not read as authoritative agreement.
  - (C) Re-verification cadence: docs older than 6 months without re-verification are STALE and MUST NOT be trusted for fresh action. Re-verify: (1) before being cited as authority for an operator-action campaign; (2) at every major release boundary (vN.0.0 tag; the release-gate sweep includes a freshness audit); (3) whenever the documented service publishes a breaking-change announcement; (4) when an operator reports an error following the guide.
  - (D) Docs for these service families MUST include explicit safety warnings cross-referenced against latest published policies with a Sources-verified date NEVER older than 90 days: Telegram/WhatsApp/messenger unofficial clients (anti-abuse observation; one-phone-one-app-id limits; ban-on-VoIP; rate-limit floods; impersonation risks; pre-login declaration emails); Cloud provider APIs AWS/GCP/Azure/Cloudflare (billing blast-radius; account-lock; quotas; least-privilege IAM; data residency); Payment systems Stripe/PayPal/banks/Mercado Pago (KYC/AML; PCI-DSS; webhook signature verification; idempotency keys; refund/chargeback); AI/LLM providers Anthropic/OpenAI/Google AI (ToS violation triggers; rate-limit/quota; data retention; safety-classifier outcomes; PII-in-prompt); Code-hosting GitHub/GitLab/GitFlic/GitVerse/Bitbucket (token-leak revocation; force-push to protected branches; API-token rate limits; secret-scanning bots); OS/package managers apt/brew/npm/pip/cargo (supply-chain compromise; signature verification; lockfile discipline; mirror trust). List NOT exhaustive: a new service with comparable risk surface gets the same requirement.
  - (E) §11.4.92 Pass 4 (deep-research validation) cannot substitute for §11.4.99; the two pass independently; deep research is mandatory for ALL operator-facing instruction docs, not just non-trivial code changes.
  - (F) Every consuming repo's CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / QWEN.md MUST carry a short-form restatement citing literal anchor 11.4.99; gate CM-COVENANT-114-99-PROPAGATION (when implemented) enforces it; paired §1.1 mutations strip the literal -> gates FAIL.
  - (G) Enforcement: a commit adding/modifying operator-facing instruction docs without (a) a "Sources verified <date>" footer in the doc AND (b) a `Sources verified` line in the commit-message footer is blocked at release-gate. A doc that goes stale (>6 months, or >90 days for risk-classified services per (D)) graduates to §11.4.90 Obsolete with `Obsolete-Details: Reason=stale-documentation; superseded-by=<replacement-doc-or-rewrite>` after the 30-day grace window per §11.4.90.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-99-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-source-check, --documentation-freshness-optional, --cite-sources-later, --trust-prior-doc-as-authoritative
- **Honest boundary:** Closes a gap §11.4.92 Pass 4 only alludes to; risk-family list is not exhaustive; propagation gate "when implemented".
- **Composes:** §11.4.4, §11.4.5, §11.4.8, §11.4.35, §11.4.90, §11.4.92, §11.4.98, §107

#### §11.4.106 — Docs Chain: mechanical documentation/DB sync engine
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:1572-1604
- **Rules:**
  - Docs Chain (the vasic-digital/docs_chain engine; Go-implemented bidirectional document-and-database dependency-propagation engine) is the canonical mechanical enforcer of the documentation-sync mandates; MANDATORY for every consuming project. Normative spec is the engine's own docs docs/CONSTITUTION_INTEGRATION.md and docs/USE_CASE_CATALOGUE.md; implementations code against the engine's contract, not a paraphrase.
  - (A) Use the engine, never ad-hoc scripts: consume it BY REFERENCE (flat-layout sibling ~/Projects/docs_chain during local dev / the constitution-exposed path once the Phase-6 submodule pointer lands), inherited like §11.4.80's codegraph_* scripts, NEVER copied into the consumer. Ad-hoc per-project scripts (sync_issues_docs.sh, generate_*_summary.sh, sync_*_export.sh, update_readme_doc_links.sh, et al.) are superseded and MUST be retired as each matching context is registered.
  - (B) Consumer-owned contexts via config: the engine is project-agnostic with NO project-specific path/chain; consumers register chains as data via .docs_chain/contexts/*.yaml at their project root, one context per file, per §11.4.28 decoupling. state.json (<project-root>/.docs_chain/state.json, regenerated by `docs_chain sync`) and *.docs_chain.tmp staging sidecars are gitignored; the consumer owns those .gitignore entries.
  - (C) Anchors it mechanizes (enforced in place of the ad-hoc script once the context is registered): §11.4.12, §11.4.53, §11.4.45, §11.4.56, §11.4.57, §11.4.59, §11.4.60, §11.4.65, §11.4.86, §11.4.93, §11.4.95, §12.10, §11.4.44. Engine-wide guarantees: change detection by content hash NOT mtime (§11.4.86); atomic-rename + SQLite-transaction commit with rollback on any transform error and optional hardlink backup (§9.2); a both-dirty sync pair surfaces a CONFLICT, never a silent merge (exit 2, §11.4.6); `verify` is the deterministic CI/pre-build sink-side gate over byte-stable transforms (§11.4.50); per-run captured evidence at qa-results/docs_chain/<run-id>/ (§11.4.69).
  - (D) It does NOT replace authoring discipline: the source author still writes the §11.4.44 revision header; the engine keeps derived exports in sync; the engine is no licence to skip authoring.
  - (E) Anti-bluff (MANDATORY): Docs Chain NEVER fakes a transform; a missing pandoc/weasyprint (or any absent tool) surfaces a typed ToolAbsentError (IsToolAbsent) and an honest §11.4.3 SKIP-with-reason, never a fake PASS, never a partial write; every sync/verify run carries real captured evidence; a metadata-only/absence-of-error/config-only PASS at the sync layer is a PASS-bluff.
  - (F) Write-seam hook enforcement (extension, 2026-07-15): sync MUST be ENFORCED AT THE WRITE SEAMS, not agent vigilance. The consumer MUST wire the engine's `verify` (and where safe `sync`) into: (1) the COMMIT seam, a pre-commit/commit-wrapper hook that REFUSES a commit whose staged set touches a chain SOURCE while its derived exports/DB rows are stale; (2) the BUILD seam, the pre-build gate; (3) the CONSTITUTION-PULL seam, the §11.4.164 post_update_hook.sh invocation. A stale CONTINUATION.md (§12.10), stale standing session-resumption file (§11.4.131), or stale memory/knowledge artefact while live state has moved is a violation of the same severity as a stale export.
  - Universal (§11.4.17); projects with no derived-export or DB-sync surface inherit the anchor latently (binds the moment they ship one; §11.4.96 pattern).
  - Coverage per §11.4.4(b): propagation gate CM-COVENANT-114-106-PROPAGATION enforces literal 11.4.106 across the consumer fleet (parent + owned-submodule CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / QWEN.md); paired §1.1 mutation strips the literal -> gate FAILs; gate-code is a separate work item.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-106-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** --ad-hoc-sync-ok, --skip-docs-chain, --fake-transform, --sync-evidence-optional
- **Honest boundary:** Engine Phases 1-4 implemented+tested but the CLI/loader is untracked and the engine is NOT yet a registered git submodule (Phase 6 planned, operator-gated); consumers MUST NOT claim behaviour a phase has not shipped. Seam hooks give eventual-consistency-at-every-write, NOT literal real-time; claiming real-time without a filesystem-watch daemon is a bluff, and the daemon is a tracked §11.4.197 upgrade path.
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.3, §11.4.4, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.12, §11.4.17, §11.4.28, §11.4.44, §11.4.45, §11.4.50, §11.4.53, §11.4.56, §11.4.57, §11.4.59, §11.4.60, §11.4.65, §11.4.69, §11.4.80, §11.4.86, §11.4.93, §11.4.95, §11.4.96, §11.4.131, §11.4.164, §11.4.197, §12.10, §9.2, §1.1

#### §11.4.153 — Comprehensive per-feature Status + Status_Summary set with mandatory video-recording confirmation
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:1608-1632
- **Rules:**
  - Every project MUST maintain under docs/features/ a feature Status document set (Status.md + its §11.4.56 Status_Summary.md) enumerating EVERY system component, EVERY client application/binary/surface (TUI/CLI/Web/desktop/mobile/API/gRPC/library/submodule/infrastructure) and EVERY feature, including features ported from any incorporated CLI-agent/submodule catalogue (§11.4.74), with NO feature left out.
  - (1) Total, categorized coverage: per-feature table organised Component -> Category, reconciled against the actual codebase; a code-present feature absent from the table, or a row with no code, is a violation; "looks complete" without a code-reconciliation pass is a §11.4.6/§11.4.118 bluff.
  - (2) Per-feature fields: Component, Feature, Category, Implementation status, Wiring status (genuinely reachable by an end user, not merely compiled, §11.4.108), Real-use status, Tests-coverage status (four-layer §11.4.4(b)), Validation status (closed vocabulary PASS / FAIL / SKIP / PENDING_FORENSICS / OPERATOR-BLOCKED per §11.4.45), and Video-recording confirmation (path to captured real-use video or honest gap marker).
  - (3) Each user-visible feature's "confirmed working" claim MUST be backed by a recorded real-use video of a genuine end-user scenario (real prompts -> real LLM/service responses -> real results); NEVER a frozen/stale frame (§11.4.107 liveness), NEVER faked/mocked/demo-loop/bluff response, NEVER an LLM error/garbage response passed off as success. Videos are captured evidence per §11.4.2/§11.4.5 at the project-declared recording path (§11.4.35). Where autonomous capture is infeasible: honest §11.4.3/§11.4.52 SKIP-with-reason + tracked migration item, NEVER a faked confirmation.
  - (4) Every recorded video MUST be analysed; any defect it surfaces MUST trigger the §11.4.102 systematic-debugging -> fix -> §11.4.146 retest -> re-record loop, iterating to a clean GO per §11.4.134 before the feature is marked confirmed; a video exposing a broken feature is a §11.4.4 test-interrupt.
  - (5) Always-in-sync mechanically: a §11.4.45-class roster/corpus-backed Status doc, kept in sync via the §11.4.106 docs_chain engine + §11.4.86 fingerprint (sha256 of the sorted feature-key roster AND sorted video-artefact roster, NOT mtime); stale = violation.
  - (6) Four-format export: HTML + PDF + DOCX (this class ADDS DOCX to §11.4.65's HTML+PDF), all in sync per §11.4.60.
  - (7) Follows the Status-doc family: §11.4.44 (revision header), §11.4.45 (maintenance + captured-evidence table + operator-blocked-at-top), §11.4.56 (two-audience parity), §11.4.57 (README doc-link row), §11.4.59/§11.4.60 (always-sync composite).
  - (8) MP4 format REQUIRED for all video confirmations (H.264, movflags +faststart, pix_fmt yuv420p). Window-specific capture ONLY (§11.4.159(A)). Vision validation REQUIRED (§11.4.159(D)). .cast (asciinema) files are supplementary only; primary evidence is the .mp4.
  - Universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies docs/features/ layout, feature roster source, recording path and DOCX exporter per §11.4.35.
  - Propagation gate CM-COVENANT-114-153-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.153); recommended gates CM-FEATURE-STATUS-COMPLETE (every code-present feature has a row + every row maps to code) and CM-FEATURE-STATUS-VIDEO-CONFIRMED (every user-visible confirmed row cites a real captured video or honest SKIP); paired §1.1 mutation (strip literal -> propagation FAILs; mark feature confirmed with no real video / drop a code-present feature -> feature-status gates FAIL; gate-code separate work item). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-153-PROPAGATION, CM-FEATURE-STATUS-COMPLETE, CM-FEATURE-STATUS-VIDEO-CONFIRMED
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-feature-status, --feature-without-video, --frozen-video-OK, --bluff-response-video-OK, --skip-video-analysis, --feature-ledger-incomplete-OK, --no-docx-export, --allow-feature-ledger-drift
- **Honest boundary:** The set guarantees a complete, video-confirmed, always-synced ledger; it does NOT prove any single feature's correctness (rests on the cited §11.4.69/§11.4.107/§11.4.123 evidence) and does NOT replace §11.4.40 full-suite retest.
- **Composes:** §11.4.2, §11.4.4, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.17, §11.4.35, §11.4.44, §11.4.45, §11.4.52, §11.4.56, §11.4.57, §11.4.59, §11.4.60, §11.4.65, §11.4.74, §11.4.86, §11.4.102, §11.4.106, §11.4.107, §11.4.108, §11.4.118, §11.4.123, §11.4.134, §11.4.146, §11.4.159, §1.1

#### §11.4.168 — Exported-document independent content + textual + full-visual validation mandate
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:1634-1654
- **Rules:**
  - Every generated/exported document (HTML, PDF, DOCX, or any format in the §11.4.65 export scope, and the §11.4.153 four-format Status set adding DOCX) MUST pass INDEPENDENT validation by a review agent structurally separate from the generator (§11.4.70/.20 dedicated subagent or distinct human; NEVER the author/generator self-checking; §11.4.92 self-evaluation precedes and never satisfies; the §11.4.142 every-change-review applied to exports).
  - Validation MUST run on BOTH the source Markdown AND every exported artifact derived from it, ALWAYS (every export, not a sampled subset), across THREE layers, ALL of which MUST hold.
  - (1) CONTENT layer: export faithfully carries source intent + data: nothing dropped, truncated, re-ordered into nonsense, garbled; every section, table, list, code block, figure caption, link present and complete (table truncated to first page, collapsed list, omitted section, link stripped of target are findings); cross-check export against source, not merely "file exists and non-empty" (§11.4.5/.69 quality bar).
  - (2) TEXTUAL layer: export human-readable: NO raw markup, NO diagram source, NO unrendered code-fence body leaking as body text. Forbidden as body text: raw Mermaid source (`mermaid`, `gantt`, `graph`, `flowchart`, `sequenceDiagram`, `classDiagram`, `stateDiagram`, `erDiagram`, `pie`, `gitGraph`, `journey`, `dateFormat`, `section ...`, `:done,`/`:active,`/`:crit,` task lines, closing-fence residue), raw HTML tags shown as visible text, raw LaTeX/math source where rendering was intended, any triple-backtick code-fence whose intended rendering was to replace the source. Detection reads the exported artifact as text (e.g. `pdftotext` on PDF, rendered DOM/text of HTML, extracted text of DOCX) and asserts forbidden tokens do NOT appear as body text.
  - (3) FULL VISUAL layer: embedded diagrams render as IMAGES not source; layout intact; no overlapping/cut-off/clipped/garbled/collapsed/blank content. Verified by RENDERING the export and inspecting the rendered result, never source or intermediate alone: `pdftotext` (catches raw diagram source as text), `pdfimages` (or format's image enumeration) to CONFIRM intended diagrams are present as images (zero embedded images where a diagram was intended is a VISUAL finding), `pdftoppm`->OCR (§11.4.117/§11.4.107(12), confidence floor + ROI) to confirm the rasterised page carries readable visual content and re-catch raw-source-as-pixels. Captured evidence per §11.4.5/.69/.107 (`pdftotext_body.txt`, `pdfimages_manifest.txt`, `ocr_pages/`, per-finding pinpoint page/region/token, expected vs actual) accompanies every verdict.
  - (4) Anti-bluff: a rubber-stamp "export looks fine" is NOT validation. The validator is self-validated with a golden-good/golden-bad pair per §11.4.107(10): golden-good (clean rendered diagram + faithful content) MUST PASS; golden-bad (export seeded with raw Mermaid gantt source as body text plus a truncated table) MUST FAIL; a validator passing golden-bad is a bluff gate investigated per §11.4.102 before further use. Validation iterates to clean GO per §11.4.134: any finding in ANY layer (BLOCKING/nit/warning) re-arms the loop (generator fixes, e.g. pre-renders diagram to an image, export regenerated, validator RE-VALIDATES) until GO with ZERO findings and ZERO warnings, every verdict backed by captured rendered-artifact evidence.
  - A document shipped WITHOUT this validation, or containing raw diagram source / unreadable garble / dropped content in the exported artifact, is a PASS-bluff at the documentation layer.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies pre-render pipeline, exporters, rendered-artifact validators (text extraction / image enumeration / rasterise->OCR) per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-168-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.168 across the consumer fleet), CM-EXPORTED-DOC-VISUALLY-VALIDATED (every exported document in the §11.4.65 scope carries an independent-validation marker from a validator structurally separate from the generator asserting the three layers PASS on the exported artifact with captured rendered-artifact evidence; validator self-validated by golden-good/golden-bad pair); paired section 1.1 mutation (strip literal -> propagation FAILs; PDF/HTML/DOCX with raw gantt lines as body text -> gate FAILs; golden-bad fixture -> self-validation FAILs); gate-code = separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-visual-validation, --raw-source-in-pdf-ok, --textual-check-suffices, --self-validate-export, --diagram-source-as-text-ok
- **Honest boundary:** Confirms the EXPORTED artifact carries source content faithfully, is textually readable and renders visuals as images; does NOT prove the source content correct (§11.4.142 review + §11.4.135 guards) and does NOT replace the §11.4.65 mtime-parity freshness gate (freshness is not readability). A FLAG_SECURE/DRM/sink-blanked surface that cannot be rasterised documents the gap per §11.4.112 and uses the §11.4.117 proxy oracle, never a faked visual PASS. Grepping HTML for class="mermaid" is a source-side check, not an exported-artifact check.
- **Composes:** §11.4.65, §11.4.73, §11.4.107, §11.4.117, §11.4.135, §11.4.138, §11.4.142, §11.4.159, §11.4.163, §11.4.165, §11.4.153, §11.4.70, §11.4.20, §11.4.92, §11.4.134, §11.4.102, §11.4.5, §11.4.69, §11.4.112, §11.4.108, §1.1, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.186 — Anti-divergence enforcement: cross-document consistency is a mandatory-before-export/commit gate
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:1656
- **Rules:**
  - Any project maintaining more than one representation of the same tracked data (delivery plan + MVP brief + workable-items DB + summaries + .md/.html/.pdf/.docx exports) MUST enforce cross-document CONSISTENCY as a deterministic gate running BEFORE any export render, any doc/DB sync `verify`, and any doc-set commit; NEVER an after-the-fact human audit run only when an operator asks.
  - (1) One no-divergence verdict, three seams: a single deterministic PASS/FAIL/SKIP verdict (a cross-document integrity validator composed with the workable-items-DB internal `validate`) gates all three write-seams (export / sync-verify / commit); a FAIL at any seam refuses that seam naming the exact offending records (§11.4.6 actionable).
  - (2) Five decidable check families: DEDUP (no two records describe one feature with divergent timeline/status/release; keyed on ticket OR normalised (subject, scope), NOT bare subject substring); TIMELINE (start <= deadline; no deadline-before-dependency; no dependency cycle; GATED exempt-but-marked); CROSS-DOC (same item across every representation carries identical timeline/status/type against a NAMED authoritative source); INTEGRITY (no orphan refs; Status<->Type §11.4.33; location<->status); STRUCTURAL (required columns; ID uniqueness+monotonicity §11.4.54).
  - (3) Drift-proof trigger: a §11.4.86 sha256-of-sorted-members fingerprint of the authoritative inputs re-arms the gate on ANY input change so a stale verify cannot pass on changed data.
  - (4) Self-validated analyzer (§11.4.107(10)): ships golden-good (MUST PASS) + one golden-bad per family (MUST FAIL, pinpointing the offender) + a negative-control (distinct same-subject tasks that MUST PASS, the false-positive guard); a validator passing golden-bad, or failing golden-good/negative-control, is itself a bluff and a release blocker.
  - (5) Reusable + decoupled (§11.4.28/.31): packaged as a depth-1 reusable engine under the constitution submodule per the §11.4.28(C) carve-out with a `helix-deps.yaml`; project-specific doc-sets + authoritative-source bindings live in a consumer-owned checkset (data, never engine code).
  - (6) Supersedes ad-hoc audits: per-cycle `*_INTEGRITY_FINDINGS.md` / `RECONCILIATION_*.md` after-the-fact audit docs are retired in favour of the gate.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-186-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.186), CM-DOC-INTEGRITY-VALIDATION (5 invariants: validator present+executable; consumer checkset present; no-divergence gate wired into each of the three seams; fingerprint sidecar fresh; `selfcheck` golden-good/golden-bad/negative-control wired into meta-test); paired section 1.1 mutation
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-divergence-gate, --audit-after-export-OK, --cross-doc-check-not-applicable, --unvalidated-analyzer-OK, --divergent-commit-OK
- **Honest boundary:** The gate proves internal CONSISTENCY (no record diverges, no timeline incoherent, every ref resolves), NOT plan CORRECTNESS (achievability/date-rightness remain operator/management decisions the gate SURFACES, never MAKES).
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.12, §11.4.33, §11.4.44, §11.4.50, §11.4.53, §11.4.54, §11.4.60, §11.4.65, §11.4.73, §11.4.75, §11.4.85, §11.4.86, §11.4.91, §11.4.93, §11.4.95, §11.4.106, §11.4.107, §11.4.108, §11.4.110, §11.4.148, §11.4.176, §11.4.28, §11.4.31

#### §11.4.212 — Main README is the canonical entry point for ALL project documentation; no orphan docs
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:1658-1672
- **Rules:**
  - The main README (`README.md` at repo root) is the canonical STARTING POINT for ALL project documentation, for this project and every project incorporating the constitution.
  - Every project document in the §11.4.65 export scope, INCLUDING the §11.4.185 manual-tests catalog, §11.4.153 per-feature Status/Status_Summary docs, Issues/Fixed trackers + summaries (§11.4.12/.53/.57), and every guide/research note/changelog/script companion doc, MUST be reachable/linked (DIRECTLY or TRANSITIVELY) from the main README. No document may be an ORPHAN; a doc no link-path from README reaches is a violation.
  - Strict generalisation of §11.4.57 (which mandated a `Tracked-Items + Status Documents` README section for the tracker/status set).
  - (A) Reachability = a link path: README -> guide -> sub-doc is fine; SOME path from README must reach every in-scope doc, not necessarily direct links.
  - (B) Always-sync (§11.4.59 / §11.4.106 docs-chain): README doc-graph kept current mechanically; a newly-added §11.4.65-scope doc no README-reachable path links is a violation the moment it lands; the manual-tests catalog MUST be linked from README.
  - (C) Reachability is a link-graph property (FINDABLE), not a claim about correctness or freshness (those stay §11.4.44 / §11.4.106 / the doc's own gates).
  - (D) Composition with §11.4.57: §11.4.57's `Tracked-Items` section remains the mandated README landing block for tracker/status set; §11.4.212 adds that EVERY other in-scope doc is reachable (§11.4.57 specialisation, §11.4.212 generalisation).
  - (E) README INTRODUCTION + ILLUSTRATION (ext. 2026-08-15): README MUST open with a SHORT introduction (what the project is, who it is for, current state at a glance) AND MUST ILLUSTRATE all work done: for every major capability, a direct summary paragraph OR a link to a detailed document explaining WHAT was done AND WHY (never orphaned links, never "see the changelog" as the only explanation). Every linked document MUST justify its existence in one sentence at the link site; a link with no "why this matters" is a violation.
  - (F) LINKAGE-COMPLETENESS RATCHET (ext. 2026-08-15): the reachability graph from README (transitively per (A)) MUST cover the full §11.4.65-scope doc-set enumeration with a monotone-decreasing UNREACHED count (mirrors §11.4.135 ratchet); a §11.4.65-scope doc not reachable from README at pre-build/release seams FAILs the extended gate; brownfield adoption per operator §11.4.66 (§11.4.224(E) fence). The `CM-COVENANT-114-212-PROPAGATION` gate stays unchanged; `CM-README-DOC-ENTRYPOINT-COMPLETE` is EXTENDED with (E)/(F); a new paired mutation strips the introduction, or removes a "why this matters" annotation, or breaks reachability of an in-scope doc -> extended gate FAILs.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies README path, manual-tests-catalog path, §11.4.65 doc-set enumeration per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-212-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.212 across consumer fleet), CM-README-DOC-ENTRYPOINT-COMPLETE (every §11.4.65-scope document reachable directly or transitively from main README; manual-tests catalog linked; extended with clauses (E)/(F)); paired section 1.1 meta-test mutation (orphan an in-scope doc -> gate FAILs; strip literal -> propagation FAILs); gate-code = separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --orphan-doc-OK, --readme-not-entrypoint, --skip-readme-link, --doc-unreachable-OK
- **Honest boundary:** Reachability is a link-graph property (every doc FINDABLE from README), not a claim about each doc's correctness or freshness.
- **Composes:** §11.4.57, §11.4.59, §11.4.65, §11.4.106, §11.4.153, §11.4.185, §11.4.44, §11.4.12, §11.4.53, §11.4.91, §11.4.135, §11.4.66, §11.4.224

#### §11.4.215 — A doc that BINDS work MUST live, tracked, in the repository where that work happens
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:1674-1686
- **Rules:**
  - Any document that BINDS work (defines a gate or acceptance criterion, states a contract the work is judged against, or carries a plan/order the work must satisfy) MUST be tracked, in the repository where that work happens, at a declared path, BEFORE it may be cited as binding.
  - (1) BINDING => TRACKED, and un-tracked => NOT BINDING: a binding claim sourced from an untracked or out-of-tree document MUST NOT be enforced against any work; land the document or decline the gate, never obey a citation of it.
  - (2) IN THE REPOSITORY THE WORK HAPPENS IN: tracked in a sibling checkout, scratch directory, chat message, issue comment, or personal note is NOT tracked for this purpose; test: can someone cloning ONLY the repo the work happens in read the binding text at its declared path? Where a binding doc governs several repos, it is inherited BY REFERENCE from a shared tracked version-controlled dependency (§11.4.28/§11.4.177), never copied, never left out-of-tree.
  - (3) The prior question §11.4.212 cannot ask: §11.4.212 enumerates the in-repo scope and checks reachability (answers "is it findable?"); §11.4.215 answers "is it here at all?". Once in-repo, §11.4.212, §11.4.44 (revision header), §11.4.65/.73 (exports), §11.4.106 (sync) all attach normally; this anchor is their precondition.
  - (4) Generalisation of §11.4.95 (authoritative tracker DB tracked, never gitignored) to ANY doc that binds work. §11.4.11 counterweight stays intact: logs, forensic captures, scratch artifacts remain out-of-tree and untracked by default; a doc's being untracked is only a defect once it is CITED as binding; binding is what pulls a document into the repository.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies repository, declared binding-doc paths, shared-dependency mechanism per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-215-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.215), CM-BINDING-DOC-IN-REPO (every doc cited as binding by a gate, order, or acceptance contract resolves to a tracked path in the repo the work happens in, or is inherited by reference from a tracked shared dependency; a citation resolving to an untracked or out-of-tree path FAILs); paired section 1.1 mutation (move a binding doc out of the tree or untrack it while a gate cites it -> FAILs; strip literal -> propagation FAILs); gate-code = separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --binding-doc-out-of-tree, --untracked-gate-definition, --cite-doc-nobody-can-read, --scratch-dir-is-good-enough, --binding-by-rumour
- **Honest boundary:** In-repo presence proves the binding text is AVAILABLE, ATTRIBUTABLE, VERSION-CONTROLLED; it proves nothing about correctness/currency/self-consistency (§11.4.44/.106/.186) nor whether the gate is well-seated (§11.4.120 seam-placement).
- **Composes:** §11.4.11, §11.4.28, §11.4.30, §11.4.35, §11.4.44, §11.4.57, §11.4.65, §11.4.73, §11.4.95, §11.4.106, §11.4.120, §11.4.177, §11.4.186, §11.4.197, §11.4.212

#### §11.4.257 — Comprehensive user-manual + guide + FAQ coverage for every component / service / feature / workflow
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:1688-1708
- **Rules:**
  - Every project MUST cover the WHOLE project (every component, service, subsystem, binary, container, plugin, feature, user-visible workflow) with three cooperating documentation classes: (a) complete USER MANUAL per component/service/product, (b) task-oriented GUIDES for every user-facing workflow, (c) properly-created FAQs derived from real operator/QA/end-user questions; always in sync with shipped code, exported per §11.4.65, reachable from README per §11.4.212, regenerated via Docs-Chain per §11.4.106, tracked as workable items when incomplete per §11.4.197. A surface shipping without its trio is a violation of PASS-bluff severity at the documentation layer.
  - Generalises §11.4.18 (script docs) and §11.4.153 (per-feature Status set) into the full three-class floor for every user-facing surface; binds §11.4.212 + §11.4.106 + §11.4.65 into the always-in-sync guarantee.
  - (A) COMPREHENSIVE COVERAGE, no orphan capability: every shipped-surface item (per the §11.4.153 feature Status roster or equivalent SSoT) MUST map to at least ONE user manual, at least ONE task-oriented guide per user workflow it exposes, and one FAQ entry per real recurring question; a capability with no manual/guide/FAQ is UNSHIPPABLE regardless of code quality.
  - (B) THREE DISTINCT CLASSES, none substitutes another: (a) MANUAL: operator reference: what it is/does, inputs/outputs/env vars/config/ports/dependencies, start/stop/status commands, logs/metrics/health surface, failure modes + remediation; complete enough to run, supervise and debug without reading source. (b) GUIDES: one per user-facing workflow (setup, configuration, integration, migration, troubleshooting, security-hardening); real journey with prerequisites, step-by-step commands, expected output per step, verification checkpoints, rollback path. (c) FAQs: from real recurring signal (operator questions, QA reports, end-user tickets, agent-found-defect narratives), NEVER fabricated marketing FAQ; every entry cites question source class + resolution + link to the manual/guide section owning the durable answer.
  - (C) ALWAYS IN SYNC: every doc carries §11.4.44 revision header; Docs-Chain (§11.4.106) bound at commit/build/constitution-pull write-seams so an edited component with stale docs REFUSES the commit; four-format export per §11.4.65 (.md + .html + .pdf, + .docx where class warrants per §11.4.153 exception); every doc reachable transitively from README per §11.4.212. FAQ entries describing now-fixed defects are RETAINED with a "resolved in vN.N.N" note, never silently deleted.
  - (D) TRACKABLE COMPLETION: missing docs are §11.4.197 items; the workable-items DB (§11.4.93/.95) carries per-surface docs-status rows so "what is documented/what is not" is a live query.
  - (E) HONESTY: a genuine gap (new capability whose docs are in flight) is HONESTLY MARKED at both the README entry point and the component's Status.md (§11.4.153) as `[DOC-PENDING: <tracker-id>]` per §11.4.223, NEVER silently omitted, NEVER faked with a placeholder paragraph saying nothing (a fake-doc is a PASS-bluff).
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-257-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.257), CM-USER-MANUAL-PER-COMPONENT, CM-GUIDE-PER-USER-WORKFLOW, CM-FAQ-FROM-REAL-QUESTIONS; paired section 1.1 meta-test mutations
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-user-manual, --guide-later, --faq-optional, --capability-without-docs-OK, --fake-doc-placeholder-OK, --source-of-truth-is-code-comments
- **Honest boundary:** Mandates the documentation EXISTS, is IN SYNC, REACHABLE; does NOT verify semantic correctness (stays §11.4.99, §11.4.194, §11.4.238 coverage-escape audit). "Comprehensive" is bounded to the shipped-surface enumeration; an internal implementation detail with no user-facing exposure has no user-manual obligation (lives under §11.4.18 or design docs).
- **Composes:** §11.4.11, §11.4.18, §11.4.44, §11.4.65, §11.4.86, §11.4.99, §11.4.106, §11.4.148, §11.4.153, §11.4.194, §11.4.197, §11.4.208, §11.4.212, §11.4.223, §11.4.238, §11.4.93, §11.4.95, §11.4.138

#### §11.4.258 — Architecture + data-flow + state-machine + sequence-diagram coverage embedded in docs
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:1712-1732
- **Rules:**
  - Every project MUST cover the WHOLE project with properly created graphs/diagrams/schemes across FOUR canonical classes: (a) SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE (services, containers, ports, dependencies, deployment topology), (b) DATA FLOW (information movement between components, storage, external systems), (c) STATE MACHINE (lifecycle of every stateful entity: workable items, orchestrator sessions, long-ops, agents, deploys), (d) SEQUENCE (per critical user workflow and per critical cross-component protocol); INCORPORATED into the existing documentation surface (README, manuals per §11.4.257, guides, Status docs per §11.4.153, design docs per §11.4.218/.219) at the natural point of use, NEVER a lone diagram directory.
  - Every diagram is (i) exported in a scale-appropriate open format (SVG structural; PNG raster fallback; source in diffable text: Mermaid, PlantUML, D2, or diffable SVG source; §11.4.220, never proprietary-tool-only master), (ii) rendered non-blank + non-degenerate + accurate (§11.4.107(10) analyzer discipline; a blank/mislabelled/truncated diagram is a bluff), (iii) reachable from README per §11.4.212, (iv) in sync via §11.4.106 Docs-Chain so a code change invalidating a diagram REFUSES the commit until updated.
  - Strengthens §11.4.218 and §11.4.219 from design-side to whole-project documentation-side diagram coverage.
  - (A) FOUR-CLASS COVERAGE: ARCHITECTURE: deployed/deployable topology (every service, container, binary, port, external dependency, host/network/storage boundary) kept true to the actual docker-compose.yml/deployment manifest/running system; DATA FLOW: source -> transformation -> sink, each edge annotated with format + protocol + trust boundary; STATE MACHINE: lifecycle of every stateful entity (workable items §11.4.15, long-ops §11.4.232, orchestrator sessions §11.4.187, agents §11.4.147, deploy artifacts §11.4.108, builds), transitions labelled with triggering event and guard; SEQUENCE: one per critical user workflow and critical cross-component protocol; actors + messages + return paths + failure branches, not only happy path.
  - (B) INCORPORATION never orphan: each diagram at point of use (architecture in README + `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; per-service data-flow in that service's manual; state-machine in the doc owning the state; sequence in the workflow's guide); a `docs/diagrams/` gallery may exist as an index but the load-bearing appearance is EMBEDDED, per §11.4.212 reachability.
  - (C) OPEN + DIFFABLE: sources in diffable text, never proprietary-tool-only masters; rendered outputs committed alongside sources; renderers §11.4.201-probed before use, absent tool => §11.4.3 SKIP-with-reason, not fake output (§11.4.222).
  - (D) ACCURACY VERIFICATION: probe render exists (Mermaid parse-check; SVG geometry check; §11.4.107(10) golden-good vs golden-bad-with-drift fixture for derived-from-code diagrams); diagram diverging from SSoT (compose file, workable-items schema, orchestrator registry) caught by §11.4.86-fingerprint diff on the SSoT + stale-diagram audit at pre-build; Docs-Chain (§11.4.106) refuses a commit changing an SSoT without a diagram refresh where a mapped diagram exists.
  - (E) DERIVED-WHERE-POSSIBLE: prefer derived/generated diagrams (compose-file-driven architecture, schema-driven state machine, route-table-driven sequence); hand-drawn diagrams are LABELED as such with an authored-date and reconciled against the SSoT at each release round.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-258-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.258), CM-ARCHITECTURE-DIAGRAM-PRESENT-ACCURATE, CM-DATAFLOW-DIAGRAM-PER-SERVICE, CM-STATEMACHINE-DIAGRAM-PER-STATEFUL-ENTITY, CM-SEQUENCE-DIAGRAM-PER-CRITICAL-WORKFLOW, CM-DIAGRAM-EMBEDDED-NOT-ORPHAN; paired section 1.1 mutations
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-architecture-diagram, --diagram-in-orphan-directory, --proprietary-master-only, --stale-diagram-OK, --dataflow-implied-from-code, --sequence-later
- **Honest boundary:** Mandates diagrams EXIST, are ACCURATE against their SSoT, EMBEDDED, RENDERED HONESTLY; does NOT require every class for every project (an internal library with no runtime deployment ships its module-dependency diagram in place of ARCHITECTURE). Bounded to the whole-project coverage the mandate names.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.65, §11.4.86, §11.4.106, §11.4.107(10), §11.4.153, §11.4.201, §11.4.212, §11.4.216, §11.4.218, §11.4.219, §11.4.220, §11.4.222, §11.4.223, §11.4.257, §11.4.15, §11.4.232, §11.4.187, §11.4.147, §11.4.108, §11.4.3

#### §11.4.259 — README quality-status badge row: closed green-amber-red vocabulary, machine-derived, production-readiness gauge
- **Source:** documentation-and-export.md:1736-1758
- **Rules:**
  - Every project MUST render, at the TOP of the main README (immediately below the H1, above the introduction), a comprehensive BADGE ROW carrying every applicable quality signal with a CLOSED color vocabulary from GREEN (ok) through AMBER (attention) to RED (not ok), plus a production-readiness gauge; EVERY badge backed by MACHINE-DERIVED source data (never hand-typed, §11.4.6). A README lacking the row, or with fabricated/stale/non-source-backed badges, is a violation of PASS-bluff severity.
  - Extends §11.4.57 with a symmetric badge section; binds §11.4.106 (Docs-Chain regeneration on every state change), §11.4.86 (fingerprint-driven sync from the SSoT), §11.4.201 (badge is a guard for the reader's eye).
  - (A) CLOSED COLOR VOCABULARY: GREEN = healthy at target (all constraints met, no findings); AMBER = attention (on-target but degrading, or off-target within acceptable band, or blocked on a tracked follow-up); RED = not ok (off-target beyond band, a §11.4.108 gate failing, a §11.4.135 uncovered guard, an open release-blocker); optional GRAY = N/A with an inline note explaining why. NO other colors/verdicts (no yellow, orange, beta gradations).
  - (B) BADGE CLASS FLOOR (minimum; project additions welcome as §11.4.35 DATA, subtraction is not): (1) BUILD status (last build green/red, artifact fingerprint); (2) TEST-BREADTH per §11.4.27/§11.4.169 (unit/integration/e2e/full-automation/security/performance/anti-bluff, one badge per type or a rollup with click-through per §11.4.224); (3) CODE COVERAGE per §11.4.224 (measured %, green >= target, amber >= ratchet-floor, red below); (4) SECURITY POSTURE per §11.4.184 SonarQube + supply-chain integrity per §11.4.246 (reproducible + hermetic + SLSA Build Level 2 fleet minimum); (5) DOCUMENTATION completeness per §11.4.257 (fraction of shipped surfaces with manual+guide+FAQ trio); (6) DIAGRAM completeness per §11.4.258 (fraction with required non-stale diagram set); (7) LIVE HEALTH where applicable (uptime/SLO/recent crash rate); (8) OPEN DEFECTS per §11.4.15 (Queued + In-progress + Reopened counts, most-reopened highlighted per §11.4.189); (9) SUPPLY-CHAIN integrity level per §11.4.246 (SLSA level tracked in `docs/security/SLSA_LEVEL.md`, fleet minimum L2); (10) ZERO-SHORTCOMINGS status per §11.4.261 (audit-sweep verdict); (11) MACHINE-EVIDENCE COVERAGE per §11.4.262 (fraction of PASS claims with captured evidence paths); (12) PRODUCTION READINESS gauge (clause D).
  - (C) MACHINE-DERIVED SOURCE DATA: every badge's color + value COMPUTED from a live source of truth, never hand-typed; every badge PROVENANCE (exact source path/query/build id) embedded in the tooltip OR a companion `docs/BADGES.md` provenance table; a badge with provenance `hand-typed` fails.
  - (D) PRODUCTION-READINESS GAUGE: composite badge GREEN when every clause-(B) badge is GREEN AND no §11.4.185 manual-QA blocker is open AND no §11.4.260 production-readiness criterion is unmet; AMBER when one or more badges AMBER but no RED and no blocker; RED when any badge RED or any blocker open. Its color is BINDING on the release decision; a RED gauge is a release-blocker (§11.4.108 layer 4 + §11.4.129 + §11.4.185 + §11.4.236).
  - (E) ALWAYS IN SYNC: badges regenerate on every state change (build completion, test run, defect open/close, doc change, release cut) via §11.4.106 Docs-Chain at the same write-seams as the rest of the doc surface; a stale badge is a §11.4.229 in-sync violation.
  - (F) BADGE SELF-VALIDATED: the badge-computer is a guard (§11.4.201): golden-GREEN fixture MUST render GREEN, golden-RED RED, golden-AMBER AMBER; a badge-computer that PASSes its golden-RED fixture is a bluff and release-blocker; paired section 1.1 mutation flips golden-RED source data and confirms the badge flips.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); palette, at-top placement, closed vocabulary, machine-derivation, production gauge are universal; specific per-project badge set is consumer §11.4.35 DATA.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-259-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.259), CM-README-BADGE-ROW-AT-TOP, CM-BADGE-CLOSED-COLOR-VOCABULARY, CM-BADGE-MACHINE-DERIVED-SOURCE, CM-PRODUCTION-READINESS-GAUGE, CM-BADGE-SELF-VALIDATED; paired section 1.1 mutations
- **No escape hatch:** --badges-optional, --hand-type-color, --skip-production-gauge, --badge-not-derived-from-source, --silent-omit-red-badge, --badge-in-footer-OK
- **Honest boundary:** Mandates every applicable badge is PRESENT + accurately derived; green badges do NOT prove the project bug-free (necessary-not-sufficient); a project with an HONESTLY red badge row is compliant. A genuinely inapplicable class is GRAY-labeled with a reason, never omitted (silence-as-badge is a §11.4.201(6) FALSE-NULL).
