### Git and data safety (23 anchors)

#### §9.1 — Mandatory safety protocol for destructive operations
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:3-42
- **Rules:**
  - Every destructive operation MUST execute in strict order (steps 1-7).
  - (1) Full backup before touching anything: hardlinked mirror `cp -al .git <backup>/<repo>.git.mirror` (near-instant, zero extra disk on same filesystem); if `.git` is small also `git bundle create <backup>/main.bundle --all`.
  - (2) Record into the backup dir: `git show-ref > refs.txt`; `git tag > tags.txt`; `git submodule status > submodules.txt`; `git rev-parse HEAD > head.txt`; `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree} > head_tree.txt`; `git ls-tree -r HEAD --full-tree | sha256sum > head_tree_content.sha256`; `git ls-tree -r HEAD --full-tree > head_tree_listing.txt`.
  - (3) Identify the target state (expected HEAD commit, tree hash, tree content hash after the op); the op MUST preserve these unless explicitly changing HEAD content.
  - (4) Run the operation (filter-repo, rebase, etc.). NEVER use `--no-verify` / bypass-hooks flags. NEVER auto-force on failure.
  - (5) Post-op verification gate, ALL MUST pass: HEAD tree hash matches pre-op target; HEAD tree content sha256 matches; all tags from `tags.txt` preserved and resolve to valid commits; all submodule pointers from `submodules.txt` match current state; project pre-build / pre-merge gates pass with zero FAIL and zero unclassified WARN.
  - (6) Only if every check in 9.1.5 passes is the op successful; otherwise restore from backup immediately (`rm -rf .git && mv <backup>/<repo>.git.mirror .git`).
  - (7) Then and only then may a force-push proceed, and still not without explicit user authorization per 9.2 (superseded by §11.4.113: force-push is absolutely forbidden).
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §9.2
- **Review addendum:** Step 7 note: the annotation that force-push is absolutely forbidden is from §11.4.113, not text of §9.1 itself.

#### §9.2 — Force-push requires explicit user authorization every time
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:44-63
- **Rules:**
  - Force-pushing (`push --force`, `push --force-with-lease`, or any divergence-recovery code path in an automated wrapper) overwrites remote history; irreversible on shared branches.
  - Automated push wrappers MUST NOT auto-force-push as fallback to any failure (size rejection, divergence, server error, anything). Historical divergence-recovery code that silently force-resets the remote is forbidden and MUST be removed or gated behind an explicit flag.
  - A human must affirmatively say "force-push" (or equivalent) in the session to authorize EACH force-push.
  - Force-push to `main` (and equivalent primary branch on owned submodules) is only authorized after the 9.1.5 gate has passed.
  - Every force-push event is recorded in `docs/changelogs/<tag>.md` under a "Force-push audit" section (target refs, backup location, validation gate output).
  - NOTE: §11.4.113 later supersedes this permitting stance; force-push is forbidden with no exception.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §9.1, §11.4.113

#### §9.3 — Hardlinked backup is the standard
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:65-71
- **Rules:**
  - Hardlinked `.git` copies are near-instant and use zero additional disk (same-filesystem inodes), so backup cost is trivial.
  - Any destructive operation without a fresh hardlinked backup is a Constitution violation regardless of repo size or operator confidence.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named ("there is no excuse")
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §9.1

#### §9.4 — Commit-message audit trail for history rewrites
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:73-82
- **Rules:**
  - After any `git filter-repo` run (or equivalent), commit a record under `docs/changelogs/` (or `docs/history-rewrites/`) containing: what was stripped and why; pre-op `.git` size vs post-op size; pre-op HEAD commit vs post-op HEAD commit; pre-op HEAD tree hash vs post-op (MUST match for non-content-changing rewrites); backup location.
  - (Section §10 follows: any commit/tag/release violating §1-§9 is non-compliant; fix = amend/revert and re-land; no exceptions for speed pressure; §9 data-safety and §12 host-session-safety violations are catastrophic and block the entire release cycle until fully remediated.)
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §9.1

#### §11.4.10 — Credentials-handling mandate
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:98-138
- **Rules:**
  - Credentials, secrets, API tokens, passwords, phone numbers, OAuth refresh tokens, signing keys, encryption keys, and any auth-bearing data used by tests, build automation, or tooling MUST NOT leak; applies to all submodules and the main project.
  - (1) No tracked-file storage: credentials NEVER live in any git-tracked file; placeholder templates (`<replace ...>` or `EXAMPLE_VALUE_DO_NOT_USE`) allowed in committed `.example` files.
  - (2) Repository-wide ignore: `.gitignore` MUST exclude `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.env`, `.<service>.env`, `*.<service>.env`, and `scripts/testing/secrets/*` (with `.example` + `README.md` exception).
  - (3) Runtime-load-only: tests load credentials at execution time from operator-populated files under `scripts/testing/secrets/` (or per-project equivalent); if missing, the test SKIPs with "credentials not configured for <service>" and does NOT proceed or use defaults.
  - (4) No echo / no log: scripts MUST NEVER print, log, or include credentials in error paths, stack traces, screen recordings, or output artifacts.
  - (5) Per-service file separation (one file per service).
  - (6) `.env` files `chmod 600`, parent directory `chmod 700`.
  - (7) Rotation on suspected leak: rotate at provider, update local files, audit captured artifacts.
  - `.gitignore` MUST be verified before every commit: `git ls-files --cached | grep -E "\\.env$"` MUST show no real `.env` files (only `.env.example`).
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** none cited

#### §11.4.10.A — Pre-store credential leak audit
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:140-207
- **Rules:**
  - When an operator provides credentials/tokens/keys to be stored in gitignored config (.env, scripts/testing/secrets/*, secrets/*), the storer MUST FIRST run a repo-wide audit for prior leaks of THOSE specific values BEFORE storing.
  - (1) Grep every tracked file for the literal value(s): `git ls-files | xargs grep -l <value>`; cover all file types (.md .json .yaml .kt .go .py .sh .sql, build configs, docs).
  - (2) Grep the entire git history: `git log -S<value> --all --source --remotes`; a history-only leak is a violation of equal severity to a tree leak.
  - (3) Report findings to the operator BEFORE storing the value; operator decides (a) rotate at provider first, (b) accept as known-compromise, or (c) abort. Storing without surfacing the audit is a PASS-bluff at the security layer.
  - (4) If a leak is found: open a forensic incident record, redact literal values from all tracked files in place (`<redacted-per-§11.4.10>` placeholders), record an OPERATOR ACTION REQUIRED for rotation per §11.4.10 sub-clause 7; the redaction commit lands on master IMMEDIATELY; the history-purge follow-up (filter-repo/BFG + force-push to every upstream) requires explicit per-operation operator authorization per §9.2 (note §11.4.113 now forbids force-push).
  - (5) Strengthen pre-push hook credential-pattern grep when a new class of literal credential is discovered (literal username+password in same file, well-known credential SHA-256 hashes, org-specific service-account naming); the extension MUST land in the same commit as the redaction.
  - Recommended gate `CM-PRE-STORE-CREDENTIAL-AUDIT`: commit message of any commit touching `.env`, `.env.example`, `scripts/testing/secrets/` or equivalent carries an `Audit-Pre-Stored:` stamp citing the audit outcome; paired mutation strips the stamp and asserts the gate FAILs.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17). No escape hatch.
- **Gates:** CM-PRE-STORE-CREDENTIAL-AUDIT
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated "No escape hatch")
- **Honest boundary:** audit findings stated as fact or PENDING_FORENSICS; "I think it's not leaked" without grep evidence is a guess.
- **Composes:** §11.4.10, §11.4.30, §11.4.6, §11.4.7, §9.2, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.30 — .gitignore + No-Versioned-Build-Artifacts Mandate
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:209-337
- **Rules:**
  - Every project module, owned submodule, service, and application MUST ship a proper `.gitignore` covering forbidden-from-VCS patterns; we MUST NOT version build artifacts, caches, tmp files, `.env` or any file containing sensitive data/API keys/tokens; any build derivative recreatable by a generating mechanism MUST NOT be versioned.
  - Forbidden classes: (1) build artefacts (`/bin/ /build/ /dist/ /out/ target/ *.exe *.dll *.so *.dylib *.a *.o *.class *.pyc`; generated sources where generator is committed e.g. `.pb.go` may be checked in OR ignored, project decides, never both; bundled assets where bundler is committed); (2) caches (`__pycache__/ .pytest_cache/ .mypy_cache/ .ruff_cache/ node_modules/ .next/ .nuxt/ .cache/ .gradle/ .idea/cache/ .vscode-test/ target/ .terraform/`, language-server caches); (3) temp files (`*.tmp *.swp *.swo *~ .DS_Store Thumbs.db *.orig *.rej`, IDE backups); (4) sensitive-data files (`.env`, `.env.*` allowing `.env.example/.sample/.template` with placeholders only; `*.pem *.key *.crt *.p12 *.pfx id_rsa* id_ed25519* *.kdbx .netrc secrets/` trees; `api_keys.sh`; any file with `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`, tokens, session cookies); (5) generated reports/logs (`*.log coverage.out *.coverage htmlcov/ *.gcda *.gcno`, non-reference screenshots/recordings); (6) OS/IDE/personal-state (`.idea/ .vscode/` except explicitly shared settings, `.history/ .svn/`); (7) test playback artefacts (§11.4.14) under an ignored evidence directory unless the capture IS the reference asset.
  - Anti-bluff invariant: a `.gitignore` line alone is insufficient; the project MUST verify no file matching forbidden patterns is currently tracked (e.g. `*.log` ignored while `app.log` is tracked is a violation of equal severity to no `.gitignore`).
  - Pre-commit attention: every commit author MUST inspect `git diff --staged` and `git status` BEFORE committing; a staged path matching a forbidden class aborts the commit and is fixed (un-stage, add to `.gitignore`, scrub if already tracked). Gate `CM-GITIGNORE-PRECOMMIT-AUDIT`: pre-commit hook or commit wrapper inspects every staged path against the forbidden-pattern matrix; hits abort with directed error; paired mutation: stage a `*.log` -> gate FAILs.
  - Cascade: applies recursively to every owned submodule (CONST-047) and nested non-owned trees in their working copy.
  - Secret-leak intersection: a `.env` leak is BOTH §11.4.30 and §11.4.10 violations; combined severity release-blocker requiring rotation + post-mortem per §11.4.10.
  - Recreatable content: if a documented/scripted/automated mechanism recreates the file from sources it is a build derivative and MUST be ignored; committed sources MUST include the generator (Makefile target, npm script, codegen invocation).
  - Never `git clean` an operator's working tree to "fix" a violation (§9.1).
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); no escape hatch beyond the enumerated exceptions (e.g. `.env.example`).
- **Gates:** CM-GITIGNORE-PRECOMMIT-AUDIT
- **No escape hatch:** none named (only the enumerated placeholder exceptions)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §1, §2, §9.1, §11.4, §11.4.10, §11.4.12, §11.4.14, §11.4.17, §11.4.18, §11.4.20, §11.4.25, §11.4.26, §11.4.27, §11.4.28, §11.4.29, §12.1, CONST-035, CONST-047
- **Review addendum:** Canon severity: equivalent to a §11.4 PASS-bluff at the repository-hygiene layer.

#### §11.4.36 — Mandatory install_upstreams on clone/add
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:339-424
- **Rules:**
  - Every Git repository added or cloned (`git clone`, `git submodule add`, `incorporate-submodule` per §11.4.31) MUST have upstreams installed via the Upstreamable utility `install_upstreams`, available on host PATH (via `.bashrc`/`.zshrc`), executed from the root of the cloned/added repo, only if an `upstreams/` (or legacy `Upstreams/`) directory with `*.sh` recipe files is present.
  - (1) cd into the new working tree. (2) If `upstreams/` has recipe `*.sh` files declaring upstream SSH URLs, MUST invoke `install_upstreams` from that directory. (3) `install_upstreams` (implementation: constitution submodule `install_upstreams.sh`, aliased/symlinked onto PATH once per host) reads recipes, configures every upstream as a named git remote, and fans out `origin` push URLs. (4) No `upstreams/` directory: no invocation required. (5) If `upstreams/` is present but `install_upstreams` is not on PATH, the operator MUST install it BEFORE making the clone usable. (6) Skipping step 2 when `upstreams/` is present is a violation (breaks §2.1).
  - Pre-commit attention: before the first commit in the new tree verify `install_upstreams` ran: `git remote -v | grep -c push` reports expected upstream count; if `1` while `upstreams/*.sh` declares more, abort the commit and run `install_upstreams` first.
  - Automation: constitution tooling (future `incorporate-submodule`, consumer `scripts/init-submodules.sh` patterns) MUST auto-invoke `install_upstreams` on any clone/add when the target has an `upstreams/` directory; manual invocation remains supported.
  - Gate `CM-INSTALL-UPSTREAMS-ON-CLONE`: pre-merge gate inspects every owned submodule pointer commit and verifies if `upstreams/` (or `Upstreams/`) is present then the local checkout has at least as many configured push URLs as the declared recipe count; paired mutation: remove one upstream from local `origin --push` config -> gate FAILs.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17). No escape hatch.
- **Gates:** CM-INSTALL-UPSTREAMS-ON-CLONE
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated "No escape hatch")
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §2, §2.1, §3, §9.2, §11.4.17, §11.4.20, §11.4.28, §11.4.29, §11.4.30, §11.4.31, CONST-043, CONST-051, CONST-052, CONST-053, CONST-054

#### §11.4.37 — Fetch-before-edit mandate
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:428-519
- **Rules:**
  - The FIRST git-touching action of any session on any consuming project MUST be: `git fetch --all --prune`; `git log --oneline HEAD..@{u}` (parent); `git submodule foreach --recursive 'git fetch --all --prune --quiet'`.
  - If `HEAD..@{u}` is non-empty the agent MUST integrate (ff-merge, rebase, or if non-fast-forward surface to operator per §11.4.4) BEFORE any local edit, scanner run, or test cycle. The fetch is non-negotiable even if the directive says "do X immediately".
  - Scope: consuming project root; every owned submodule (§11.4.28) recursively; the constitution submodule itself (generalises §11.4.26 step 1 to ANY edit); any dependency cloned via `incorporate-submodule` (§11.4.31) or `git submodule add` (§11.4.36).
  - Anti-bluff: the fetch+log check MUST produce captured evidence (actual `HEAD..@{u}` output, even if empty); skipping on "I just fetched" / "nothing changed in N minutes" is a §11.4.6 violation.
  - Failure modes prevented: redundant work, false confidence, divergent history.
  - Gate `CM-FETCH-BEFORE-EDIT-AUDIT` (when implemented): audits recent commit range against upstream HEAD at the commit's parent; FAIL if parent was not upstream HEAD when authored; paired mutation: synthetic commit whose parent is N commits behind then-current upstream HEAD must FAIL.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17). No escape hatch.
- **Gates:** CM-FETCH-BEFORE-EDIT-AUDIT
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated "No escape hatch")
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §2.1, §11.4.4, §11.4.6, §11.4.17, §11.4.20, §11.4.26, §11.4.28, §11.4.31, §11.4.32, §11.4.36
- **Review addendum:** Canon severity: equivalent to a §11.4 PASS-bluff at the planning layer.

#### §11.4.41 — Pre-Force-Push Merge-First Mandate
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:522-653
- **Rules:**
  - NOTE: §11.4.113 supersedes the terminal force-push step; the merge-first machinery remains the integration discipline.
  - Any force-push (`--force`, `--force-with-lease`, `+<ref>`, equivalent history rewrite on any remote) authorised under §9.2 / CONST-043 MUST be preceded by a mechanical 4-step merge-first pipeline, in order.
  - (1) Fetch every remote-side reference: `git fetch --all --prune --tags` against every remote (origin + every upstream); capture output.
  - (2) Integrate every divergent commit locally: compute `git log --oneline HEAD..<remote>/<branch>` per remote; for non-empty ranges integrate via `git rebase <remote>/<branch>` (local work is a strict superset to land on top), OR `git merge <remote>/<branch>` (independent additions both preserved), OR operator-confirmed cherry-pick (remote has subset already present locally in different form).
  - (3) Audit the integrated tree: (a) no conflict markers (`grep -rn '^<<<<<<< \|^=======$\|^>>>>>>> ' .` empty across governance+source+test files; third-party illustrative docs excepted); (b) no file silently dropped (`git diff --stat HEAD@{1} HEAD` shows only expected additions); (c) every previously-passing test still passes (§11.4.4 + §11.4.40 baseline); (d) every pre-merge captured-evidence artifact still validates.
  - (4) Execute force-push only after steps 1-3 yield captured clean-integration evidence: `git push --force-with-lease <remote> <ref>` (NEVER `--force` without `--with-lease` unless authorised per §9.2 sub-clause 6 for a remote lacking lease semantics); one force-push event per CONST-043 authorisation, no batch authorisation.
  - Two-gate composition: Gate A (CONST-043) operator types explicit per-operation authorisation; Gate B (§11.4.41) agent runs the 4-step pipeline and presents evidence to the operator BEFORE the push. Both required.
  - Verification artefact: every governed force-push emits a `docs/changelogs/<tag>.md` "Force-push merge-first audit" section with 7 elements: (i) `git fetch` output, (ii) per-remote `HEAD..<remote>/<branch>` log before integration, (iii) integration strategy per remote with rationale, (iv) post-integration conflict-marker scan (must be empty), (v) post-integration test suite delta (only expected changes), (vi) `--force-with-lease` push output with lease SHA evidence, (vii) CONST-043 authorisation quote.
  - Cascade (CONST-047): anchor (verbatim or by `§11.4.41` / `CONST-061` reference) MUST appear in every owned submodule's `CONSTITUTION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`.
  - Gate `CM-FORCE-PUSH-MERGE-FIRST` walks `docs/changelogs/<tag>.md` Force-push entries for the 7 audit elements; paired mutation strips any element -> gate FAILs.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); no escape hatch (operator-pressure "just force-push, fix later" is the failure mode closed).
- **Gates:** CM-FORCE-PUSH-MERGE-FIRST
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated "No escape hatch")
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §9.2, §11.4.4, §11.4.6, §11.4.17, §11.4.26, §11.4.32, §11.4.37, §11.4.40, §11.4.113, CONST-043, CONST-047, CONST-061
- **Review addendum:** Canon severity: equivalent to a §11.4 PASS-bluff at the remote-data-integrity layer.

#### §11.4.71 — Pre-Push Fetch + Investigate + Integrate Mandate
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:654-687
- **Rules:**
  - Everyday-push variant of §11.4.41: governs EVERY push, in every repository (main + every submodule). Before pushing to any upstream we MUST fetch and pull all changes, investigate what differs from our previous HEAD, understand what/why/impact on our project and System, incorporate mandatory changes, cover them with all supported test types producing REAL PROOFS in anti-bluff manner.
  - Mandatory 5-step cycle: (1) Fetch all remotes `git fetch --all --prune --tags` (per-remote loop if `--all` unavailable), capture stdout. (2) Pull all upstream branches `git pull --no-rebase <remote> <branch>` for each remote whose tip differs; resolve conflicts per §11.4.41 step 2 (rebase/merge/cherry-pick by judgment, NOT auto `--ours`/`--theirs`). (3) Investigate diff vs OUR previous HEAD: `git log --oneline <previous-head>..HEAD` + `git diff --stat <previous-head>..HEAD` + read EVERY commit body; for each foreign commit understand what changed, why, and how it affects our project/System. (4) Integrate mandatory changes (new anchor/gate/propagation requirement) with §11.4.4(b) four-layer coverage (pre-build gate + post-build inspection + on-device test + HelixQA Challenge) + §11.4.43 TDD-fix RED-test-first; every PASS carries §11.4.5 captured evidence. (5) Then push to every configured remote in per-repo cascade order (canonical first, then mirrors); verify with `git ls-remote <remote> <branch>`.
  - Per-repo scope: parent repo; constitution submodule (all 6 remotes); every owned submodule; every nested submodule; every HelixQA dependency (Challenges, Containers, DocProcessor, LLMOrchestrator, LLMProvider, VisionEngine, HelixQA).
  - Audit trail: every push MUST be reconstructable from `docs/changelogs/<tag>.md` + per-repo `git log` (pre-push `HEAD..@{u}`, foreign work pulled, new tests/evidence); enforcement may be automated by extending `scripts/commit_all.sh` to refuse pushes without an audit-trail entry.
  - Foreign-commit integration decisions cite the commit by SHA (§11.4.6).
  - Gate `CM-COVENANT-114-71-PROPAGATION` enforces the literal across the fleet; paired mutation strips literal -> FAIL; paired meta-test asserts the audit-trail log exists and lists pulled foreign-commit SHAs.
  - NOTE: §11.4.113 later tightens this anchor (no force-push; fast-forward only).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-71-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-fetch, --no-investigate, --fast-push, --trust-upstream
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.4(b), §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.26, §11.4.32, §11.4.37, §11.4.40, §11.4.41, §11.4.42, §11.4.43
- **Review addendum:** Non-compliance is a release blocker regardless of context.

#### §11.4.84 — Working-tree quiescence rule for subagent commits
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:689-718
- **Rules:**
  - No subagent commit may proceed while any concurrent mutation gate, paired-mutation experiment, or other in-flight mutation is live in the same checkout.
  - Before `git add`, the committing agent MUST grep its own working tree for mutation markers (`MUTATED for paired`, `// always pass`, `return json.Marshal` shortcut paths, `// MUTATION` / `# MUTATION`, `_mutated_*` filename suffixes; consuming project MAY extend) and explicitly account for every modified file in the staging area. Any unexplained file in staging triggers ABORT.
  - (1) Subagent and main-thread commit flows MUST run a pre-`git add` quiescence check: grep for markers; list every modified/untracked/staged file and match each against the subagent's declared scope (outside scope -> ABORT); cross-check `git status --porcelain` against the task description (unaccounted -> ABORT).
  - (2) Any active mutation gate MUST be serialised: runs to completion (mutate -> assert FAIL -> restore -> assert PASS) and the tree verifiably clean BEFORE any unrelated commit in the same checkout.
  - (3) Concurrent subagents in the SAME checkout (no `git worktree add`) MUST coordinate via lockfile/marker file (e.g. `.git/MUTATION_IN_PROGRESS`); `scripts/quiescence_check.sh` (when implemented) is the universal lock helper.
  - (4) For parallel work combine §11.4.20/§11.4.70 subagent-driven mandate with `git worktree add` for isolated working trees (SHOULD).
  - (5) Post-commit, an automated `mutation-residue-scanner` (consumer `scripts/mutation_residue_audit.sh`) MUST run before push; any commit containing a mutation marker -> push BLOCKED, commit reverted or amended before mirrors are updated.
  - Reason: a logo-fix commit swept an `// always pass` JWT-bypass mutation into a pushed commit.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker; a mutation marker in a tagged commit is a critical defect.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** --allow-residue, --skip-quiescence, --mutation-cleanup-later
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §1.1, §11.4.10, §11.4.17, §11.4.20, §11.4.27, §11.4.70, §11.4.71, §107

#### §11.4.88 — Background-push mandate: commit-lock release immediately after commit, push runs detached
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:722-748
- **Rules:**
  - (A) Flock release IMMEDIATELY after commit lands: once `git commit` returns 0, `.git/.commit_all.lock` MUST be released BEFORE `do_push` is invoked.
  - (B) Push runs detached: after flock release the push is spawned via `nohup ./push_all.sh ... > <log> 2>&1 &` then `disown`; the orchestrator exit code reports COMMIT success, NOT push success (push success logged separately and reconciled by §11.4.71 on next interactive turn).
  - (C) Per-remote serialization, multi-remote parallelism: `push_all.sh` MUST acquire a per-remote flock (`.git/.push.<remote>.lock`) so concurrent pushes to the same remote serialize but different remotes run in parallel.
  - (D) Failure surface: backgrounded push failures land in `qa-results/push_failures/<timestamp>_<remote>.log`; the next autonomous-loop tick MUST check that directory (per §11.4.87(A)) and surface failures (auto re-push, or notify operator on auth/quota issue). Silent push-failure is a PASS-bluff at the distribution layer.
  - (E) Synchronous-push escape: explicit `--sync-push` CLI flag on `commit_all.sh` preserves legacy synchronous behaviour for `--force-with-lease` paths (§11.4.41) where push outcome must gate the next step; the ONLY escape.
  - Reason: a synchronous push held the commit flock ~5h, blocking all commits.
  - Gates: `CM-COVENANT-114-88-PROPAGATION` enforces the literal in every CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/QWEN.md; `CM-BACKGROUND-PUSH-WIRED` verifies commit_all.sh releases flock before `do_push`, spawns push via `nohup ... &`, and push_all.sh acquires per-remote flock; paired §1.1 mutations strip literals -> FAIL.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker; synchronous push without `--sync-push` is severity-equivalent to a PASS-bluff.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-88-PROPAGATION, CM-BACKGROUND-PUSH-WIRED
- **No escape hatch:** none beyond `--sync-push` for §11.4.41 force-push events
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §2.1, §9.2, §11.4.41, §11.4.42, §11.4.71, §11.4.87

#### §11.4.113 — Absolute no-force-push + merge-onto-latest-main mandate
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:752-783
- **Rules:**
  - Force-push is STRICTLY FORBIDDEN with NO exception: `git push --force`, `--force-with-lease`, `push +<ref>`, or any history-rewriting op overwriting a remote ref non-fast-forward, against every governed repository (main repo, constitution submodule, every owned and nested submodule, every upstream). No operator-approval path, no "after merge-first audit" path.
  - Mandated 6-step integration procedure per repo/submodule with commits to publish or diverged mirrors: (1) fetch all remotes `git fetch --all --prune --tags` against origin + every upstream, capture output; (2) set base to the LATEST commit on canonical `main`/`master` (most-advanced mirror tip), never a stale local branch point; (3) carefully MERGE every change to be published on top (union merge preserving BOTH sides); NEVER `-s ours`, NEVER rebase/reset/`--allow-unrelated-histories` that could drop commits; the merge commit MUST descend from every mirror tip so every push is fast-forward; (4) resolve every conflict carefully: no conflict markers (`grep -rn '^<<<<<<< \|^=======$\|^>>>>>>> '` empty), no file dropped, every previously-passing gate/test still passes (§11.4.4 + §11.4.40), evidence artefacts still validate; (5) commit the merge, staging only intended files (NEVER `git add -A` in a submodule with untracked build content per §11.4.30); (6) push to ALL upstreams as fast-forward; if an upstream reports non-fast-forward do NOT force: return to step 1 for that upstream, fetch, MERGE (union), re-validate step 4, re-push.
  - Tightens §11.4.41 / §11.4.71 / §9.2 / CONST-043: their merge-first/fetch-first machinery stays; only the terminal "then force-push" step is struck; even WITH operator approval and a clean audit force-push is forbidden. §9 backup discipline still applies to non-push history operations.
  - No `--no-verify` to slip a forced ref past a hook; no "lease semantics unavailable so plain --force OK" path. A force-push that lands is a critical defect.
  - Propagation gate `CM-COVENANT-114-113-PROPAGATION` enforces literal `11.4.113`; recommended gate `CM-NO-FORCE-PUSH-ABSOLUTE` scans tracked scripts and hooks for any `push --force` / `--force-with-lease` / `push +<ref>` and rejects it; a §11.4.109-class PreToolUse guard blocks the force-push command class at the tool-call boundary; paired mutations inject `git push --force` -> FAIL; strip literal -> FAIL. Gate-code lands as separate work item.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-113-PROPAGATION, CM-NO-FORCE-PUSH-ABSOLUTE
- **No escape hatch:** --force, --force-with-lease, --allow-force-push, --force-push-authorised, --skip-merge-onto-main
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §2.1, §9, §9.2, §11.4.4, §11.4.6, §11.4.26, §11.4.30, §11.4.37, §11.4.40, §11.4.41, §11.4.71, §11.4.88, §11.4.109, §11.4.17, §11.4.35, CONST-043

#### §11.4.121 — No-commit-while-build-writes-tracked-artifacts mandate
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:787-807
- **Rules:**
  - A commit (especially `git add -A` / any broad stage) MUST NOT run while a build/packaging/generation step is actively writing artifacts INTO tracked directories (race stages a partial or stale artifact: a §11.4.108 SOURCE->ARTIFACT integrity failure in VCS).
  - The commit MUST be deferred until the artifact-writing build step has COMPLETED so (1) the tree is quiescent at the artifact layer and (2) committed artifacts are the FRESH whole outputs of the completed build.
  - Before committing tracked build outputs the committer MUST verify the writing step finished (process exit, completion marker, or per-artifact mtime >= build-start); a build in flight writing tracked dirs is a HOLD on the commit.
  - Build-output analogue of §11.4.84; binds only to steps writing into TRACKED directories (gitignored `out/`/`dist/` exempt). Committing source changes not touching the build's tracked-artifact dirs mid-build is fine.
  - The consuming project supplies which build steps write which tracked directories and its completion-signal mechanism per §11.4.35.
  - Propagation gate `CM-COVENANT-114-121-PROPAGATION` (literal `11.4.121`); recommended gate `CM-NO-COMMIT-DURING-ARTIFACT-WRITE` (commit wrapper refuses to stage tracked build-artifact directories while a build writing them is in flight, via build-in-progress lock / completion marker); paired mutations strip literal / remove the in-flight check -> FAIL. Gate-code is a separate work item.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-121-PROPAGATION, CM-NO-COMMIT-DURING-ARTIFACT-WRITE
- **No escape hatch:** --commit-during-build, --stage-partial-artifact-OK, --assume-build-finished, --skip-build-completion-check
- **Honest boundary:** "The build probably finished" is not "the build finished" - verify with exit code / marker / mtime, not assumption.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.17, §11.4.30, §11.4.35, §11.4.58, §11.4.84, §11.4.88, §11.4.96, §11.4.103, §11.4.108

#### §11.4.179 — Corruption-isolated parallel git streams
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:811-811
- **Rules:**
  - When corruption-isolation is a requirement, parallel git work streams MUST each be an isolated repository with its OWN `.git` (own object store, index, lock namespace), NOT `git worktree` checkouts sharing one common `.git` (a shared common-dir is a single point of failure: one stale `index.lock`/`.commit_all.lock`/`.push_all.lock` freezes every stream; one corrupted object store loses all).
  - Each stream's `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` MUST resolve INSIDE the stream's own tree; a common-dir resolving to a shared parent is a violation.
  - Where CoW/reflink disk-feasibility is the constraint use the §11.4.167 reflink-clone-with-own-`.git` path (btrfs/XFS/ZFS/APFS reflink shares extents but keeps per-stream `.git`).
  - Consuming project supplies its reflink mechanism and clone layout per §11.4.35.
  - Gates: `CM-COVENANT-114-179-PROPAGATION` (literal `11.4.179`); recommended `CM-GIT-STREAMS-OWN-COMMON-DIR` (every registered stream's common-dir resolves inside its own tree); paired mutations (register a stream with shared-parent common-dir -> FAIL; strip literal -> FAIL); gate-code separate work item.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-179-PROPAGATION, CM-GIT-STREAMS-OWN-COMMON-DIR
- **No escape hatch:** --shared-common-git, --worktree-when-isolation-required, --skip-git-isolation
- **Honest boundary:** Own-`.git` isolation contains lock/corruption blast radius; it does NOT remove need for per-repo stale-lock reaping (§11.4.180) nor ff-only no-force integration (§11.4.113).
- **Composes:** §11.4.167, §11.4.119, §11.4.176, §9.2, §11.4.58, §11.4.180, §11.4.113, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.180 — Commit/push (single-writer) wrappers MUST auto-reap provably-stale locks before acquiring
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:813-813
- **Rules:**
  - Every commit/push/single-writer wrapper MUST, before acquiring its own lock, auto-reap any PROVABLY-stale git lock: holder PID DEAD (`kill -0` fails), OR (no PID recorded) older than a defined threshold AND no live wrapper/git process holding that repo.
  - Reap covers the wrapper's own lock plus git-internal existence-based locks (`index.lock`, `HEAD.lock`, `refs/**/*.lock`) that git does not auto-release on holder death.
  - MUST NEVER remove a lock whose holder is ALIVE (corrupts a concurrent writer, §9.2).
  - Each reap decision (REAPED / KEPT + reason) is logged as captured evidence; liveness PROVEN via `kill -0`, never assumed (§11.4.6).
  - A wrapper blocking indefinitely on a dead-holder lock is a violation.
  - Consuming project supplies wrapper, reap helper, stale-age threshold per §11.4.35.
  - Gates: `CM-COVENANT-114-180-PROPAGATION` (literal `11.4.180`); recommended `CM-WRAPPER-STALE-LOCK-AUTO-REAP` (reaps provably-stale locks before acquiring, never removes a live-held lock, logs each decision); paired mutations (reaper removes a live lock OR skips reap-before-acquire -> FAIL; strip literal -> FAIL); gate-code separate work item.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-180-PROPAGATION, CM-WRAPPER-STALE-LOCK-AUTO-REAP
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-stale-lock-reap, --force-remove-live-lock, --block-on-dead-holder
- **Honest boundary:** Reaping clears dead-holder deadlock; it does NOT substitute for own-`.git` isolation (§11.4.179).
- **Composes:** §11.4.84, §11.4.88, §11.4.6, §9.2, §11.4.116, §11.4.179, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.181 — Consistent controlled feature-branch naming: one feature/logic-group => ONE canonical branch name
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:815-815
- **Rules:**
  - One feature / logical group of workable items MUST map to EXACTLY ONE canonical branch name, used IDENTICALLY on the main repo AND every owned submodule the group touches; NEVER two differently-named branches for one feature, NEVER per-repo naming drift. No false results, mis-alignment or inconsistency.
  - (1) Single canonical name per group, minted ONCE per §11.4.167 D scheme: `feature/<slug>` on the branch axis + `<prefix>-<base>-feat-<slug>` on the tag axis; `<slug>` lowercase snake/kebab (§11.4.29). Untouched submodules stay on base branch (not force-branched), but any branched submodule MUST use the identical name.
  - (2) Single source of truth: the canonical name is recorded ONCE in a tracked registry (§11.4.176 claim registry / §11.4.93 workable-items DB `logic_group -> branch` mapping, a `branch_name` field) and LOOKED UP, never re-derived; the claim reserving a group also reserves its canonical branch name. Creating a branch not matching the registry, or minting a SECOND canonical name for a group, is a violation (§11.4.6).
  - (3) Mechanical enforcement (§11.4.75): gate `CM-BRANCH-NAME-CONSISTENCY` verifies every live feature branch (main + each owned submodule) maps to a registered group and carries the identical name; FAILs on (a) unregistered feature-branch name, (b) two differently-named branches bound to one group, (c) a submodule branch diverging from the group's main-repo canonical name. Paired mutation: register one group under two names -> FAIL.
  - (4) Risk-free reconciliation (§9.2/§11.4.113/§11.4.84): create/checkout the canonical branch at merge-base, MERGE the mis-named branch's commits onto it (union; no `-s ours`/rebase/reset that drops commits), verify no commit lost (`git log <canonical>..<misnamed>` empty after merge) and no conflict markers, push fast-forward to all upstreams (NEVER force), THEN retire the mis-named branch only after the merge is confirmed on all mirrors; delete-before-merge is forbidden.
  - Gates: `CM-COVENANT-114-181-PROPAGATION` (literal `11.4.181`) + `CM-BRANCH-NAME-CONSISTENCY`; gate-code separate work item. Consuming project supplies registry, branch/tag scheme, owned-submodule set per §11.4.35.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-181-PROPAGATION, CM-BRANCH-NAME-CONSISTENCY
- **No escape hatch:** --allow-divergent-branch-names, --skip-branch-registry, --rename-branch-freely, --per-repo-branch-name-OK, --two-names-one-feature-OK
- **Honest boundary:** "The branches are probably the same feature" is not a determination; bind to a group via the registry record (claim id / logic-group id), never guess.
- **Composes:** §11.4.167, §11.4.176, §11.4.178, §11.4.179, §11.4.28, §11.4.29, §11.4.93, §11.4.113, §11.4.84, §9.2, §11.4.6, §11.4.75, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.188 — Regular main->feature merge cadence
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:817-817
- **Rules:**
  - Every long-lived feature branch AND every parallel-development track (§11.4.58/§11.4.103/§11.4.167/§11.4.176/§11.4.178/§11.4.179) MUST regularly `git merge origin/main` (canonical trunk) INTO its own branch THROUGHOUT the work, NOT only at the end. Generalises §11.4.167(D) to EVERY feature branch on EVERY track (small/medium branches and any worktree/CoW track included).
  - (1) WHAT: fetch latest canonical `main`/`master` and merge INTO the working branch; a branch not integrating trunk within cadence is flagged STALE.
  - (2) CADENCE: after EVERY trunk tag, at minimum DAILY while the branch is live, AND before starting any significant new chunk of work; many small merges, never one big deferred merge.
  - (3) HOW: MERGE, NEVER rebase a shared/tagged/pushed branch (§9/§11.4.113); FETCH-FIRST every remote (§11.4.37/§11.4.71); §9.2 hardlinked pre-op backup before any LARGE/conflict-heavy/risky merge; resolve conflicts with ZERO conflict markers committed, ZERO file silently dropped, union preserved (§11.4.41 step 3); integrate ONLY when QUIESCENT (§11.4.84); prefer running merge + verification in BACKGROUND parallel to the main stream (§11.4.88/§11.4.89/§11.4.103); NEVER force-push the merged result (§11.4.113).
  - (4) CONSISTENCY + ANTI-BLUFF: after EVERY merge prove consistency: post-merge pre-build smoke gate GREEN (§11.4.42 step-3), `git grep` for `<<<<<<<` / `=======` / `>>>>>>>` returns EMPTY, no pre-merge commit from either side lost, with captured evidence (§11.4.5/§11.4.69); a "clean" claim without those checks is a bluff.
  - Consuming project supplies trunk ref name, cadence unit, post-merge smoke command, per-track worktree/CoW mechanism per §11.4.35.
  - Gates: `CM-COVENANT-114-188-PROPAGATION` (literal `11.4.188`); recommended `CM-REGULAR-MAIN-MERGE-INTO-FEATURE` (every live branch integrated trunk within cadence; last integration is a real merge not a rebase; smoke + zero-marker + no-lost-commit passed); paired mutations (stale branch / rebase of shared branch / committed conflict marker -> FAIL); gate-code separate work item.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-188-PROPAGATION, CM-REGULAR-MAIN-MERGE-INTO-FEATURE
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-main-merge, --merge-only-at-end, --rebase-shared-branch, --defer-trunk-sync, --no-post-merge-smoke, --force-push-after-merge, --big-items-only-trunk-sync
- **Honest boundary:** Regular trunk-integration keeps the branch mergeable/low-conflict; it does NOT prove the branch's work correct (still §11.4.108 + §11.4.40) and is NOT the approval-gated back-merge to trunk (§11.4.167(I)/§11.4.40/§11.4.41).
- **Composes:** §9, §9.2, §11.4.6, §11.4.17, §11.4.37, §11.4.41, §11.4.42, §11.4.71, §11.4.84, §11.4.88, §11.4.89, §11.4.103, §11.4.113, §11.4.167, §11.4.176, §11.4.178, §11.4.179, §11.4.181

#### §11.4.195 — Branch-structure governance: taxonomy + merge-after-live-QA + flavor/product non-merge
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:819-852
- **Rules:**
  - Operator rules: taxonomy `feat/<NAME_OF_FEATURE>`, `product/<NAME_OF_PRODUCT>`, `flavor/<NAME_OF_FLAVOR>`; tracks on FEATURE branches or `main` MUST, after full confirmation + validation + verification + full LIVE MANUAL TESTING (§11.4.185), MERGE to `main` COMPLETELY (all submodules + main repo), ff-only, NEVER force-push, no commit lost (§9.2); entirely-new FLAVOR/PRODUCT tracks do ALL work on flavor and/or product branches (both may exist) which do NOT merge to `main` the same way; commit + push ALL branches to ALL upstreams (§2.1), ff-only.
  - (A) Taxonomy (extends §11.4.181/§11.4.167(D)): prefix declares class and lifecycle: `feat/` = FEATURE (merges to main after live-manual-QA, clause B); `product/` = PRODUCT line and `flavor/` = FLAVOR line (do NOT merge to `main` the standard way, clause C). Slug lowercase snake/kebab (§11.4.29). Canonical name minted ONCE and used IDENTICALLY across main + every touched owned submodule (§11.4.181), recorded once in the §11.4.176 claim registry / §11.4.93 `logic_group -> branch` mapping and LOOKED UP (§11.4.6). Untouched submodules stay on base. A project using a different feature prefix (e.g. `feature/...`) is compliant if it is the ONE canonical name per §11.4.181; reconcile by the §11.4.181 MERGE-onto-canonical path (ff-only, no commit lost), never a silent rename.
  - (B) FEATURE/main tracks MUST, before merging to `main`, satisfy IN ORDER: automated four-layer (§11.4.4(b)) + §11.4.40 full-suite retest, THEN full LIVE MANUAL TESTING by QA (§11.4.185 FINAL human gate; automated GREEN necessary NOT sufficient). Only after §11.4.185 confirmation may the merge proceed; it MUST be COMPLETE (main repo AND every touched owned submodule), ff-only onto latest `main` (§11.4.113), NEVER force-push, NO commit lost / NO history rewrite (§9.2/§11.4.41 step 3: union, zero markers, zero dropped files), pushed to ALL upstreams (§2.1, ff-only). Binds §11.4.185 as precondition of the §11.4.167(I)/§11.4.188 approval-gated back-merge.
  - (C) FLAVOR/PRODUCT lines do ALL work on `product/<NAME>` and/or `flavor/<NAME>` (both may coexist); work does NOT flow into `main` via clause B (divergent line, own release lifecycle). STILL obeys §11.4.113, §9.2, §2.1, and §11.4.188 (it MAY merge `main` INTO itself; only line-into-trunk is gated/withheld).
  - (D) Push discipline: commit + push ALL branches (feature, product, flavor) to ALL upstreams, ff-only, NEVER force-push. New-branch creation is inherently ff (§9.2); branch creation from an existing HEAD (`git branch <name> <sha>`) is non-disruptive and MAY proceed in a dirty tree under §11.4.84 provided no commit is in flight (`.git/index.lock` absent, no live `git-commit`/`pack-objects`).
  - Gates: `CM-COVENANT-114-195-PROPAGATION` (literal `11.4.195`); recommended `CM-BRANCH-TAXONOMY-CLASS` (every controlled branch prefix is `feat/`|`product/`|`flavor/`|reserved `main`/`master`; a `product/`|`flavor/` branch is NOT the source of a merge onto `main`; a `feat/`|`main` back-merge cites a §11.4.185 confirmation); paired mutations (product branch merged to main, or feat back-merge with no §11.4.185 citation -> FAIL; strip literal -> FAIL); gate-code separate work item.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-195-PROPAGATION, CM-BRANCH-TAXONOMY-CLASS
- **No escape hatch:** --any-branch-prefix-OK, --merge-product-to-main, --skip-live-qa-before-merge, --force-push-branch, --partial-submodule-merge
- **Honest boundary:** Governs branch STRUCTURE and integration DIRECTION; does not prove any branch's work correct (still §11.4.108 + §11.4.40 + §11.4.185).
- **Composes:** §2.1, §9, §9.2, §11.4.6, §11.4.17, §11.4.29, §11.4.35, §11.4.40, §11.4.41, §11.4.84, §11.4.93, §11.4.113, §11.4.167(D)/(I), §11.4.176, §11.4.178, §11.4.181, §11.4.185, §11.4.188, §11.4.191

#### §11.4.234 — Dedicated hook-validation script: commit/push mechanism is ALWAYS unblocked
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:854-870
- **Rules:**
  - (A) DEDICATED SCRIPT AS SINGLE COMMIT/PUSH ENTRYPOINT: every consumer MUST ship a dedicated, executable, idempotent script (Lava binding `scripts/commit-push-all.sh`; consumers bind their own path as DATA per §11.4.35) that runs in order: (1) submodule/workspace sync, (2) commit of all pending state, (3) the hook validations as an EXPLICIT stage (unmodified hook logic fed the real push range; cheap checks always, long gates stage-separated), (4) push to ALL configured upstreams (§2.1), (5) closing green/clean verification (clean status + zero unpushed commits, recursive over submodules). Prints per-stage evidence, safe to re-run; direct `git commit`/`git push` on the main repo ceases to be the routine workflow (§2).
  - (B) HOOKS MUST NOT BLOCK THE MECHANISM: automatic git hooks via `core.hooksPath` MUST NOT gate routine commit/push in a way that can leave the repo uncommittable/unpushable. Disconnecting = `core.hooksPath` unset, hook file preserved UNMODIFIED in the repo, `--no-verify` NEVER the routine path. Validation relocates to the explicit script stage (A) and tag/release gates; never deleted.
  - (C) NO GATE IS LOST: every check the disconnected hook performed MUST remain executed (script validation stage, tag/release gate, or documented scheduled run); silently dropping a check is a PASS-bluff; the script's stage list MUST name every check it runs and every check it defers with deferral target recorded.
  - (D) ALWAYS-UNBLOCKED INVARIANT: commit/push MUST always be able to complete; a failing validation yields a clear per-check report plus documented remediation path, never an opaque hung/rejected push; long multi-minute gates MUST be separable from cheap checks and skippable via an explicit documented flag (Lava binding `LAVA_SYNC_SKIP_CI=1`), every skip recorded in the commit message or evidence pack; the escape is a recorded deferral, not a bypass: the skipped gate remains owed and is caught at the next full run or tag gate.
  - Gates: `CM-COVENANT-114-234-PROPAGATION` (literal `11.4.234`, block-start); `CM-DEDICATED-HOOK-VALIDATION-SCRIPT` (A), `CM-HOOKS-NEVER-BLOCK-PUSH` (B), `CM-NO-GATE-LOST-ON-HOOK-DISCONNECT` (C), `CM-COMMIT-PUSH-ALWAYS-UNBLOCKED` (D); paired mutations (full gate rewired as blocking pre-push hook -> (B) FAIL; hook disconnected AND check dropped from every stage -> (C) FAIL; validation failure strands commits with no remediation report -> (D) FAIL; strip literal -> FAIL). Gate-code separate work item, NOT claimed shipped.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumers supply script path, upstream-remote list, cheap-vs-long gate split, skip-flag name as DATA per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-234-PROPAGATION, CM-DEDICATED-HOOK-VALIDATION-SCRIPT, CM-HOOKS-NEVER-BLOCK-PUSH, CM-NO-GATE-LOST-ON-HOOK-DISCONNECT, CM-COMMIT-PUSH-ALWAYS-UNBLOCKED
- **No escape hatch:** none beyond the recorded (D) deferral; forbidden flags: --no-verify-routine, --skip-all-gates-silently, --delete-blocking-hook, --push-without-any-validation
- **Honest boundary:** Relocates WHERE validation executes; does not weaken any substantive gate, does not mandate deleting hooks, does not authorise `--no-verify` routinely, does not make a failing gate pass - it keeps the mechanism reachable while the failure is remediated.
- **Composes:** §2, §2.1, §11.4.32, §11.4.113, §11.4.201, §11.4.227, §11.4.233, §11.4.17, §11.4.35, §11.4.6
- **Review addendum:** Honest boundary: the anti-bluff covenant, the tag-time full gate and the §11.4.32 sweep all still bind at their own seams.

#### §11.4.252 — Fail-closed-on-dangerous-combination for mutating / credential surfaces
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:872-876
- **Rules:**
  - Every code path COMBINING >= 2 dangerous capabilities MUST FAIL CLOSED: refuse the operation unless every capability's precondition is verifiably satisfied; NEVER fail open on ambiguous/missing/unresolvable input (generalisation of §11.4.201 guard-honesty).
  - Dangerous-combination taxonomy (closed set of 6): (1) MUTATION of shared resource (DB/filesystem/container state/config); (2) UNTRUSTED INPUT (user string/network bytes/external env var/unverified file); (3) CREDENTIAL ACCESS (secret read/authenticated API call/signing key use); (4) EXTERNAL SIDE EFFECT (email/webhook/MQ publish/payment endpoint); (5) SHELL/EXEC (subshell/binary with user-influenced args/template eval with user values); (6) IRREVERSIBLE (delete/drop/truncate; force-push already absolutely forbidden by §11.4.113). Any path combining >= 2 MUST fail closed.
  - Invariant: (1) VERIFY every precondition (authorization + input shape + credential presence + target identity); (2) REFUSE when ANY is unverifiable, with ERROR EXIT naming the specific unresolved precondition; (3) EMIT captured evidence per §11.4.5 of the refusal; (4) NEVER default to allow/proceed/retry-with-relaxed on ambiguity (§11.4.101 conservative-safe default = REFUSE).
  - Fail-open anti-patterns refused: `catch { /* ignore */ }`, `credential = credential || default`, `if (!valid) { log("warn"); return proceed(input); }`, `target = user_input || default_target`, unbounded `retry { dangerous(); }`.
  - Distinct from graceful degradation. The 6-class taxonomy is a closed-set formalisation, not literal per-class enumeration [MATERIAL-THIN].
  - Gates: `CM-COVENANT-114-252-PROPAGATION` (literal `11.4.252`); recommended `CM-DANGEROUS-COMBINATION-FAIL-CLOSED`; paired §1.1 mutation. Classification: universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-252-PROPAGATION, CM-DANGEROUS-COMBINATION-FAIL-CLOSED
- **No escape hatch:** --fail-open-on-error, --swallow-exception, --default-missing-credential, --proceed-on-ambiguous-input, --retry-until-succeeds
- **Honest boundary:** Distinct from graceful degradation (e.g. a cache-miss returning a cache-miss response is not a dangerous combination); taxonomy is closed-set formalisation, not per-class enumeration.
- **Composes:** §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.10, §11.4.66, §11.4.101, §11.4.113, §11.4.194, §11.4.201, §1.1, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.253 — Idempotency under retry + DB-level durable uniqueness guard
- **Source:** git-and-data-safety.md:880-884
- **Rules:**
  - Every retryable operation (network calls with auto-retry, at-least-once MQ consumers, cron with overlapping schedules, HTTP endpoints with client-retry, DB transactions with retry-on-serialisation-failure, deploy pipelines with rerun) MUST BE IDEMPOTENT: N executions produce the same observable end state as one.
  - Idempotency ENFORCED at the LOWEST LAYER where "same end state" is durably provable, typically a DATABASE UNIQUENESS CONSTRAINT on a caller-supplied idempotency key, NEVER only application-layer check-then-insert (races). Prevents double-charge/email/delete/effect.
  - Idempotency-key discipline: every retryable op accepts (or generates and passes forward) a unique identifier naming THIS logical op; the persistence layer has a UNIQUE INDEX/CONSTRAINT on the key column; a second attempt is REFUSED by the DB at durable level, not by app logic reading-then-writing; the refusal is caught by the caller as "duplicate - already succeeded" = SUCCESS.
  - Anti-patterns: (i) check-then-insert without unique index; (ii) app-level dedup table read without spanning transaction; (iii) key scoped to app instance (in-memory, not shared); (iv) effect persisted BEFORE key (crash between = double-effect on retry); (v) no key at all on "set X to V" reasoning (safe for pure sets, NOT INSERTs / MQ emissions / external side effects); (vi) idempotency key expires (time-bounded idempotency is a §11.4.6 mislabelling if caller expects unbounded).
  - Chaos verification per §11.4.85: (1) SIMULTANEOUS RETRIES (same key from 2 concurrent callers); (2) MID-OPERATION CRASHES (kill receiver between "check exists" and "insert effect"); (3) RETRY AFTER APPARENT SUCCESS (caller believes failure, receiver persisted; retry MUST recognise duplicate).
  - External-system side effects (e.g. Stripe/PayPal charge + local DB write): the idempotency key MUST pass through to the external; if the external lacks support the op is not fully idempotent and MUST be labelled honestly per §11.4.6.
  - Gates: `CM-COVENANT-114-253-PROPAGATION` (literal `11.4.253`); recommended `CM-IDEMPOTENCY-DB-LEVEL-UNIQUE-GUARD` + `CM-IDEMPOTENCY-CHAOS-VERIFIED`; paired §1.1 mutation. Classification: universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-253-PROPAGATION, CM-IDEMPOTENCY-DB-LEVEL-UNIQUE-GUARD, CM-IDEMPOTENCY-CHAOS-VERIFIED
- **No escape hatch:** --check-then-insert-OK, --application-dedup-suffices, --skip-idempotency-chaos-test, --claim-idempotent-without-key, --expire-idempotency-marker-silently
- **Honest boundary:** An operation whose external dependency lacks idempotency-key support is not fully idempotent and must be labelled so (§11.4.6); pure "set X to V" effects may be safe without a key.
- **Composes:** §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.85, §11.4.201, §11.4.252, §1.1, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.11 — File-layout discipline
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:3-38
- **Rules:**

  - Logs and forensic artifacts go under operator-controlled directories (~/Documents/, qa-results/, /tmp/, OS-equivalent); NEVER scattered at repo root, NEVER inside working source trees, NEVER tracked unless they are reference assets explicitly required for evidence-replay.

Moving them is operator-blocked per §11.4.66 until explicitly authorised.
  - Audit-snapshot files (docs/audit/anti_bluff_audit.md, PRE_SONOS_TAG_READINESS.md, D1_WIFI_FAIL_CLASSIFICATION.md, any future ones) DO move under docs/audit/ per the general principle.

#### §11.4.17 — Universal-vs-project classification of new rules
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:40-85
- **Rules:**
  - Before any new rule, mandatory constraint, covenant clause, gate declaration or MUST-bearing statement is added to a project's Constitution/CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md or a child submodule's equivalents, the author MUST classify it as Universal or Project-specific.
  - Universal (applies to ANY project regardless of language/framework/platform/domain) goes into this constitution submodule's Constitution.md + CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md and propagates by inheritance. Project-specific (references specific hardware, vendor, model, SoC, vendor-fork, project-internal package, deployment topology, company-internal asset) goes into the project's own Constitution/CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md or the affected submodule's equivalents.
  - A rule mentioning hardware part numbers, vendor names, specific package identifiers, geographic regions or company-internal asset names is project-specific by definition and cannot be lifted to universal without genericising. A universal rule MAY reference patterns but MUST NOT name specific vendors.
  - Every new rule's commit message MUST include a one-line classification statement (e.g. "Classification: universal - applies to any project ..."); a commit adding a rule without it is a §11.4.17 violation.
  - Uncertain authors SHOULD default to project-specific (narrower scope).
  - Pre-build gate audits the last N commits for rule additions and asserts each carries a classification statement; paired mutation strips the classification literal and asserts the gate FAILs.
- **Gates:** CM-UNIVERSAL-VS-PROJECT-CLASSIFICATION
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** none cited

#### §11.4.26 — Constitution-Submodule Update Workflow Mandate
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:87-174
- **Rules:**
  - Before ANY agent/operator modifies constitution/Constitution.md, constitution/CLAUDE.md or constitution/AGENTS.md of a consuming project, the following pipeline MUST run in order with NO step skipped.
  - (1) Fetch + pull first: from inside the constitution/ submodule worktree run git fetch for every configured remote then git pull --ff-only origin <branch> (or --rebase if non-FF-mergeable; NEVER --strategy=ours / --allow-unrelated-histories without explicit operator authorization). Submodule MUST be at upstream tip before any local edit.
  - (2) Apply the change: edit MUST classify itself per §11.4.17 (only universal additions belong in the constitution submodule; project-specific go to the consumer's files) and MUST include the verbatim user mandate (if any) as forensic anchor.
  - (3) Validate before commit: run the submodule's meta_test_inheritance.sh (or equivalent) to confirm the inheritance chain resolves; verify no merge-conflict markers (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>) remain; verify Constitution + CLAUDE + AGENTS cross-reference the new clause consistently.
  - (4) Commit + push to ALL upstreams: stage only the governance files (NEVER git add -A inside the constitution submodule); commit message cites the user mandate (verbatim quote) and the §11.4.17 classification line; push to EVERY configured remote. A commit on one upstream but not others is a §11.4.26 violation equivalent to a §2.1 violation.
  - (5) Conflict resolution: if pull --ff-only reports non-fast-forward, merge carefully: inspect both sides, preserve the union of governance content (no clause silently dropped), re-classify per §11.4.17, validate per step 3. Force-push is FORBIDDEN (§9.2). Nothing may be broken, faulty, corrupted or unusable.
  - (6) Post-merge validation + verification: after push, re-clone (or git submodule update --remote --init) in a throwaway worktree and re-run the consumer's inheritance-cascade verifier (e.g. scripts/verify-governance-cascade.sh) to confirm the new clause reaches every owned submodule per CONST-047; any cascade gap MUST be closed in the same change-window.
  - (7) Update the consuming project's pointer: the .gitmodules-tracked submodule pointer MUST be bumped to the new constitution HEAD in the SAME commit as any downstream cascade work; out-of-sync pointers are a §11.4.26 violation.
  - Applies regardless of who initiates (operator, primary agent, subagent per §11.4.20, automated lint suggestion); cannot be shortcut by "fetch later" / "push to other upstreams next commit".
  - A constitution-submodule change violating §11.4.26 is a release blocker for every consuming project. No escape hatch.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated in prose: no escape hatch)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §2, §2.1, §3, §9.1, §9.2, §11.4.17, §11.4.20, §11.4.22, §11.4.25, CONST-047
- **Review addendum:** Canon severity: letting the constitution fragment across upstreams is the structural equivalent of a §11.4 PASS-bluff at the governance layer, and a violation is equivalent in severity to a force-push without §9.2 authorization.

#### §11.4.28 — Submodules-As-Equal-Codebase + Decoupling + Dependency-Layout Mandate
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:178-365
- **Rules:**
  - Scope: owned-by-us submodules, i.e. upstream origin under vasic-digital, HelixDevelopment, red-elf, ATMOSphere1234321, Bear-Suite, BoatOS123456, Helix-Flow, Helix-Track, Server-Factory, or any additional org the operator authorises (discoverable via gh org list / glab / public APIs).
  - (A) Equal-codebase invariant: every owned submodule is an equal part of the consuming project's codebase; analysis, extension, test creation, gap-filling, bug-fix and documentation (manuals, guides, diagrams, graphs, SQL definitions, website pages) apply to each on equal basis. A round improving only the main project while leaving an owned-submodule deficiency unaddressed is a §11.4.28 violation. §11.4.25 coverage ledgers MUST list every owned submodule as in-scope.
  - (B) Decoupling/reusability invariant: owned submodules MUST remain fully decoupled from any consuming project: no project-specific context, hardcoded paths, hostnames, asset names, naming schemes or runtime assumptions in their source tree. Each MUST be project-not-aware, fully reusable, modular (public surface is the only integration contract), completely testable (every public surface has standalone tests per §11.4.27 that pass when checked out standalone without parent rigging).
  - A commit adding project_name/... strings, deployment hostnames or other parent context to a submodule's source tree is a violation; the honest path is configuration injection (env var, config file, constructor parameter), never a hardcoded reach into the parent tree.
  - (C) Dependency-layout invariant: every dependency an owned submodule consumes MUST be accessible from the parent project root at <project_root>/<submodule_name>/ (flat) or <project_root>/submodules/<submodule_name>/ (grouped).
  - Nested-submodule chains are FORBIDDEN: a submodule MUST NOT have its own .gitmodules entries pulling in further owned-by-us repos; every dependency of submodule X MUST be added to the parent at the canonical path and reached via documented import/SDK path/runtime resolver.
  - EXCEPTION (operator Option-2 decision, 2026-07-07): ONLY the constitution submodule itself MAY host its own reusable-engine submodules under constitution/submodules/<name>/, PROVIDED each (i) ships a §11.4.31 helix-deps.yaml at its root AND (ii) declares ZERO further own-org submodules (DEPTH-1 ONLY; a nested engine that itself nests an own-org submodule is still FORBIDDEN). Applies to NO other repository; arbitrary consumer submodules remain forbidden from nesting and MUST use the root-flattened helix-deps.yaml bridge.
  - Third-party submodules (not under our orgs) are exempt and MAY appear at any depth.
  - Audit gates: CM-OWNED-SUBMODULE-EQUAL-ENGINEERING (project-side): each release-gate sweep verifies every owned submodule has current test runs, coverage entries (§11.4.25) and documentation freshness on par with main; stale ones surface as violations (Status Operator-blocked or In progress per §11.4.21, never ignored).
  - CM-OWNED-SUBMODULE-DECOUPLING (submodule-side): each owned submodule's pre-commit hook (or equivalent) greps the staged diff for parent-project names/hostnames/asset names; hits abort the commit until refactored to configuration injection.
  - CM-OWNED-SUBMODULE-LAYOUT (project-side): pre-merge sweep verifies (i) every owned submodule sits at <root>/<name>/ or <root>/submodules/<name>/, (ii) no owned submodule contains a nested .gitmodules entry whose upstream is in our org list - EXCEPT the constitution submodule's depth-1 engines with helix-deps.yaml and zero further own-org submodules (depth-2 chain or missing manifest FAILs), (iii) every dependency declared by an owned submodule has a corresponding parent-project submodule entry at the canonical path. Paired §1.1 mutation: add a second-level own-org .gitmodules entry inside a constitution-anchored engine -> FAILs; drop the engine's helix-deps.yaml -> FAILs; restore -> PASSes. Paired mutations for all three gates: plant forbidden pattern -> FAIL; restore -> PASS.
  - Workflow: plan engineering rounds in submodule-aware tranches; §11.4.25 coverage ledger row format is extended with a `submodule` column; cross-submodule refactors touching shared types/interfaces ship as a single change-window with parent + every affected owned submodule advanced in lockstep (§3 submodule-first-commit + §2.1 multi-upstream push).
  - A round violating §11.4.28 is a release blocker (severity-equivalent to a §11.4 PASS-bluff at the codebase-completeness layer). No escape hatch.
- **Gates:** CM-OWNED-SUBMODULE-EQUAL-ENGINEERING, CM-OWNED-SUBMODULE-DECOUPLING, CM-OWNED-SUBMODULE-LAYOUT
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated in prose: no escape hatch)
- **Honest boundary:** Third-party submodules are exempt from the nesting invariant; the nesting carve-out is constitution-submodule-only and depth-1 only.
- **Composes:** §1, §1.1, §3, §11.4.11 (n/a), §11.4.17, §11.4.20, §11.4.21, §11.4.25, §11.4.26, §11.4.27, §11.4.31, §11.4.35, §11.4.74, §2.1, CONST-047, CONST-051(C)

#### §11.4.29 — Lowercase-Snake_Case-Naming Mandate
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:367-499
- **Rules:**
  - Every directory, submodule and file under the parent project's working tree MUST use a lowercase snake_case name (ASCII letters/digits/underscores, words separated by `_`). Existing violators (ExampleModule/, Challenges/, Containers/, ExampleAgent/, HelixQA/, Security/, Github-Pages-Website/, Upstreams/, Dependencies/, etc.) MUST be renamed in the migration window.
  - Every reference MUST be updated atomically with the rename: config files, docs, user manuals, diagrams, scripts, source-code imports, links, governance files. Reference drift after a rename is a §11.4.29 violation of equal severity.
  - Exceptions (common-sense scope; MUST NOT break language/technology conventions): programming-language source roots mandating a specific case (Java/Kotlin package paths, Android resource folders, Apple framework directories, C#/Swift project layouts) keep language-mandated names while the submodule root follows our convention; vendor/upstream third-party submodules keep upstream names; build-tooling artefacts (node_modules/, __pycache__/, .git/, target/, build/, bin/) keep tool-mandated names. Test: "does renaming break the technology?" trumps snake_case.
  - Upstreams/ -> upstreams/ transition: the constitution submodule's installer (install_upstreams.sh, exported on operator paths via .bashrc/.zshrc) MUST support BOTH Upstreams/ and upstreams/ layouts during migration; it reads whichever exists, lowercase wins if both. Uppercase fallback MAY be retired only by deliberate amendment after every project migrated.
  - The Upstreamable/Project-Toolkit machinery MUST be fetched + pulled before any rename batch and MUST itself comply; any Upstreamable submodule lacking BOTH-directory support is a release blocker for the rename program.
  - Test coverage of renames: every batch MUST ship (i) a regression test that every reference resolves to the new name (no stale refs), (ii) a full CONST-050(B) test-type matrix run against the post-rename tree, (iii) anti-bluff (CONST-035) wire-evidence captured during runtime verification; a batch without all three is a violation.
  - Cascade: applies recursively through every owned submodule layer (CONST-047) and equally to the consuming project and owned submodules (CONST-051). Per CONST-051(C) renamed paths MUST be the only canonical location; old-name aliases remain only as transitional symlinks if absolutely required and MUST be removed on next-N-cycle review (recommended >=3 release cycles).
  - Phased execution: fine-grained phases per operator instruction (comprehensive brainstorming, phase-divided plan, fine-grained tasks/subtasks, every change covered by every applicable test type), run in parallel with mainstream work (§11.4.20 subagent delegation).
  - No escape hatch beyond the enumerated common-sense exceptions.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named (only the enumerated common-sense exceptions)
- **Honest boundary:** Spirit is operator ergonomics + reference discoverability, not pedantic uniformity at the cost of technology compatibility; a half-completed rename leaving broken references is worse than none.
- **Composes:** §1, §1.1, §11.4.12, §11.4.17, §11.4.18, §11.4.20, §11.4.25, §11.4.26, §11.4.27, §11.4.28, CONST-035, CONST-047, CONST-050(B), CONST-051

#### §11.4.31 — Submodule-Dependency-Manifest Mandate
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:501-646
- **Rules:**
  - Every owned-by-us submodule MUST ship a machine-readable version-controlled dependency manifest at canonical path helix-deps.yaml (or helix-deps.json / helix-deps.toml if the ecosystem strongly prefers; only ONE canonical file per submodule; its name MUST appear in the submodule's README.md + governance trio).
  - Manifest schema (CONST-051(C)-aligned): schema_version: 1; deps: list of {name (canonical name, snake_case per §11.4.29), ssh_url, ref (branch or pinned tag), why, layout (flat = <root>/<name>/ | grouped = <root>/submodules/<name>/)}; transitive_handling: {recursive: true, conflict_resolution: operator-required}; language_specific_subtree: false (set true for Android/Kotlin/Apple roots per §11.4.29 exception).
  - Transitive handling: each declared dep ships its own helix-deps.yaml; the incorporator MUST recurse; top-level project gets the union flattened to root. Two submodules declaring the same dependency at different refs = CONFLICT: operator MUST resolve; the incorporator aborts, NEVER silently picks one.
  - Tooling contract: a consuming project MUST be able to bootstrap its entire own-org dependency graph by running `incorporate-submodule <ssh-url>` (canonical name; in the constitution submodule's scripts/ or a parent project's bin path). The script adds the submodule at its declared canonical path (flat vs grouped), reads its helix-deps.yaml, recurses on any dep missing from the project root, aborts with a directed error on conflict, and emits a final manifest-of-manifests at <root>/.helix-manifest.yaml listing every submodule + its declared deps.
  - Anti-bluff guarantee: every manifest MUST be paired with a verification proof (Challenge script per §11.4.27 + CONST-050(B)) that bootstraps a throwaway consuming project from scratch in a temp dir, runs incorporate-submodule against the manifest, verifies the produced layout matches the manifest (every dep at declared layout path; no extras; none missing), runs the submodule's own test suite against the bootstrapped layout and asserts pass, and captures wire evidence (§11.4.2) of every step. A manifest without this proof is a §11.4.31 violation (equal to a PASS-bluff at the dependency-graph layer).
  - Cascade: every owned submodule MUST ship helix-deps.yaml at its root, recursively; the constitution submodule ships a manifest declaring its own deps (currently empty). The verifier (scripts/verify-governance-cascade.sh or successor) MUST check every owned submodule for manifest presence.
  - The §11.4.28(C) constitution carve-out does not weaken this: a depth-1 constitution-anchored engine still ships its own helix-deps.yaml.
  - No escape hatch.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated in prose: no escape hatch)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §1, §3, §11.4.2, §11.4.12, §11.4.17, §11.4.18, §11.4.20, §11.4.25, §11.4.26, §11.4.27, §11.4.28, §11.4.29, §11.4.30, CONST-047, CONST-050(B), CONST-051(C)

#### §11.4.32 — Post-Constitution-Pull Validation Mandate
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:648-715
- **Rules:**
  - Whenever a consuming project's constitution submodule is fetched + pulled with ANY content change (rule addition/revision, gate addition, anchor reference, version bump), the project MUST execute a full-project + recursive-submodule validation sweep BEFORE the new constitution HEAD is treated as canonical for any other work.
  - Sweep is implemented as scripts/verify-all-constitution-rules.sh (canonical name) which: (1) re-runs the governance-cascade verifier (scripts/verify-governance-cascade.sh) covering every §11.9 + CONST-* anchor across every owned submodule (recursive per CONST-047); (2) for each rule with a programmatically implementable gate (e.g. CONST-053 .gitignore audit, CONST-051(C) nested-own-org-chain audit, CONST-052 case-conformance audit, CONST-050(A) mock-path-from-production audit, CONST-035 anti-bluff smoke-scan) runs that gate against the post-pull tree; (3) any failure produces a directed FAIL entry naming the rule + canonical fix (e.g. `FAIL: CONST-053 - *.log tracked at the-project/foo.log`); (4) failures populate the project's Issues tracker per §11.4.15 with Status Reopened and Type Bug; (5) the agent/operator MUST resolve every FAIL before treating the new HEAD as canonical, closure per the §11.4 anti-bluff covenant (positive-evidence-only, captured wire evidence).
  - Pull-time invocation: `git submodule update --remote constitution` MUST trigger the sweep automatically (post-update hook OR the operator's commit wrapper when advancing the constitution pointer); manual invocation (./scripts/verify-all-constitution-rules.sh) MUST also be available.
  - Anti-bluff: a sweep that exits PASS without running every implementable gate is a violation; its meta-test (paired mutation §1.1) MUST plant a known violation of each enforced gate and assert the sweep reports FAIL for it.
  - It is the enforcement engine for every other §11.4.x and CONST-NNN rule; without it every other rule is a decorative anchor. Classification universal; No escape hatch.
