#### §11.4.35 — Canonical-root inheritance clarity
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:717-847
- **Rules:**
  - The three files in the constitution submodule (constitution/Constitution.md, constitution/CLAUDE.md, constitution/AGENTS.md) are the CANONICAL ROOT (a.k.a. "parent" files) and contain only universal rules per §11.4.17.
  - The three files in the consuming project's repo root (<project-root>/CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, optionally Constitution.md) are CONSUMER EXTENSIONS; they MUST start with the inheritance pointer per constitution/CLAUDE.md "How inheritance works" and contain only project-specific rules (particular hardware, vendor names, regulatory regions, internal asset names, project-private conventions).
  - Invariant 1: when in doubt about which file to edit, reusable-across-projects -> constitution submodule file; project-private specifics -> consumer file; default to consumer-side when uncertain.
  - Invariant 2 (terminology anchor): "the parent CLAUDE.md"/"the root Constitution" = constitution/<filename>, never the consumer's; "the project CLAUDE.md"/"this project's AGENTS.md" = <project-root>/<filename>. Agents MUST resolve ambiguous pronouns via this rule.
  - Invariant 3: universal rules added to the consumer side are misfiled; before adding a MUST to the consumer file assess whether it would benefit other projects, and if yes lift it to the constitution submodule first.
  - Invariant 4: project-specific rules added to the constitution submodule are misfiled; if the rule references project-private specifics, demote it to the consumer file (or genericise first).
  - Invariant 5: the CM-COVENANT-114-N-PROPAGATION gate family verifies anchor TEXT for §11.4.N exists in EVERY CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md; constitution files carry canonical text, consumer files carry compact propagation pointers referencing the canonical authority by file path; both forms count as valid presence.
  - Invariant 6: the consumer's CLAUDE.md MUST start with either the native import `@constitution/CLAUDE.md` or the portable pointer-block (`## INHERITED FROM constitution/CLAUDE.md` heading); the two are equivalent.
  - Invariant 7 (no silent demotion/promotion): moving a rule between layers MUST be a visible commit (git mv of a section, or an explicit "Lifted from <project> to constitution per §11.4.35" / "Demoted from constitution to <project> per §11.4.35" line in the commit message); agents MUST NOT silently re-author a §11.4.X anchor in the wrong layer and call it propagation.
  - Recommended pre-build gate CM-CANONICAL-ROOT-CLARITY verifies (a) consumer CLAUDE.md opens with the inheritance pointer, (b) the constitution submodule's three files exist at the expected path, (c) no `## INHERITED FROM` block in the constitution submodule's own files.
  - Misfiling a rule between layers IS a violation regardless of intent; fix is git mv + commit per invariant 7, not leaving both copies (duplicates silently diverge).
- **Gates:** CM-CANONICAL-ROOT-CLARITY, CM-COVENANT-114-N-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated in prose: no escape hatch)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.17, §11.4.18

#### §11.4.74 — Submodule-catalogue-first discovery + extend-don't-reimplement
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:849-882
- **Rules:**
  - Before scaffolding ANY new module, package, helper or utility the contributor (human or AI) MUST survey the canonical Submodule catalogue: orgs vasic-digital (github.com/vasic-digital, gitlab.com/vasic-digital) and HelixDevelopment (github.com/HelixDevelopment, gitlab.com/HelixDevelopment), mirrored across all four hosts per §2.1 so surveying one mirror yields the full catalogue.
  - Inventory via the canonical INDEX submodules-catalogue.md in this submodule (142 repos at landing, categorised, one-line capability each); it MUST be regenerated quarterly or after any non-trivial repo create/rename per its section 3 recipe.
  - Reuse before reimplement: if a Submodule provides the functionality (or 80%+), the project MUST add it as a Git submodule, not write it fresh.
  - Extend in-place when 80%+ matches: missing features MUST be added TO THAT SUBMODULE (PR upstream + bump the consuming project's pointer), never as a separate consuming-project helper duplicating the 80%.
  - Same development-cycle rules apply to every Submodule under the two orgs: §11.4 anti-bluff, §1.1 paired mutation, §11.4.10 credentials, §11.4.61 metadata table + ToC, §11.4.65 universal Markdown export, §11.4.73 spec versioning (if it has its own spec), §2.1 multi-mirror push, §3 propagation order.
  - Document the survey: each new feature's tracker entry (Issues.md row, ADR, PR description) MUST contain a `Catalogue-Check:` field with one of: `reuse <org/repo>@<sha>`; `extend <org/repo>@<sha>` (reference the upstream PR); `no-match <date>` (surveyed both orgs on that date, none covers it; operators re-validate in review).
  - Planned gate CM-SUBMODULE-CATALOGUE-CHECK: for every new module/package in a non-trivial PR (heuristic >=200 LOC new non-test code), scan the PR description/linked tracker row for a Catalogue-Check line; absence is FAIL; paired mutation strips the line and asserts FAIL.
  - Non-compliance is a process violation; severe cases (duplicate implementation landed without catalogue check) are release blockers.
- **Gates:** CM-SUBMODULE-CATALOGUE-CHECK
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §3, §4, §11.4.28, §11.4.31, §11.4.32, §11.4.36, §2.1, §1.1, §11.4.10, §11.4.61, §11.4.65, §11.4.73

#### §11.4.75 — Mechanical Enforcement Without Exception
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:886-1026
- **Rules:**
  - Constitutional invariants MUST be enforced mechanically at FIVE independent layers; bypassing one does not bypass the discipline: (1) local pre-commit git hook refusing staged .md lacking sibling .html+.pdf (and other staged-only invariants); (2) commit_all.sh integration - the canonical project commit script invokes the same checks and auto-runs sync_all_markdown_exports.sh to self-repair before commit; (3) local pre-push git hook re-running siblings + propagation-gate subset on every commit in the push; (4) post-commit auto-repair hook detecting orphan .md in the just-committed manifest, auto-generating siblings via pandoc + weasyprint, creating a `chore(§11.4.75): auto-export ...` follow-up commit (idempotent + recursion-guarded); (5) local-only equivalent: remote CI surfaces (GitHub Actions, GitLab pipelines, Jenkins, CircleCI) are DISABLED per User mandate 2026-05-20 (workflow file preserved at .github/workflows/constitution-compliance.yml.disabled-local-only), and Layer 5 is the operator's local final-gate ritual before tagging: `bash device/rockchip/rk3588/tests/pre_build_verification.sh` + `bash scripts/testing/meta_test_false_positive_proof.sh`.
  - Helper contracts (mandatory): scripts/install_git_hooks.sh (idempotent installer copying hooks from tracked scripts/git_hooks/ into .git/hooks/, hooked into scripts/setup.sh so fresh clones auto-install; verifies itself with --verify); scripts/git_hooks/pre-commit (Layer 1), pre-push (Layer 3), post-commit (Layer 4), commit-msg (bypass-rationale enforcement); _constitution_sibling_check function in scripts/commit_all.sh (Layer 2).
  - Bypass policy: layers 1+3 can be bypassed by --no-verify (Layer 5 re-runs the same check before tag creation; tags are NEVER created without it per §11.4.40); Layer 2 bypassed by direct git commit (Layer 1 catches); Layer 4 cannot be bypassed by --no-verify. Skipping the local Layer 5 ritual blocks tag creation.
  - Legitimate bypasses MUST be audited: when --no-verify is detected via touch-file marker .git/ATMO_LAST_BYPASS_ATTEMPT, the commit-msg hook REQUIRES a `Bypass-rationale: <reason>` footer; docs/audit/bypass_events.md accumulates the audit trail.
  - Five pre-build gates with paired §1.1 meta-test mutations: CM-COVENANT-114-75-PROPAGATION (anchor literal across canonical files), CM-GIT-HOOKS-INSTALL-SCRIPT (installer present + executable), CM-GIT-HOOKS-SOURCE-DIR (4 hook bodies present + executable), CM-COMMIT-ALL-SIBLING-CHECK (_constitution_sibling_check in commit_all.sh), CM-CI-WORKFLOW-PRESENT (CI workflow + >=3 required jobs). CM-COVENANT-114-75-PROPAGATION enforces the literal across the ~44-file consumer fleet; stripping the literal -> FAILs.
  - No escape hatch: no --skip-hooks, --bypass-enforcement, --allow-orphan-md, --ci-not-applicable, --mechanical-enforcement-not-needed flag. The --no-verify route IS the deliberate audit-trail bypass, made mechanical by the commit-msg footer requirement.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker regardless of context. (Anchor was renumbered from §11.4.74 per §11.4.41 merge-first.)
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-75-PROPAGATION, CM-GIT-HOOKS-INSTALL-SCRIPT, CM-GIT-HOOKS-SOURCE-DIR, CM-COMMIT-ALL-SIBLING-CHECK, CM-CI-WORKFLOW-PRESENT
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-hooks, --bypass-enforcement, --allow-orphan-md, --ci-not-applicable, --mechanical-enforcement-not-needed
- **Honest boundary:** No single layer is bypass-proof in isolation (by design); bypassing all five simultaneously is mechanically impossible. Layer 5 is local-only (remote CI disabled); a future PWU may re-enable remote CI.
- **Composes:** §1.1, §9, §11.4, §11.4.1, §11.4.4, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.40, §11.4.41, §11.4.43, §11.4.51, §11.4.52, §11.4.58, §11.4.65, §11.4.66, §11.4.67, §11.4.69, §11.4.70, §11.4.71, §11.4.72, §11.4.73, §11.4.74

#### §11.4.76 — Containers-submodule mandate
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1028-1057
- **Rules:**
  - For ANY containerized workload (Docker, Podman, Qemu, Kubernetes, container-backed emulators such as Android emulator or VM-based testbeds) every consuming project MUST use the canonical Containers Submodule https://github.com/vasic-digital/containers (git@github.com:vasic-digital/containers.git, module digital.vasic.containers), mirrored across the four §2.1 hosts (GitHub + GitLab + GitFlic + GitVerse).
  - (1) Use it as authoritative library for runtime auto-detection, endpoint discovery, lifecycle/health management, compose orchestration, cross-build, emulator integration and on-demand service boot.
  - (2) Install as a Git submodule: `git submodule add git@github.com:vasic-digital/containers.git <path>/containers`; go.mod (or equivalent) consumes via `replace digital.vasic.containers => ./<path>/containers` in development; production builds resolve through pinned commit SHAs.
  - (3) On-demand-infra invariant: tests, CLI doctor commands and local-dev workflows depending on Postgres/Redis/OTel/message-brokers/emulators MUST invoke the Containers Submodule's pkg/boot + pkg/compose + pkg/health APIs to bring infra up automatically; operators MUST NOT be required to manually start podman machine / docker compose up before tests.
  - (4) Extend, never reimplement: a missing runtime (e.g. new emulator type) or lifecycle primitive (e.g. new health-check kind) MUST be added to vasic-digital/containers (PR upstream + bump pointer), never as a parallel in-project implementation.
  - (5) Anti-bluff: every integration test claiming to exercise a containerized component MUST actually boot it via the Containers Submodule; tests passing without containers running (short-circuit fakes bypassing boot) are a §11.4 bluff; a passing test MUST imply infra was up.
  - (6) Composition with §11.4.74: a tracker row touching containerization MUST record `Catalogue-Check: extend vasic-digital/containers@<sha>` (or reuse); `no-match` is valid only if the project demonstrates the Containers API cannot model the workload.
  - Planned gate CM-CONTAINERS-USED: for every PR touching Dockerfile*, *compose*.yml, *podman*.yml, Vagrantfile, or code under a directory matching (test|integration|e2e)/.*infra, scan for an import of digital.vasic.containers/...; absence in a non-trivial container-touching PR is FAIL; paired mutation strips the import and asserts FAIL.
  - Non-compliance is a process violation; landing containerized infra without consuming the Containers Submodule (reinventing compose orchestration in-project) is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-CONTAINERS-USED
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §3, §11.4.28, §11.4.31, §11.4.36, §11.4.65, §11.4.74, §11.4.75, §1.1, §2.1

#### §11.4.77 — Regeneration-mechanism-required mandate
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1061-1109
- **Rules:**
  - Every .gitignore entry excluding either (a) more than ~100 MiB of content, OR (b) any artifact essential to building/running/testing the project, MUST be accompanied by a documented + automated mechanism that re-obtains or re-generates the content on a fresh clone. Closed set: (1) Re-obtain (download from authoritative source: vendor tarball, SDK installer, npm/pip/cargo/go-mod registry, container image registry, dedicated git submodule, S3, GCS, vendor-internal artifact server) via a script deterministic on a fresh clone; (2) Re-generate (produce from tracked source via a script: build pipeline, codegen, asset rendering, captured-evidence replay, container build, kernel build, image packaging).
  - Required artefacts per qualifying entry (each independently mandatory): (1) metadata file .gitignore-meta/<entry-slug>.yaml (or project-canonical equivalent declared in the project's CLAUDE.md) carrying gitignore-pattern verbatim, mechanism-type: re-obtain | re-generate, script-path (repo-relative deterministic entrypoint), expected-disk-usage, vendor-url-or-source when applicable, integrity {algorithm: sha256 | md5, value: hex} when fetchable from a known-stable mirror, requires-network: true|false, requires-credentials: true|false (and which credentials slot per §11.4.10); (2) entry in the post-clone bootstrap script (scripts/setup.sh or equivalent), runnable non-interactively on a fresh clone or as an idempotent step (scripts/setup.sh --regenerate <entry-slug>); (3) pre-build gate verifying regenerated content is present at the expected path OR the regeneration script ran successfully (e.g. stamp file .gitignore-meta/.regenerated/<entry-slug>.ok with mtime >= source freshness window); (4) documentation update - README plus relevant docs/guides/*.md describing the mechanism, manual fallback (vendor URL, alternative mirrors), time + disk-usage budget, per-§11.4.10 credentials requirements.
  - No escape hatch: a bare .gitignore entry excluding significant/essential content without the mechanism is a §11.4 PASS-bluff variant; there is no --skip-regen-mechanism, --gitignore-is-enough, --operator-already-has-content flag.
  - Sister-anchor bindings: mechanism MUST be verified end-to-end on a sandbox clone BEFORE the .gitignore entry lands (§11.4.6; "LIKELY works" forbidden); generated HTML/PDF siblings are an instance of re-generate via sync_all_markdown_exports.sh (§11.4.65); uncertain whether an entry qualifies -> ASK the operator (§11.4.66); integrity hash and vendor URL MUST be re-validated against upstream before pushing the governing commit (§11.4.71; stale hashes are a §11.4.6 violation); extend an existing Submodule's downloader/decompressor rather than reimplement (§11.4.74); local pre-commit hook (Layer 1) MUST refuse a commit adding .gitignore lines without a corresponding .gitignore-meta/*.yaml, and the Layer 5 gate replays on every push (§11.4.75; paired mutation: strip a metadata YAML entry -> gate FAILs); container images excluded from VCS are regenerated via vasic-digital/containers pkg/boot + tracked Dockerfiles and the YAML references the Containers Submodule build path (§11.4.76); the mechanism MUST be pre-tested in a sandbox clone with a hardlinked-backup safety net before live use, and a script silently corrupting content on a fresh clone is a §9 violation (§9/§9.2); submodules consuming the constitution inherit §11.4.77 and their own .gitignore entries are subject to it (§3).
  - Planned gate CM-GITIGNORE-REGEN-MECHANISM: for every PR adding a line to .gitignore (or any *.gitignore in a sub-tree), find a matching .gitignore-meta/ entry, verify script-path exists and is executable, verify the YAML parses and carries required keys, verify the post-clone bootstrap references the mechanism; bare-line additions are FAIL; paired §1.1 mutation strips one required key (e.g. script-path:) and asserts FAIL.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker regardless of context.
- **Gates:** CM-GITIGNORE-REGEN-MECHANISM
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-regen-mechanism, --gitignore-is-enough, --operator-already-has-content
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §3, §9, §9.2, §11.4, §11.4.6, §11.4.10, §11.4.65, §11.4.66, §11.4.71, §11.4.74, §11.4.75, §11.4.76

#### §11.4.78 — CodeGraph code-intelligence mandate
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1113-1187
- **Rules:**
  - Every consuming project MUST install, initialize and USE CodeGraph (https://github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph, npm @colbymchenry/codegraph) as its code-intelligence layer for AI coding agents (local SQLite semantic graph exposed over MCP; 100% local, no cloud/external API). Using it is not optional.
  - (1) Install: `npm install -g @colbymchenry/codegraph` (Node.js 18+); npm global prefix MUST be user-writable; installation MUST NOT require sudo/su (§9/§12). Native modules (better-sqlite3, tree-sitter) compile on install with WASM fallback.
  - (2) Initialize + index: `codegraph init` at project root creates .codegraph/config.json (tracked) and .codegraph/codegraph.db (regenerable artifact, gitignored per §11.4.30/§11.4.77 with `codegraph index` as declared regeneration mechanism). The config.json exclude list MUST exclude (a) other-owned submodules and vendored trees and (b) non-negotiably every credential/secret path (.env*, keystores, signing keys, service-account JSON) per §11.4.10; a secret reaching the index is a §11.4.10 violation. `codegraph index` builds, `codegraph sync` keeps fresh.
  - CRITICAL filter mechanism: CodeGraph v1.x is zero-config: built-in skip lists (node_modules, vendor, dist, build, target, .venv, Pods, .next) PLUS the project root .gitignore decide what is indexed; config.json include/exclude are NOT used for filtering (documentation-only/deprecated). Control scope with root-anchored .gitignore patterns (start with `/`) and `!` negations to re-include owned paths under a default-skipped parent (e.g. !/vendor/widevine_*).
  - MUST-EXCLUDE classes: (a) build outputs/regenerable artifacts (/out/, /prebuilts/, /rockdev/, /RKTools/, .compressed/); (b) caches/dependencies/tooling (.gradle/, __pycache__/, .venv/, flash_logs/, logs/); (c) credentials/secrets/QA-recording artifacts (/secrets/, scripts/testing/secrets/, **/*.env, /qa-results/, /recordings/).
  - ALL SOURCE CODE MUST REMAIN INDEXABLE, including AOSP platform trees (frameworks/, external/, art/, cts/, bionic/, packages/, system/, kernel-5.10/, hardware/*/, vendor/, device/*/) - tracked source MUST NOT be gitignored for CodeGraph purposes; only the rubbish classes may be excluded. A 1M+ tracked-file project yields a 30-40 GB first index; later `codegraph sync` is fast (git diff).
  - Universal mandatory-exclude baseline (binds EVERY consuming project; project may add its own but MUST NOT drop any class): (a) build outputs/regenerable artifacts: /out/, /build/, /dist/, /target/, bin/, obj/, .compressed/, any generator-produced tree; (b) caches/dependency/tooling dirs: **/ccache/, **/.ccache/, .gradle/, __pycache__/, .pytest_cache/, .mypy_cache/, .ruff_cache/, node_modules/, .next/, .cache/, .terraform/, .venv/, logs/; (c) credentials/secrets: .env, .env.*, **/*.env, secrets/, **/*secret*, keystores/signing-keys/service-account JSON, every credential-bearing path per §11.4.10 (never negotiable); (d) QA/recording/large regenerable corpora: **/qa-results/, **/recordings/, prebuilt-binary trees. Realized via root-anchored .gitignore patterns. Own-org submodule sources stay INCLUDED per §11.4.79; third-party vendored trees EXCLUDED. Dropping any class is a §11.4.78/§11.4.79 violation; no source-code tree may be excluded to satisfy it.
  - (3) Wire every supported CLI agent: register the MCP server (`codegraph serve --mcp`, stdio) with every AI coding CLI the developers use; project-scoped and committed where supported (Claude Code .mcp.json, OpenCode opencode.json, Qwen Code .qwen/settings.json, Crush .crush.json), host-local where the agent stores MCP config outside the repo (Kimi CLI ~/.kimi/mcp.json). Every MCP config MUST reference the bare `codegraph` command resolved on PATH, never a hardcoded host path. Claude Code is canonical primary agent; others MUST work too.
  - (4) Anti-bluff verification mandatory: a verification suite (reference: scripts/verify-codegraph.sh + tests/codegraph/, six layers): index reality, query correctness, MCP-protocol JSON-RPC, per-agent connectivity, per-agent end-to-end LLM drive, and a falsifiability rehearsal proving the suite FAILs when the index is deliberately broken. The per-agent end-to-end layer MUST use an unforgeable challenge (fact obtainable only via a CodeGraph MCP tool, e.g. node count via codegraph_status). An agent that genuinely cannot be driven (missing credentials, exhausted quota, environment incompatibility) is a documented SKIP gap per §11.4.3, never a faked PASS.
  - (5) Every project MUST carry docs/CODEGRAPH.md (or canonical equivalent) covering install, init, indexing, per-agent wiring, the verification suite, troubleshooting, kept in sync per §11.4.12/§11.4.65.
  - (6) Catalogue-first: CodeGraph is a third-party tool consumed as the published npm package; it does NOT enter as a git submodule and does NOT add a Git remote.
  - Planned gate CM-CODEGRAPH-WIRED: verifies .codegraph/config.json exists with §11.4.10 secret-exclusions, every developer-used agent carries a CodeGraph MCP registration, and the verification suite exists and is executable; paired §1.1 mutation removes a secret-exclusion and asserts FAIL.
  - EXTENSION (2026-09-24; where it conflicts with clause-2 filter wording THIS extension governs): (7) ONE MECHANISM, INHERITED BY REFERENCE: scope renderer (<constitution>/scripts/codegraph/scope_render.py + scope_enumerate.js + scope_baseline.txt + template scope.example.yaml), single sanctioned writer entry (codegraph_safe.sh + codegraph_safe_helper.py + codegraph_guard.sh + disk_tripwire.sh), version-keyed runner patcher (fk_index_patch.py + runner_patches/), bulk-window hazard probe (fk_cascade_probe.py), progress-proven watchdog (index_watch.py), scope proof (codegraph_scope_guard.py) and <constitution>/scripts/lumen/gen_lumenignore.py MUST live in the constitution submodule and be INVOKED BY REFERENCE (§11.4.28/§11.4.80/§11.4.177); a consumer copy/fork/vendored duplicate/hand-rolled equivalent is a violation (§11.4.227). Each tool MUST be documented (§11.4.18) and test-first with paired mutations (§11.4.224/§1.1); a tool lacking its own tests MUST NOT be pointed at a live index; OWED (tracked §11.4.197): own tests for index_watch.py and fk_cascade_probe.py, for runner patches lockfix1 and datafrag1 (excluded from the default patch set for that reason), and the §11.4.18 companion guide of every tool named.
  - (8) THE CONSUMER SUPPLIES DATA, NEVER MECHANISM (§11.4.35): exactly one declarative scope file (schema = scope.example.yaml): own-org list, project-specific rubbish paths, pathological inputs (files that stall the parser - declared, never retried to timeout), explicit re-include negations, per-submodule class overrides WITH a reason, accepted indexed-file count and tolerance, efficiency thresholds (§11.4.275(D)). It MUST NOT drop a baseline class.
  - (9) CONFIG TRUTH = what the INSTALLED CLI version actually reads, established from that version's own loader code (§11.4.99, §11.4.6; never from memory); a config file the CLI does not read is dead documentation and MUST NOT be cited as scope. The effective scope artifact is GENERATED by the renderer from baseline classes + §11.4.79 classification + consumer DATA; hand edits refused; a missing/malformed config that the CLI silently falls back from is a FAIL, never a warning.
  - (10) SCOPE PROOF BEFORE "READY" (supersedes size-based evidence): the scope guard MUST enumerate files through the installed runner's OWN discovery code and assert, each with a control needle (§11.4.273): indexed-file count within consumer tolerance of accepted count; zero files under third-party roots; zero secret-class files (§11.4.10); at least one file under every own-org root (§11.4.79). Database size is NEVER evidence of a real index. Completeness (pending work == 0) is §11.4.275(C).
  - EXTENSION (2026-09-25, host-adaptive V8 heap budget in the single writer entry): codegraph_safe.sh preflight() MUST compute the Node.js heap budget from MEASURED MemAvailable (half of it, floored at 8192 MiB, never hardcoded, §12.11/§11.4.6) and export NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=<budget> before every init/index/sync launch; an unmeasurable budget REFUSES the run (die 6), never a silent fallback to the stock ~4 GiB V8 limit (§11.4.201). Regression tests test_unit_safe.sh U44/U45; companion doc docs/scripts/codegraph_safe.md (§11.4.18). Reason: a bulk index run on a 584,328-file project crashed at the stock heap limit (rc=134) discarding ~85 min.
  - CORRECTION (2026-09-25, operator: no caps for codegraph/lumen): the earlier 65536 MiB cap is SUPERSEDED; the heap ceiling is now MemTotal*60/100 (MiB), computed fresh each preflight from /proc/meminfo (the real §12.6 bound, never a fixed number). Regression test U46 proves the cap is real and independently computed.
  - EXTENSION (2026-09-25 round 2, MCP wiring): the project's .mcp.json MUST register a `codegraph` MCP server (this project: command `bash constitution/scripts/codegraph/codegraph_mcp_serve.sh`), a project-tracked, §11.4.177-decoupled wrapper that resolves the SAME validated patched runner codegraph_safe.sh uses (via fk_index_patch.py --print-bin, re-derived every launch) rather than trusting stock-on-PATH; this REFINES clause 3 (a project with a patched-runner requirement uses the wrapper; others MAY use the bare command). The wrapper MUST ALWAYS pass `--path <project> --no-watch` (--no-watch never optional): serve --mcp with the watcher auto-syncs (WRITES) the DB and daemonizes, and a permanently registered server otherwise collides with bulk index/sync (two writers, one DB -> "database is locked"). Staleness is cleared deliberately by `codegraph sync`, never automatically. Required tests (scripts/codegraph/tests/test_codegraph_mcp_serve.sh): T01 resolved runner == fk_index_patch.py --print-bin; T02 --path+--no-watch always present; T03 --path targets exactly the resolved project; T04 incident replay (real init'd scratch project, real serve --mcp, real file mutation, DB mtime unchanged proves zero writes); T05 $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR used verbatim when set; T06 fails closed (non-zero) when patched-runner resolution cannot proceed. Project-root fallback MUST try git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree before --show-toplevel.
  - Non-compliance is a process violation; a project worked on by AI agents without CodeGraph installed, wired and anti-bluff-verified is in breach.
- **Gates:** CM-CODEGRAPH-WIRED
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** .mcp.json registration takes effect on a fresh session; end-to-end callability of codegraph_explore/codegraph_node is OWED as a tracked §11.4.197 follow-up. The mechanism cannot mechanically guarantee every agent always chooses it over raw grep/find/glob (soft property of tool selection).
- **Composes:** §1.1, §9, §12, §12.6, §12.11, §12.12, §11.4.3, §11.4.6, §11.4.10, §11.4.12, §11.4.14, §11.4.18, §11.4.28, §11.4.30, §11.4.35, §11.4.65, §11.4.74, §11.4.77, §11.4.79, §11.4.80, §11.4.99, §11.4.102, §11.4.108, §11.4.177, §11.4.197, §11.4.201, §11.4.224, §11.4.227, §11.4.263, §11.4.273, §11.4.275

#### §11.4.79 — Own-org submodules MUST be included in the CodeGraph index
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1189-1237
- **Rules:**
  - Every consuming project's CodeGraph config MUST distinguish submodule classes: Own-org (full write access via the project's CLIs; canonical orgs vasic-digital on GitHub/GitLab/GitFlic/GitVerse + HelixDevelopment on GitHub) MUST be INCLUDED so agents resolve symbols, callers and impact across the whole repo graph; Third-party (no write access, vendored only, the §11.4.74 no-match -> vendor path, e.g. gopkg.in/telebot.v3) MUST be EXCLUDED. The classifier is write-access via the project's own CLIs, not subjective internal/external. Refines (does not contradict) §11.4.78 step 2.
  - Operational step 1: fetch + pull latest of every submodule before re-indexing (`git submodule update --remote --merge`), verify the project still builds; third-party pins (e.g. telebot.v3 pinned at v3.3.8 to keep the Go import path stable) MUST be respected and rolled back if --remote advances past the load-bearing pin.
  - Step 2: adjust .codegraph/config.json exclude so third-party submodule paths are explicitly listed and own-org submodule paths MUST NOT appear in exclude (re-pointed by clause 8 below to the scope DATA file + renderer).
  - Step 3: re-index with the project's canonical CodeGraph initialiser (e.g. scripts/codegraph_setup.sh) via codegraph index/sync (re-pointed by clause 8: ONLY through the single writer entry of §11.4.80(5)).
  - Step 4: the project's scripts/codegraph_validate.sh (§11.4.78 verification) MUST probe at least one symbol that lives ONLY inside an own-org submodule (e.g. bg.TaskQueue from submodules/background/interfaces.go); success proves the include path reached submodule sources, not a §107 PASS-bluff against a stale index.
  - Step 5: paired §1.1 mutation: temporarily add the own-org submodule path to exclude, re-index, run validate - it MUST FAIL on the cross-submodule probe; restore. Every validate probe added per step 5 MUST land with a mutation pair.
  - The exclude list MUST still cover every .env*, keystore, signing key, service-account JSON regardless of submodule ownership (§11.4.10).
  - EXTENSION (2026-09-24): (6) Mechanical classification: own-org vs third-party is DERIVED by the constitution's renderer (§11.4.78(7)) by walking .gitmodules RECURSIVELY (nested gitlinks included) and matching each submodule's remote-URL organisation against the consumer's own-org DATA list (§11.4.78(8)); third-party code nested INSIDE an own-org submodule is third-party; a per-submodule override is DATA with a recorded reason, never an unexplained edit.
  - (7) Stale render fails: adding, removing or re-pointing a gitlink without re-rendering makes the render stale; the scope guard (§11.4.78(10)) MUST FAIL on a stale render; the receipt carries the input hashes it was built from.
  - (8) Steps 2-3 re-pointed: "adjust config.json exclude" means edit the consumer scope DATA file and re-render through the constitution renderer; step 3 re-index runs ONLY through the single writer entry of §11.4.80(5). Tracked first-party source skipped by default by the engine is re-included by GENERATED negations, never by hand.
  - Non-compliance is a process violation; an AI-agent-worked project whose own-org submodules are excluded from CodeGraph (when they could be included) is in breach; severe cases (own-org submodules silently excluded WITHOUT an audit trail in .codegraph/config.json comments) are release blockers.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §1.1, §11.4.10, §11.4.74, §11.4.78, §11.4.80, §107

#### §11.4.80 — CodeGraph regular-update + sync automation mandate
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1239-1292
- **Rules:**
  - Every consuming project MUST regularly check for CodeGraph npm-package updates, install the latest stable version, and re-sync its local index. Automation lives in the constitution submodule and is inherited BY REFERENCE (never copied into project scripts/); invoke e.g. `bash ${CONST_DIR}/scripts/codegraph_update.sh && bash ${CONST_DIR}/scripts/codegraph_sync.sh .`.
  - Deliverable 1: `<constitution>/scripts/codegraph_update.sh` compares installed `@colbymchenry/codegraph` with npm latest, runs `npm update -g` (or `npm install -g ...@latest`) when newer, records old+new version+timestamp in `docs/codegraph/Status.md`, exits 0 only when `codegraph --version` shows the expected post-update output. Idempotent (same-day re-run is a no-op). The "update succeeded" PASS MUST observe the new version, not just npm exit code.
  - Deliverable 2: `<constitution>/scripts/codegraph_sync.sh` runs, inside the consuming project (argument or `find_constitution.sh` parent walk): `codegraph status` (baseline) -> `codegraph sync .` -> `codegraph status` (post) -> `scripts/codegraph_validate.sh` (§11.4.78 step 4). Each step's output is appended to the project's `docs/codegraph/Status.md`. The sync MUST consult `codegraph help` BEFORE invoking any command to verify the subcommand still exists with the same shape. Canonical command list: `codegraph` (installer), `install`, `init [path]` (--index), `uninit [path]` (--force), `index [path]` (--force, --quiet), `sync [path]`, `status [path]`, `query <search>` (--kind, --limit, --json), `files [path]` (--format, --filter, --max-depth, --json), `context <task>` (--format, --max-nodes), `affected [files...]`, `serve --mcp`.
  - Deliverable 3: append-only `docs/codegraph/Status.md` + `docs/codegraph/Status_Summary.md` ledgers tracking every CodeGraph event (install, npm-update, sync, index regeneration, validate runs with PASS/FAIL counts, HRDs opened/closed). Both MUST be exported to `.html` and `.pdf` siblings on every edit (§11.4.65); Status_Summary is the operator-readable derived index (§11.4.53).
  - Cadence: automation MUST run at least weekly (§11.4.45); projects MAY run more often, never less.
  - EXTENSION clause 4: an update MUST first probe the new version (config filename + keys its loader reads, bulk-window hazard probe, applicability of every version-keyed runner patch). If the patched runner cannot be re-derived and re-proven for the new version, the upgrade REFUSES loudly and keeps the prior version (§11.4.201) - never a silent fall-back to the stock runner. A runner patch without its own RED->GREEN test, paired mutation and equivalence proof on a byte copy (never the live database) MUST NOT be applied to a live index (§11.4.224 / §1.1).
  - EXTENSION clause 5: every `init`/`index`/`sync` goes through the constitution's single writer entry (§11.4.78(7)), which MUST (i) refuse while ANY live process whose real command line (§11.4.196(D)) targets the same root is running, whatever the lock file's age; (ii) classify a run as BULK by the size of the PENDING work (unresolved backlog, files still to parse), NEVER by the size of what is already stored; (iii) route bulk runs only through the proven patched runner, detached, under the clause-6 watchdog and a disk tripwire. Readers of a live index open it read-only/immutable and never run full-table counts; experiments run on fixtures or copy-on-write copies.
  - EXTENSION clause 6: every long run is supervised by a PROGRESS-PROVEN watchdog (§11.4.232(C)); a process alive but not advancing is a STALL -> loud stop + tracked item (§11.4.197), never "still running".
  - EXTENSION clause 7: the weekly floor is realised by an actual timer/hook plus the constitution-pull hook (§11.4.164), each run leaving a ledger entry; a missing validator is a FAIL, never a warning or silent exit 0.
  - EXTENSION clause 8: the embedded command list is illustrative; the authority is a live `codegraph help` diff against the previous run (e.g. a `telemetry` command exists that the list omits). Telemetry MUST be off for the Local-Only posture; whether it is off is a per-host FACT to be captured, not assumed.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); applies to every project with CodeGraph configured per §11.4.78. Non-compliance is a process violation; severe cases (no `codegraph_update.sh` run in >2 weeks AND open AI-agent work) are release blockers.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** Manual "run codegraph index when I remember" is the forbidden failure mode; stale indexes silently mislead agents. Cadence is a floor, not contractually fixed, because environments differ.
- **Composes:** §11.4.78, §11.4.79, §11.4.10, §11.4.45, §11.4.53, §11.4.65, §107, §1.1, §11.4.196(D), §11.4.201, §11.4.224, §11.4.232(C), §11.4.197, §11.4.164, §11.4.17
- **Review addendum:** Paired §1.1 mutation: temporarily downgrade the installed codegraph version; the script MUST detect drift and self-correct; then restore.

#### §11.4.109 — Mandatory Anti-Forgetting Enforcement: PreToolUse guard hook + subagent constitutional preamble + orchestrator pre-action checklist
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1298-1380
- **Rules:**
  - Short tag `anti-forgetting-enforcement`. Reason: a rule the orchestrator forgets to paste into subagent prompts is a social contract with memory, not enforcement (emulator subagents ran raw host-direct emulator/adb commands instead of routing through the Containers submodule). Two-layer model: hook = floor, preamble = ceiling.
  - Every consuming project MUST deploy all three components together.
  - (A) PreToolUse guard hook: a shell script wired as a `PreToolUse` hook in the agent runtime's project-scoped settings (e.g. `.claude/settings.json`) intercepting every Bash tool call and BLOCKING forbidden classes. It reads the tool invocation JSON from stdin (`.tool_name` + `.tool_input.command`); exits 0 for non-Bash tools and empty/missing commands; for Bash pattern-matches the mandatory blocked classes; exits 2 on match with stderr text citing the governing clause as the refusal reason.
  - Mandatory blocked classes: (1) raw host-direct Android emulator launch / APK install / instrumentation run (`emulator -avd ...`, `$ANDROID_HOME/emulator/emulator ...`, `adb install ...`, `adb -s ... install ...`, `am instrument ...`) per §11.4.76 + project-layer emulator clauses; (2) force-push / hook bypass / signature bypass (`git push --force`, `-f`, `--force-with-lease`, `--no-verify`, `--no-gpg-sign`) per §11.4.41 + §11.4.71; (3) privilege escalation (`sudo`, `su`, `su -`, `su -l`); (4) host power management (`systemctl suspend/hibernate/poweroff/reboot/halt/kill-user/kill-session`, `loginctl`, `pm-suspend/hibernate`, `shutdown`) per §12.
  - Escape hatch: a command containing the literal marker `# guardrails:allow <reason>` is WARNED (stderr) but NOT blocked - EXCEPT host-power commands, which are categorically non-overridable.
  - Canonical implementation: `constitution/scripts/hooks/guard-forbidden-commands.sh`; consumers MUST reference it at that path (inherited by reference per §11.4.80), NEVER copy it. Portable: no `jq` hard dependency (awk fallback), no project-specific paths, no hardcoded credentials.
  - Hook anti-bluff: a hermetic test suite of at least 20 cases MUST verify every blocked class exits 2, every allowed command exits 0, the escape hatch fires for non-power classes, and host-power rejects even with the marker. Paired §1.1 mutation: remove the `emulator -avd` pattern -> emulator case exits 0 -> test FAILs -> restore -> PASS.
  - (B) Subagent Constitutional Preamble: a canonical document at `docs/AGENT_GUARDRAILS.md` (or the project's equivalent path recorded in its CLAUDE.md) containing a verbatim self-contained `SUBAGENT CONSTITUTIONAL PREAMBLE` block covering the top-10 mandatory constraints the hook cannot pattern-match (anti-bluff intent, resource caps, evidence honesty, continuation maintenance, hardcoding prohibition, distribute gate, remote policy, no-guessing vocabulary, etc.) plus the hook-enforced classes; with clear instruction that the orchestrator MUST paste it verbatim into every subagent dispatch. It MUST be mechanically verifiable by `check-constitution.sh` and contain the literal `11.4.109`. Paired mutation: remove the preamble's hook-reference sentence -> checker FAILs.
  - (C) Orchestrator Pre-Action Checklist in the same document, with an `ORCHESTRATOR PRE-ACTION CHECKLIST` heading, covering at minimum: before any subagent dispatch confirm the preamble is pasted verbatim; before any emulator/device action confirm the run routes through the Containers submodule CLI not host-direct, no live device is targeted, and the gate host is eligible (else honestly BLOCKED); before any distribute action confirm Challenge Tests EXECUTED (not compiled) against the exact artifact, version code bumped, CHANGELOG entry present, debug-stage evidence present if two-stage distribute applies; before any push/destructive git action confirm no force flags without per-operation operator approval, remote is the approved set only, and for history rewrite a hardlinked `.git` backup made first; before any host-affecting command confirm it is not in the host-power blocked class. Each item traceable to a governing clause cited inline; verifiable by `check-constitution.sh`.
  - Mechanical enforcement: consumer `check-constitution.sh` (or `verify-all-constitution-rules.sh`) MUST verify ALL of: (1) `constitution/scripts/hooks/guard-forbidden-commands.sh` exists at the canonical path; (2) the agent settings file contains a `PreToolUse` entry referencing the canonical script; (3) `docs/AGENT_GUARDRAILS.md` exists with the `SUBAGENT CONSTITUTIONAL PREAMBLE` and `ORCHESTRATOR PRE-ACTION CHECKLIST` headings; (4) a hermetic hook test (e.g. under `tests/hooks/`) exists and passes; (5) the literal `11.4.109` is present in every per-scope governance file (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, QWEN.md) of the consumer and its owned submodules per §11.4.35.
  - Paired §1.1 meta-test mutations: (a) remove the PreToolUse entry -> gate (2) FAILs; (b) delete AGENT_GUARDRAILS.md -> (3) FAILs; (c) remove the canonical hook script -> (1) FAILs; (d) strip the literal from a consumer CLAUDE.md -> propagation gate FAILs.
  - Inheritance: applies recursively to every submodule/feature/artifact/project; submodule constitutions MAY add stricter rules (more blocked classes, checklist items, test counts) but MUST NOT relax any clause.
  - Principle: a constraint that depends on an agent remembering it is a hope, not a constraint.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); universal blocked list covers the four unconditional classes; consumers extend per §11.4.35. Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-ANTI-FORGETTING-ENFORCEMENT (enforces 1-4), CM-COVENANT-114-109-PROPAGATION (enforces 5)
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-pretooluse-hook, --no-guardrails-doc, --anti-forgetting-optional, --single-layer-sufficient
- **Honest boundary:** The hook blocks command-class violations only; the preamble covers rules the hook cannot pattern-match. UNCONFIRMED: the operator's verbatim anti-forgetting quote is pending (tracked in CONTINUATION.md).
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.1-§11.4.16, §11.4.6, §11.4.10, §11.4.75, §11.4.76, §11.4.78, §11.4.79, §11.4.80, §11.4.81, §11.4.84, §11.4.98, §11.4.102, §12, §11.4.41, §11.4.71, §11.4.35, §11.4.17, §1.1

#### §11.4.140 — Universal action-prefix system (`ACTION_NAME ::`)
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1384-1501
- **Rules:**
  - Every project MUST support an extensible action-prefix system: when a prompt's FIRST non-blank line starts with an uppercase token followed by `" :: "` (grammar `^([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*) :: `, anchored at line start, UPPERCASE-only, exactly one space each side of `::`), the agent MUST (1) look the token up in the action registry (tracked `constitution/actions/registry.yaml`, or `$HELIX_ACTION_REGISTRY`); (2) if registered, REPLACE the `ACTION_NAME :: ` prefix with that action's `expansion` text and apply its `rules`; (3) execute the REMAINDER under the expanded instruction (expand -> rescan -> execute residual).
  - Two mandatory layers. LAYER 1 (universal, always-on): the recognition instruction MUST be mirrored into EVERY agent context carrier the constitution maintains (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, QWEN.md, GEMINI.md per §11.4.35) so every CLI agent (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Codex CLI, Copilot CLI, Cursor, Aider, Cline, Continue, Roo Code, future agents) self-applies it. LAYER 2 (mechanical, where a pre-submit seam exists): a prompt-preprocessing hook reading the SAME registry applies expansion deterministically (Claude Code `UserPromptSubmit`/`UserPromptExpansion` injecting via `additionalContext`; per-agent slash-command equivalents generated from the registry for Gemini/Qwen/Codex). LAYER 2 is the §11.4.109 anti-forgetting upgrade for prompt prefixes.
  - Grammar, all hold: (1) anchored at the start of the first non-blank line ONLY; mid-prose tokens never match; (2) UPPERCASE-only token `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*`; (3) separator exactly `" :: "`; (4) stacked prefixes (`A :: B :: rest`) apply outer-to-inner, left-to-right; (5) a leading `\` escapes the prefix (literal, no expansion); (6) an unknown token matching the grammar shape but NOT registered is NEVER silently expanded or dropped - the agent asks which registered action was meant (§11.4.66 + §11.4.105) or treats it literally, and NEVER invents an expansion (§11.4.6); (7) any non-conforming prompt is ordinary (no-op).
  - GRAMMAR_ADDENDUM: four further equivalent forms are recognised: `PREFIX::ACTION_NAME :: <rest>` (namespaced), `/ACTION_NAME <rest>` (bare slash), `/PREFIX::ACTION_NAME <rest>` (namespaced slash), `ACTION_NAME ---> <rest>` (bare arrow) with namespaced `PREFIX::ACTION_NAME ---> <rest>`; PREFIX is an action NAMESPACE (reserved default `DEFAULT`); the namespace separator `::` carries NO surrounding spaces (distinct from the action-body `" :: "` and arrow-body `" ---> "`, each with one ASCII space either side). The bare slash form yields to a colliding built-in/host slash command; the namespaced slash form is always unambiguous. A leading `\` escapes any form (`\BACKGROUND :: x`, `\BACKGROUND ---> x`, `\/BACKGROUND x`).
  - Registry is the single source of truth; adding an action = adding ONE `actions[]` row (`name`, `version`, `summary` >= 6 words per §11.4.91, `expansion`, optional `rules` + `composes_with`) with no code change in either layer. Both layers read the same file.
  - Registered entries: `BACKGROUND` (operator's verbatim expansion: "The following prompt that we will provide MUST BE executed in background in parallel with all main work streams using the subagents-driven development approach! All work done MUST PRODUCE rock solid evidence covered with hard physical proof(s) that all done is working as expected and as specified without any false results and without any bluff!"; composes §11.4.20/.70/.58/.103/.89/.5/.69/.107 + §11.4). `REMINDER` re-surfaces scheduled CRITICAL status-UNCERTAIN work: FIRST verify the actual current status from captured evidence (never assume, §11.4.6), THEN act on the delta (report proof if complete, resume from the exact point if partial, action NOW if not started, or surface the block per §11.4.66/§11.4.101), ALWAYS producing a status verdict; composes §11.4.6/.87/.94/.97/.103/.108/.130/.147. Severity markers `CRITICAL` (highest priority/potentially release-blocking; maximum urgency and rigor ahead of lower-priority work; track it; auto-activate §11.4.102 when an issue is involved), `IMPORTANT` (high priority, below CRITICAL), `NOTE` (capture the remainder as durable CONTEXT via request-history §11.4.208/§11.4.210 + persistent memory when a non-obvious project fact; not an urgent action unless it contains an explicit action; record only what the note says, §11.4.6); each supports all six §11.4.140 forms incl. single-colon `CRITICAL:`/`IMPORTANT:`/`NOTE:`; registering NOTE promotes `NOTE:` from ordinary-prose no-op to a registered action. They tag HOW the remainder is handled, not a workable-item Type (§11.4.16).
  - Decoupled and reusable (§11.4.28): registry + hook + expander carry zero project-specific data and are consumed by reference (the §11.4.80 pattern); a consuming project ships its own registry or inherits the default. Loads out-of-the-box via the §11.4.75 install seam.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-140-PROPAGATION, CM-ACTION-PREFIX-SYSTEM
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-action-prefix, --ignore-prefix, --no-registry, --invent-expansion-OK, --single-layer-only
- **Honest boundary:** Transparent mechanical free-form `^PREFIX ::` interception is genuinely available ONLY on Claude Code today; on other agents the free-form form is honoured by LAYER 1 (agent self-applies) and the slash-command equivalent is the mechanical convenience; the split is documented, never papered over (§11.4.3/§11.4.6). Gate-code is a separate work item.
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.17, §11.4.20, §11.4.28, §11.4.35, §11.4.58, §11.4.66, §11.4.69, §11.4.70, §11.4.75, §11.4.80, §11.4.89, §11.4.91, §11.4.93, §11.4.103, §11.4.105, §11.4.107, §11.4.109

#### §11.4.141 — Token-efficiency mandate
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1503-1531
- **Rules:**
  - Operator mandate: cut AI-agent token spend to 30-40% of current (a 60-70% reduction) WITHOUT degrading quality, performance or safety and WITHOUT breaking any existing mechanism. Every project worked on by AI agents MUST adopt the regime below and MUST PROVE the reduction with a measured anti-bluff harness, never an asserted number (§11.4.6/§11.4.123). The 60-70% is the warm-cache target; the rule requires the measured best-safe reduction with cited evidence.
  - M1 (primary): prompt-cache the static governance prefix. Always-loaded governance MUST form a byte-stable prefix with a cache breakpoint at its end and nothing volatile rendered ahead of it. Caching is transparent (cannot remove a rule or change a verdict; changes only billing); the only failure is a silent invalidator (timestamp/UUID/unsorted-JSON ahead of the breakpoint), detectable via `cache_read_input_tokens`. Operative discipline: batch governance edits and keep CLAUDE.md + the constitution byte-stable mid-session (every governance edit busts the cache). SDK callers use `cache_control:{type:"ephemeral"}`; Gemini/Qwen use their context cache via API-key auth.
  - M2 (secondary): subagent model-tiering + output-to-file. Route MECHANICAL, NON-JUDGMENT subagent work (search, grep, status, doc-export, file-presence, read-only probes) to a cheaper/smaller model (Haiku-class); RESERVE the strong model for ALL reasoning, fix-design (§11.4.102), verdicts, code-review (§11.4.125), demotion-evidence (§11.4.7). Subagents persist large output to a file and return a pointer instead of a 350-520K-token inline transcript. The strong model owns every decision and PASS/FAIL; the cheap model never emits a verdict. Bounded by §12.6 and the §11.4.58/§11.4.103 stream caps.
  - M3: thin always-loaded INDEX + on-demand detail. The always-loaded file is a concise index (one line per fix/anchor), full bodies fetched on demand. Invariants: (a) each index line carries the literal `11.4.N` anchor token so propagation scans pass; (b) canonical full text stays in the tracked gate-scanned `constitution/Constitution.md` - de-duplicated, never deleted; (c) the full body is reachable in one hop.
  - M4: retrieval/CodeGraph-first over full-file loading (structural questions -> CodeGraph §11.4.78/.79 or semantic search; region questions -> grep-scoped read; never re-read a harness-tracked file).
  - M5: output-token reduction - terse conductor status (no restatement of unchanged governance); `effort:"low"` on the mechanical-subagent allowlist only; structured output where a sink consumes it. Presentation-only; captured-evidence artefacts unchanged.
  - M6: tool-call efficiency - batch independent calls, reuse harness-tracked file state and persisted tool outputs.
  - M7: compaction/context-editing for long sessions - prune stale tool-results/old thinking; never touches the governance prefix or on-disk evidence.
  - Mandatory measured proof: a token-accounting harness measuring tokens per development cycle BEFORE vs AFTER on a frozen deterministic workload, split into `input_tokens` / `cache_read_input_tokens` / `cache_creation_input_tokens` / `output_tokens` from the authoritative Anthropic `usage` object (NEVER tiktoken; NEVER client-side `total_cost_usd` - recompute cost from raw fields with published prices), reproduced N times to identical verdict (§11.4.50). Pass = AFTER <= 40% of BEFORE OR the measured best-safe reduction with a cited cold-cache reason. The AFTER run MUST ALSO show ZERO regression on the pre-build full sweep, the meta-test mutation sweep (every gate still FAILs its paired mutation), every propagation gate, a strong-model reasoning-path probe (M2/M5 tiered nothing that decides), and a cache-warm proof (`cache_read_input_tokens > 0`). Cost reduction with quality/safety regression is a §11.4 FAIL.
  - No measure may break or degrade any existing mechanism: §11.4 covenant family, §11.4.50, §11.4.125, §11.4.40 and the §12.6 memory ceiling are unconditionally preserved.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies model IDs, mechanical-subagent allowlist, governance files, structural-index tool and frozen workload per §11.4.35. Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-141-PROPAGATION, CM-TOKEN-EFFICIENCY
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-token-efficiency, --no-cache-governance, --assert-reduction-without-measuring, --tier-down-reasoning, --inline-all-governance, --tiktoken-estimate-OK
- **Honest boundary:** The headline 60-70% is a warm-cache target; the rule requires the measured reduction. Gate-code is a separate work item. Research/design/measurement docs live at `docs/research/token_efficiency/{RESEARCH,DESIGN,MEASUREMENT,TEST_PLAN}.md`.
- **Composes:** §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.20, §11.4.40, §11.4.50, §11.4.58, §11.4.69, §11.4.70, §11.4.78, §11.4.79, §11.4.80, §11.4.103, §11.4.106, §11.4.123, §11.4.125, §11.4.128, §12.6, §1.1, §11.4.7, §11.4.102, §11.4.35, §11.4.17
- **Review addendum:** Recommended-gate mutation: inject a per-turn volatile token ahead of the governance cache breakpoint; `cache_read_input_tokens` collapses and the gate FAILs. Stated prices: cache read about 0.1x, cache write 1.25x (5-minute TTL) or 2x (1-hour), output about 5x input.

#### §11.4.156 — All CI/CD automation (GitHub Actions / GitLab pipelines / equivalents) MUST be disabled
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1533-1547
- **Rules:**
  - Every governed repository (main repo, constitution submodule, every owned and nested submodule we author and push) MUST ship with ALL server-side CI/CD DISABLED. No push to any owned upstream may trigger a GitHub Actions run, GitLab pipeline, or equivalent (Jenkins, CircleCI, Travis, Drone, Woodpecker, Bitbucket Pipelines, Azure Pipelines, any `on: push`/`schedule`/`workflow_dispatch` workflow). Generalises and makes ABSOLUTE the §11.4.75 Layer-5 posture; enforcement migrates to the LOCAL §11.4.75 five-layer git-hook ritual + the §11.4.40 pre-tag sweep, never a remote runner.
  - (A) Zero active CI at the repository root: no active `.github/workflows/*.yml|*.yaml`, no `.gitlab-ci.yml`, no `.gitlab/**` pipeline include, nor equivalent provider config at the ROOT of any governed repo/submodule.
  - (B) Disabled means a push triggers ZERO runs: delete the config OR rename it to a non-active name (the §11.4.75 `.disabled` / `.disabled-local-only` convention). A workflow with live `on:` triggers but `if: false` jobs still queues runs and is NOT compliant.
  - (C) Scope = repositories we author + push. Vendored/third-party source whose nested `.github/workflows` or `.gitlab-ci.yml` sit BELOW the repo root (AOSP `external/**`, `prebuilts/**`, `packages/modules/**`, vendored submodules) are INERT, OUT of scope, and MUST NOT be mass-edited (§11.4.29 vendor exemption). Test: "does a push to one of OUR upstreams trigger a run?" - yes => disable; structurally inert => document + leave (verify inertness as FACT, §11.4.6).
  - (D) No new CI may be added; introducing any active workflow/pipeline into a governed repo is a release blocker.
  - (E) Pre-push verification: before any push verify no root-level active CI exists (`git ls-files | grep -E '^\.github/workflows/.*\.ya?ml$|^\.gitlab-ci\.yml$'` returns empty for authored repos); a §11.4.109-class PreToolUse guard + the recommended gate enforce this.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies its repo/submodule set + provider list per §11.4.35. Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-156-PROPAGATION, CM-NO-ACTIVE-CI
- **No escape hatch:** --allow-ci, --enable-workflow, --keep-pipeline, --remote-ci-OK, --ci-exempt
- **Honest boundary:** File-level disabling stops FILE-triggered runs only; provider-side server settings the agent cannot reach (org-default required workflows, branch-protection required checks, scheduled exports) MUST be disabled in provider settings by the operator, and the agent documents what it cannot reach rather than claiming completeness. Gate-code is a separate work item.
- **Composes:** §11.4.75, §11.4.29, §11.4.6, §11.4.40, §11.4.42, §11.4.109, §11.4.113, §2.1, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.157 — GEMINI.md maintained in lockstep with CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / QWEN.md
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1549-1563
- **Rules:**
  - `GEMINI.md` is a FIRST-CLASS governance context carrier, EQUAL to CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / QWEN.md, never optional or best-effort. Every governance addition or edit MUST land in ALL FIVE carriers in lockstep (canonical `Constitution.md` + CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md + QWEN.md + GEMINI.md, plus any other per-agent context file a runtime introduces) in the SAME change-window, each with synchronized `.html`/`.pdf`/`.docx` exports per §11.4.65.
  - (A) Five-carrier lockstep: no governance change is complete until GEMINI.md carries it; GEMINI.md is added explicitly to the §11.4.26 pipeline's stage-2 propagation set and stage-3 cross-reference validation.
  - (B) No silent drift: a GEMINI.md whose highest rule number lags the other mirrors is a §11.4.157 violation (same severity class as a §11.4.65 stale-export drift); the gap MUST be back-filled.
  - (C) Equal status, equal rules: GEMINI.md restates the SAME literal `11.4.N` anchors the propagation gates require (§11.4.35), so the propagation-gate fleet count INCLUDES GEMINI.md.
  - (D) Consumer projects too: the lockstep binds the consumer's repo-root CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/QWEN.md/GEMINI.md per §11.4.35; a project maintaining the other three but not GEMINI.md is non-compliant.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-157-PROPAGATION, CM-GEMINI-MD-LOCKSTEP
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-gemini-md, --gemini-optional, --gemini-lag-OK, --four-carrier-suffices
- **Honest boundary:** The pre-existing §11.4.142-§11.4.155 GEMINI.md back-fill is a tracked remediation unit; this rule makes the drift a release-blocking debt, and claiming GEMINI.md is "in sync" while the back-fill is incomplete is itself a §11.4.157 violation. Gate-code is a separate work item.
- **Composes:** §11.4.26, §11.4.35, §11.4.17, §11.4.44, §11.4.65, §11.4.140, §11.4.156, §1.1, §11.4.6

#### §11.4.161 — Rootless container runtime mandate
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1565-1581
- **Rules:**
  - Every project MUST use Podman in rootless mode (or an equivalent rootless runtime) for ALL containerized workloads. Docker in rootful mode, `sudo`, or any escalation to root for container management is STRICTLY FORBIDDEN unless the target platform genuinely has no rootless option AND that constraint is documented per §11.4.112 (structurally-impossible, with cited authoritative sources).
  - The `vasic-digital/containers` Submodule (§11.4.76) MUST be the SOLE container orchestration layer: every container operation goes through its `pkg/boot` / `pkg/compose` / `pkg/health` primitives. No ad-hoc `docker`/`podman` commands outside the Submodule; a missing capability MUST be extended in the Submodule upstream (§11.4.74), not worked around with a raw command.
  - On-demand-infra invariant (refines §11.4.76): all container integration tests MUST boot infra on-demand via the Submodule (`pkg/boot` is the test entrypoint), not depend on a pre-running daemon or operator-side manual `podman machine start`. Operators are NEVER required to start `podman machine` / `docker compose up` / `podman-compose up` manually. A test claiming to exercise containerized components while silently depending on an already-running daemon is a §11.4 PASS-bluff at the test-infrastructure layer.
  - A platform that genuinely lacks rootless containers is documented per §11.4.112 and uses the Submodule's rootful mode with a documented extra risk acceptance - never ad-hoc rootful Docker.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies its rootless runtime, containers-Submodule integration and any platform constraint documentation per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-161-PROPAGATION, CM-ROOTLESS-CONTAINER-RUNTIME
- **No escape hatch:** --allow-rootful, --sudo-container-OK, --ad-hoc-docker-permitted, --no-containers-submodule, --pre-started-daemon-OK
- **Honest boundary:** Rootless execution removes the container-to-root escalation vector only; it does NOT replace §11.4.10 credentials handling (leak audit and .gitignore still apply) nor §12.3 container hygiene (memory limits, OOM policy, restart backoff). "The platform probably has rootless" is not a finding (§11.4.6). Gate-code is a separate work item.
- **Composes:** §11.4.76, §11.4.74, §11.4.10, §11.4.112, §12.3, §11.4.6, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.164 — Universal Constitution Auto-Propagation & Hook System
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1583-1609
- **Rules:**
  - Every fetch+pull of the constitution submodule MUST trigger an automatic post-update hook that installs/registers newly added or modified components, making the pull a COMPLETE governance-update transaction. Canonical hook: `constitution/scripts/post_update_hook.sh`, inherited by reference (§11.4.28), NEVER copied.
  - (a) Change detection: detect changed constitution files (`Constitution.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `QWEN.md`, `GEMINI.md`, and any file under `scripts/`, `hooks/`, `skills/`, `mcp/`, `plugins/`) by comparing HEAD before vs after via `git diff --name-only HEAD@{1} HEAD` (or the merge/pull equivalent).
  - (b) Skill registration: for any new/modified file under `skills/`, install/register it with the CLI agent's skill system (§11.4.102(B)); the hook invokes a consumer-provided script at the canonical path `scripts/register_skills.sh`.
  - (c) MCP registration: for any new/modified file under `mcp/`, register the MCP server with the agent's MCP config (e.g. `.mcp.json` or `settings.json`) via the consumer-provided `scripts/register_mcp.sh`.
  - (d) Hook installation: for any new/modified file under `hooks/`, install into `.git/hooks/` or the runtime hooks directory and make executable; an existing same-name hook is overwritten only if the new file's mtime is newer (§11.4.122 safe default - never overwrite a consumer's custom hook without a newer upstream version).
  - (e) Script validation: for any new/modified file under `scripts/`, (i) make executable, (ii) validate syntax - `sh -n` for POSIX-sh, `bash -n` for bash (§11.4.67), (iii) validate any `helix-deps.yaml` or `.gitignore-meta/` entries per §11.4.31/§11.4.77.
  - (f) Summary report: emit counts of skills registered, MCP servers registered, hooks installed, scripts made executable and validated, to stdout AND `.constitution/state/last_update.log` (gitignored per §11.4.30).
  - (g) Graceful failure: if any component installation fails, log per §11.4.6 with exact file:line and continue with the rest; one failure does not abort the transaction; failures appear in the summary and are findings for §11.4.102.
  - (h) Anti-bluff: the hook is tested by a paired §1.1 mutation that adds/removes a skill in the constitution submodule, pulls, and asserts the hook detects the change; a hook reporting "nothing to install" when a new skill was added is a §11.4 PASS-bluff.
  - Consumer obligation: every project that fetches/pulls the constitution MUST invoke the post-update hook after the fetch (project-defined per §11.4.35: a `post-update` git hook via `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`, or a post-pull script calling `constitution/scripts/post_update_hook.sh`). Not invoking it is non-compliance.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies skill-registration script, MCP-registration script, hook-installation mechanism and post-pull invocation method per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-164-PROPAGATION, CM-CONSTITUTION-AUTO-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** The hook installs/registers components but does NOT guarantee the consumer runtime accepts them (incompatible MCP deps, skill runtime version) and does NOT replace the §11.4.32 post-constitution-pull validation sweep. Installation failures not investigated are the finding §11.4.102 captures. Gate-code is a separate work item.
- **Composes:** §11.4.28, §11.4.32, §11.4.35, §11.4.67, §11.4.77, §11.4.102(B), §11.4.122, §11.4.31, §11.4.30, §11.4.6, §11.4.17, §1.1

#### §11.4.173 — Containerized + distributed build mandate
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1613-1613
- **Rules:**
  - EVERY build of EVERY component (source compile, artifact/package/installer/container-image production, codegen, asset render - any language/platform) MUST run INSIDE a specialized build container provisioned via the `digital.vasic.containers` submodule (§11.4.76), NEVER on the bare host.
  - Build containers MUST be DISTRIBUTED to the designated remote build host(s) (e.g. `thinker.local`) via the SAME containers-submodule distribution mechanism the infra uses (§11.4.76 Distributor / remote compose over SSH, §11.4.161 rootless), so the build EXECUTES remotely; on completion the produced artifacts MUST be brought BACK to the originating main host (scp/rsync/volume copy).
  - Building outside a container, or on the bare host, is FORBIDDEN - a release blocker.
  - Build-host target + build-container definitions are config-injected (§11.4.28), never hardcoded in the submodule; a missing build-container capability is added by EXTENDING the containers submodule upstream (§11.4.74), never by an ad-hoc host build.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-173-PROPAGATION, CM-CONTAINERIZED-DISTRIBUTED-BUILD
- **No escape hatch:** --build-on-host, --skip-container-build, --local-build-ok, --no-distributed-build, --bare-host-build
- **Honest boundary:** Guarantees reproducibility, host-isolation and capacity offload; does NOT replace the §11.4.40 full-suite retest, §11.4.108 four-layer artifact->runtime verification, or §11.4.38 installable-asset evidence, which still run against the brought-back artifact.
- **Composes:** §11.4.76, §11.4.161, §11.4.74, §11.4.28, §11.4.24, §11.4.82, §11.4.121, §11.4.38, §11.4.108, §12.6, §11.4.6, §11.4.40, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.177 — Developer-tooling project-decoupling + invocation-directory operation
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1615-1615
- **Rules:**
  - No project-specific script, hook, alias or binary may be wired (copied, symlinked, PATH-exported or aliased) into a global or shared developer-tooling PATH.
  - Shared tooling MUST be project-agnostic and operate on the INVOCATION directory (cwd, or an explicit path/config argument), NEVER on a hardcoded project path.
  - A project-specific helper lives in and runs from its own repo; a reusable helper is promoted to the shared toolkit ONLY after being stripped of every project-specific assumption (paths, device serials, package names, region endpoints) and taking its target from the invocation context.
  - A project script reachable on the global/shared PATH is a decoupling violation of equal severity to importing project-specific code into a shared submodule (§11.4.28).
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies concrete tool paths + invocation-config mechanism per §11.4.35. Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-177-PROPAGATION, CM-TOOLING-PROJECT-DECOUPLED
- **No escape hatch:** --global-symlink-ok, --hardcode-project-path, --wire-into-shared-path
- **Honest boundary:** Decoupling guarantees project-agnosticism, not correctness; the tool still needs its own tests. Gate-code is a separate work item.
- **Composes:** §11.4.28, §11.4.29, §11.4.35, §11.4.11, §11.4.6, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.184 — Mandatory SonarQube static-analysis CLI + local tooling installed and PATH-discoverable
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1617-1617
- **Rules:**
  - Every project/host that runs static analysis MUST have the SonarQube scanner CLI (`sonar-scanner`) installed AND durably discoverable on the system PATH via the shell rc (`.bashrc`/`.zshrc`), like the Firebase/GitHub/GitLab CLIs, PLUS the shared `constitution/scripts/sonarqube/` tooling (`sonarqube_install_check.sh`, `sonarqube_lib.sh`, `sonarqube_run_scan.sh`, `sonarqube_container.sh`, `compose/`) consumed BY REFERENCE (§11.4.28/§11.4.177/§11.4.80-style, NEVER copied per project).
  - (1) Installed + PATH-durable: the scanner CLI resolves in every fresh shell (a durable rc export, e.g. a generic `Factory/software/*/bin` glob or explicit line, not an ephemeral session PATH).
  - (2) Shared tooling present + GREEN: `sonarqube_install_check.sh` exits 0 (scanner + rootless podman per §11.4.161 + podman-compose + curl + ES-ready host `vm.max_map_count`) before any scan-dependent work.
  - (3) Anti-bluff: "installed/configured" is PROVEN by `command -v sonar-scanner` resolving AND the install-check exit 0, never assumed; a claimed-installed-but-absent CLI is a §11.4 bluff.
  - (4) Rootless (§11.4.161): the local SonarQube server runs via rootless podman through the container tooling, never rootful docker/sudo.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies install path + rc-export mechanism per §11.4.35. Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-184-PROPAGATION, CM-SONARQUBE-CLI-INSTALLED
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-sonarqube-install, --sonar-cli-optional, --ad-hoc-sonar-path, --rootful-sonar-OK
- **Honest boundary:** Names the scanner CLI + shared local-server tooling; the former Semgrep mandate (§11.4.166) stays REPEALED and this is a DISTINCT operator-mandated tool. Mandates TOOLING availability, not a scan on every build. Gate-code is a separate work item.
- **Composes:** §11.4.28, §11.4.36, §11.4.74, §11.4.75, §11.4.109, §11.4.161, §11.4.166, §11.4.177, §11.4.6

#### §11.4.184(I) — HawkScan (DAST) + OWASP ZAP + gitleaks + Trivy: mandatory local security-tooling extension
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1619-1634
- **Rules:**
  - Every project/host that runs security scanning MUST have four additional tools installed and locally runnable through the constitution's `scripts/<tool>/` tree, mirroring the `scripts/sonarqube/` five-file structure: `<tool>_lib.sh` (sourced, never executed), `<tool>_install_check.sh` (three-tier presence/version verifier), `<tool>_container.sh` (rootless-podman lifecycle where a local server is needed), `<tool>_run_scan.sh` (drives the scan, polls for completion, writes a Markdown report to `qa-results/<tool>/<ts>/`, never printing secrets), `compose/docker-compose.<tool>.yml` for containerized tools. Consumed BY REFERENCE, never copied (§11.4.28/§11.4.80).
  - gitleaks (secrets scanner): fully open-source, no account, runs locally with no network callout; installable via package manager or upstream release binary; complements and does NOT replace or conflict with the constitution's `credential_scan_lib.sh` pre-commit-hook detector - both run.
  - Trivy (dependency/container/IaC vulnerability scanner): fully open-source, no account, local against filesystem/image/repo, no network callout beyond its own vulnerability-DB pull (cacheable, refreshable offline).
  - OWASP ZAP (DAST): fully open-source, no account, runs as a local rootless-podman container (`zaproxy/zap-stable`, §11.4.161) against a locally reachable target, no external SaaS dependency.
  - HawkScan (DAST, StackHawk): the one SaaS-backed tool; image `docker.io/stackhawk/hawkscan` always authenticates against StackHawk's backend. Setup has an unavoidable manual operator-only component (free-tier signup at `app.stackhawk.com` + one "Application" per scanned project to obtain an `applicationId`). `scripts/hawkscan/run.sh` MUST fail OPEN, never closed: with no `HAWK_API_KEY` set, or the placeholder `applicationId` present, it prints a clear loud non-blocking warning and exits 0. A missing third-party credential is an operator setup gap, never a build/gate failure.
  - Key-acquisition guides for tools needing one (today HawkScan only) live at `scripts/hawkscan/README.md` and propagate with the scripts.
  - None of the four is declared in `helix-deps.yaml` (§11.4.31 schema is for git-clonable source dependencies); presence/configuration is governed by this clause plus the install-check scripts. Semgrep is deliberately NOT added; §11.4.166's repeal stands.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker for gitleaks, Trivy and ZAP; HawkScan's bar is "correctly scaffolded with a fail-open credential guard", never "scanned", until an operator completes the two manual steps.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-184-PROPAGATION (continues to cover; no new anchor number), CM-GITLEAKS-INSTALLED, CM-TRIVY-INSTALLED, CM-ZAP-CONTAINER-AVAILABLE, CM-HAWKSCAN-SCAFFOLDED
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-gitleaks, --trivy-optional, --zap-off, --hawkscan-required
- **Honest boundary:** Mandates tooling presence and local runnability only; does NOT run a scan, claim any project scanned, or claim findings triaged. HawkScan can never be claimed "configured" by an agent alone; a project without the account/Application MUST show the non-blocking warning, never a fabricated pass. For HawkScan "scaffolded" means the runner correctly detects/reports missing credentials. Gate-code is a separate work item, not claimed shipped.
- **Composes:** §11.4.184, §11.4.166, §11.4.31, §11.4.28, §11.4.80, §11.4.161, §11.4.10, §11.4.6, §11.4.227

#### §11.4.196 — Native-alias-first priority + per-alias real-signal limit/subscription tracking + auto-rebind-on-recovery + resource-detection-by-real-identity
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1637-1645
- **Rules:**
  - The multi-track alias-binding + rate-limit/subscription-tracking layer of the §11.4.187 ruler MUST implement ALL of (A)-(E): use ALL operational claude-NATIVE aliases FIRST (not session-limited, not weekly-limit-reached, not expired-subscription) before ANY provider alias; track limits/subscription from REAL signals (never faked, §11.4.6); rebind upward when a higher-priority native recovers; fix the `pgrep -f` substring-match guard footgun.
  - (A) NATIVE-ALIAS-FIRST: every OPERATIONAL native (`claudeN`) alias is selected before ANY provider alias, UNCONDITIONALLY while >=1 native is operational. The guarantee is STRUCTURAL: a native/provider CLASS partition scanned native-class-completely-before-provider-class (§11.4.111 resolve-by-CLASS), so a provider can NEVER win while a non-cooled native exists regardless of roster file order. Within a class the operator order (native equal-capability, then providers deepseek->xiaomi->opencode->kimi->...) is authoritative decision-DATA (§11.4.28), never re-invented.
  - (B) PER-ALIAS REAL-SIGNAL TRACKING: operational state from REAL captured signals: the §11.4.187 429 signature (`isApiErrorMessage`+`apiErrorStatus:429` / `api_error_status:429`) sub-classified into closed reason-CLASS set `{session | weekly | subscription}` from real message markers; each limited alias records its CLASS + operational-again EPOCH with DIFFERENT windows - session (self-heals at reset, short), weekly (until weekly reset, long), subscription (INDEFINITE: operational-again UNKNOWN until a REAL renewal signal, parked with a far-future sentinel; NEVER guess a renewal date - operator/config supplies it). A limited alias is NEVER auto-selected until its epoch passes (session/weekly) or an explicit renewal/recovery signal clears it (subscription).
  - (C) AUTO-USE-ON-RECOVERY: when a higher-priority native recovers, rebind tracks UPWARD (`promote`-class operation keyed off a comparable priority-rank: native class before provider, then config order), PRESERVING each track's worktree AND device leases (leases key on the STABLE track id; §11.4.119/§11.4.187). Idempotent - a track already on the best operational alias is untouched.
  - (D) RESOURCE-DETECTION BY REAL IDENTITY: a host-safety "heavy work in flight" guard MUST identify a real resource (heavy build, live worker) by its ACTUAL command line read from the OS (`/proc/<pid>/cmdline`), NEVER by a bare `pgrep -f REGEX` substring match that false-matches a process merely MENTIONING a token: a pattern-CARRIER (args quoting the alternation pattern; a worker whose prompt embeds the token; a launcher/monitor/test), a same-tool ENGINE process, or the guard's own process/parent (§12.12 self/sibling footgun). The guard re-reads each matched PID's real cmdline and excludes carrier/engine/worker/self classes; an UNREADABLE/vanished cmdline is conservatively counted as the real resource (REFUSE - safe reversible default, §11.4.101/§12.8).
  - (E) ANTI-BLUFF: every piece carries four-layer coverage (pre-build gate + on-host test + paired §1.1 mutation + captured evidence §11.4.69), each with a §11.4.115 RED-polarity reproduction on the pre-fix artifact + §11.4.50 determinism.
  - (F) CONFIGURED != IN USE (extension): (1) EVERY worker/agent spawn path MUST bind THROUGH the orchestrator (the §11.4.187 launcher); a worker started outside it is UNMANAGED (never rebound on recovery, never rate-limit-tracked, never counted against the host budget) and is a §11.4.196 violation; (2) readiness is defined by RUNTIME SIGNATURE (§11.4.108), not configuration: the set of binding-registry rows MUST EQUAL the set of live workers (each live worker appears with its bound alias; each row corresponds to a live-or-honestly-terminal worker); an empty/partial registry alongside live workers is FALSE-READY; (3) claiming "ready"/"in use" from a valid config + installed script WITHOUT captured registry<->live-worker equality is a §11.4/§11.4.6 bluff; (4) `CM-ALIAS-PRIORITY-LIMIT-TRACKING` ALSO asserts that equality, with a paired mutation (leave a live worker unregistered -> gate FAILs).
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-196-PROPAGATION, CM-ALIAS-PRIORITY-LIMIT-TRACKING
- **No escape hatch:** --provider-before-operational-native, --fake-limit-state, --guess-renewal-date, --no-rebind-on-recovery, --substring-match-build-guard, --skip-real-signal-classification
- **Honest boundary:** Mandates the MECHANISM + REAL-signal derivation of "operational"; genuine live per-subscription quota-isolation proof requires live tokens in an operator-scheduled acceptance window, never conflated with a mock/hermetic-contract GREEN. Gate-code for the recommended gate is a separate work item.
- **Composes:** §11.4.187, §11.4.182, §11.4.176, §11.4.111, §11.4.101, §11.4.103, §11.4.6, §11.4.108, §11.4.115, §11.4.119, §12.12, §12.6, §12.8, §11.4.198, §11.4.147, §11.4.28, §11.4.50, §11.4.69, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.197 — Research / kicked-off-work completion mandate
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1647-1667
- **Rules:**
