  - Every research effort, kicked-off improvement, design doc, spike, prototype, PoC or partially-landed feature a project STARTS MUST be driven to FULL completion OR explicitly evidence-backed CLOSED. There is no third "sitting un-wired in the backlog" state; "we researched/designed/started it" is never terminal. A `docs/research/*` doc, design doc, spike branch or half-wired feature neither COMPLETED-and-wired nor explicitly closed is a violation (same class as a §11.4 PASS-bluff at the requirements-integrity layer). Loss of requirements and failure to incorporate started work are FORBIDDEN.
  - COMPLETED means ALL hold: (1) implemented; (2) WIRED - integrated AND used by default, not merely present behind a dead flag / uncalled function / unreferenced module / never-selected path (§11.4.124 dead-code gap + §11.4.108 layer-2/3 SOURCE->ARTIFACT->RUNTIME gap); (3) confirmed + validated + verified with captured physical evidence per §11.4.5/§11.4.69/§11.4.107 on a clean deployment per §11.4.108 runtime-signature, never metadata-only/config-only/absence-of-error/grep-without-runtime; (4) tracked to a terminal Status per §11.4.15/§11.4.33.
  - Explicitly CLOSED means deliberately terminated with a documented evidence-backed reason from the existing vocabulary: §11.4.90 `Obsolete` (superseded-by-design-change / superseded-by-later-mandate / duplicate-of / not-reproducible / feature-removed), §11.4.112 `structurally-impossible` (with cited proof), or §11.4.122 operator-confirmed drop - NEVER silent abandonment. "No time"/"lower priority" is `Operator-blocked` per §11.4.21 (with self-resolution-exhaustion audit) or a still-open tracked item, NOT a close.
  - Mechanical tracker binding (§11.4.93): every research effort/design doc/kicked-off improvement MUST map to at least one tracked workable item (ATM-NNN per §11.4.54) whose completion the loop enforces. A research doc with NO tracked implementing item, or a tracked item stalled un-wired past the project's cadence, is a violation. The autonomous loop (§11.4.87/.94/.97/.103/.126/.192) MUST treat every un-wired research effort as an actionable queue item.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies its research-doc tree path + tracker binding per §11.4.35. Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-197-PROPAGATION, CM-RESEARCH-COMPLETION-TRACKED
- **No escape hatch:** --research-may-stay-unwired, --skip-completion-tracking, --abandon-without-close, --present-but-unwired-is-done, --backlog-research-OK, --lose-requirement-OK
- **Honest boundary:** "Fully completed" is bounded by wired+verified OR evidence-backed closed; it does NOT mean every speculative idea must ship - every STARTED effort reaches a documented terminal state, proven never assumed. Gate-code is a separate work item.
- **Composes:** §11.4.8, §11.4.87, §11.4.94, §11.4.97, §11.4.103, §11.4.126, §11.4.192, §11.4.118, §11.4.123, §11.4.124, §11.4.150, §11.4.90, §11.4.112, §11.4.122, §11.4.21, §11.4.93, §11.4.54, §11.4.108, §11.4.15, §11.4.33, §11.4.5, §11.4.69, §11.4.107, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.198 — Default working mechanisms: multi-alias native-first orchestration AND heavy token-optimization are ALWAYS-ON defaults
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1669-1685
- **Rules:**
  - Two mechanisms are STANDING always-on defaults for EVERY configuration (single- OR multiple-agent; single- OR multi-track), never a per-request opt-in.
  - (A) Multi-alias native-first orchestration is the DEFAULT: every OPERATIONAL claude-NATIVE alias before ANY provider per §11.4.196 (priority + real-signal limit tracking + auto-rebind-on-recovery), driven by the §11.4.187 ruler, MUST be the default execution substrate for ALL work, not only multi-track. A single-track/single-agent session STILL binds its worker through the native-first alias-priority mechanism (best operational native + rebind on recovery); a multi-track/multi-agent config uses it across every track (§11.4.176 exactly-once claim + §11.4.182 track+branch+alias label). Running on an arbitrary/hardcoded/provider-first alias when an operational native exists, or bypassing alias-priority because "it is just one agent", is a violation.
  - (B) Heavy token-optimization is the DEFAULT: the §11.4.141 discipline (compact-in-CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md + full-one-hop-away anchor layout, targeted reads over whole-file dumps, subagent context isolation per §11.4.20/§11.4.70, evidence-hash references not evidence dumps) MUST be applied ALWAYS - every read, dispatch, doc edit - for single- AND multi-track work. Token-heavy patterns (re-reading whole large files when a slice suffices, dumping full evidence into context, monolithic non-subagent execution of parallelisable work) when a token-efficient path exists are violations.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-198-PROPAGATION, CM-DEFAULT-MECHANISMS-ALWAYS-ON
- **No escape hatch:** --single-agent-skips-alias-priority, --provider-first-default, --token-optimization-optional, --heavy-tokens-OK, --not-default-mechanism
- **Honest boundary:** "Default" means engaged automatically without an operator request; it does NOT weaken host-safety - fan-out stays under the §12.6 60% memory ceiling, §12.12 thread-headroom check and §11.4.58 parallel-agent cap (contending/redundant agents are not "using the default", §11.4.183). §11.4.198 BINDS the mechanisms as always-on; their mechanics live in §11.4.196/§11.4.187/§11.4.141. Gate-code is a separate work item.
- **Composes:** §11.4.141, §11.4.187, §11.4.196, §11.4.182, §11.4.176, §11.4.183, §11.4.103, §11.4.58, §11.4.20, §11.4.70, §11.4.126, §12.6, §12.12, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.227 — Governance-corpus self-custody: named-gate ledger ratchet + anchor-block integrity
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1687-1707
- **Rules:**
  - The rule corpus is bound by the same custody it imposes. Reason (measured 2026-07-22): 413 named CM-* gates, 241 (58%) with no implementation in either canonical gate site, plus 85 "gate-code = separate work item" deferrals; propagation gates asserting literal-presence >= 1 reward restatement over implementation (two anchor blocks duplicated divergently in all four mirrors while presence gates stayed green; the §11.4.140/§11.4.141 anchor-number collision).
  - (A) NAMED-GATE LEDGER + IMPLEMENTATION RATCHET: every `CM-*`-class gate token named anywhere in the governance corpus MUST, at every build (governance repo and every wired consumer), be either IMPLEMENTED (token present in an EXECUTABLE gate site; prose carriers NEVER count, §11.4.201(7)(a)) or covered by a REGISTERED DEFERRAL row pointing at a tracked work item (§11.4.197). Silent gate debt is refused at the build seam. The unimplemented count is a MONOTONE-DECREASING ratchet, validated per §11.4.201(8) against the definition of done (at the correct end-state the count is 0). A gate NAME that vanishes without an explicit removal citation FAILs (deleting names to lower the count is closed; repeals stay legal and visible, §11.4.166 pattern). An anchor's "done" state is its SEAM landing, not its TEXT landing. Brownfield adoption (ratchet down from measured baseline vs hard-fail day one) is an operator §11.4.66 decision mirroring §11.4.224(E), never an invented ratchet.
  - (B) ANCHOR-BLOCK INTEGRITY: every propagation-class gate MUST count anchor BLOCK-STARTS (structural line-anchored heading patterns), never bare literals: (i) exactly ONE block per anchor per governance file - 0 is absence, >1 is DUPLICATION; FAIL naming anchor and file; (ii) content-hash EQUALITY across the declared lockstep mirror set (§11.4.157) - divergent copies FAIL naming both files (compact-vs-full variance ACROSS layers, canonical vs mirror, remains legitimate; equality binds only within the lockstep set; canonical-vs-mirror semantic drift is §11.4.186's job); (iii) mid-body citations of an anchor literal are CARRIERS and never count (§11.4.201(7)(a)); (iv) ZERO blocks extracted from a governance file is BLIND-OR-EMPTY, never clean (§11.4.201(6)); (v) one anchor NUMBER heading two different mandates is a COLLISION and FAILs (§11.4.54 never-reuse applied to anchor ids); (vi) the extractor MUST capture full dotted ids so a sub-anchor (`...10.A`) never prefix-matches its parent (`...10`).
  - (C) Consolidation pressure: nothing mechanical decides semantic contradiction between two different anchors; only the decidable projections are mechanized (block counts, lockstep hashes, anchor numbers; fenced verdict scopes stay §11.4.112(5), seam declarations stay §11.4.120); the remainder is §11.4.142/§11.4.194 review territory. This adds the enforcement-ratio INSTRUMENT, not a growth ban; counterweights remain §11.4.17 classification, §11.4.141 token-efficiency and the §11.4.166 visible-repeal precedent.
  - Regular-cycle + review + pull binding: the ledger regenerates and diffs on every governance edit and every build (never on-demand); a change that NAMES a gate is review-checked for implementation-or-deferral per §11.4.194(6)(c); on every constitution fetch/pull the §11.4.32 post-pull sweep + the §11.4.164 hook run the ledger + block-integrity checks against the post-pull tree, with violations tracked (§11.4.15) and cleared - no parallel mechanism.
  - Reference mechanisms SOL-05 (gate ledger + ratchet) and SOL-06 (anchor-block integrity) under `docs/research/quality/solutions/` are RED-first POCs with golden fixtures, NOT wired, and carry no force until wired by separate tracked work items (§11.4.197/§11.4.205).
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumers (and this governance repo) supply gate-site list, deferral registry and lockstep mirror set as DATA per §11.4.35. Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-227-PROPAGATION (itself block-start-shaped per (B)), CM-GATE-LEDGER-RATCHET, CM-ANCHOR-BLOCK-INTEGRITY
- **No escape hatch:** --name-gate-without-seam, --silent-gate-debt-OK, --delete-name-to-lower-count, --presence-gte-1-suffices, --duplicate-anchor-OK, --mirror-drift-OK, --reuse-anchor-number
- **Honest boundary:** Semantic contradiction between anchors is stated as not mechanizable, only the decidable projections are; the SOL-05/SOL-06 POCs are proven but not wired. Gate-code for the recommended gates is a separate work item, NOT claimed shipped (§11.4.6).
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.15, §11.4.17, §11.4.32, §11.4.54, §11.4.66, §11.4.75, §11.4.141, §11.4.157, §11.4.164, §11.4.166, §11.4.186, §11.4.194(6), §11.4.197, §11.4.201, §11.4.205, §11.4.224(E), §11.4.112(5), §11.4.120, §11.4.140, §11.4.142

#### §11.4.228 — Cross-agent extension lifecycle: per-platform compatibility, source tracking, catalog with matrix, auto-wiring on constitution pull
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1709-1754
- **Rules:**
  - Reason (one clause): constitution skills existed in source but were un-wired to any platform ("docs say present, runtime says absent", the gap §11.4.108 forbids); 14 of 18 local skills had no origin record.
  - (A) Every governed extension (Skill, MCP server, ACP bridge, LSP, plugin, provider alias, embedding, daemon, any future class) MUST ship a per-platform compatibility declaration covering at minimum Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code.
  - (A)(1) Closed vocabulary per platform: SUPPORTED (verified with a recorded per-platform liveness probe), UNTESTED (present, not verified; tracked per §11.4.197), UNSUPPORTED (platform genuinely cannot load the class; per §11.4.112 with cited evidence), CONFIG-ONLY (declared in config, never verified as wired per §11.4.139).
  - (A)(2) An extension MUST NEVER cause loops, hangs, crashes or broken behavior in any platform that loads it; doing so is a violation of PASS-bluff severity.
  - (A)(3) Cross-platform liveness testing is mandatory (§11.4.169 closed test-type set): a per-platform liveness test (does the agent load it and produce correct output) on every declared-SUPPORTED platform at minimum. Infeasible platform (no runtime on host) = honest §11.4.3 SKIP-with-reason recorded in the declaration, NEVER a faked PASS.
  - (B)(1) Every extension MUST carry machine-readable provenance: origin repository URL, commit SHA (or tag+delta description when UNTRACED), canonical file path; stored in `EXTENSION_SOURCE.yaml` in the extension directory or a consumer-maintained registry. No provenance = UNTRACED and a tracked §11.4.197 item; never silently trusted.
  - (B)(2) Symlinks (or git submodule pointer, or reflink share) are preferred over copies. Where a copy is genuinely required, the SOURCE record MUST state canonical origin and why a copy was necessary. Blind copies without provenance are §11.4.124-class dead-code-in-waiting.
  - (B)(3) Every governed project MUST maintain an extensions catalog (`docs/extensions/EXTENSIONS_CATALOG.md` or equivalent declared per §11.4.35) listing every active extension, its source, per-platform compatibility status and last-verified timestamp. Catalog is §11.4.86 roster/corpus-backed (sha256 fingerprint of the sorted extension keyset, NOT mtime) and re-syncs on any extension change. Catalog is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH; ad-hoc per-agent skill directories without catalog entries are UNCATALOGUED and a tracked §11.4.197 item.
  - (C)(1) Catalog MUST carry a per-platform compatibility matrix (rows = extensions, columns = governed platforms, cells = clause (A)(1) vocabulary). A cell with no recorded status is UNTESTED by default, never assumed compatible.
  - (C)(2) Catalog MUST be maintained per §11.4.65 (four formats .md, .html, .pdf, .docx), updated on every extension add/change/removal, with §11.4.44 revision header.
  - (C)(3) Catalog MUST include per extension x platform liveliness evidence (load-ok / load-failed-for-reason / skip-with-reason) with timestamp and evidence path per §11.4.69 `feature_class=extension_loading`. A platform declared SUPPORTED with no recorded probe is UNTESTED overridden (a §11.4.6 violation).
  - (C)(4) Catalog auto-syncs via §11.4.106 docs-chain or equivalent; a stale catalog with extension drift is a PASS-bluff.
  - (D) The §11.4.164 `post_update_hook.sh` seam MUST be extended: after detecting changed extension artifacts in the constitution submodule it MUST do (D)(1)-(D)(6).
  - (D)(1) Detect all governed agent platforms on the host (Claude Code via `.claude/`, OpenCode via `.opencode/` or `opencode.json`, Gemini CLI via `~/.gemini/` or project `GEMINI.md`, Qwen Code via `.qwen/` or project `QWEN.md`); detection logic is consumer DATA per §11.4.35, never a hardcoded list. A platform with no detection mechanism = honest DETECTION_UNSUPPORTED gap recorded in the catalog, NOT a reason to skip other platforms.
  - (D)(2) Wire each constitution skill not already present into each detected platform: Claude Code symlink `.claude/skills/<skill-name>/` -> `constitution/skills/<skill-name>/`; OpenCode symlink `.opencode/skills/<skill-name>/` -> `constitution/skills/<skill-name>/`; Gemini CLI and Qwen Code per-platform equivalent (consumer DATA).
  - (D)(3) Register new/changed MCP servers into each platform's MCP configuration (`.mcp.json`, `opencode.json`, equivalents) via the existing §11.4.164 MCP-registration seam, applied to every detected platform.
  - (D)(4) Self-validate after wiring (platform `--list-skills`/`--list-extensions` equivalent, else filesystem check: directory present and parseable). A failed wiring is logged as a §11.4.32 post-pull finding, never silently absorbed.
  - (D)(5) The hook MUST be idempotent (no duplicate symlinks, no corrupted configs, no loss of non-constitution extensions) and every operation MUST be dry-run-capable.
  - (D)(6) Auto-wiring makes extensions REACHABLE; it does not guarantee runtime acceptance (honest UNTESTED/UNSUPPORTED gaps, never faked pass) nor correctness.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies platform detection, wiring commands, registry path, catalog path as DATA (§11.4.35).
  - Recommended gate behaviours: per-platform compat gate FAILs on a declared-SUPPORTED platform with no liveness probe; source-tracked gate FAILs on a blind copy without provenance; catalog gate FAILs on missing matrix, missing four-format export, stale sha256 fingerprint or drift; auto-wired gate FAILs on a constitution skill not wired into a detected SUPPORTED platform, with explicit DETECTION_UNSUPPORTED / UNSUPPORTED SKIP-with-reason as the §11.4.201(1) false-positive guard. All paired §1.1 mutations; gate-code = separate work item, NOT claimed shipped.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker regardless of context.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-228-PROPAGATION, CM-EXTENSION-PER-PLATFORM-COMPAT, CM-EXTENSION-SOURCE-TRACKED, CM-EXTENSION-CATALOG-DOCUMENTED, CM-CONSTITUTION-EXTENSIONS-AUTO-WIRED
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-per-platform-compat, --single-platform-OK, --extension-without-provenance, --copies-over-symlinks-OK, --skip-extension-catalog, --catalog-format-optional, --skip-auto-wire, --manual-wiring-suffices, --untraced-extensions-OK
- **Honest boundary:** Auto-wiring guarantees reachability only, not that each platform's runtime accepts the extension (different skill format, incompatible MCP protocol, missing runtime are recorded UNTESTED/UNSUPPORTED gaps) and not extension correctness (§11.4.108 and the extension's own tests still bind).
- **Composes:** §11.4.164, §11.4.157, §11.4.65, §11.4.86, §11.4.106, §11.4.69, §11.4.124, §11.4.3, §11.4.112, §11.4.139, §11.4.32, §11.4.108, §11.4.197, §11.4.169, §11.4.142, §11.4.194, §11.4.17, §11.4.35, §11.4.44, §11.4.6, §11.4.201, §1.1

#### §11.4.272 — Dynamic, on-demand skill/extension activation: active capability surface is the minimum needed now
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1756-1784
- **Rules:**
  - Reason: a host skill pool of 955 skills cost ~29,153 B (~7,288 tok, bytes/4 ESTIMATE) of names per turn, or 101,279 B (~25,319 tok) with descriptions (3.5x cliff the project does not control).
  - Every project whose agent platform exposes a capability surface (Agent Skills, plugins, extensions, tool sets) MUST keep the ACTIVE surface at the minimum genuinely needed, everything else activatable ON DEMAND; ALL of (A)-(H) hold.
  - (A) Consumer declares as DATA (§11.4.35) a small `core` set always active plus the pool it may draw from. Anything not core is inactive by default and activated only when a task needs it. An entry added to core is paid in every turn of every session and MUST earn that.
  - (B) A deactivated capability MUST remain FINDABLE: an always-available index lists the whole catalogue with active/inactive state. `superpowers:using-superpowers` (§11.4.102(B)) continues to bind unconditionally (if any skill could apply, even at 1% relevance, find it in the index and invoke it rather than improvise). Saving tokens by making a capability unfindable is FORBIDDEN.
  - (C) Fail safe, never silent (§11.4.201): a failed activation MUST tell the agent explicitly the capability is NOT available and exit non-zero. A dangling or unreadable activation MUST be rolled back.
  - (D) Concurrency-safe by reference counting (§11.4.119/§11.4.176): where sessions share a checkout, one session's deactivation MUST NOT strip a capability another session uses. Claims are reference-counted and released only when no other claimant is PROVEN live (§11.4.180 liveness, §11.4.174 ownership-verified); an unprovable holder is reported as such, never silently assumed dead OR alive.
  - (E) Honest asymmetry: build on the platform's PROVEN behaviour, not documented behaviour. Measured: activation hot-loads (appears in the running session without restart) but deactivation does NOT hot-unload (deleted skill still invokable from cache). Saving = minimal session-start baseline plus on-demand growth; claiming deactivation frees tokens in the live session is a bluff. The platform's `permissions.deny` `Skill(name)` rule blocks invocation but does NOT remove the entry from the rendered list (saves zero tokens); a first-party mechanism must be TESTED for the relied-on property (§11.4.74 satisfied by evidence).
  - (F) A budget gate MUST budget the active surface in BOTH the name-only and the description-eager render modes, so an upstream switch to eager rendering breaks a gate loudly.
  - (G) Both modes (REQ-NOTE-0001): engine lives in the constitution submodule (§11.4.28, by reference, never copied; §11.4.80/§11.4.177), but a project that does NOT vendor the submodule MUST still get a working command or an HONEST LOUD refusal, never a silent no-op. Resolution order: environment override, in-project submodule, any ancestor's, operator-configured host checkout, documented host fallback, then honest degradation naming WHAT is unavailable, WHY, WHERE it looked, WHAT still works. Degradation MUST use an exit code distinct from "operation failed" and MUST state the existing static capability set is untouched.
  - (H) Prune-to-core is the DEFAULT (operator decision 2026-09-07) and is NOT a §11.4.122 removal. Session initialisation MUST prune by default (demote every non-core capability) rather than merely raise core; raise-only satisfies (A) in letter and voids it in substance (measured: 19 active/422 B/~105 tok per turn vs 3 active/65 B/~16 tok).
  - (H) Pruning is not removal because by construction: (1) LISTED - catalogue index still shows every pruned capability; (2) ACTIVATABLE - one command returns it, hot-loading per (E); (3) NOT DELETED - link-style activation loses only the link; a capability whose only copy is in the active location is MOVED to a preserved store that is itself a searched source, zero bytes destroyed.
  - (H) A demotion that cannot be done safely MUST refuse LOUDLY and leave the capability ACTIVE per (C): another live session holds a claim per (D); preserved store already holds an entry of that name (never clobber, §9.2); the move fails or lands unreadable (REVERT); capability would not be re-activatable.
  - (H) Relocation MUST be relocation-safe: path-relative references inside it are re-pointed at the identical resolved target before the move; if insufficient, the post-move readability check refuses and reverts (§11.4.6).
  - (H) An explicit documented opt-out MUST exist at session scope (environment override) and project scope (manifest flag), session scope winning; the opt-out keeps the engine in play. Where the engine is unreachable (G), pruning inherits G's honest refusal; a session is NEVER left silently holding fewer capabilities than it believes.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies manifest, pool sources, preserved-store location, budget limits, opt-out names, host fallback as DATA.
  - Recommended gate behaviours: surface-budget gate (both render modes); activation-fail-safe gate (non-zero exit with explicit reason, nothing dangling); prune-preserves-content gate (after prune every demoted capability still LISTED, still ACTIVATABLE, content byte-identical; unsafe demotion refuses and leaves ACTIVE). Paired mutations: squeeze budget below real surface -> gate FAILs; break an activation target -> refuse, no dangling link; remove engine -> shim exits with its distinct engine-absent code, never 0; make demotion destructive / strip relocation-safety / strip other-live-session claim check -> prune gate FAILs. Gate-code beyond shipped scripts = separate work item, NOT claimed shipped.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-272-PROPAGATION, CM-SKILL-SURFACE-BUDGET, CM-SKILL-ACTIVATION-FAIL-SAFE, CM-SKILL-PRUNE-PRESERVES-CONTENT
- **No escape hatch:** --all-skills-always-on, --skip-activation-engine, --hide-inactive-skills, --silent-activation-failure, --ignore-surface-budget, --assume-skill-loaded
- **Honest boundary:** Reduces per-turn cost of the capability LIST only (not a skill body once invoked, which is already lazy); does not make any capability more correct; not a substitute for §11.4.102(B) discovery nor a licence to hide a needed capability.
  - Prune-by-default inherits (E)'s asymmetry: saving lands at the next session start for entries the platform already cached; prune runs AT session initialisation and its in-session effect is never overclaimed.
- **Composes:** §9.2, §11.4.6, §11.4.28, §11.4.35, §11.4.74, §11.4.80, §11.4.102(B), §11.4.119, §11.4.122, §11.4.141, §11.4.164, §11.4.174, §11.4.176, §11.4.177, §11.4.180, §11.4.201, §11.4.17, §11.4.227, §1.1

#### §11.4.273 — Measuring-instrument verification: a census that informs a decision must be control-needled before its result is believed
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1788-1826
- **Rules:**
  - Reason: fifteen ad-hoc measurements in one session returned plausible actionable results that were instrument artefacts (e.g. a census matching one of two block-opener forms manufactured 24 phantom dangling anchors; `$?` read after a pipeline or clobbered by a command substitution in the same statement; a denylist with two needles searched with one reported a live credential as eliminated; `comm` on numerically-sorted input; `grep -w` treating `-` as boundary; `while read` dropping a final line without newline; wrong env knob so the mutation tree was never loaded).
  - Gap closed: §11.4.201 governs blocking guards/gates and §11.4.107(10) analyzers; neither covers the ad-hoc census that INFORMS (grep, set difference, exit-code read, field lookup, row count) whose output is a FACT a decision is built upon.
  - Any measurement whose result will drive a decision, claim, classification or report MUST be control-needled BEFORE its result is acted on or communicated.
  - (a) POSITIVE control: a value KNOWN present must be found (catches pattern too narrow, wrong field name/path/knob, silently empty stage).
  - (b) NEGATIVE control: a fabricated value KNOWN absent must NOT be found (catches pattern too broad, substring/word-boundary match, default fabricating a hit).
  - (c) An EMPTY result is never a finding on its own: it may mean genuinely absent, instrument could not look, looked in the wrong place, or output shape differed; report only once (a) shows the instrument can see a positive.
  - (d) A result that CONTRADICTS directly-observed evidence is presumed an instrument fault until proven otherwise.
  - (e) The instrument used to establish a FACT is itself evidence: a captured claim cites the command that produced it (§11.4.5/§11.4.2).
  - (f) When the criterion is a SET (denylist, literal list, taxonomy, multi-column key) the control MUST cover EVERY member; needling one proves only that member is searchable. Enumerate the set, assert the search covers it, state the member count in the captured claim.
  - (g) Capture an exit status BEFORE any other expansion can overwrite it: assign `$?` to a variable on its own line immediately after the command and report the variable.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies concrete instruments and needle values per §11.4.35.
  - Recommended gate: decision-bearing census cites its positive and negative control; paired mutation: accept a decision-bearing census with no control -> FAILs; strip the literal -> propagation gate FAILs; gate-code = separate work item, NOT claimed shipped.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-273-PROPAGATION, CM-CENSUS-CONTROL-NEEDLED
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-control-needle, --empty-is-absent, --trust-the-grep, --census-needs-no-proof, --obvious-result-exempt, --one-needle-covers-the-set, --read-status-after-substitution
- **Honest boundary:** Control needles prove an instrument can distinguish PRESENT from ABSENT, not that it measures the RIGHT property; nor correctness for inputs unlike the needles (a needle resembling expected data will not reveal failure on dissimilar data).
- **Composes:** §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.2, §11.4.107(10), §11.4.118, §11.4.201, §11.4.17, §11.4.35, §11.4.227, §1.1

#### §11.4.274 — Mechanical work belongs in a script, not in an agent's context: extract it, test it, re-scan on a cadence
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1830-1848
- **Rules:**
  - Reason: five review agents consumed ~400-450k tokens EACH, dominated by deterministic mechanics (copy tree, apply one-line mutation, run suite, read summary, restore, verify byte-identical, compare counts) run one tool call at a time.
  - Work that is DETERMINISTIC, REPEATABLE and contains NO JUDGMENT MUST be delegated to a properly written script or small compiled utility and invoked, not performed turn-by-turn inside an agent's context. Belongs in a tool: mutation apply/run/restore/verify loops; suite fan-outs and result tabulation; before/after comparisons; scratch-tree setup/teardown; residue and quiescence scans; census and inventory queries; artifact fingerprinting; evidence collection and layout; any step already written as a fixed recipe.
  - (a) EXTRACT: when an agent performs the same mechanical sequence more than twice, that sequence is a tooling defect; it is extracted into a named script/utility and invoked thereafter. Bar is behavioural: if steps can be written down exactly, they can be executed exactly.
  - (b) The extracted tool is itself governed: documentation a reader can act on (§11.4.18), user guide/manual entry where operator-facing, tests that validate behaviour and produce MACHINE evidence deterministically (§11.4.50/§11.4.5) including failure paths, exit-code semantics (§11.4.201) and control needles for its own measurements (§11.4.273). Replacing a slow correct process with a fast unproven one is a regression.
  - (c) RE-SCAN ON A CADENCE: every project periodically scans itself for mechanical work still done by agents (recurring command sequences in transcripts/logs, repeated inline recipes across scripts, steps documented as "run these commands in order") and refactors findings out; a standing recurring obligation.
  - (d) JUDGMENT MUST NOT be scripted: root-cause determination (§11.4.102), review verdicts (§11.4.125/§11.4.142/§11.4.194), the decision that a fix is correct, choice of what to measure, reading whether captured evidence supports a claim, and any "is this the right thing to check" assessment. A script that renders a verdict is a bluff gate (§11.4.201). SCRIPT gathers and executes; AGENT decides what it means. Cost is never a reason to move a decision into a script; script output is evidence for a judgment, never a substitute.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies scripts, utility language, scan cadence, transcript/log sources per §11.4.35.
  - Recommended gates: a mechanical sequence performed by an agent more than twice has an extraction item; every extracted tool carries docs + tests + deterministic machine evidence. Paired §1.1 mutation; gate-code = separate work item, NOT claimed shipped.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-274-PROPAGATION, CM-MECHANICAL-WORK-EXTRACTED, CM-EXTRACTED-TOOL-DOCUMENTED-AND-TESTED
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-extraction, --agent-can-do-it, --one-off-is-fine, --script-the-review, --extract-without-tests
- **Honest boundary:** Applies to MECHANICAL work only; misapplying it to judgment is worse than not applying it; script output is evidence for a judgment, never a verdict.
- **Composes:** §11.4.18, §11.4.50, §11.4.5, §11.4.141, §11.4.201, §11.4.273, §11.4.124, §11.4.102, §11.4.125, §11.4.142, §11.4.194, §11.4.17, §11.4.35, §11.4.6, §11.4.227, §1.1

#### §11.4.275 — Semantic (Lumen) index + indexing-efficiency gate + universal agent/subagent accessibility
- **Source:** governance-and-constitution-meta.md:1850-1880
- **Rules:**
  - Reason: a semantic search server was configured yet reported 0 files/no model/never indexed; the structural index cut tokens 69.2% over 8 both-correct queries yet answered 5 of 15 WRONG (grep+read 2 of 15); one uncached full-table query was 93.4% of resolve time; FK cascade stalled bulk window; launcher classified `sync` by stored rows not pending backlog; vendor reaps locks by age not liveness and a writable open recreates dropped indexes without the lock; an errored instrument's empty result nearly read as absent.
  - (A) UNIVERSAL ACCESSIBILITY: every code index the project maintains (structural CodeGraph §11.4.78, semantic Lumen, any future index) MUST be reachable by EVERY AI agent AND every dispatched subagent through a server DEFINITION they can actually resolve (project-scoped committed configuration or installed plugin; never a per-user toggle only the main session sees). A configuration that ENABLES a server which nothing DECLARES is a violation. Proof = a real tool call FROM A DISPATCHED SUBAGENT returning an index-only fact (§11.4.78(4) unforgeable challenge), per agent; an agent that cannot be driven is a documented §11.4.3 SKIP, never a faked PASS.
  - (B) SEMANTIC INDEX PROVEN, NOT CONFIGURED: embedding model provisioned (rootless per §11.4.161) and proven by a REAL embed call returning the declared dimensionality (a model listing is not evidence). Scope GENERATED from the SAME class source as the structural scope (§11.4.78(7)-(8), via constitution `scripts/lumen/gen_lumenignore.py`) so third-party and secret classes are excluded identically. Health = files AND chunks non-zero + known-symbol search hit + negative control + freshness within a consumer-declared TTL.
  - (C) COMPLETE BEFORE READY: called ready only when PENDING work is zero (unresolved-reference backlog, files still to parse, embedding queue), state reports complete, file count within consumer tolerance of accepted expected count, required schema indexes exist. Calling a partial index ready is a PASS-bluff. Every count and empty result behind the verdict is control-needled (§11.4.273); an errored or silenced instrument proves nothing.
  - (D) EFFICIENCY MEASURED DETERMINISTICALLY AND REPORTED HONESTLY: benchmark harness runs a FIXED query set with GOLDEN answers against the index route AND a grep+read baseline, N >= 3 iterations with identical canonical result hash (§11.4.50), recording per query bytes, estimated tokens (declared estimator), p50/p95 latency, correctness vs golden. Token reduction computed ONLY over queries BOTH routes answered correctly; wrong answers reported separately BY QUERY ID, never averaged away. Harness self-validating (tampered golden fixture rejected; mutated estimator caught). Thresholds (minimum reduction, maximum wrong-answer count, latency ceilings) are consumer DATA (§11.4.35), never constitutional literals. A route saving tokens but wrong more often than baseline is NOT a win; a report showing only the saving is a bluff.
  - (E) ROUTING FOLLOWS THE MEASUREMENT: structural questions go to the structural index, conceptual questions to the semantic index, BEFORE grep+read (§11.4.141), EXCEPT query classes the benchmark shows answered wrongly: those fall back to grep+read and the gap is tracked (§11.4.197), never hidden.
  - (F) PERFORMANCE DEFECTS ROOT-CAUSED, PATCHED, PROVEN: a measured hot spot or stall is root-caused (§11.4.102) and fixed in the version-keyed patched runner with RED->GREEN, a paired mutation and an equivalence proof on a byte copy, then gated on every upgrade per §11.4.80(4).
  - (G) SAFETY: writes obey §11.4.80(5) (one writer entry, liveness not lock age, bulk classified by pending backlog); live reads are read-only/immutable; experiments run on fixtures or copy-on-write copies.
  - Latent binding (§11.4.96 pattern): a project with no semantic index is bound by (A)-(G) only for indexes it maintains; semantic clauses bind the moment it adds one; absence of a semantic index is never evidence (B)-(E) were satisfied.
  - EXTENSION 2026-09-25: clause (D) benchmark was run live via `constitution/scripts/lumen/lumen_verify.sh` (test file `scripts/lumen/tests/test_lumen_verify.sh`); harness now lives inside the constitution tree, superseding the "prototype outside the tree" statement; only `CM-CODE-INDEX-BENCH` gate CODE remains owed. 13-query pre-declared golden set (9 conceptual, 2 structural, 2 deliberately-unsupported), 3 byte-identical runs; recall 9/11 = 0.818; reduction computed only over the 9 correct answers (mean-of-per-query 30.1%) with negative-reduction outliers reported; `.sh` zero-result root-caused from Lumen's own index DB and chunker source (`supportedExtensions` lacks `.sh`, `.kt`, `.txt`) as a chunker-coverage gap, tracked per (E) + §11.4.197.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies own-org list, scope DATA, accepted counts, tolerances, TTL, benchmark queries/golden answers and thresholds as DATA (§11.4.35); all mechanism inherited by reference (§11.4.28/§11.4.80/§11.4.177).
  - Recommended gate behaviours: accessibility (every indexed space answers an unforgeable challenge from a dispatched subagent; enabled-but-undeclared server FAILs); complete-before-ready (pending == 0, state complete, count within tolerance); model-proven; scoped-fresh; bench (N>=3 identical hashes, reduction over both-correct only, wrong answers listed by id, thresholds from consumer DATA); scope-proof; upgrade-probe-gated; writer-exclusive; bulk-by-backlog; stall-watchdog. Paired mutations: enable server with no resolvable definition; ready with pending > 0; drop wrong-answer list or compute reduction over all queries; unload the embedding model; classify bulk by stored rows; drop liveness check -> each gate MUST FAIL; golden-FALSE: an unchanged complete reachable index MUST NOT fire any gate. Propagation gate literal block-start exactly once per governance file, lockstep across mirrors per §11.4.227(B). Gate CODE = separate work item, NOT claimed shipped.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-275-PROPAGATION, CM-CODE-INDEX-AGENT-ACCESSIBLE, CM-CODE-INDEX-COMPLETE-BEFORE-READY, CM-LUMEN-MODEL-PROVEN, CM-LUMEN-SCOPED-FRESH, CM-CODE-INDEX-BENCH, CM-CODEGRAPH-SCOPE-PROOF, CM-CODEGRAPH-UPGRADE-PROBE-GATED, CM-CODEGRAPH-WRITER-EXCLUSIVE, CM-CODEGRAPH-BULK-BY-BACKLOG, CM-CODEGRAPH-STALL-WATCHDOG
- **No escape hatch:** --index-partial-ready, --enabled-is-declared, --main-session-only-index, --skip-model-proof, --reduction-without-wrong-answers, --bulk-by-row-count, --lock-age-is-liveness
- **Honest boundary:** Proves an index is REACHABLE, COMPLETE, correctly SCOPED and MEASURED; does not prove every answer correct (fixed sample; wrong-answer classes stay tracked), nor that the benchmark represents every query shape.
  - Does NOT license narrowing index scope to hit a threshold (scope narrowing is a §11.4.66 operator decision).
- **Composes:** §11.4.3, §11.4.6, §11.4.10, §11.4.35, §11.4.50, §11.4.65, §11.4.66, §11.4.78, §11.4.79, §11.4.80, §11.4.96, §11.4.99, §11.4.102, §11.4.141, §11.4.161, §11.4.177, §11.4.196(D)(F), §11.4.197, §11.4.201, §11.4.224, §11.4.227, §11.4.232(C), §11.4.273, §11.4.28, §11.4.17, §1.1

### Host and resource safety (21 anchors)

#### §11.4.24 — Build-resource stats tracking mandate
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:3-116
- **Rules:**
  - Applies to every project with a build exceeding 1 minute wall-clock. Classification: mixed (discipline universal, implementation project-specific).
  - (1) MUST run a host-side resource sampler for every build, as a sibling background process (not inside the build's process tree), reading /proc/meminfo, /proc/loadavg, /proc/stat, /proc/diskstats (or platform equivalents) at a fixed interval (recommended 5 s); samples written as TSV.
  - (2) On stop, compute per-build summaries per metric (memory used, CPU%, load average, disk read/write): min, max, mean, p95. p95 is required because mean alone hides extended peaks.
  - (3) Append one TSV row per build to a registry (build_id, status SUCCESS/FAIL/UNKNOWN, start/end timestamps, per-metric min/max/mean/p95, total disk read/write). The registry is the single source of truth; the Markdown report is derived.
  - (4) Maintain ever-values (min/max/mean across ALL builds), recomputed on every Markdown regeneration, surfaced at the TOP of the report.
  - (5) Stats.md auto-generated and exported to Stats.html + Stats.pdf through the normal export pipeline; triple kept in sync per 11.4.12; committed via the lightweight doc-sync wrapper per 11.4.22.
  - (6) Sort per-build entries most recent first and, where applicable, group by version tag.
  - (7) Track status per build SUCCESS/FAIL/UNKNOWN; on FAIL capture the reason (exit code, OOM, ANR, etc.). Never silently drop FAIL entries.
  - (8) Sampler performance budget: under 50 MB RSS and under 5% CPU; must not add to the pressure it measures. Pure /proc reads + awk is the reference; vmstat/pidstat acceptable; psrecord and heavy-Python-import samplers are forbidden.
  - (9) The stop hook MUST be called from both success AND failure paths of the build wrapper; hooking only the success path is a PASS-bluff at the telemetry layer.
  - Pre-build gate (recommended): CM-BUILD-RESOURCE-STATS-TRACKER verifies monitor script exists+executable, Stats.md exists, build wrapper invokes start AND stop, doc-sync wrapper enumerates the Stats.{md,html,pdf} triple, exporter advertises the build-stats slug; paired mutation hides the monitor script, gate must FAIL.
- **Gates:** CM-BUILD-RESOURCE-STATS-TRACKER
- **No escape hatch:** Build-resource tracking is not optional polish (no flag named; stated as no escape hatch).
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.12, §11.4.18, §11.4.22, §12.6, §12.7, §12.9

#### §11.4.58 — Parallel-development methodology (PWU pipeline)
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:118-331
- **Rules:**
  - Project work proceeds through the Parallel Work Unit (PWU) pipeline, not a sequential phase-chain. Each PWU is a self-contained workable item with mandatory components: ATM-NNN id (11.4.54), Issues.md entry (11.4.15+11.4.16), file-scope manifest, 11.4.43 RED test, source patch, pre-build gate (11.4.4(b) layer 1), post-flash test (layer 3), paired 1.1 meta-test mutation, layer 4 HelixQA Challenge bank entry, captured-evidence directory (11.4.5+11.4.52).
  - Five stages: Stage 1 DEVELOP (parallel, N PWU agents in isolated worktrees); Stage 2 MERGE (serial, conductor one PWU at a time via commit_all.sh flock + 11.4.41 4-step merge-first pipeline); Stage 3 REBUILD+FLASH (parallel where possible; AOSP build in bounded scope, flash serialised on USB hardware); Stage 4 VALIDATE (parallel on D3+D4+meta-test+coverage-audit); Stage 5 SWEEP (parallel: HelixQA bank, Issues to Fixed migration, README doc-link refresh per 11.4.57, HTML+PDF exports). Stage 1 of round N+1 starts while Stages 4+5 of round N run.
  - Four-layer lock hierarchy: L1 parent serial flock .git/.commit_all.lock (held only during Stage 2, released between PWUs); L2 per-submodule git ops; L3 contention-path advisory locks at qa-results/pwu-locks/<sha256(path)>.lock for the 10 forbidden cross-PWU paths (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, Constitution.md, CONTINUATION.md, Issues.md, Fixed.md, pre_build_verification.sh, meta_test_false_positive_proof.sh, build.sh, commit_all.sh+push_all.sh, device.mk+BoardConfig.mk, atmosphere-*.sh, init.*.rc); L4 per-PWU git worktree.
  - Conflict detection at Stage 2 entry: git fetch --all --prune --tags + git diff main...HEAD -- <scope> + cross-PWU scope overlap check; overlap rejects the PWU to Stage 1 for rebase (11.4.41 step 2).
  - Conductor REFUSES to merge a PWU lacking all four anti-bluff checks: C1 11.4.43 RED test captured evidence (file exists, non-zero exit in log, timestamp predates source patch); C2 1.1 paired meta-test mutation (applied, gate FAILs, restored, gate PASSes); C3 11.4.50 deterministic consistency (3 iterations normal, 10 for cycle-validation, ALL identical exit codes AND evidence hashes); C4 11.4.5 captured evidence (audio: WAV with non-trivial RMS + ffprobe channel count; video: recording with ffprobe frame count > 0 + analyzer matched event; UI: uiautomator dump with element state; or HelixQA result.json PASS + positive-evidence chain).
  - HelixQA coverage MANDATORY for every user-visible PWU: Challenge bank entry in tools/helixqa/banks/atmosphere.yaml referencing the ATM-NNN, dispatching to the on-device test, scoring PASS only on positive captured evidence. Metadata-only, configuration-only, absence-of-error, grep-without-runtime-evidence PASS all REJECTED at the merge gate.
  - Agent roles: Conductor (1, main thread; issues ATM-NNN, dispatches, runs Stage 2 serially, runs Stages 3-5, owns contention-path edits, maintains docs/CONTINUATION.md section 3); PWU agent (4-6 background; one PWU each in isolated worktree; signals qa-results/pwu-<atm>/READY_FOR_MERGE); Validator (4 background); Sweeper (2 background). Max concurrent ~12 at peak, bounded by 12.6 60% memory budget.
  - Conductor refuses dispatch if host_check_safety fails; AOSP build still hard-capped -j2 in bounded scope per 12.7; 12.8/12.8b/12.8c gates still block on stray gradle/kotlin daemons.
  - Pre-build gates: CM-PWU-LOCK-HIERARCHY (scripts/testing/pwu_acquire_path_lock.sh and pwu_release_path_lock.sh exist, executable, reference the 10 forbidden paths from section 3.4 of docs/guides/PARALLEL_DEVELOPMENT_METHODOLOGY.md); CM-PWU-ANTI-BLUFF-COVERAGE (every PWU Ready-for-merge or beyond has C1-C4 evidence under qa-results/pwu-<atm>/evidence/); CM-PWU-MERGE-QUEUE-DISCIPLINE (no commits on main without qa-results/pwu-queue/merged/<atm> marker); CM-PWU-PARALLEL-AGENT-LIMIT (no more than 6 concurrent background PWU agents); CM-COVENANT-114-58-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.58 across 42 files in the reference consumer family).
  - Paired mutations: move acquire-lock script aside; touch READY_FOR_MERGE without red-test-output.log; land commit on main without merged marker; spawn a 7th concurrent PWU agent; strip 11.4.58 literal; each corresponding gate must FAIL.
  - Classification universal (11.4.17); consumers implement tooling in docs/guides/PARALLEL_DEVELOPMENT_METHODOLOGY.md.
- **Gates:** CM-PWU-LOCK-HIERARCHY, CM-PWU-ANTI-BLUFF-COVERAGE, CM-PWU-MERGE-QUEUE-DISCIPLINE, CM-PWU-PARALLEL-AGENT-LIMIT, CM-COVENANT-114-58-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-merge-queue, --allow-bypass, --no-anti-bluff-check, --unlimited-agents, --sequential-phase-chain-mode (an urgent fix is split into a single trivial PWU and run through the pipeline)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.4, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.7, §11.4.9, §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.33, §11.4.19, §11.4.41, §11.4.42, §11.4.43, §11.4.45, §11.4.49, §11.4.50, §11.4.52, §11.4.54, §11.4.57, §12.6, §12.7, §12.8, §12.10, §9.2, §1.1
- **Review addendum:** Applicability: projects with multiple owned submodules, a sequential commit/push tool and a captured-evidence testing discipline. Peak-agent bound: about 6 GB total, within a 38 GB budget.

#### §11.4.96 — Safe-parallel-work-with-long-build catalogue + mandate
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:335-385
- **Rules:**
  - Operational catalogue extending 11.4.94 (always check parallel-work feasibility before idle), 11.4.89, 11.4.58, for the canonical long workload (5-7 h AOSP containerised build per 12.9).
  - SAFE during the build (closed set): (A) Markdown/documentation work (docs/, *.md, README, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, QWEN.md, Status, Issues/Fixed and summaries, changelogs, research notes); (B) generator and helper script work under scripts/ (host-side, never consumed by the build); (C) pre-build/meta-test gate authoring + paired 1.1 mutations (picked up by the NEXT pre-build run); (D) on-device test authoring under device/rockchip/rk3588/tests/test_*.sh; (E) constitution submodule edits + push to all 6 remotes; (F) project submodule commit + push (background per 11.4.88); (G) read-only live-ADB probes of D3/D4 (dumpsys, getprop, cat /proc/asound, screencap, logcat -d); (H) subagent dispatch per 11.4.20/11.4.70 (multiple subagents coordinate via 11.4.84 quiescence); (I) web research and external API queries with 11.4.10 credential discipline; (J) workable-items DB operations per 11.4.93+11.4.95; (K) pre-build verification + meta-test execution run per 11.4.89 background discipline.
  - UNSAFE during the build (closed set): (alpha) git checkout / git reset --hard / git clean -df on the source tree (defer or use worktree per 11.4.84); (beta) mass file deletions/renames under device/, frameworks/, hardware/, vendor/, kernel-5.10/, external/, packages/, bionic/, bootable/, build/, system/, cts/, tools/, prebuilts/ etc.; (gamma) submodule pointer updates that affect built APKs (presenter, smarttube-player, vlc-player etc.); (delta) out/ directory mutations; (epsilon) make clean / m clobber / rm -rf out/; (zeta) container destruction (podman stop atmosphere-aosp-build, podman pod rm), operator-explicit only; (eta) disk-filling operations pushing the host below the 12.9 free-space minimum; (theta) host-session-safety breaches per 12 (suspend, hibernate, logout, unbounded memory in user.slice).
  - Conductor MUST, before EVERY pause point during a long build, consult this catalogue, identify all (A)-(K) items in the priority queue per 11.4.42+11.4.72, and dispatch at least one per 11.4.20/11.4.70 with 11.4.89 background discipline. "Build is running, nothing else to do" is NEVER true.
  - Subagent default: (A), (E), (F) conductor-direct; (B), (C), (D), (G), (I), (J) subagent-dispatchable; (H) is itself subagent dispatch; (K) backgrounded per 11.4.89 and polled.
  - Conductor scheduling a wake/sleep during an active AOSP build without dispatching at least one (A)-(K) item is a 11.4.94+11.4.96 violation (PASS-bluff at the operating-mode layer). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
  - Gates: CM-COVENANT-114-96-PROPAGATION; CM-PARALLEL-WORK-DURING-BUILD-AUDIT (when implemented; audits commits during build windows); paired 1.1 mutations strip the catalogue literals and gates FAIL.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-96-PROPAGATION, CM-PARALLEL-WORK-DURING-BUILD-AUDIT
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.20, §11.4.42, §11.4.58, §11.4.70, §11.4.72, §11.4.82, §11.4.84, §11.4.85, §11.4.87, §11.4.88, §11.4.89, §11.4.92, §11.4.93, §11.4.95, §11.4.94, §12.6, §12.7, §12.8, §12.9

#### §11.4.111 — Resolve-by-stable-name-not-by-enumeration-index mandate
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:389-407
- **Rules:**
  - Short tag: resolve-by-stable-name. Reason: a static index binding (card=0) pointed at the wrong device after a second device enumerated first.
  - Any binding between a configuration/policy/code site and a hardware device, resource handle, or enumerated entity (audio cards, display connectors, NICs, storage devices, GPU render nodes, input devices, camera indices, container/process slots, any registry with discovery-time ordinals) MUST resolve the target by a stable identifier (name, UUID, serial, label, controller-name, content-derived hash, sink-reported identity) and MUST NOT resolve by enumeration index/ordinal/slot number, UNLESS the platform documents that ordinal as deterministically pinned and the pinning mechanism is itself part of the binding, captured and asserted.
  - Where a stable identifier exists at one layer of a stack, every other layer binding the same resource MUST use the same identifier; mixed by-name/by-index is forbidden.
  - Where a sink-reported/capability-derived identity exists (e.g. EDID/ELD-style), prefer it.
  - If the platform provides no stable identifier and only an ordinal exists, the binding MUST (a) pin the ordinal deterministically via the platform's own mechanism, (b) capture that pin in the binding's runtime signature per 11.4.108, (c) document the residual fragility as UNCONFIRMED-class risk per 11.4.6.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies its stable-identifier mechanism and layers that must agree per 11.4.35.
  - Gates: CM-COVENANT-114-111-PROPAGATION; recommended CM-RESOLVE-BY-NAME-NOT-INDEX (diff-driven scan flagging a new index binding to a resource with a stable identifier unless deterministic pin + runtime signature present); paired mutations plant an unpinned index binding / strip the literal and gates FAIL. Gate code is a separate work item.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-111-PROPAGATION, CM-RESOLVE-BY-NAME-NOT-INDEX
- **No escape hatch:** --allow-index-binding, --ordinal-is-stable-enough, --skip-name-resolution, --trust-unpinned-index
- **Honest boundary:** When only an ordinal exists the binding must pin it, capture the pin, and document residual fragility as UNCONFIRMED; never trust an unpinned ordinal.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.8, §11.4.17, §11.4.35, §11.4.69, §11.4.108, §11.4.110

#### §11.4.119 — Single-resource-owner partitioning for parallel hardware testing
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:409-429
- **Rules:**
  - Short tag: single-resource-owner-partitioning. Reason: two streams driving media on the same device corrupt each other's evidence.
  - When multiple parallel work/test/discovery streams exercise shared hardware or any exclusive-access resource (media-playback path, single HDMI/audio sink, exclusive device handle, single serial/JTAG line, GPU under exclusive capture), exactly ONE stream MUST own each such resource at a time.
  - The owner drives the resource; every other concurrent stream targeting it MUST be READ-ONLY (passive probes: dumpsys, /proc, /sys reads, sink-side network probes, log tails).
  - Parallelism is partitioned by resource: distinct devices/sinks/handles run fully concurrent (stream-per-device); the same device's exclusive resource is single-owner.
  - Ownership MUST be enforced by an advisory lock/token (per 11.4.58 L3 + 11.4.84 hardware analogue), not by convention; a second stream MUST be unable to silently start media on a device another stream owns.
  - Ownership is event-driven: claim when the resource frees, release the moment work completes so the next queued stream can claim it (11.4.103 auto-backfill).
  - A PASS captured under contention is an evidence-integrity bluff.
  - A read-only stream MUST NOT issue any state-changing command (no am start, input injection, setprop, playback) against a device it does not own.
  - When the resource cannot be partitioned, streams MUST serialize on it (single-owner over time).
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies resource inventory and lock mechanism per 11.4.35. Strict refinement of 11.4.58/11.4.103 for hardware contention.
  - Gates: CM-COVENANT-114-119-PROPAGATION; recommended CM-SINGLE-RESOURCE-OWNER-PARTITION (streams acquire a per-resource ownership lock before any state-changing command; concurrent same-resource streams read-only); paired mutation removes lock acquisition and gate FAILs. Gate code a separate work item.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-119-PROPAGATION, CM-SINGLE-RESOURCE-OWNER-PARTITION
- **No escape hatch:** --allow-concurrent-resource-drivers, --skip-ownership-lock, --read-only-may-mutate, --contended-evidence-OK
- **Honest boundary:** A read-only stream is genuinely read-only; where a resource cannot be partitioned streams serialize over time rather than run concurrently and hope.
- **Composes:** §11.4.5, §11.4.69, §11.4.13, §11.4.50, §11.4.58, §11.4.82, §11.4.84, §11.4.103, §11.4.118

#### §11.4.128 — Always-on device-recording mandate
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:433-443
- **Rules:**
  - For EVERY test/debug device the project uses and every device where the operator is known to do manual testing, across every reachable transport (USB/wireless ADB, SSH, serial, network introspection API), the project MUST ALWAYS live-record all available data it can later analyse: all activities, all logs (system, kernel, dropbox, crash/ANR traces), performance metrics (CPU, memory, I/O, thermal, load), every sink-side/downstream introspection report per 11.4.13, and any other live-changeable parameter.
  - (1) Extra-careful and side-effect-free: never harm the device or degrade its performance; non-invasive read-only probes only, bounded sampling intervals, bounded write volume, an observer-effect budget. A recorder that perturbs the device is a violation, not evidence.
  - (2) Background + parallel + subagent-driven (11.4.103, 11.4.70); never blocks the main stream.
  - (3) Token-conscious, record-now analyse-later: raw data MUST NOT be processed without need; default is capture-and-store. Only exceptions: release-tag preparation (11.4.40 full-suite retest / 11.4.42 release-gate) or an explicit operator request. Eager continuous analysis for no tracked reason is a violation.
  - (4) Raw corpus is git-ignored (with a 11.4.77 regeneration declaration: re-run the recorder) AND excluded from the code-intelligence index (11.4.78/11.4.79); only curated analysis/evidence is committed, only during release preparation per 11.4.83 (docs/qa/<run-id>/).
  - (5) Deterministic layout: <recording-root>/YYYY-MM-DD/<combined main+submodules state hash>/<DEVICE>_<SERIAL>/recording_NNN/<files> (monotonic NNN per device per state-hash).
  - (6) Anti-bluff: a recorder claimed running but producing no growing corpus is a bluff; a cited curated finding MUST trace to a real raw-corpus path; recorder health (alive + corpus growing) is itself captured evidence per 11.4.5/11.4.69.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies serials, transport probes, recorder helper, recording-root, metric set (11.4.35).
  - Gates: CM-COVENANT-114-128-PROPAGATION; recommended CM-DEVICE-RECORDING-ALWAYS-ON (recorder present, raw corpus git-ignored and index-excluded, deterministic layout); paired mutation strips literal. Gate code a separate work item.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-128-PROPAGATION, CM-DEVICE-RECORDING-ALWAYS-ON
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-recording, --record-without-layout, --commit-raw-corpus, --index-raw-corpus, --analyse-corpus-always, --invasive-probe-OK
- **Honest boundary:** Re-recording does not byte-reproduce a past device state (stated as caveat of the regeneration declaration).
- **Composes:** §11.4.2, §11.4.5, §11.4.13, §11.4.69, §11.4.40, §11.4.42, §11.4.70, §11.4.77, §11.4.78, §11.4.79, §11.4.83, §11.4.103, §11.4.119

#### §11.4.144 — Tracked/recorded-device availability-following mandate
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:445-455
- **Rules:**
  - Every device the project records or tracks (test/debug/manual-testing, any transport) MUST be availability-FOLLOWED: connection state continuously monitored; a drop is never silently abandoned and never presented as continuous recording (a silent corpus hole is a PASS-bluff at the recording-integrity layer).
  - On a tracked device leaving its reachable state the system MUST automatically: (a) DETECT and log an honest offline event into the recording corpus; (b) WAIT for return using the project's ALREADY-DEFINED reconnection timings (same grace/reconnect/poll budgets as the recovery path; never invented numbers); (c) RE-ATTACH and resume recording/tracking the moment the device returns, logging an honest online/resume event; (d) ESCALATE to the sanctioned device-recovery path (11.4.69 feature class device_recovery) if the device does not return within the defined timeout, via the authorization-gated entry point ONLY, never bypassing its gate and never performing a destructive recovery (e.g. power-cycle) autonomously without that authorization (11.4.21/11.4.101); while blocked keep following and log the blocked escalation honestly.
  - A drop producing a silent corpus hole, a never-resumed recording, or a never-escalated permanent absence is forbidden.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies transport, device set, reconnection timings, recovery entry point (11.4.35).
  - Gates: CM-COVENANT-114-144-PROPAGATION; recommended CM-DEVICE-AVAILABILITY-FOLLOWED (recorder wires a per-device availability watchdog reusing defined timings, escalating only via gated recovery); paired mutations strip watchdog wiring / let absence go unlogged / strip literal. Gate code a separate work item.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-144-PROPAGATION, CM-DEVICE-AVAILABILITY-FOLLOWED
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-availability-following, --silent-recording-gap-OK, --no-reconnect-wait, --invent-reconnect-timing, --skip-recovery-escalation, --autonomous-power-cycle-OK
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.128, §11.4.69, §11.4.6, §11.4.14, §11.4.21, §11.4.101

#### §11.4.147 — Crashed-agent respawn-until-complete + no-work-loss registry mandate
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:459-479
- **Rules:**
  - Every dispatched agent/subagent MUST be tracked through its full lifecycle so a crash never loses, forgets, or corrupts work. A crashed agent is NOT a completed agent (11.4.6); abnormal termination is evidence the work unit is OPEN.
  - (a) Mandatory durable, append-only, machine-readable REGISTRY entry per dispatch: stable agent/work-unit id, task + file-scope (11.4.58 PWU manifest), declared output path(s) + captured-evidence dir (11.4.5/11.4.69), dispatch timestamp, status from CLOSED SET {dispatched | in-flight | crashed | respawned | complete}. Registry reuses the 11.4.116 sync substrate (append-only JSONL events + atomically-rewritten snapshot); an entry with no dispatch event cannot show complete. It is the single source of truth for "is this work owed?"; an unregistered dispatch is itself a violation.
  - (b) Mechanical crash detection + respawn-until-complete: any abnormal termination (transient API/rate-limit error, socket close, any non-completion exit, or terminal error after runtime retries) flips the entry to crashed and keeps the unit OPEN; an open unit MUST be respawned (fresh agent claims same id + scope + preserved state) repeatedly until complete. Respawn is autonomous per 11.4.101. Transient causes use the project's ALREADY-DEFINED backoff/retry budgets (never invented); a deterministically reproducible non-transient error is investigated per 11.4.102 before further respawn, never blind-retried.
  - (c) Partial state: crashed agent's uncommitted edits + output doc MUST be PRESERVED (not discarded, not blindly committed). Before resuming run the 11.4.84 quiescence check (all modified files accounted against scope; no mutation / always-pass / _mutated_* residue; no torn artifact). Then either (i) RESUME idempotently if consistent, or (ii) CLEAN-RESTART from known-good base (9.2 pre-op backup) when inconsistent. Per-agent git worktree isolation (11.4.58 L4 / 11.4.84).
  - (d) Completion: a unit is DONE only when an agent reaches complete with required captured evidence landed. Loop done-condition (11.4.87/94/97/126) MUST NOT read satisfied while any entry is dispatched/in-flight/crashed/respawned-not-yet-complete; zero-idle survey (11.4.94) treats every non-complete entry as open actionable. complete without landed evidence is a PASS-bluff.
  - (e) API-QUOTA/RATE-LIMIT EXHAUSTION is a first-class crash class: (1) record the REAL limit signal and its reason-class per 11.4.196(B) {session | weekly | subscription} from the captured 429 signature; (2) REBIND the killed unit to the next OPERATIONAL alias per 11.4.196(A)/(C) (native-first, provider fallback) and RESPAWN there; when EVERY alias is cooled, bounded-PARK per 11.4.101 carrying its operational-again epoch, stays crashed/OPEN, never complete; (3) respawned agent RESUMES from the killed agent's captured transcript + on-disk partial state at its exact last point (clause (c)), never blind restart; (4) loop done-condition MUST NOT read satisfied while any quota-killed entry is non-complete; "quota ran out" is a PARK, never a DONE.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies registry path/format, crash-detection signal source, respawn mechanism, backoff budgets (11.4.35).
  - Gates: CM-COVENANT-114-147-PROPAGATION; recommended CM-CRASHED-AGENT-RESPAWN-TRACKED (every dispatched agent has registry entry; every crashed entry respawned until complete; loop done-condition reads no non-complete entries; partial state preserved and 11.4.84-checked before resume); paired mutations (strip literal; mark crashed entry complete without evidence; drop dispatch without entry). Gate code a separate work item.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-147-PROPAGATION, CM-CRASHED-AGENT-RESPAWN-TRACKED
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-agent-registry, --crash-equals-done, --no-respawn, --discard-partial-state, --blind-commit-partial, --forget-dead-agent, --loop-done-with-crashed-entries
- **Honest boundary:** Registry + respawn guarantee work is not lost or corrupted, NOT that it is correct; respawned output still crosses 11.4.108 verification, 11.4.125/11.4.142 review, and 11.4.40 retest.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.58, §11.4.84, §11.4.87, §11.4.94, §11.4.97, §11.4.126, §11.4.101, §11.4.116, §11.4.102, §11.4.108, §11.4.125, §11.4.142, §11.4.40, §9.2, §11.4.128, §11.4.144, §11.4.196, §11.4.198

#### §11.4.154 — Window-scoped capture + fresh-corpus rotation for feature/QA recordings
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:481-491
- **Rules:**
  - (A) Window-scoped capture, NOT whole-screen: a recording proving a feature MUST capture ONLY the window/surface/viewport under test (app window, terminal pane, browser tab/viewport, device/emulator/simulator frame), never the whole desktop/monitor or unrelated windows. Reasons: leaks unrelated private content (11.4.10/11.4.83), dilutes the 11.4.107 liveness/frame-advance oracle, unreliable for 11.4.137-class OCR/ROI oracle.
  - Capture MUST target the window/region by stable identity (window id/title, device serial, browser context, tmux/terminal target) per 11.4.111, never a fixed full-screen device index.
  - Where the platform cannot capture below whole-screen for the surface, record an honest 11.4.3 SKIP-with-reason + tracked migration item, never a whole-screen capture passed off as window-scoped.
  - (B) Fresh-corpus rotation: when a new recording run for a scope begins, the prior run's stale recording files for that scope MUST be removed FIRST. "Remove old" means the agent's OWN prior recordings for the SAME scope at the project-declared recording path, NEVER another project's/scope's or operator-authored files; when uncertain, do NOT delete, surface it (11.4.122). Curated evidence committed under docs/qa/<run-id>/ (11.4.83) is NOT deleted; rotation operates on the raw working path (11.4.128).
  - (C) MP4 auto-conversion REQUIRED: any .cast produced MUST be auto-converted to .mp4 via agg + ffmpeg immediately after capture; .mp4 is primary evidence, .cast supplementary. Commands: `agg input.cast output.mp4 --renderer-res 1920x1080` then `ffmpeg -i output.mp4 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart final.mp4`.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies window-capture mechanism per surface class, recording path, scope-key (11.4.35).
  - Gates: CM-COVENANT-114-154-PROPAGATION; recommended CM-WINDOW-SCOPED-FRESH-CORPUS-RECORDING (window/surface-scoped capture + new run removes its own prior in-scope recordings first); paired mutations. Gate code a separate work item.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-154-PROPAGATION, CM-WINDOW-SCOPED-FRESH-CORPUS-RECORDING
- **No escape hatch:** --whole-screen-capture-OK, --skip-window-scope, --keep-stale-recordings, --no-corpus-rotation, --full-desktop-recording
- **Honest boundary:** Rotation never deletes foreign/operator-authored files or committed docs/qa evidence; uncertain files are surfaced, not deleted.
- **Composes:** §11.4.2, §11.4.5, §11.4.10, §11.4.83, §11.4.86, §11.4.107, §11.4.111, §11.4.122, §11.4.128, §11.4.137, §11.4.153, §9.2, §11.4.6, §11.4.3

#### §11.4.155 — Project-name-prefixed feature/QA recording filenames
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:493-505
- **Rules:**
  - Every recorded video the project produces (feature/QA recordings 11.4.153, window-scoped captures 11.4.154, always-on device recordings 11.4.128, raw or curated artefacts under the recording path and docs/qa/<run-id>/ 11.4.83) MUST have a filename that STARTS WITH the PROJECT-NAME prefix, always, no exception.
  - Prefix resolution order (closed-set, deterministic, identical to 11.4.151): (1) HELIX_RELEASE_PREFIX from the project's .env (authoritative when set; .env git-ignored per 11.4.30; variable documented in tracked .env.example per 11.4.77); (2) fallback = lowercased snake_case project root directory name (no spaces) per 11.4.29.
  - Same resolved prefix for every recording in a checkout, so `ls '<PREFIX>---'*` enumerates the corpus.
  - Canonical filename form: <PREFIX>---<feature-or-scope>---<run-id>.<ext> (triple-hyphen separator).
  - The recording prefix MUST equal the 11.4.151-resolved release-tag prefix in the same checkout; divergence is itself a violation.
  - The prefix does not relax 11.4.154 rotation (only own prior in-scope <PREFIX>---* files are removed; foreign-prefix or operator-authored files are surfaced, never deleted, per 11.4.122 + 9.2).
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies prefix value, env var, recording path (11.4.35).
  - Gates: CM-COVENANT-114-155-PROPAGATION; recommended CM-RECORDING-PROJECT-NAME-PREFIX (every recording filename and committed docs/qa recording artefact starts with resolved <PREFIX>--- identical to 11.4.151 prefix); paired mutations. Gate code a separate work item.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-155-PROPAGATION, CM-RECORDING-PROJECT-NAME-PREFIX
- **No escape hatch:** --no-recording-prefix, --recording-without-project-name, --unprefixed-recording, --prefix-optional-for-recording, --differing-recording-prefix
- **Honest boundary:** The prefix guarantees attribution/greppability, NOT content validity (still 11.4.107, 11.4.137, 11.4.153 layers).
- **Composes:** §11.4.151, §11.4.128, §11.4.153, §11.4.154, §11.4.111, §11.4.83, §11.4.6, §11.4.29, §11.4.30, §11.4.35, §11.4.77, §11.4.86, §11.4.122, §9.2

#### §11.4.174 — Shared-host process-ownership verification mandate
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:507-507
- **Rules:**
  - On any host where other projects/users/agents may run concurrently, EVERY inspection of, conclusion about, or action on a process, build, daemon, port, lock-file, or system-state signal MUST FIRST positively verify the target is OURS before diagnosing or acting. Diagnosis from another project's process is a 11.4.6 guessing-class error; killing/signalling/restarting/altering a process not positively ours is a 12 + 11.4.133-class safety violation.
  - (a) Positive-ownership discriminator REQUIRED: attribute only via a strong signal: cwd inside THIS project's tree, argv naming this project's scripts/artifacts/repo path, a PID we launched and recorded (11.4.147 launched-PID registry), or lock/port/socket path under our tree. A loose name match (pgrep java/gradle/node/python/podman/zig) is NEVER sufficient.
  - (b) NEVER kill/signal/restart a process not positively ours; the 12.8 remediation `pkill -f GradleDaemon` MUST be scoped to OUR daemons (cwd/argv under our tree), never host-wide.
  - (c) Contention: when our work waits on another project's process, surface it per 11.4.66/11.4.101 and keep progressing non-blocked work; do NOT kill the other process.
  - (d) Every pgrep/ps filter MUST exclude the checking command's OWN argv AND other-project matches; prefer matching our absolute repo path.
  - (e) Applies to all state: ports, lock files, gradle/maven caches, podman pods, tmux sessions, temp files.
  - Classification universal.
  - Gates: CM-COVENANT-114-174-PROPAGATION; recommended CM-PROCESS-OWNERSHIP-VERIFIED (process-killing or build-state-diagnosing scripts attribute by cwd/argv/launched-PID, never bare name match; pgrep filters exclude self); paired mutation replaces ownership-verified attribution with bare pgrep. Gate code a separate work item.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-174-PROPAGATION, CM-PROCESS-OWNERSHIP-VERIFIED
- **No escape hatch:** --assume-process-ours, --loose-pgrep-ok, --kill-any-matching-process, --skip-ownership-check
- **Honest boundary:** Ownership verification prevents mis-attribution and cross-project damage; it does not prove our process healthy (needs our own build log, outputs, launched-PID).
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.101, §11.4.66, §11.4.147, §12, §12.8, §11.4.133

#### §11.4.225 — Scheduler-quota burst-throttling telemetry + interactive-scope isolation from bursty fleets
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:509-525
- **Rules:**
  - (A) DIAGNOSTIC: any investigation of progressive/bursty/load-correlated interactive degradation (sluggish TUI/terminal, editor lag, stalls worsening with parallel-agent or worker count) MUST sample the scheduling scope's THROTTLING ACCOUNTING (cgroup v2 cpu.stat nr_throttled + throttled_usec) as DELTAS over a measured window under load, as a fraction of elapsed enforcement periods, WITH a quiet-phase control sample, BEFORE any cause verdict. Healthy averages (CPU average, load average, memory, thread counts) are structurally blind to this and are 11.4.201(6) false-nulls; an averages-only verdict is a 11.4.6 guess. Same discipline for every quota'd scheduler (container CPU limits, VM caps, hypervisor shares/steal): throttle/steal accounting is the authoritative source.
  - (B) DESIGN: an interactive-latency-sensitive process (terminal-multiplexer server, TUI, editor, operator shell) MUST NOT be co-resident in a fixed-quota, NO-BURST scope with a bursty multi-process fleet (subagents, build workers, test runners). The project MUST (1) grant the shared scope a burst allowance sized for the fleet's measured spike profile, OR (2) isolate the interactive process in its OWN scope (or leave it unquoted where host policy allows), OR both.
  - Quota values MUST be HOST-ADAPTIVE: computed from real detected capacity with a documented floor and cap (12.11 discipline; never hardcode), never a fixed literal; a quota change is verified by READING THE LIVE scope's values BACK (11.4.108).
  - Composes with 12.6 (memory) and 12.12 (threads) as the THIRD orthogonal host-exhaustion axis; no axis's instrument substitutes for another.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies scope layout, quota/burst values, sampling windows, instruments (11.4.35).
  - Gates: CM-COVENANT-114-225-PROPAGATION; CM-QUOTA-THROTTLE-TELEMETRY (every progressive-degradation verdict cites throttle-accounting deltas + quiet-phase control; averages-only verdict FAILs); CM-INTERACTIVE-SCOPE-NOT-QUOTA-STARVED (no interactive process co-resident in fixed-quota no-burst scope with a bursty fleet; quota defaults host-adaptive with live read-back); paired mutations. Gate code a separate work item.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-225-PROPAGATION, CM-QUOTA-THROTTLE-TELEMETRY, CM-INTERACTIVE-SCOPE-NOT-QUOTA-STARVED
- **No escape hatch:** --averages-prove-healthy, --skip-throttle-telemetry, --fixed-quota-default-OK, --interactive-in-fleet-scope-OK, --no-burst-needed, --skip-quiet-phase-control
- **Honest boundary:** Throttle telemetry proves where enforcement periods were lost, not that throttling is the only degrader. Clause (B) bounds placement and sizing; it does not exempt the fleet from 12.6/12.8/12.12 or license removing a quota host policy requires.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.24, §11.4.102, §11.4.108, §11.4.128, §11.4.201, §11.4.103, §11.4.183, §12.6, §12.8, §12.11, §12.12

#### §11.4.254 — Boot-time invariant assertion + capability matrix
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:527-533
- **Rules:**
  - Every service/process/long-running executable MUST assert BOOT-TIME INVARIANTS at startup and FAIL FAST + LOUD if any is violated, BEFORE accepting requests or performing work: required env vars present+valid; config files parseable with declared schema version matching; dependencies reachable; credentials present and not expired; schema migrations applied; feature-flag states declared; host resources present (disk/memory/thread limits per 12.12, port availability).
  - Invariant classes: (i) environment, (ii) configuration, (iii) dependencies, (iv) credentials, (v) schema, (vi) capabilities, (vii) host.
  - Fail-fast-loud: (1) emit structured error to stderr + captured log naming the specific failed invariant; (2) exit non-zero (traditionally 78 EX_CONFIG for config; consumer supplies per 11.4.35); (3) do NOT accept requests / begin main loop / bind listening port. Partial boot is worse than refusing to start.
  - CAPABILITY MATRIX: consumer's docs/services/CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md (11.4.35) declares per service (i) boot-time invariants, (ii) runtime capabilities OFFERED, (iii) capabilities REQUIRED from other services. Regenerated/verified every commit per 11.4.106 docs-chain + 11.4.86 fingerprint. Undeclared endpoints emitted = violation; undeclared upstream dependencies = violation.
  - Cited cases: plaintext catalog.db despite "encrypted at rest" (fix = boot-time check that fails closed verifying cipher_version); stubbed-core-behind-claim (capability matrix with every adapter reporting IsImplemented()/attempted-vs-not + a challenge failing against a no-op stub).
  - Dual to 11.4.252 fail-closed on dangerous combinations. Classification universal.
  - Gates: CM-COVENANT-114-254-PROPAGATION, CM-BOOT-TIME-INVARIANT-ASSERTED, CM-CAPABILITY-MATRIX-PRESENT-AND-IN-SYNC; paired mutations.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-254-PROPAGATION, CM-BOOT-TIME-INVARIANT-ASSERTED, CM-CAPABILITY-MATRIX-PRESENT-AND-IN-SYNC
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-boot-time-assertion, --boot-partial-OK, --default-missing-env-silently, --capability-matrix-optional, --service-with-undeclared-dependency-OK
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.35, §11.4.86, §11.4.106, §11.4.108, §11.4.128, §11.4.244, §11.4.252, §12.12, §1.1, §11.4.239
- **Review addendum:** Canon cites §11.4.239 only in a citation note, not in its Composes list.

#### §11.4.263 — Process-group signal-safety mandate (never signal pgid <= 1)
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:535-599
- **Rules:**
  - Reason (BOB-126): an AsyncMock subprocess with unset pid coerced to int 1, so os.killpg(os.getpgid(1), SIGKILL) became kill(-1, SIGKILL), killing the whole UID session; seven forced logouts over ~48h; a suppress(Exception) swallowed nothing because the syscall succeeded.
  - (A) NEVER signal pgid <= 1: no code path may call os.killpg / kill(-pid, sig) / killpg(2) / pkill -<pgid> / subprocess.killpg / Process.killpg where pgid (or pid in the negative-pid kill form) is <= 1. killpg(1,sig) == kill(-1,sig) signals every process the caller may signal; portable across BSD/macOS.
  - (B) VALIDATE pid and pgid as int > 1 BEFORE every process-group signal call (isinstance int, never a mock/string/None; > 1, never init's pgid, never 0, never negative; same for pid in negative-pid form). Python: guard isinstance(pid,int) and pid>1, then pgid=os.getpgid(pid), isinstance(pgid,int) and pgid>1, then os.killpg. Go: guard pgid>1 before syscall.Kill(-pgid, sig); test doubles must return int(pgid)>1. Rust: nix killpg accepts only Pid::from_raw(n) with n>1, rejecting the current-group sentinel. Bash: validate [[ "$pgid" -gt 1 ]] before kill -<pgid> / pkill -g. C: same integer guard for killpg and kill(-pid,sig).
  - (C) TESTS mocking subprocess/proc objects MUST: (1) set mock.pid = <large int, e.g. 12345> explicitly, never rely on mock library defaults; (2) patch the process-group signaling call itself (e.g. patch.object(module.os,'killpg')); (3) assert the mocked killpg was called with pgid > 1.
  - (D) Defense-in-depth: guard present in BOTH production code AND test; removing either must break at least one test. Layer 1 pre-build grep for killpg/kill(-...) calls not preceded by guard; Layer 2 post-build CodeGraph query of callers vs guard presence; Layer 3 runtime kernel audit rules on SIGKILL with a0=0xffffffff (kill(-1)) or a0=0x00000001 in the pidfd_send_signal case; Layer 4 paired 1.1 mutation regression test invoking the killpg path with a mock pid and asserting not called with pgid <= 1.
