  - (F) Standing default from the first prompt: every code review (11.4.125/142/194) MUST scan for process-group signal calls and verify the guard; every subagent writing subprocess-cleanup code MUST include the guard; every test-writing subagent MUST include mock.pid = <int>.
  - Classification universal.
  - Gates: CM-COVENANT-114-263-PROPAGATION; CM-KILLPG-PGID-GUARD (every killpg/kill(-pid) site has pid>1 && pgid>1 guard); CM-TEST-MOCK-PID-EXPLICIT-INT (every subprocess mock sets pid as int and patches killpg); paired mutations.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-263-PROPAGATION, CM-KILLPG-PGID-GUARD, CM-TEST-MOCK-PID-EXPLICIT-INT
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-killpg-guard, --mock-pid-optional, --killpg-1-is-ok, --kill-minus-1-permitted, --suppress-catches-syscall, --test-may-not-explicit-pid
- **Honest boundary:** Hardens process-group signal APIs only; does not prohibit well-scoped killpg of own groups (start_new_session=True children), not extended to low-blast signals (guard still recommended), and does not prevent kernel OOM-killer/systemd-oomd (12.6 and 11.4.225 apply).
- **Composes:** §11.4.1, §11.4.4, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.85, §11.4.107, §11.4.115, §11.4.126, §11.4.201, §11.4.225, §11.4.226, §11.4.125, §11.4.142, §11.4.194

#### §12.1 — Forbidden operations (host-session safety)
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:603-622
- **Rules:**
  - Forbidden, directly OR indirectly: (1) suspending the host (systemctl suspend, pm-suspend, loginctl suspend, DBus org.freedesktop.login1.Suspend, GNOME idle-suspend, lid-close handler); (2) hibernating/hybrid-sleeping (any Hibernate / HybridSleep / SuspendThenHibernate method); (3) logging out the user (loginctl terminate-session, pkill -u <user>, systemctl --user --kill, anything signalling user@<uid>.service); (4) unbounded-memory operations inside the user@<uid>.service cgroup: any single command expected to exceed ~4 GiB RSS MUST be wrapped in a bounded execution scope (e.g. bounded_run wrapping systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=...); (5) programmatic rfkill toggles, lid-switch handlers, power-button handlers; (6) disabling systemd-logind, GDM, or session managers, even temporarily.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** none cited

#### §12.2 — Required safeguards for heavy scripts
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:624-636
- **Rules:**
  - Every script performing heavy work (build, transcription, model inference, large compression, multi-GB git operations) MUST: (1) source the project's host-safety helper library at the top; (2) call its pre-flight check and abort if it fails; (3) wrap any subprocess expected to exceed ~4 GiB RSS in a bounded execution scope so the kernel OOM killer is contained and cannot escalate to user.slice; (4) cap parallelism (-j) to fit available RAM (per-job-peak-RSS divided into the budget).
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** none cited

#### §12.3 — Container hygiene
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:638-647
- **Rules:**
  - Containers (Docker/Podman) the project owns or relies on MUST: (1) declare an explicit memory limit (mem_limit / --memory / MemoryMax); (2) set OOMPolicy=stop in their systemd unit to avoid retry loops; (3) use exponential-backoff restart policies, never immediate retry; (4) be clean-slate destroyed and rebuilt after any host crash or session loss so stale lock files do not keep producing failures.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** none cited

#### §12.6 — Memory-Budget Ceiling, 60% maximum
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:649-677
- **Rules:**
  - Project procedures MUST NOT use more than 60% of total system RAM; the remaining 40% is reserved for the operator's other workloads (all processes must be able to function normally).
  - Protections: (1) HOST_SAFETY_MAX_MEM_PCT defaults to 60; (2) HOST_SAFETY_BUDGET_GB computed at source-time from MemTotal x MAX_PCT/100 in GiB; (3) bounded execution scopes clamp MemoryMax down to the budget if the caller asks for more; (4) build parallelism = min(nproc, floor(budget_gb / per_job_peak_rss_gb)); (5) heavy work MUST be wrapped in a bounded execution scope so the kernel OOM-kills only the scope and user@<uid>.service stays alive.
  - No operator-facing override flag exists; bypassing it is the bluff the 11.4 covenant prohibits.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** No operator-facing override flag exists (no flag names given).
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4

#### §12.10 — Continuation document, sacred invariant
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:679-719
- **Rules:**
  - A single canonical machine-readable handoff document docs/CONTINUATION.md MUST always reflect live project state so any agent (human, Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, Codex, Gemini CLI, any LLM) can resume exactly where the previous session left off by reading this one file.
  - (1) docs/CONTINUATION.md MUST exist at the project root; absence is a release blocker.
  - (2) Every non-trivial state change MUST update it in the same commit as the work.
  - (3) Top-of-file timestamp updated on every edit; stale timestamps trigger gate failure.
  - (4) Section 3 "Active work" lists every IN PROGRESS/BLOCKED item with enough detail to resume without conversation context (concrete commands, file paths, monitor IDs).
  - (5) Section 0 "How to use this document" contains the verbatim resumption prompt, a single block pasteable into any CLI agent.
  - (6) Document MUST be self-contained; no hyperlinks to ephemeral external systems as the only source of truth.
  - No operator-facing override flag for the existence requirement.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** No operator-facing override flag exists (no flag names given).
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** none cited

#### §12.11 — Maximal dynamic resource utilization for containerized builds
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:721-739
- **Rules:**
  - Reconciliation: the 12.6 60% ceiling and the consuming project's bare-metal -j cap REMAIN for any heavy work inside user@<uid>.service / user.slice (shares session OOM fate). A build in its OWN container cgroup with its OWN MemoryMax (rootless-Podman sanctioned containerized build) is a different accounting domain; the container OOM-kills itself, not the session, so a high envelope is host-safe by construction.
  - For the containerized build path ONLY, use the maximal SAFE fraction of host capacity, computed dynamically per host; NOT a fixed low -j, NOT clamped to the 12.6 60% figure.
  - (1) Auto-detect host capacity, never hardcode: read real nproc, MemTotal, SwapTotal, and hard process/thread rlimit (RLIMIT_NPROC / ulimit -Hu) at launch; a launcher printing an unmeasured envelope violates 11.4.6.
  - (2) Reserve explicit host headroom (cores AND RAM): all capacity MINUS a reserved slice for the operator's live session; headroom explicit and captured in the printed envelope; preserves 12.6's spirit without its 60% number.
  - (3) -j scales nproc-awarely, not just memory-awarely: respect BOTH the memory governor floor((container_mem_gb - build_constant_overhead_gb) / per_job_peak_rss_gb) AND the process/thread rlimit (exceeding RLIMIT_NPROC causes EAGAIN fork storms that wedge the build). Where hard nproc is too low, either (a) run at the proven-safe lower -j, OR (b) on a privileged path raise the rlimit (e.g. prlimit) and drop back to the unprivileged uid (e.g. setpriv) before launching so the container keeps rootless identity; launcher MUST print which mode it chose.
  - (4) Caps REMAIN for bare-metal/user.slice path: 12.6's 60% ceiling and the bare-metal -j cap are not relaxed for any work inside user@<uid>.service; a bare-metal heavy build must not claim the 12.11 envelope; 12.11 SCOPES 12.6, does not weaken it.
  - (5) Never break, bottleneck, or get stuck: reserved headroom genuinely free (verifiable post-launch: session memory-available stays above reserved floor), no swap-thrash inside the container (bound MemorySwapMax), do not exceed process rlimit; maximal-SAFE not maximal-reckless.
  - (6) Evidence-based tuning (11.4.6 + 11.4.24): envelope driven by captured host metrics and the build's resource profile; a bigger -j without captured headroom evidence violates 11.4.6 and 12.11(5); when in doubt the reserved-headroom floor wins.
  - Reference implementation (ATMOSphere): scripts/build_maxres.sh over scripts/build_containerized.sh; reserves fixed core count + RAM floor (e.g. 72% MemTotal to container, clamped so a fixed-GiB slice stays free), computes JOBS_MEM, governs -j against real hard nproc (unprivileged -> proven-no-EAGAIN count; privileged root re-exec raises RLIMIT_NPROC via prlimit then setpriv-drops to the unprivileged uid -> -j = min(cpus, JOBS_MEM)); --dry-run prints full envelope and launches nothing.
  - Classification universal. Gates: CM-COVENANT-12-11-PROPAGATION (literal 12.11 across CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/QWEN.md/GEMINI.md); recommended CM-MAXRES-DYNAMIC-BUILD (launcher (a) auto-detects nproc/MemTotal/RLIMIT_NPROC, (b) reserves headroom, (c) governs -j against memory model AND process rlimit, (d) prints the envelope, (e) does not hardcode a fixed low -j for the containerized path AND does not relax 12.6 for any user.slice path); paired mutations (strip 12.11 literal; hardcode -j2 or strip rlimit-aware governor). Gate code a separate work item.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-12-11-PROPAGATION, CM-MAXRES-DYNAMIC-BUILD
- **No escape hatch:** --fixed-jobs, --no-dynamic-detection, --ignore-host-capacity, --relax-user-slice-cap, --bare-metal-maximal
- **Honest boundary:** "Maximal" means maximal-safe: an envelope that wedges the host is a violation. 12.11 grants the large envelope only across the container-cgroup boundary and never weakens 12.6 for user.slice work.
- **Composes:** §12.1, §12.2, §12.3, §12.6, §12.10, §11.4.6, §11.4.24, §11.4.133, §9.2, §11.4.35

#### §12.12 — Process/thread-limit (RLIMIT_NPROC) awareness for parallel subagent/multi-process work
- **Source:** host-and-resource-safety.md:741-761
- **Rules:**
  - The limit: parallel subagent/multi-process work is bounded by the OS per-user process/thread limit `ulimit -u` (RLIMIT_NPROC), which on Linux counts ALL threads AND processes of the real UID (not per-process). Ambient tooling (MCP servers, language runtime worker pools, mongod/chrome/prisma-class servers, local LLM servers) consumes a large FIXED fraction before project work starts. Reason: a host at `ulimit -u 4096` sat at ~3900-4005 threads from ambient MCP alone; a 4th Go-heavy subagent (GOMAXPROCS=nproc) hit EAGAIN / `failed to create new OS thread (errno=11)`; stopping three non-essential MCP servers freed ~1345 threads (3827 -> 2482).
  - Mandate: BEFORE scaling to N parallel subagents/processes the agent MUST check thread headroom and treat thread-limit exhaustion as a §12 host-safety event that YIELDS UNCONDITIONALLY, same standing as §12.6 (memory) and §12.7 (AOSP -j cap). It is an ORTHOGONAL exhaustion axis to §12.6: both MUST be checked independently.
  - Diagnosis (mandatory before scaling): `ulimit -u` (soft) + `ulimit -Hu` (hard) + LIVE count `ps -L --no-headers -u "$USER" | wc -l` (threads, not just processes); headroom = soft limit minus live count.
  - Exhaustion signals (captured, never guessed, §11.4.6): EAGAIN, `fork: retry: Resource temporarily unavailable`, `failed to create new OS thread`, or `cannot allocate memory` from a fork/clone/thread-spawn call; DISTINCT from OOM and MUST NOT be conflated.
  - When headroom is low the agent MUST SERIALIZE (fewer concurrent subagents/processes) and avoid Go-heavy / GOMAXPROCS=nproc-class spikes; dispatching parallel work blind at near-limit headroom is forbidden (a subagent hitting EAGAIN mid-operation, e.g. mid-`git push`, risks incomplete/corrupted state, §9.2).
  - Raising the limit, three techniques (cite the mechanism used, never guess): (a) no-restart on a running process: `prlimit --pid <PID> --nproc=<soft>:<hard>` (requires root, e.g. via `su -c`) to raise the HARD limit; new children inherit; (b) persistent system-wide: `/etc/security/limits.conf` (`<user> hard nproc <N>` + matching `soft` line) or systemd `LimitNPROC=<N>`, effective NEXT login/session; (c) self-raise within current session: raise own SOFT limit up to existing HARD limit via `ulimit -u <N>` where N <= hard; can NEVER exceed hard ceiling without method (a).
  - Caveat (§11.4.6): `su -c "ulimit -u N"` sets the limit ONLY inside that transient subshell, does NOT retroactively affect a running session; a running process keeps the RLIMIT_NPROC captured at its launch.
  - Freeing threads is operator-authorized only (§11.4.122): stopping non-essential MCP servers/background tooling REQUIRES explicit operator authorization; the agent MUST NOT autonomously kill operator tooling without asking.
  - Self-kill hazard: `pkill -f <pattern>` / `pgrep -f <pattern>` match the FULL command line including the killer's own invocation if the pattern appears in it; any cmdline-pattern-based kill list MUST explicitly exclude the caller's own `$$` / `$PPID` (and the conductor's PID when dispatched as a subagent) before executing.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies ambient-tooling roster and ulimit values per §11.4.35.
  - Recommended gate behaviour: parallel-dispatch orchestration checks `ulimit -u` + live thread count BEFORE scaling concurrency; a cmdline-pattern kill helper excludes the caller's own PID. Paired §1.1 mutation: strip the `12.12` literal -> propagation gate FAILs; strip headroom-check call before a scale-up or remove the self-PID exclusion -> headroom gate FAILs; gate-code = a separate tracked work item.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker regardless of context.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-12-12-PROPAGATION, CM-NPROC-HEADROOM-CHECK
- **No escape hatch:** --ignore-thread-limit, --dispatch-blind, --skip-headroom-check, --autonomous-tooling-kill, --assume-ulimit-scope
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §12, §12.6, §12.7, §11.4.58, §11.4.103, §11.4.101, §11.4.122, §9.2, §11.4.6, §11.4.17, §11.4.35, §1.1

### Multi-track and parallelism (13 anchors)

#### §11.4.103 — Continuous parallel-stream working routine (main stream FREE, >=3 background streams, auto-backfill)
- **Source:** multi-track-and-parallelism.md:3-35
- **Rules:**
  - Standing default working routine, not a per-request opt-in. Promotes the multi-stream pattern; binds §11.4.87/.88/.89/.94/.96 into one always-on routine.
  - (A) Main stream stays FREE: every commit AND every push MUST run detached in the background (`nohup ... > <log> 2>&1 &` + `disown`, per §11.4.88). Main stream MUST NOT block on a commit landing or a push/mirror completing; once the local commit is durable it returns to the priority queue. Blocking on a push is a violation.
  - (B) Whenever the queue holds three or more non-contending actionable items, MUST run at least THREE parallel background streams alongside the main stream (subagent-driven per §11.4.70/.20, isolated per §11.4.58 PWU worktree model + §11.4.84 quiescence).
  - (B) Auto-backfill: the moment any stream is FULLY done (item closed with anti-bluff evidence per (E), or merged) a new stream MUST IMMEDIATELY start, claiming the next-highest-priority non-contending item; the active-stream count NEVER drops below 3 while actionable items remain. Dropping below 3 while 3+ disjoint actionable items wait, or serialising parallelisable work, is a violation. Count may fall below 3 ONLY when no non-contending actionable items remain OR every remaining item is externally blocked (§11.4.94/.97/.101). Upper bounds: §12.6 60% memory ceiling and §11.4.58 6-concurrent-agent cap (standing band 3-6 background streams).
  - (C) Streams filled in strict priority order: most-critical and most-user-visible first; audio fixes always apex priority (§11.4.72); research/refactor/low-stakes only after the critical set is dispatched (§11.4.42).
  - (D) While a heavy build (containerised AOSP rebuild §12.9, or any heavy `gradle`/`m -j` build) is in flight, streams MUST restrict to the §11.4.96 SAFE catalogue (investigation/forensics, docs, test-authoring, gate + paired-mutation authoring, read-only on-device probes, submodule edits, web research, workable-items DB ops, backgrounded pre-build/meta-test runs). MUST NOT launch a second `gradle`/`m -j`/containerised build concurrently (§12.8, §12.7 OOM cascade). UNSAFE-during-build ops (§11.4.96 (alpha)-(theta)) deferred to between-build windows.
  - (E) Every item closed by a parallel stream MUST carry real captured evidence: root cause proven or marked `UNCONFIRMED:`/`UNKNOWN:`/`PENDING_FORENSICS:` (§11.4.6), captured evidence (§11.4.5/.69), determinism (§11.4.50), paired §1.1 mutations, §11.4.102 investigation on any problem. Closing on metadata-only/config-only/absence-of-error/grep-without-runtime evidence is a PASS-bluff.
  - (F) Idle ONLY when every queued item is genuinely blocked on an external result it cannot accelerate (hardware, network upstream, in-flight build/test/push) OR operator STOP OR §12 host-safety demands it. "Nothing visible to do" with progressable non-contending items is never valid; posing a question and idling while non-blocked items remain is a violation; an unavoidable block parks one work unit, not the loop (§11.4.101).
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17); non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-103-PROPAGATION (literal `11.4.103` across consumer CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/QWEN.md; paired §1.1 mutation strips literal -> FAIL; gate-code separate work item)
- **No escape hatch:** --block-main-stream, --synchronous-commit, --synchronous-push, --single-stream-only, --skip-parallel-streams, --serialise-actionable-work, --idle-without-queue-survey
- **Honest boundary:** none stated beyond (D)/(F) limits and the §12.6/§11.4.58 upper bounds; gate-code is a separate work item.
- **Composes:** §11.4.58, §11.4.70, §11.4.20, §11.4.72, §11.4.87, §11.4.88, §11.4.89, §11.4.94, §11.4.96, §11.4.97, §11.4.101, §11.4.102, §11.4.42, §11.4.84, §11.4.4(b), §12.6, §12.7, §12.8, §12.9, §9.2, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.167 — Big-work-item feature work-stream lifecycle (own CoW project copy, own branch/tags, no merge until approved, trunk merged in)
- **Source:** multi-track-and-parallelism.md:39-155
- **Rules:**
  - Every BIG work item (new feature or drastic/large fix) MUST be developed as its own isolated feature work-stream: own full project copy in a sibling directory, own feature branch, own per-feature flashable builds + feature release tags, separate from trunk until manually approved after testing, trunk regularly merged INTO every stream.
  - (A) One big item = one stream in a sibling copy (`<project>`, `<project>_<slug-1>`, ...), `<slug>` lowercase per §11.4.29. Trunk copy is canonical `main`. Small changes stay on trunk; big-item threshold is the project's own (§11.4.35).
  - (B) Disk-feasible duplication MANDATORY, naive copies FORBIDDEN: copy MUST use a near-zero-disk mechanism (reflink/CoW clone `cp -a --reflink=auto` / snapshot on btrfs/XFS/ZFS/APFS; elsewhere a shared-object-store mechanism e.g. `git worktree` + externalized build output + sparse). Full deep copy or full `git clone` per stream of a large tree is FORBIDDEN where it would exhaust free space. Mechanism MUST be verified to consume ~0 disk for a fresh stream with captured evidence (§11.4.69) before reliance. Build output (`out/`-class) MUST be per-stream and excluded from the CoW clone; one shared compiler cache (ccache-class) across streams.
  - (C) Own `feature/<slug>` branch; per-feature builds tagged with a scheme embedding the slug, e.g. `<base-version>-feat-<slug>[-<iter>]`, `<iter>` monotonic per §11.4.54 (composes §11.4.151). The feature branch is NEVER merged to trunk until the operator manually approves after testing: requires §11.4.40 full-suite retest GREEN on a clean target, then §11.4.41 merge-first integration, then §11.4.113 ff-only (no-force) merge.
  - (D) Trunk MUST be merged INTO every live feature stream frequently (at minimum after every trunk tag / daily); `git merge`, never rebase a shared/tagged branch. A stream not synced within the cadence is flagged stale.
  - (E) Branching AND tagging cascade to ALL submodules the moment a submodule is modified: it gets its own `feature/<slug>` branch; per-feature tags mirrored on EVERY touched submodule at same HEAD and ff-only-pushed to all owned remotes (§11.4.113). Untouched submodules stay trunk-pinned. Merge-to-trunk applies same cascade. Worktree-submodule path is a documented hazard; CoW-clone preferred.
  - (F) Single-builder host: feature builds MUST QUEUE (FIFO + advisory lock; §11.4.58 L1/§12.7/§12.8), never contend. Finite devices: per-device exclusive ownership (§11.4.119) serialises tests; excess streams queue. Build queue MUST garbage-collect idle streams' regenerable build output (§11.4.77).
  - (G) Every change in any stream crosses the full gauntlet: independent code review (§11.4.142/.125/.134), multi-angle impact research (§11.4.145), anti-bluff captured-evidence testing (§11.4/.5/.69/.107). A stream is NOT a quality carve-out.
  - (H) Stream registry (single source of "is this stream owed?", §11.4.116/.147) tracks branch, base tag, build/out state, last-trunk-merge, merge-approval state. Creation atomic-on-success (clone to `.partial`, rename on success) and resumable (§11.4.84 quiescence on resume). Retiring a stream requires §9.2 pre-op backup + a guard that feature work is merged/approved (unmerged work blocks auto-deletion). §12 and the 60% memory ceiling (§12.6) bound clone + build.
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies filesystem/CoW mechanism, sibling-dir + tag naming, build/device queue counts, big-item threshold (§11.4.35). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-167-PROPAGATION, CM-FEATURE-WORKSTREAM-COW-CLONE, CM-FEATURE-WORKSTREAM-NO-MERGE-UNTIL-APPROVED, CM-FEATURE-WORKSTREAM-TRUNK-SYNC-CADENCE, CM-FEATURE-WORKSTREAM-SUBMODULE-CASCADE (paired §1.1 mutations: strip literal; create stream via full deep copy; merge feature with no approval marker; stale stream past cadence; modify submodule without its branch/tag -> respective gate FAILs; gate-code separate work item)
- **No escape hatch:** --full-clone-per-feature, --deep-copy-stream, --skip-cow-clone, --merge-feature-without-approval, --no-trunk-sync, --skip-submodule-cascade, --unbounded-parallel-builds, --shared-device-no-lock, --retire-unmerged-stream, --feature-stream-quality-carveout
- **Honest boundary:** guarantees isolation, disk-feasibility, greppable identity and controlled trunk-feature merge discipline; does NOT prove any stream's work correct (still §11.4.108 runtime-signature + §11.4.40 retest).
- **Composes:** §9, §9.2, §11.4.6, §11.4.17, §11.4.28, §11.4.29, §11.4.35, §11.4.40, §11.4.41, §11.4.54, §11.4.58, §11.4.66, §11.4.69, §11.4.71, §11.4.77, §11.4.84, §11.4.103, §11.4.108, §11.4.113, §11.4.116, §11.4.119, §11.4.125, §11.4.142, §11.4.145, §11.4.147, §11.4.151, §12, §12.6, §12.7, §12.8, §12.9, §1.1

#### §11.4.176 — Conflict-free multi-track work-division + exactly-once claim registry + capability-aware deadlock-proof device-lock
- **Source:** multi-track-and-parallelism.md:157
- **Rules:**
  - Applies when multiple concurrent tracks (§11.4.167, §11.4.58/.103) share a pool of workable items and a scarce pool of exclusive hardware; two arbitration layers are MANDATORY, conflict-free by construction not convention. Reasons: prevent multiple tracks working the same item/logical group; no conflicts, race conditions, data corruption, codebase loss; deadlock-proof device locking.
  - (A) Work-item layer: every item, OR every logical GROUP sharing files/subsystem/feature/schema, is assigned to AT MOST ONE track at a time.
  - (A1) Exactly-once: lock-arbitrated append-only claim registry (extends §11.4.147 + §11.4.116) records `claim(item|group, track, ts, ttl)`; a track MUST claim-before-touch; a second claim on a claimed item is DENIED.
  - (A2) Logical-group cohesion: items sharing file-scope/subsystem/feature/schema are one group claimed WHOLE by one track (§11.4.58 L3 disjoint file-scope is the enforcement).
  - (A3) Conflict-free by construction: disjoint file-scope partition (§11.4.58 L3) + per-track worktree/CoW isolation (§11.4.167).
  - (A4) No codebase loss: §9.2 hardlinked backups, §11.4.113 ff-only merge-onto-latest-main (NEVER force-push), §11.4.84 quiescence, §11.4.41 merge-first.
  - (A5) Anti-bluff: assignment and merge verifiable (registry event stream + captured merge evidence); results ALWAYS produced (a claimed-but-abandoned item's claim TTL-expires and returns to the pool, §11.4.147).
  - (B) Hardware layer: when N tracks outnumber M exclusive devices, exactly ONE track owns each device at a time (§11.4.119). A track leases ONE OR MORE devices selected by required CAPABILITY (pool records per-device capabilities; leases capability-matched; multi-device leases supported).
  - (B) Arbiter DEADLOCK-FREE by construction (all four Coffman conditions broken): hold-and-wait ELIMINATED (multi-device acquire all-or-nothing inside one critical section); circular-wait ELIMINATED (acquire NON-BLOCKING: wins whole set or returns EBUSY immediately); no-preemption RELAXED (lease TTL + heartbeat + reap, crashed holder's lease auto-expires, §11.4.147); only lock ever held is a short bounded flock over the atomic check-and-claim critical section, released before device work. Registry = append-only JSONL event stream + atomically-rewritten snapshot (§11.4.116).
  - (C) Both layers universal, decoupled, project-not-aware (§11.4.17/.28/.35): consumer injects claim-store, device pool, metric sources at runtime; nothing project-specific in canonical root. Resource-tuning (parallel-stream count, per-stream memory budget §12.6, device-lease breadth, build-queue depth §11.4.167) MUST be EVIDENCE-BASED from captured metrics (§11.4.24/.5), never guessed (§11.4.6).
  - Classification universal; non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-176-PROPAGATION, CM-WORK-DIVISION-EXCLUSIVE-CLAIM, CM-NO-CROSS-TRACK-SCOPE-OVERLAP, CM-LOGICAL-GROUP-COHESION, CM-DEVICE-LOCK-DEADLOCK-FREE (arbiter ships an all-or-nothing + non-blocking + TTL-reap stress/chaos proof with paired §1.1 mutation; gate-code separate work item)
- **No escape hatch:** --allow-cross-track-overlap, --skip-claim-registry, --split-logical-group, --blocking-device-acquire, --allow-partial-device-hold, --tune-resources-by-guess
- **Honest boundary:** none stated explicitly.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.17, §11.4.24, §11.4.28, §11.4.35, §11.4.41, §11.4.58, §11.4.84, §11.4.85, §11.4.103, §11.4.113, §11.4.116, §11.4.119, §11.4.147, §11.4.167, §12.6, §9.2

#### §11.4.178 — Track-qualified identity for parallel work streams (session-name collision ban)
- **Source:** multi-track-and-parallelism.md:159
- **Rules:**
  - Parallel work streams sharing hardware, a git backing store, a tmux/session namespace, a lock namespace, or any single-owner resource MUST be addressed by a TRACK-QUALIFIED identity `<project>__<track>__<role>`, NEVER a bare directory basename (reason: checkouts sharing a basename collapse into one session/lock/log key and cross-wire tmux targets, locks, device claims, log dirs).
  - Every registry row, session name, lock path, log directory, and device claim MUST carry the track-qualified key; a bare-basename identity for a resource with >= 2 concurrent claimants is a violation.
  - Multi-project-per-track layout (2026-07-10): a `/mnt/track<N>` parent is NOT single-project; multiple projects coexist, each in its own subdirectory `/mnt/track<N>/<project_name>/` (project's canonical lowercase snake_case name per §11.4.29); the per-track working copy of project P on track N is ALWAYS `/mnt/track<N>/<project_name>/`, never the bare track root and never a shared basename.
  - A project adopting this constitution + multi-track engine (§11.4.187) MUST create AND register its own `/mnt/track<N>/<project_name>/` per track under its project-qualified identity; MUST NOT assume it owns the track root or that a track hosts only one project.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies `<project>`/`<track>`/`<role>` vocabulary (§11.4.35). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-178-PROPAGATION, CM-TRACK-QUALIFIED-IDENTITY (every session name/lock path/log dir/device claim for a multi-claimant resource carries the track-qualified key; paired §1.1 mutation: bare basename -> FAIL; strip literal -> FAIL; gate-code separate work item)
- **No escape hatch:** --bare-basename-ok, --skip-track-qualifier, --shared-session-name
- **Honest boundary:** a unique identity prevents cross-wiring; it does not itself arbitrate ownership (that is §11.4.119 + §11.4.176).
- **Composes:** §11.4.111, §11.4.119, §11.4.176, §11.4.29, §11.4.58, §11.4.187, §11.4.35, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.182 — Track+branch work-stream identity label (T<N>/<branch> - alias - model - effort) on every agent/subagent/work-stream label
- **Source:** multi-track-and-parallelism.md:161 (base anchor) and :256 (2026-07-26 model/effort-in-label extension, which cites and extends this anchor)
- **Rules:**
  - (1) Every agent/subagent/work-stream label AND every operator-facing reference to a work stream (dispatch descriptions, status reports, resume/handoff docs, progress lines) MUST START with the prefix `(T<N>/<branch> - <alias>)`: `<N>` track number, `<branch>` git branch, `<alias>` claude-toolkit alias in use; e.g. `(T1/main - claude1) ATM-312 ...`.
  - (2) Label is DERIVED, never typed from memory/guessed (§11.4.6): `<N>` from checkout path (`/mnt/track<N>/...`; honest `?` if not under a numbered track), `<branch>` from `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, `<alias>` from `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` basename `.claude-<alias>` (honest `?` when unset/non-matching). Consumer supplies a deterministic labeler (reference `scripts/multitrack/track_branch_label.sh`).
  - (3) Mechanical enforcement (§11.4.75/.109): PreToolUse guard hook (reference `constitution/scripts/hooks/guard-track-branch-label.sh`, inherited BY REFERENCE per §11.4.177, never copied) BLOCKS any Agent/Task/TaskCreate dispatch whose `description` (or `subagent` label) does not START with `^\(T[0-9]+/[^)]+\) `; non-agent tools pass through. Pre-build gate asserts labeler + hook exist, executable + parseable, hook wired in runtime settings, convention doc exists.
  - (4) A `?` in the track OR alias field is a valid honest label; enforced FORMAT is numeric-track `[0-9]+`, so a dispatch from a non-track checkout is surfaced (blocked) not silently mislabeled.
  - TRUNK RULE (2026-07-28): work on canonical trunk (`main`/`master`) is ALWAYS Track 1 - label reads `(T1/main - ...)`, NEVER `(T?/main - ...)`, regardless of checkout path. BRANCH decides first; checkout path decides only for non-trunk branches; labeler derives branch BEFORE track number and maps `main|master -> 1`. Labels MUST be re-derived from the script at dispatch time and kept in real-time sync with live branch/alias/model/effort; a remembered or stale label is itself a violation.
  - EXTENSION (1) LABEL FORM: extended to `(T<N>/<branch> - <alias> - <model> - <effort>)`; `<model>` = model CURRENTLY answering for that alias. Native Claude alias: SHORT name (`opus`/`sonnet`/`haiku`/`fable`, case-insensitive-substring-derived from the model id the platform reports for the most recent turn, obtained live at emission). Provider alias (`deepseek`, `xiaomi`, `kimi-for-coding`, `opencode`, ...): the REAL provider model id from that provider's host-config registry (same value the alias launch mechanism uses, single source of truth).
  - EXTENSION (2) MODEL DERIVATION (never guessed): closed two-case split on `<alias>` shape: native -> read model id from CURRENT session's own transcript (LAST assistant-turn's reported model -> short name); provider -> read from host multi-account-toolkit provider registry (`CMA_PROVIDER_MODEL`). Unresolvable lookup yields honest `?`, never a fabricated/last-known value; an obtained id matching none of the four short-names is printed VERBATIM. The 3-field legacy form remains VALID/ACCEPTED during migration; guard `LABEL_RE` admits both forms and NEVER treats an honest `?` model or absent model field as a block-cause.
  - EXTENSION (3) FLAWLESS ALIAS/PROVIDER<->MODEL CONSISTENCY: the alias/provider field and `<model>` MUST be mutually consistent AT ALL TIMES: model shown MUST genuinely belong to the alias/provider shown, and alias name MUST be current; guaranteed by construction (model read from THAT alias's own live transcript / THAT provider's own registry entry). A derivation emitting a model not belonging to the shown alias is a violation.
  - EXTENSION (4) REAL-TIME ALWAYS-IN-SYNC (§11.4.229/§11.4.106(F)): label is STATELESS and RE-COMPUTED at EVERY emission (every labeler run and every PreToolUse guard firing on Agent/Task/TaskCreate) against LIVE environment (current `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, session id, transcript tail, provider `.env`), so a mid-session model switch is reflected in the very next emission.
  - EXTENSION (5) HONEST SUBAGENT-INTROSPECTION LIMIT: native-alias transcript lookup is proven reliable from the DISPATCHING process's shell (guard-hook context); NOT proven when a background subagent introspects its own model in its own subprocess where it shares the parent's transcript with no subagent-vs-conductor marker - recorded as an open limitation to be tracked (§11.4.197), never claimed solved.
  - EXTENSION (6) DIVERGENT-LABELER RECONCILIATION (§11.4.227): the LIVE labeler wired via `.claude/settings.json` is `constitution/scripts/multitrack/track_branch_label.sh`; top-level `scripts/multitrack/` is a thin pass-through wrapper that `exec`s the canonical copy (§11.4.177), so it cannot drift; reconciliation landed in commit `a48e919f52d` and is gate-enforced at `pre_build_verification.sh:41911-41915` (gate follows the `exec` wrapper).
  - EXTENSION (7) EFFORT FIELD: 5-field label appends `<effort>` from closed set `{low | medium | high | xhigh | max}` (same ladder as §11.4.231(F)). (a) read from whatever LIVE effort signal the path exposes (Workflow-tool `agent()` `effort` argument, a future Agent-tool effort parameter, env/config setting); no signal or value outside the set -> honest `?`, never fabricated. (b) The Claude Code Agent tool exposes `model` but NO `effort` parameter so subagent effort degrades to `?` there; Workflow `agent()` does take `effort`. (c) 3-field and 4-field forms remain VALID; `LABEL_RE` admits all three shapes and NEVER treats absent or `?` effort as a block-cause. (d) effort is selected TOGETHER WITH model by §11.4.231 and never contradicts it; a stale effort beside a fresh model, or effort outside the closed set, is a violation. (e) effort is stateless and recomputed at every emission.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies track-root layout, labeler, hook wiring, governance-file set (§11.4.35). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-182-PROPAGATION (literal `11.4.182` across consumer fleet), CM-TRACK-BRANCH-LABEL (extended to assert labeler emits parseable `<model>` AND `<effort>`, guard accepts 3/4/5-field forms, alias/provider<->model consistency holds). Paired §1.1 mutations: strip hook prefix-check -> hook test-suite FAILs; strip literal -> propagation FAILs; strip `<model>` derivation or emit a model not belonging to shown alias -> extended gate FAILs; gate-code separate work item, NOT claimed shipped.
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-track-label, --unlabeled-agent-OK, --bare-work-stream-reference, --no-track-branch-prefix, --label-from-memory (the existing list applies unchanged to the extended label)
- **Honest boundary:** `?` in a field is a valid honest label, not a bluff. The live label has no persisted artifact, so Docs-Chain (§11.4.106) does not apply to it; any PERSISTED label-history/model-switch log is a tracked §11.4.197 follow-up, never faked as shipped. The extension does not re-mint the anchor (no second block-start per §11.4.227(B)).
- **Composes:** §11.4.178, §11.4.29, §11.4.75, §11.4.109, §11.4.177, §11.4.6, §11.4.58, §11.4.103, §11.4.119, §11.4.116, §11.4.147, §11.4.231, §11.4.209, §11.4.211, §11.4.229, §11.4.106, §11.4.208, §11.4.197, §11.4.227

#### §11.4.183 — Maximal multi-agent utilization per work-stream + full-constitution-application + zero-bluff mandate
- **Source:** multi-track-and-parallelism.md:163
- **Rules:**
  - Every track/work-stream MUST maximize multi-agent working approaches (subagent-driven, independent review agents, parallel background streams with auto-backfill, every other applicable agent form) so every track produces the most completed work at highest quality in least time.
  - (1) Maximize agent utilization per track: every track (main + every parallel background stream per §11.4.58/.103) MUST default to subagent-driven execution for non-trivial work (§11.4.20/.70); dispatch independent review agents structurally separated from the author (§11.4.125/.142/.165, iterated to clean GO per §11.4.134); use every other applicable specialised-agent form; never one monolithic foreground agent doing everything a task naturally decomposes into.
  - (2) Full-constitution application: every track MUST apply the ENTIRE constitution (every universal rule, mandatory constraint, guide, derived technology: gates, mutation pairs, sync engines, recording/evidence pipelines, lock/claim registries). No rule may be silently ignored, skipped, avoided or judged less relevant; partial application is itself a violation equal in severity to skipping a mandated gate.
  - (3) Zero-bluff: NEVER false/faulty results, untested/unverified work, or bluff of any kind on any track; BINDS the §11.4 anti-bluff covenant (§11.4/.1/.2/.5/.6/.7/.50/.69/.107) as an unconditional per-track invariant: every "done" carries captured evidence (§11.4.5/.69/.107), every gate/mutation pair genuinely falsifiable (§1.1), no track reports progress it did not perform (§11.4.126).
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies track layout, subagent runtime, review-agent roster (§11.4.35). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-183-PROPAGATION, CM-MAX-AGENTS-PER-TRACK (every active track shows subagent/review-agent dispatch evidence for non-trivial work, not solitary foreground execution); paired §1.1 mutations (strip literal; record a track skipping dispatch for non-trivial work with no genuine single-agent justification); gate-code separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --single-agent-OK, --skip-review-agents, --partial-constitution-application, --serialise-parallelisable-work
- **Honest boundary:** "maximize agents" is bounded by §12.6 60% host-memory ceiling, §11.4.58 parallel-agent cap, genuine parallelizability, and §11.4.119 single-resource-owner; contending, redundant or non-parallelizable agents are NOT maximization; bar is maximum USEFUL parallel throughput, never raw agent count.
- **Composes:** §11.4.20, §11.4.58, §11.4.70, §11.4.92, §11.4.94, §11.4.97, §11.4.103, §11.4.119, §11.4.125, §11.4.126, §11.4.134, §11.4.142, §11.4.165, §12.6

#### §11.4.187 — Automatic multi-track ruler orchestration (inherited, out-of-the-box conductor spawning headless per-track workers)
- **Source:** multi-track-and-parallelism.md:165
- **Rules:**
  - Every project MUST ship multi-track orchestration as a UNIVERSAL, AUTOMATIC, OUT-OF-THE-BOX, INHERITED capability (not per-project reimplementation) via a single conductor session that programmatically SPAWNS, DRIVES, RESUMES, MONITORS, CONTROLS per-track headless workers.
  - (1) Headless spawn: workers launch via native headless `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose`; worker `session_id` captured from the FIRST `init` event (never invented); success/failure read from the terminal event's `result.is_error`, NEVER the process exit code; continuation uses `--resume <session_id>` from the SAME cwd + env as the spawn.
  - (2) Per-subscription auth + rate-limit fallback: every spawn `unset`s ambient `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and sets the selected alias's `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`/`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; on a captured rate-limit signature (`isApiErrorMessage`+`apiErrorStatus:429`, quota-exhausted vs transient distinguished by evidence) the ruler REBINDS the track onto the next healthy alias (cross-track reuse permitted), falls back to a provider alias where configured, and bounded-parks (§11.4.101) rather than hanging when all aliases are cooled.
  - (3) Crash-resilient ruler self-supervisor: ruler's own state (per-track alias/session_id/worktree/last-verdict) persisted durably (write-temp-then-rename, NEVER tmpfs) so an external watchdog detects a dead ruler PID and re-hydrates every track binding from durable state + §11.4.116 event stream (§11.4.147 at ruler layer).
  - (4) Idempotent bootstrap + auto-install + conductor-stays-home: one idempotent bootstrap command wires the system (cwd-hook install, config validation, reconciliation), auto-invoked on every constitution pull via §11.4.164 `post_update_hook.sh`; the `conductor:`-designated alias/session is NEVER bound into a track worktree (resolver returns nothing) so the conductor runs from the main checkout.
  - (5) Project-agnostic engine, consumer-owned data: whole mechanism (config loader, alias->worktree resolver, cwd-hook, bind/fallback/cooldown orchestrator, session launcher, rate-limit monitor, supervisor) lives at `constitution/scripts/multitrack/`, inherited BY REFERENCE (§11.4.28(B)/§11.4.177), NO project literal; consumer supplies per-host `config/multitrack/<hostname>.yaml` (tracks/mounts/serials/aliases/conductor) as DATA, never an engine edit.
  - Anti-bluff (§11.4/.108): every piece carries four-layer coverage (pre-build gate + on-host test + paired §1.1 mutation + captured evidence §11.4.69), each fix declares a runtime signature verified on a clean host.
  - Classification universal; non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-187-PROPAGATION, CM-MULTITRACK-ENGINE-IN-CONSTITUTION (scripts present under `constitution/scripts/multitrack/`, no project literal, `bash -n`+`sh -n` clean per §11.4.67), CM-MULTITRACK-AUTOINSTALL-WIRED, CM-MULTITRACK-BOOTSTRAP-IDEMPOTENT, CM-MULTITRACK-BIND-ON-START, CM-MULTITRACK-FALLBACK-MONITOR, CM-MULTITRACK-HEADLESS-SPAWN, CM-MULTITRACK-RULER-SUPERVISOR (paired §1.1 mutation: strip literal; re-introduce a project literal or downgrade rebind to exit-code success detection -> gate FAILs)
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-multitrack, --manual-multitrack-only, --no-auto-install, --per-project-reimpl-OK, --exit-code-is-success-signal
- **Honest boundary:** mandates the MECHANISM; genuine per-subscription quota-isolation proof requires live tokens exercising real rate-limit boundaries (operator-scheduled live acceptance window); a mock-driven GREEN proves the spawn/resume/fallback CONTRACT, never live-quota behaviour, and the two are never conflated.
- **Composes:** §11.4.20, §11.4.28, §11.4.58, §11.4.70, §11.4.101, §11.4.103, §11.4.111, §11.4.116, §11.4.119, §11.4.126, §11.4.128, §11.4.131, §11.4.147, §11.4.164, §11.4.167, §11.4.176, §12.6, §12.8, §11.4.177, §11.4.67, §11.4.69, §11.4.108, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.191 — Work-to-track/branch binding enforcement (a logic-group's work never committed or dispatched on the wrong track/branch)
- **Source:** multi-track-and-parallelism.md:167
- **Rules:**
  - Every logical group of workable items binds to EXACTLY ONE canonical `(track, branch)` recorded ONCE in the single source of truth (§11.4.93 workable-items DB: `logic_groups.destination` = authoritative branch + `canonical_track` column + `group_paths` file-scope manifest). NO change belonging to a group may LAND on, nor be DISPATCHED to, a different track/branch. File-scope generalisation of §11.4.181/.182 from branch-NAME to work-PLACEMENT consistency (reason: committing onto an existing branch is not a branch CREATE, so no gate checked which files land on which branch).
  - (1) Single source of truth: the `logic_group -> (branch, track, path-globs)` binding recorded once in the DB and LOOKED UP, never re-invented (placing a group's file-scope on a non-canonical branch/track is a §11.4.6 violation).
  - (2) Preventive hook (§11.4.109/.177): PreToolUse guard `guard-work-track-binding.sh` (inherited BY REFERENCE, never copied) BLOCKS (exit 2) a git-commit-class Bash call whose to-be-committed file set contains a path owned by a group whose canonical branch/track differs from the current checkout, AND BLOCKS an Agent/Task dispatch whose §11.4.182 label track/branch differs from the canonical (track, branch) of the ticket's group; fail-closed on unreadable registry; `# guardrails:allow <reason>` is the audited escape.
  - (3) Detective gate (§11.4.110/.108): `CM-WORK-TRACK-BINDING-ENFORCED` asserts on `merge-base(HEAD,main)..HEAD` that every `group_paths`-owned file's group destination equals current branch (and canonical_track equals current track when pinned); runtime signature FAIL-on-wrong-placement / PASS-on-canonical-placement on a clean checkout.
  - (4) Risk-free reconciliation (§9.2/.113/.84): a mis-placed change is reconciled by MERGING its commits onto the group's canonical branch (union, no commit lost, no `-s ours`/reset), ff-only push to all upstreams (NEVER force-push), then removing it from the wrong branch only after the merge is confirmed on all mirrors.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies `(track, branch)` map, `group_paths` seed, commit-wrapper wiring (§11.4.35). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-191-PROPAGATION, CM-WORK-TRACK-BINDING-ENFORCED (paired §1.1 mutation)
- **No escape hatch:** --allow-cross-track-commit, --skip-work-binding, --commit-any-branch-OK, --dispatch-any-track-OK, --no-file-scope-check
- **Honest boundary:** none stated beyond the fail-closed/audited-escape behaviour.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.28, §11.4.29, §11.4.35, §11.4.58, §11.4.75, §11.4.84, §11.4.93, §11.4.95, §11.4.109, §11.4.110, §11.4.113, §11.4.119, §11.4.167, §11.4.176, §11.4.177, §11.4.178, §11.4.181, §11.4.182, §9.2

#### §11.4.192 — Continuous multi-track auto-backfill (a FREE track is immediately re-assigned its next domain work-set)
- **Source:** multi-track-and-parallelism.md:169
- **Rules:**
  - The moment any track's worker COMPLETES its current work-set (items closed with anti-bluff evidence, or merged), that FREE track MUST be IMMEDIATELY assigned the NEXT-highest-priority actionable work-set from its OWN domain (its §11.4.191 logic_group / canonical branch). A track is NEVER idle while its domain holds actionable items; the conductor/ruler continuously re-assigns with no stopping. Promotes §11.4.103(B) (stream backfill) into the multi-track layer (track backfill, keyed to canonical (track, branch) domain).
  - (1) On completion the conductor/ruler (§11.4.187) MUST look up the next actionable work-set for that track's domain, CLAIM it exactly-once (§11.4.176), and DISPATCH it as the track's new §11.4.182-labelled work stream, without waiting for a scheduled wake or operator prompt.
  - (2) Priority: the track domain's highest-priority actionable item (§11.4.42/.72, audio-first where in scope), never an arbitrary pick.
  - (3) Source-side advances even when validation is gated: when the next item's on-device validation is blocked on pending build/device availability (§11.4.108 clean-target / §11.4.185 manual-QA / operator-gated flash), the track MUST still advance SOURCE-SIDE work (investigation, RED-test §11.4.115, source patch, pre-build gate + paired §1.1 mutation, docs) and honestly SKIP-with-reason (§11.4.3/.52) ONLY the genuinely device-gated validation portion.
  - (4) A track idles ONLY when its domain has zero remaining actionable items OR every remaining item is externally blocked with no source-side advancement possible (§11.4.94(A)/.97/.101). "The merges are done" / "the current item is done" / "nothing visible right now" is NEVER a valid idle reason while progressable items exist. An unavoidable per-item block PARKS one item, not the track (§11.4.101).
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies track->domain map + priority source (§11.4.35). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-192-PROPAGATION, CM-CONTINUOUS-MULTITRACK-BACKFILL (a track with a completed worker AND remaining actionable domain items but no new dispatch -> FAIL; paired §1.1 mutation: let a free track idle, or treat "merges done" as valid idle reason; gate-code separate work item)
- **No escape hatch:** --allow-idle-track, --skip-backfill, --stop-multitrack, --merges-done-is-idle, --defer-track-reassign
- **Honest boundary:** a track idles only in the (4) closed set; "nothing visible" is never valid. Gate-code is a separate work item.
- **Composes:** §11.4.42, §11.4.58, §11.4.72, §11.4.94, §11.4.97, §11.4.101, §11.4.103, §11.4.167, §11.4.176, §11.4.178, §11.4.179, §11.4.182, §11.4.187, §11.4.191, §11.4.108, §11.4.115, §11.4.185, §11.4.3, §11.4.52

#### §11.4.230 — Parallelized-pipeline methodology (build/validate overlap, affected-stages-only re-run, parallel multi-device testing, fan-out subagents always, incremental delivery granularity with a declared QA-build cadence; clause (D) added 2026-10-04)
- **Source:** multi-track-and-parallelism.md:189-204 for clauses (A)-(C); clause (D): Constitution.md (constitution tip a71b1767) lines 10986-11004 (groups/ at this tip does not carry clause (D), see pin-upstream-findings.md)
- **Rules:**
  - Binds §11.4.58/.89/.103/.119/.128/.144 into one discipline and adds three invariants; a strengthening bind, never a weakening (parallelization capstone like §11.4.103).
  - (A) PIPELINE-OVERLAP: validation/verification MUST run CONCURRENTLY WITH the build wherever a stage does NOT depend on the build's own not-yet-produced artifact. Deploy the moment the build is done (build completion is the deploy trigger; §11.4.121, §11.4.108 ordering). WHILE a build runs, run in parallel per §11.4.96 SAFE catalogue: pre-build source-layer gates + meta-test mutation sweeps + coverage/clash checks (§11.4.110), independent code review on batch SOURCE (§11.4.125/.142/.194), doc/DB sync (§11.4.106), on-device validation of the PRIOR build (§11.4.119).
  - (A) On any NON-huge-blocker discovery the cycle MUST: (1) bump the version code (new distinctly-identifiable candidate; never reuse the failing artifact's id; §11.4.111, §11.4.200); (2) fix at proven root cause (§11.4.102 first, §11.4.115 RED on the broken artifact); (3) RE-RUN ONLY THE AFFECTED STAGES, parallelized (its own targeted validation FIRST per §11.4.130, then the affected regression set), NOT a serial restart of the entire cycle.
  - (A) Efficiency target: **4-5x reduction in time-to-a-manual-QA-capable-release** versus fully sequential, a MEASURED target tracked as build-and-validate wall-clock deltas (§11.4.24), never assumed.
  - (A) Honest boundary: current build's ARTIFACT-layer and RUNTIME-ON-CLEAN-TARGET validation (§11.4.108 layers 2/3) CANNOT precede its own artifact; a gate whose precondition is the build output belongs at a post-build seam (§11.4.120; §11.4.69 `artifact_not_yet_built`); only deploy-INDEPENDENT stages overlap; current-artifact validation begins the moment it exists, in parallel across devices per (B). Affected-stages-only is bounded to NON-huge-blocker discovery: a HUGE BLOCKER (release-blocking defect / cycle-invalidating regression / blast radius reaching other fixes) still triggers §11.4.129 STOP -> fix-all -> full RESTART (restart, never resume). Does NOT weaken §11.4.129, §11.4.40, §11.4.130, §11.4.132, §11.4.185.
  - (B) PARALLEL MULTI-DEVICE TESTING + RECORDING: every available reachable test device MUST be exercised CONCURRENTLY, one validation stream per device when independent, each stream the SINGLE EXCLUSIVE OWNER of that device's exclusive resources (§11.4.119; concurrent streams on same device read-only). Every device ALWAYS-RECORDED (§11.4.128, non-invasive, deterministic layout) and AVAILABILITY-FOLLOWED (§11.4.144: dropped device logs honest offline event + reconnect-and-resume, never silent corpus hole or faked continuity). Recording CAPTURE + ANALYSIS MUST be fanned out through a BOUNDED WORKER-POOL (Go worker-pool or equivalent), bounded by §12.6 memory + §12.12 thread headroom. Per-device PASS cites its own captured-evidence artefact (§11.4.5/.69/.107) on a CLEAN/fresh deployment (§11.4.108 runtime-signature, §11.4.200 per-device deployed-artifact identity); highest-risk/most-reopened cases (§11.4.132/.189) get deepest scrutiny FIRST on every device. Genuinely-shared exclusive resources (one HDMI/audio sink, one playback path) serialise per §11.4.119 even across devices.
  - (C) FAN-OUT-SUBAGENTS-ALWAYS: subagent fan-out (§11.4.20/.70, §11.4.187, §11.4.192) is the STANDING DEFAULT for EVERY genuinely-parallelizable effort (batch investigation, test/gate-authoring, per-device validation, per-PWU development §11.4.58, doc/research), not per-request opt-in and not reserved for big tasks. Running a parallelizable effort monolithically in the foreground when a fan-out path exists is a violation.
  - (C) Bounds: genuine parallelizability (contending/redundant/serially-dependent subagents are waste); §12.6 60% memory; §12.12 `RLIMIT_NPROC` thread headroom; §11.4.58 <=6 concurrent-agent cap; §11.4.119 (no two subagents driving one exclusive device); critical-state sequencing (commits/pushes/tags stay serial per §11.4.88/.113). Fan-out exceeding a host-safety ceiling or contending a single resource is a violation.
  - (D) INCREMENTAL DELIVERY GRANULARITY + DECLARED QA-BUILD CADENCE (operator mandate 2026-10-04, CRITICAL; research-derived): a long-running spec/feature ships every already-proven-correct increment as it clears its own bar, never withholding delivery until the WHOLE spec is done. Operator wording in canon: work incorporated right away; deterministic machine-evidenced validation of all supported test types; intensive testing (gates, checks, fixing, polishing) keeps running in BACKGROUND while specs are built phase by phase, story by story, task by task; builds go to QA for manual testing AS SOON AS POSSIBLE and REGULARLY; background agents keep all workable items and documents in sync. Gap closed: clause (A) overlaps validation with ONE candidate's build, §11.4.235(A) makes a batch build-eligible on source-correctness, §11.4.235(D) makes that per slice; none obliges an ELIGIBLE increment to be DELIVERED, sets a cadence, says how an incomplete spec stays safe, or binds the hand-off to tracker truth. ALL of (D.1)-(D.6) hold.
  - (D.1) THE DELIVERY UNIT IS THE INCREMENT, NOT THE SPEC: each vertical, independently testable slice (§11.4.148 slicing, Small + Testable) integrates into its INTEGRATION BRANCH (trunk for main-targeted work, else the feat/ / product/ / flavor/ branch of §11.4.195 it lives on) and joins the next QA deliverable cut from that branch the moment THAT increment holds its OWN source-correctness GO per §11.4.235(A)/(D). An increment on several coexisting integration branches is obligated separately per branch. A feat/ QA build is the live-manual-testing vehicle §11.4.195(B) requires BEFORE trunk-merge (precursor, never consequence); product/ and flavor/ lines get cadence builds from their own branch; (D) relaxes neither §11.4.195(B) nor (C). Withholding a build-eligible increment because other increments are unfinished, or because its/other increments' test-instrumentation or process-doc loops are open, is a violation. An increment without its own source-correctness GO is not deliverable; incremental delivery never licenses shipping unreviewed or unproven work.
  - (D.2) INCOMPLETE-SPEC, SAFE DELIVERABLE: the deliverable stays correct on every user-reachable path: EITHER the increment is a complete independently valuable vertical slice, OR the unfinished surface is LATENT (unreachable by construction, behind a release toggle, or branch-by-abstraction). A toggle is PERMITTED, never mandated, and is inventory with a carrying cost: every release toggle carries a tracked §11.4.197 removal item and a consumer-declared expiry (§11.4.35); a toggle past expiry is a §11.4.261 finding; one that must outlive its expiry is extended ONLY through a §11.4.271 waiver (rostered non-producer authoriser, new unelapsed expiry, named tracked item), never by a silent expiry edit, by enabling the unproven path, or by deleting finished work. A latent path is NOT an advertised capability (§11.4.266) until enabled and proven.
  - (D.3) A DECLARED QA-BUILD CADENCE, NOT A ONE-SHOT: every project declares as DATA (§11.4.35) its QA-build trigger: `per-increment`, `periodic` (fixed interval) or `whichever-first`; an undeclared project gets `per-increment` (safe default, §11.4.101). A periodic or whichever-first interval is recorded as DATA with a written justification and stated in every QA hand-off record (no numeric maximum is set; any cap is an operator decision, §11.4.66). When an integration branch holds build-eligible content not yet in a QA build cut from it and the trigger has fired, a QA deliverable MUST be cut from that branch and handed to QA for ongoing manual testing (§11.4.185). Builds COALESCE: a build in flight covers every increment that landed before it started, later increments roll into the NEXT build; a build that FAILS or is REFUSED at §11.4.236 covers NOTHING; "completed" means HANDED TO QA, not merely the build process exiting 0. Each deliverable is a §11.4.235(B) cycle boundary with its own monotonic version increment (§11.4.151), passes §11.4.236 readiness on its own candidate fingerprint, built once then promoted (§11.4.264). The §11.4.236 mandated validation for a cadence build is at minimum the source-correctness GO plus the §11.4.235(A) pre/post-build gates, PLUS every operator-declared blocker bound to the QA-deploy seam and any §11.4.239 critical-invariant scenarios the increment touches, NOT the open background-hardening backlog. "Deliverable" is project-defined DATA (binary, container, device image, or for dev-tooling/governance features the demonstrable testable state at a fingerprinted commit).
  - (D.4) CONTINUOUS BACKGROUND HARDENING THAT NEVER BLOCKS THE NEXT INCREMENT: test-instrumentation hardening, gate/check/mutation authoring, polishing, and fixes for QA findings on already-delivered increments run as standing background streams (§11.4.103/§11.4.192/clause (C)), each a tracked item (§11.4.197) driven to its own zero-finding GO (§11.4.134, not relaxed), landing on its integration branch as it reaches GO and riding the NEXT cadence build. They never gate a LATER increment's build-eligibility, with two exceptions that follow from existing anchors: an open source-defect finding (§11.4.235(D)) in code the later increment touches or depends on is a source-defect of that increment too; and a huge blocker still triggers §11.4.129 STOP, fix-all, full restart.
  - (D.5) NEVER-STALE TRACKING IS A PRECONDITION OF EVERY HAND-OFF: §11.4.106(F), §11.4.229, §11.4.202/§11.4.208/§11.4.210, §11.4.148 and §11.4.197 apply at EVERY increment landing and EVERY cadence build; each QA hand-off records the deliverable's fingerprint and the exact set of tracked items it contains; a hand-off whose tracker or documents disagree with the deliverable (item done whose fix is absent from that build, or a fix in the build no item records) is a §11.4 PASS-bluff at the delivery layer.
  - (D.6) QA FINDINGS ON EARLY INCREMENTS ARE STILL COVERAGE ESCAPES: earlier more frequent QA builds do not make manual QA the discovery mechanism; every defect manual QA finds triggers the §11.4.238(C) coverage-escape audit and a new automated check.
  - (D) honest boundary: changes WHEN and HOW OFTEN proven-correct work reaches QA, NOT what gates a release candidate; it does not prove any increment correct (that stays §11.4.108 / §11.4.235); does not weaken §11.4.129, §11.4.40 (a cadence QA build is not a tag), §11.4.185, §11.4.236, §11.4.264/§11.4.265, §11.4.134 or §11.4.235(D)'s conservative default (an unclassifiable finding is a source-defect). Research grounding stated honestly in canon (DORA small batches, Hodgson toggle taxonomy, branch-by-abstraction, SAFe cadence, GitHub Next Continuous AI as direction only); no published methodology combining per-increment QA delivery with continuous agent hardening streams was found, the composition is the clause's own synthesis. §11.4.230's next free clause letter is (E); never reuse (A)-(D).
  - (D) recommended gates: CM-INCREMENT-DELIVERED-NOT-SPEC-WITHHELD (FAIL: an increment holding its source-correctness GO is absent from every handed-to-QA or in-flight QA build from its integration branch after the trigger fired and no build from that branch is in flight, with coalescing so waiting on an in-flight build's successor is never a FAIL and a failed/refused build counts as neither completed nor in flight; FAIL, the §11.4.201(1) dual guard: an increment WITHOUT that GO appears in a QA build), CM-QA-BUILD-CADENCE-DECLARED (FAIL: build-eligible content uncovered after the trigger fired with no build in flight; a periodic/whichever-first interval with no justification; an absent declaration must resolve to per-increment, never to no cadence), CM-RELEASE-TOGGLE-TRACKED-EXPIRY (FAIL: a toggle with no tracked removal item or no expiry, or past expiry), CM-QA-HANDOFF-TRACKER-IN-SYNC (FAIL: a hand-off item set disagrees with the deliverable's contents); paired §1.1 mutations; gate-code is a separate work item, NOT claimed shipped.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies device set + serials, build/flash tooling, recording layout, worker-pool implementation (§11.4.35). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-230-PROPAGATION, CM-PIPELINE-OVERLAP-VALIDATION (build running with zero deploy-independent validation stages concurrent while SAFE-catalogue work is queued -> FAIL; non-huge-blocker discovery restarting whole cycle -> FAIL), CM-PARALLEL-DEVICE-WORKER-POOL (independent devices validated serially, or recording capture/analysis serialised onto one processor when a worker-pool path exists -> FAIL), CM-FAN-OUT-SUBAGENTS-DEFAULT (parallelizable effort run monolithically with fan-out path and host-safety headroom -> FAIL); paired §1.1 mutations; gate-code separate work item, NOT claimed shipped
- **No escape hatch:** --sequential-build-then-validate, --restart-whole-cycle-on-discovery, --serial-device-testing, --serialise-recording-processing, --no-fan-out, --monolithic-parallelizable-work; clause (D) adds, in canon's own words, "No escape hatch — no `--withhold-until-spec-complete`, `--hardening-gates-next-increment`, `--no-qa-cadence`, `--untracked-release-toggle`, `--stale-tracker-at-handoff`, `--manual-qa-as-discovery` flag." (all twelve flags bind)
- **Honest boundary:** current-artifact layers 2/3 cannot overlap their own build; affected-stages-only bounded to non-huge-blocker; fan-out bounded by host-safety and genuine parallelizability; 4-5x is a measured target never assumed.
