#### §11.4.231 — Nano-precision model-tier selection (lightest-capable-first, dynamic escalation, effort tiering)
- **Source:** multi-track-and-parallelism.md:206-229
- **Rules:**
  - Every work effort MUST use the LIGHTEST CAPABLE model, escalating only as complexity rises; neither "always heaviest" nor "always lightest" is compliant.
  - (A) Every dispatched effort (main or subagent, single- or multi-track) is assigned the LIGHTEST tier from the closed capability-ordered ladder `sonnet < opus` genuinely sufficient to complete it correctly; `sonnet` is the DEFAULT working tier, `opus` for every review and other heavy work (operator mandate 2026-09-26). The review/merge-conflict-resolution substrate is a SEPARATE pinned Opus-xhigh tier per (E), not a ladder rung; `fable` is not a rung and not a permitted dispatch tier; `haiku` excluded per (D.1).
  - (A) Tier selection is a DECIDABLE heuristic evaluated against at minimum: (i) task scope (single mechanical edit / focused single-file / multi-file or multi-component); (ii) reasoning depth (lookup-and-apply vs multi-factor root-cause per §11.4.102/.194); (iii) blast radius (isolated file vs shared state, hardware safety §11.4.133, governance/gate seams §11.4.227); (iv) novelty. Illustrative bindings (consumer maps its own per §11.4.35): `sonnet` = trivial/mechanical AND moderate work (greps, doc-sync regeneration, status reads, format/lint fixes, boilerplate, focused single-component debug, bounded single-file implementation, straightforward research/audit reads); `opus` = complex and other heavy work including every review (architecture/design, multi-factor reasoning §11.4.194(1), cross-feature blast-radius §11.4.92 Pass 2/3, hard root-cause that resists first-pass hypothesis). Genuinely UNDECIDABLE complexity starts at the NEXT tier UP (§11.4.101), never guessed downward.
  - (B) DYNAMIC MID-FLIGHT SWITCHING: tier is RE-ASSESSED continuously; a task that proves harder mid-flight MUST ESCALATE for its remainder (continuing under-powered is a false economy). A heavy task that decomposes into light bounded subtasks dispatches THOSE on a lighter tier via fan-out (§11.4.20/.70/.183); capability-matching applies at EVERY dispatch granularity.
  - (C) ALWAYS-ON COMPOSITION: standing default from the first prompt (mirrors §11.4.126/.198), applied TOGETHER WITH, never substituting: §11.4.141 token-optimization, §11.4.183 max-useful-parallelism (tier-match each stream), §11.4.187/.192 (each track's worker tier-assigned, not one blanket tier), §11.4.196/.198 (governs TIER within whichever alias is selected). None of these five is weakened/duplicated; this adds the TIER axis.
  - (D) "Lightest capable" is a CONJUNCTION, not a discount: a tier producing shallow investigation, guessed root cause, under-verified fix, or any bluff is UNDER-POWERED, a FALSE ECONOMY and a violation of equal severity to a PASS-bluff. Capability determinations are evidence-based (§11.4.6/.5/.69/.107): "always works fine on sonnet" without captured basis is forbidden. A dispatcher MUST NOT assign any tier outside `sonnet < opus` - never `fable`, never `haiku` where (D.1) applies. A serving model the platform selects without dispatcher assignment is recorded honestly in the §11.4.182 label (never re-labelled); it is neither a dispatch-tier violation nor a licence to assign that model.
  - (D.1) `haiku` PROHIBITED where it cannot receive its governing context: measured fact (2026-09-26) in the reference repository a `haiku` dispatch failed with "Prompt too long (~421k tokens vs 200k limit)" (request id `req_011CfSBXm7Kn6enyUT1UEaWd`, in `docs/requests/agent_registry.jsonl`). A consumer MAY re-admit `haiku` as a rung below `sonnet` ONLY on its OWN captured evidence (§11.4.6/.35) that a `haiku` dispatch receives full governing context and completes correctly - never by assumption, never by trimming governing context. A failed `haiku` dispatch is recorded honestly as failed (§11.4.147), never silently retried on the same tier.
  - (E) HARD PINS OVERRIDE THE DEFAULT for their scopes: §11.4.209 (every mandatory independent code-review, §11.4.125/.142/.194 iterated to GO per §11.4.134, runs on Opus at `xhigh` effort as PRIMARY substrate, with a genuine-unavailability Sonnet fallback amended 2026-10-04; no Fable, no Haiku, no other model; BLOCKED only when BOTH Opus and Sonnet are genuinely unavailable, never a lower tier or any other model) and §11.4.211 (every main->feature/product/flavor merge-CONFLICT resolution on the SAME Opus-xhigh-primary-plus-Sonnet-fallback substrate, blocked only when both are genuinely unavailable). Review and conflict resolution are NOT eligible for sonnet/opus-by-complexity dispatch; dispatching them elsewhere than the §11.4.209/§11.4.211 Opus-xhigh-primary-plus-sanctioned-Sonnet-fallback substrate violates THOSE anchors. (This project's own extension keeps these two scopes Opus-xhigh-only, see the §11.4.209 project-extension line.)
  - (F) EFFORT-TIER SELECTION: every effort also gets the LIGHTEST reasoning-EFFORT from closed ladder `low < medium < high < xhigh < max`, chosen by the same clause-(A) heuristic. Illustrative: `low`/`medium` trivial/mechanical; `high` moderate-to-complex (focused debug, multi-factor analysis); `xhigh`/`max` hardest verification/merge-conflict/architecture work.
  - (F.1) effort is re-assessed continuously and escalates mid-task when complexity proves higher; heavy tasks decomposing into light subtasks dispatch those at lighter effort.
  - (F.2) Harness boundary: effort-tiering is REAL where the path exposes an effort control and a DOCUMENTED CAPABILITY-GAP where not: the Claude Code Agent tool exposes `model` but NO `effort` parameter (label `<effort>` degrades to `?`); Workflow tool `agent()` DOES take `effort`. Label reports whichever path is live, never fakes one.
  - (F.3) Hard-pin floor: §11.4.209 reviews and §11.4.211 merge-conflict resolutions run at `xhigh` on Opus as PRIMARY substrate (or, on a captured genuine Opus-unavailability FACT, on the sanctioned Sonnet fallback of §11.4.209/§11.4.211, amended 2026-10-04; Fable and Haiku remain forbidden in every role); the general effort ladder NEVER tiers those scopes below `xhigh` where the dispatch path can set it; a review/merge-conflict resolution run below `xhigh` on a path that COULD set it, or on a model other than Opus or the sanctioned Sonnet fallback, is a §11.4.209/§11.4.211 violation, not a valid application of this ladder.
  - (F.4) "Lightest capable effort" is a conjunction; under-effort yielding a shallow/guessed/under-verified result is a false economy and PASS-bluff-severity violation.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies its own tier<->task-class mapping and model-name ladder (the `sonnet`/`opus` ladder, `haiku` prohibition, Opus-xhigh pins are this project's concrete instantiation); re-admitting a lighter rung only on own captured evidence per (D.1). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-231-PROPAGATION (literal as block-start, exactly-once per governance file, lockstep content-hash equality per §11.4.227(B)), CM-MODEL-TIER-LIGHTEST-CAPABLE (tier exceeding heuristic for a later-confirmed-trivial task is WARN/candidate only; HARD-FAILS: (i) review or merge-conflict effort not on the pinned substrate, (ii) task proven harder mid-flight that did not escalate, (iii) dispatch assigned `fable` or `haiku` where (D.1) applies). Paired §1.1 mutations: review labeled `sonnet` -> FAIL; logged escalation event with no tier-escalation record -> FAIL; dispatch assigned `fable`/`haiku` -> FAIL; golden-FALSE: task staying on initial tier with no escalation event MUST NOT fire (§11.4.201(1)); gate-code separate work item, NOT claimed shipped
- **No escape hatch:** --always-heaviest-model, --always-lightest-model, --skip-complexity-reassessment, --fixed-tier-per-session, --relax-review-pin, --relax-merge-conflict-pin, --per-request-tier-opt-in
- **Honest boundary:** "lightest capable" means capable, not cheapest-regardless; tier adequacy provable only in retrospect so the gate hard-fails only the decidable violations; effort-setting depends on harness capability reported honestly.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.20, §11.4.70, §11.4.92, §11.4.101, §11.4.102, §11.4.194, §11.4.126, §11.4.141, §11.4.183, §11.4.187, §11.4.192, §11.4.196, §11.4.198, §11.4.209, §11.4.211, §11.4.182, §11.4.147, §11.4.133, §11.4.227, §11.4.5, §11.4.69, §11.4.107, §11.4.201, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.232 — Anti-mess long-op orchestration (registry, single-owner-per-purpose, proven liveness, handoff-on-stop, safe reaping, consistency sweep, escape)
- **Source:** multi-track-and-parallelism.md:231-254
- **Rules:**
  - Binds EVERY long-op (any op expected to exceed the §11.4.89 background-execution threshold: verification sweep, meta-test sweep, build, flash/deploy, test/QA suite, dispatched subagent) to a long-op orchestration layer. Reason: no single source of truth existed for what long-op runs, who owns it, its state and proven liveness; an un-observable bad state is a bluff at the orchestration layer.
  - (A) SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH: every long-op MUST register BEFORE it runs and reach a terminal state `complete|failed|reaped|handoff|blocked-escape` when it ends, in a durable (never-tmpfs, write-temp-then-rename; §11.4.116 append-only event stream + atomic snapshot) registry recording `{op_id, purpose_key, owner, pid|pgid, cwd, state, last_heartbeat, heartbeat_seq, progress_offset, log_path, verdict, evidence_path}`. Success read from the op's terminal verdict/result, NEVER its process exit code. A long-op with no registry record, or a record with no live op, is a FALSE-READY drift state.
  - (B) SINGLE-OWNER-PER-PURPOSE: no two same-`purpose_key` long-ops run at once; acquisition is a probe-race-safe claim keyed on `purpose_key` (§11.4.119); a live claim forces exactly ONE of REUSE (attach) or explicit SUPERSEDE (graceful logged handoff), never a silent second run.
  - (C) LIVENESS TRUTH-SOURCE: progress PROVEN, never inferred from process-alive: each long-op emits a monotonic heartbeat and/or advancing progress offset; a watchdog reads the DELTA over a window and flags HUNG on no-advance past the op's declared no-progress budget (§11.4.201(6)-(7)/§11.4.89); `kill -0` is necessary-not-sufficient; a stale heartbeat/non-growing log is NEVER "progressing"; a consumer blocked on an unclosed producer write-end (§11.4.201(12)) is caught by the flat heartbeat.
  - (D) OWNERSHIP-HANDOFF-ON-STOP: stopping/killing an owner MUST hand its long-ops to the registry (`handoff`, re-adoptable per §11.4.147) or deliberately reap them (`reaped`, reason logged); NEVER silently orphan or cascade-kill; long-ops launch detached (own process-group); stop path records each owned op's disposition. Loop done-condition not satisfied while a `handoff` op is un-adopted.
  - (E) SAFE REAPING: reap an orphaned/hung op ONLY on PROVEN staleness (holder PID dead via `kill -0`, OR no-progress budget exceeded per (C)), resolved by the process's real `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` (§11.4.196(D)/§12.12), never bare `pgrep`/substring; a LIVE ADVANCING op is NEVER reaped (§9.2); every REAPED/KEPT decision + resolved evidence logged (§11.4.180).
  - (F) CONSISTENCY INVARIANT SWEEP: fast check before every gated transition (build/flash/tag) and on a standing cadence asserting: no duplicate owner per purpose, no orphan, no stale lock (§11.4.180), no hung op, no registry-vs-reality drift (live set == registry live rows). Any violation is surfaced (named, actionable) and the gated transition REFUSED until resolved. The sweep is itself a guard (§11.4.201): golden-TRUE + golden-FALSE-with-carrier fixtures, conservative-safe REFUSE on unresolvable signal, resolved evidence printed on every refusal.
  - (G) UN-COMPLETABLE-BLOCKER ESCAPE: a gate that cannot reach a terminal verdict MUST degrade, after a bounded budget, to an explicit evidence-backed decision, never an indefinite silent block: §11.4.102 first (hung vs duplicate vs wrong-seam/§11.4.120 re-seat-at-activation); NOT-YET-RUNNABLE -> §11.4.69 `artifact_not_yet_built` (non-blocking on intermediate artifact, blocking only on the release candidate per §11.4.135); genuinely un-completable -> §11.4.101 (autonomous reversible SKIP-with-reason + tracked §11.4.197 item, ELSE bounded §11.4.66 operator decision); the loop keeps progressing other items; escape NEVER fabricates a PASS.
  - Reuse-not-rewrite: generalises the multitrack per-track agent registry (§11.4.147/.116/.187) to any long-op, bound through per §11.4.196(F); no parallel mechanism invented. Classification universal; consumer supplies long-op set, purpose keys, no-progress budgets, stop-hook wiring (§11.4.35). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-232-PROPAGATION, CM-LONGOP-REGISTRY-SINGLE-SOURCE (A), CM-LONGOP-SINGLE-OWNER-PER-PURPOSE (B), CM-LONGOP-LIVENESS-HEARTBEAT (C), CM-LONGOP-OWNERSHIP-HANDOFF-ON-STOP (D), CM-LONGOP-SAFE-REAP-PROVEN-STALE (E), CM-ORCHESTRATION-CONSISTENCY-SWEEP (F), CM-UNCOMPLETABLE-BLOCKER-ESCAPE (G); paired §1.1 mutations per clause (two same-purpose sweeps; liveness from `kill -0` only; stop leaving op with no terminal/handoff record; reap a live-advancing op or reap by bare-`pgrep`; live op with no registry row passing the sweep; un-completable gate blocking with no escape; strip literal); gate-code separate work item, NOT claimed shipped
- **No escape hatch:** --allow-duplicate-longop, --infer-liveness-from-pid, --silent-orphan-on-stop, --reap-live-op, --skip-consistency-sweep, --block-without-escape, --longop-without-registry
- **Honest boundary:** reduces orchestration mess; does NOT make product bugs impossible or a gate correct (§11.4.108/.201 still bind), nor remove the operator from genuine blocks; a heartbeat proves ADVANCE not CORRECTNESS; the registry proves what CLAIMS to run, (F) proves registry==reality.
- **Composes:** §11.4.89, §11.4.101, §11.4.116, §11.4.119, §11.4.120, §11.4.135, §11.4.147, §11.4.180, §11.4.187, §11.4.196(D)(F), §11.4.201(1)(6)-(12), §11.4.207, §11.4.69, §11.4.102, §11.4.66, §11.4.197, §12.6, §12.12, §9.2


#### §11.4.233 — Standing anti-mess control plane (level-triggered idempotent invariant-catalogue reconciliation loop; dependency-pointer preflight)
- **Source:** multi-track-and-parallelism.md:258-281
- **Rules:**
  - A standing control plane (desired-state/actual-state reconciliation loop, control-plane/data-plane pattern) over the WHOLE persistent System state; reason: existing enforcers are EDGE-TRIGGERED, so a mess arising without an edge firing is unobserved (e.g. uncommitted-batch pile-up, stale locks held by dead holders). Planes: R repository, G governance, S tracking, P runtime.
  - (A) DECLARED INVARIANT CATALOGUE: one machine-readable consumer-owned catalogue (DATA, §11.4.28/.35) enumerating every consistency invariant across the planes, each `{id, plane, desired-condition, detector, reconcile-class in {auto-safe | operator-gated | owned-by <anchor>}, evidence-shape}`; the catalogue IS the desired clean state; an un-catalogued mess class is an honest tracked GAP (§11.4.6/.197), never claimed covered.
  - (B) LEVEL-TRIGGERED LOOP: re-derives ACTUAL state (not an event) and diffs against the catalogue BEFORE every gated transition (commit-batch/build/flash/merge-to-trunk/tag/constitution-pull) AND on a standing cadence (§11.4.94/.103); uses a §11.4.86 fingerprint diff drilling to the offending record, never a whole-scan where a fingerprint suffices.
  - (C) IDEMPOTENT RECONCILE-OR-REFUSE: each drift takes exactly one dedup-keyed action: RECONCILE-AUTO-SAFE (reversible + evidence-determinable + bounded-blast per §11.4.101; e.g. reap provably-dead lock §11.4.180, regen stale derived doc §11.4.106, scope-group-commit a placement-clean batch §11.4.191, retire merged worktree §11.4.167), idempotent; OR REFUSE-THE-GATE + bounded operator decision (irreversible/high-blast/indeterminate: id-colliding SSoT §11.4.206, anchor collision §11.4.227, partial cross-repo merge, divergent mirror; §11.4.101/.66). A gated transition NEVER proceeds while a catalogued invariant is violated and un-reconciled; other non-blocked items keep progressing.
  - (D) SAGA FORWARD-RECONCILE (no-loss): a partially-applied cross-repo operation is reconciled complete-forward under a §9.2 pre-op backup (finish remaining legs / bump pointer / complete merge zero-markers-zero-drop §11.4.41 step 3 / ff the lagging mirror), NEVER force-push/reset/`-s ours` (§11.4.113/§9.2); compensation is §9.2 backup-restore only.
  - (E) THE LOOP IS A GUARD (§11.4.201): every detector ships golden-TRUE + golden-FALSE-with-carrier fixtures (§11.4.107(10)); a false-positive REFUSAL of a clean state is a FAIL-bluff exactly as a false-negative PASS is a PASS-bluff; every "no drift" null control-needle-proven (§11.4.201(6)-(12)); conservative-safe REFUSE on unresolvable signal, resolved evidence printed on every refusal.
  - (F) CONTROL-PLANE / DATA-PLANE SEPARATION: control plane DETECTS + RECONCILES state and NEVER performs data-plane work (build/commit/merge/long-op; §11.4.232 + wrappers); the two never merge; control plane's own state durable (§11.4.205(6) temp->fsync->rename, never tmpfs, may reuse §11.4.207).
  - (G) DEPENDENCY-POINTER PREFLIGHT (extension 2026-08-20): clause (A)'s Plane-R catalogue is EXTENDED with THREE distinct mess classes, all of which fail closed: (i) STALE (parent's recorded pointer behind submodule's intended ref); (ii) ABSENT/UNINITIALISED (declared but not checked out; empty directory read as satisfied dependency); (iii) UNFETCHABLE (recorded pointer resolves on NO configured remote, the `not our ref` condition; invisible in the originating checkout, fails only on fresh clone). Preflight MUST: resolve every submodule pointer, verify it matches the intended ref, fail closed on a missing checkout, and for truly load-bearing components assert a runtime signature on the flashed/deployed artifact (§11.4.108 RUNTIME-ON-CLEAN-TARGET layer). It is a HARD gate that fails the build, not a warning. Fail-closed principle: an absent/unverifiable dependency treated as satisfied is a bluff vector.
  - (G) Reconcile-class: REFUSE-THE-GATE for classes (ii) and (iii); AUTO-SAFE only for a class-(i) drift whose correct pointer is evidence-determinable. Per (E) detector ships a golden-TRUE fixture per class and a golden-FALSE fixture (fully-initialised tree at intended refs) it MUST NOT fire on (§11.4.201(1)).
  - Reuse-not-rewrite: level-triggered COMPOSER over existing per-domain enforcers (§11.4.180/.186/.106/.191/.206/.227/.232/.147/.167), inheriting each detector; composes §11.4.232 (Plane P data-plane) as the plane it does not touch. Classification universal; consumer supplies invariant catalogue, plane detectors, gated-transition list, cadence, reconcile-class bindings (§11.4.35). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-233-PROPAGATION, CM-ANTIMESS-INVARIANT-CATALOGUE (A), CM-ANTIMESS-LEVEL-TRIGGERED-LOOP (B), CM-ANTIMESS-RECONCILE-OR-REFUSE (C), CM-ANTIMESS-SAGA-FORWARD-NO-LOSS (D), CM-ANTIMESS-LOOP-IS-A-GUARD (E), CM-ANTIMESS-CONTROL-DATA-PLANE-SPLIT (F), CM-DEPENDENCY-POINTER-PREFLIGHT-FAIL-CLOSED (G; paired §1.1 mutation: de-initialise a submodule -> FAIL; point a gitlink at a commit no remote serves -> FAIL; golden-FALSE fully-initialised tree MUST NOT fire). Other paired §1.1 mutations: drop standing-cadence trigger; proceed on catalogued drift; saga force-push/reset; detector refusing clean golden-TRUE or passing golden-FALSE-with-carrier; control plane invoking data-plane build/commit; strip literal. Gate-code separate work item, NOT claimed shipped.
- **No escape hatch:** --edge-triggered-only, --skip-consistency-catalogue, --proceed-on-drift, --reconcile-with-force-push, --unvalidated-detector, --control-plane-does-work, --assume-clean-without-reconcile
- **Honest boundary:** converges only CATALOGUED invariants (extensible catalogue, never "provably mess-free"); does not make a gate correct (§11.4.108/.201); does not auto-fix irreversible drift (operator-gated); eventual-consistency-at-every-gate-and-cadence, not a real-time daemon (§11.4.205(7)). Dependency preflight proves the dependency's SOURCE is present at the intended ref, NOT that the built artifact contains it (that is §11.4.108 ARTIFACT layer + the runtime-signature step).

### Project lifecycle and release (46 anchors)

#### §11.4.8 — Deep-web-research-before-implementation
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:3-26
- **Rules:**
  - Before designing a non-trivial fix, implementing a new feature, or declaring an architectural choice, perform deep web research to verify the approach is informed by current state of the art.
  - Research surface: (1) official docs of platform/framework/language/service; (2) vendor technical guides for hardware/cloud/library; (3) open-source codebases that solved analogous problems; (4) coding tutorials and technical articles; (5) issue trackers of relevant projects.
  - A fix that re-invents a wheel, or reproduces a known-broken pattern when the open-source community already solved it, is a section 11.4 violation by omission.
  - Every non-trivial fix's commit message (or its entry in the project's Issues/Fixed file) MUST cite the research sources: at least one external link OR the literal "NO external solution found - original work".
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4

#### §11.4.9 — Batch-source-fixes-before-rebuild
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:27-38
- **Rules:**
  - In a multi-defect closure cycle, all source-side fixes that do NOT require runtime validation to design MUST be landed BEFORE the next artifact rebuild.
  - Forbidden anti-pattern: Fix A -> rebuild -> flash -> cycle -> fix B -> rebuild (serializes operator time onto rebuild latency).
  - A fix that DOES require an interim rebuild MUST say so in its commit message as `REQUIRES_REBUILD: <reason>`.
  - Default is the batch path; rebuild-now is the operator-authorized exception.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** none cited

#### §11.4.20 — Subagent-driven-by-default mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:40-110
- **Rules:**
  - In a multi-agent runtime, the primary agent MUST default to subagent delegation for any task meeting AT LEAST ONE: (1) multi-step scope (3+ discrete editing/creation/verification phases); (2) parallelisable work (2+ independent tasks, no shared mutable state); (3) long-running diagnostic loops (probe/re-test, build-flash cycles, soak tests); (4) domain-specific/specialised workflows (code review, security audit, infra change review, performance triage, doc propagation across N files).
  - Foreground work is allowed only when at least one holds: single edit or single file read with no follow-up; task needs mid-execution operator clarification; task gates critical state (commit, push, tag cascade) that must be sequenced before the next operator action; task is under ~30 seconds so spin-up exceeds the work.
  - Anti-stall: parent MUST (a) scope tightly (4-6 tightly-scoped tasks, no "complete everything" prompts); (b) require checkpoint commits after each major task; (c) explicitly prohibit destructive ops (`git reset --hard`, `git push --force`, `--no-verify`); (d) give discipline pointers (§11.4.6, §11.4.10, §11.4.17). Watchdog is ~600 s of no-progress in Claude Code.
  - A subagent returning "completed" without captured evidence in commits/outputs/artifacts is a PASS-bluff at the multi-agent layer; parent MUST verify claims against repo state (`git log`, `git status`, post-completion gate runs).
  - Parallel subagents MUST be partitioned onto non-overlapping files; parent's `commit_all.sh --auto-cascade` bundles dirty files into atomic commits.
  - Operating exclusively in the foreground when delegation is feasible is not permitted.
- **Gates:** CM-SUBAGENT-DELEGATION-AUDIT (when implemented per consuming project; paired mutation required)
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated in prose: no escape hatch for foreground-only work)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.10, §11.4.17, §11.4
- **Review addendum:** Canon wording is SHOULD: the primary agent SHOULD only do foreground work when at least one of the listed conditions holds; it is not an absolute prohibition.

#### §11.4.40 — Full-suite retest before release tag mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:112-197
- **Rules:**
  - A release tag (any `vX.Y.Z` / `X.Y.Z-suffix` identifier) MUST NOT be created until a COMPLETE retest with ALL existing tests has run on a clean baseline AFTER every workable item in the batch is done, fixed, polished, and individually verified.
  - A spot-check retest of only batch-touched tests is FORBIDDEN.
  - The complete retest comprises: (1) pre-build verification full sweep, 0 FAIL; (2) post-build verification full sweep against the freshly-assembled image, 0 FAIL; (3) on-device 4-phase cycle (e.g. `test_all_fixes.sh`) on EVERY owned device, phases Immediate Fresh Flash / After Reboot / After Factory Reset / After Final Reboot, none skipped, summaries captured; (4) meta-test full mutation sweep (every paired mutation in `meta_test_false_positive_proof.sh` or equivalent); (5) test bank full sweep (every Challenge covered by a full QA session); (6) Issues.md/Fixed.md state audit (no silent demotion; every Reopened item has §11.4.34 Reopened-Details; every closure has §11.4.5 captured evidence; no Status outside §11.4.15 closed set); (7) CONTINUATION.md sync check per §12.10.
  - Expected duration 12-48 hours; NOT optional, NOT abbreviated; delay the release rather than skip.
  - Per-fix retest per §11.4.4 stays mandatory; §11.4.40 is the additional final integrity check after the batch.
  - Full-suite retest is the authoritative captured-evidence baseline: if a §11.4.7-promoted item passed per-fix retest but FAILs the full-suite retest, the closure MUST be reverted and the item moved back to `In progress`.
  - Per-feature on-device validation (§11.4.39) runs as part of step 3.
  - Pre-tag gate verifies within the last 72 hours of the candidate commit: (a) full pre-build + post-build run, (b) on-device 4-phase on every owned device, (c) meta-test full sweep, (d) Issues/Fixed audit pass; evidence captured in `docs/changelogs/<tag>.md` per §11.4.4(c).
  - Paired mutation (§1.1): strip the `Full-suite retest evidence` block from a changelog -> gate FAILs.
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-FULL-SUITE-RETEST-MANDATE
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-full-retest, --quick-release
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.4, §11.4.5, §11.4.7, §11.4.15, §11.4.17, §11.4.34, §11.4.39, §12.10, §1.1
- **Review addendum:** Step 5 applies if a Challenge-driven test bank exists: then every Challenge MUST be covered.

#### §11.4.42 — Iteration-discipline mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:199-297
- **Rules:**
  - Work proceeds in priority-ordered iteration cycles; a closed five-step loop run in order; advancing past a step before its acceptance condition is met is a bluff.
  - Step 1 priority-ordered fix selection: filter tracker to Status in `Queued | In progress | Reopened | Operator-blocked` (§11.4.15), sort by severity DESC then intra-group criticality DESC (§11.4.12), select ONLY `Top critical` or `Middle critical` items; `Low` items are DEFERRED until the critical batch closes.
  - Step 2 batch implementation: land source-side fixes per §11.4.9; every fix gets §11.4.4 four-layer coverage (pre-build gate + post-build gate + on-device test + paired mutation).
  - Step 3 smoke-test gate after flash: (a) anti-bluff baseline (`meta_test_false_positive_proof.sh` for gates touched), (b) every `test_*.sh` matching a fix in the batch, (c) critical-path regression probe (boot + launcher + WiFi + audio + secondary-display routing core), (d) §11.4.39 per-feature on-device validation for touched features. Target under 30 minutes on the parallel fleet. MUST emit zero FAIL and zero unclassified WARN.
  - Step 4 full-system-test gate: ONLY if smoke is GREEN AND no new operator/user report arrived during the validation window, run the §11.4.40 complete retest (all 7 steps). If smoke FAILed OR a new report arrived, full-system test is FORBIDDEN; loop back to step 1 with the new evidence in the queue.
  - Step 5 release-readiness or loop: if full-system test GREEN and no new report during it, batch is release-ready (§11.4.40 tagging may proceed pending operator authorization); otherwise loop to step 1.
  - Priority taxonomy: `Top critical` = severity C AND intra-group criticality 5; `Middle critical` = severity C with intra-group 1-4 OR severity M with any score; `Low` = severity L; severity WARN treated as Low.
  - The loop continues until the operator explicitly authorizes a release; no upper bound on iterations; "we've cycled enough" is not a stopping condition; the cycle MUST NOT be truncated to ship faster.
  - Every smoke and full-system PASS MUST carry positive captured evidence of user-visible behaviour (§11.4.2, §11.4.5); Tests AND HelixQA Challenges bound equally.
  - Subagents doing autonomous work default to the §11.4.42 path. Add capacity (devices, agent slots) rather than skip steps.
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-42-PROPAGATION (mirrors CM-COVENANT-114-40-PROPAGATION 1:1; paired mutation strips the anchor literal from one consumer file -> gate FAILs)
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-priority-batch, --skip-smoke, --full-suite-only, --release-without-loop
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.2, §11.4.4, §11.4.5, §11.4.7, §11.4.9, §11.4.12, §11.4.15, §11.4.17, §11.4.34, §11.4.39, §11.4.40

#### §11.4.46 — Validate-recent-work-before-post-flash-tests mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:299-400
- **Rules:**
  - After every device flash the orchestrator MUST first run a recent-work validation pass before any full post-flash suite (`test_all_fixes.sh` or equivalent): enumerate recent work from Issues.md / Fixed.md / CONTINUATION.md section 3, map each to its on-device test, run ONLY those, classify each result per §11.4.6, demand 100% green before the full suite is permitted. If validation fails, go fix; do not run post-flash tests (abort any in progress).
  - Recent work (closed set): `docs/Issues.md` actionable headings with Status in `{In progress, Ready for testing, Reopened}`; `docs/Fixed.md` headings closed within `--max-age-days N` (default 7); `docs/CONTINUATION.md` section 3 "Active work" sub-headings marked IN PROGRESS or BLOCKED.
  - Test binding: by section-letter or Fix # match against `test_*.sh` filenames OR an explicit `Test:` line in the heading. Items with no on-device test are §11.4.4 four-layer violations, flagged VALIDATION-PASS-BLOCKED until the test lands.
  - Machine-enforced sequence: (1) `scripts/testing/recent_work_validate.sh --device <serial>` writes `/data/local/tmp/.recent_work_validated` on the device IFF all targeted tests PASS with captured evidence; (2) full suite (`test_all_fixes.sh`) checks the marker at entry; absent or older than the last flash boot epoch -> refuses with exit code 11; (3) marker invalidated on reboot (boot epoch stored in marker, re-validated).
  - Each recent-work item landing a fix in the batch MUST have a paired §11.4.43 RED test (before fix) and the same test GREEN (after); GREEN with no prior RED is a bluff and the gate FAILs.
  - Classify validation FAILs per §11.4.6: PRODUCT defect (block full suite, surface to operator), TEST-INFRA defect (fix at source layer per §11.4.1, re-run), BLUFFY-THRESHOLD (e.g. wrong SLO floor, re-baseline), UNCONFIRMED (not reproducible in isolation; tag per §11.4.7 PENDING_CYCLE_RETEST, never silently demote).
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-46-PROPAGATION (anchor literal in every CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md of the covenant set), CM-AF-RECENT-WORK-VALIDATION-GATE (`scripts/testing/recent_work_validate.sh` exists, executable, sources anti-bluff library; full-suite orchestrator contains entry-gate check), CM-AF-VALIDATION-ARTIFACT-FILE (marker path `/data/local/tmp/.recent_work_validated` literal-identical across helper, orchestrator, propagation block, and this section). Paired mutations strip the anchor / remove the entry-gate / flip the marker path -> respective gate FAILs.
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-validation, --full-suite-always, --ignore-recent-work

#### §11.4.47 — Firebase Data Review Mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:402-506
- **Rules:**
  - Before every bigger working round (pre-build, pre-flash, pre-tag, daily, post-deployment burn-in) execute the Firebase review pass via `scripts/firebase/review_round.sh`: query Crashlytics (fatals + non-fatals + ANRs) + Analytics + Performance, classify by the severity table, dedup-map to existing Issues.md entries via the three-tier algorithm, draft new Issue entries for unrecognised findings. Skipping the pass is a PASS-bluff.
  - Five mandatory elements, ALL must hold: (1) trigger cadence: pre-build (blocking, freshness under 24 h), pre-flash (blocking, under 24 h), pre-tag (blocking, under 6 h), daily 09:00 UTC default (non-blocking sweep), post-deployment burn-in T+24 h (non-blocking); (2) three-source query, ALL of Crashlytics + Analytics + Performance (skipping one is a PASS-bluff); (3) every problematic finding maps to a new Issues.md entry OR a recognised existing entry via dedup, both carrying a full Firebase Console URL in metadata; (4) three-tier dedup: Tier 1 exact Firebase Issue-ID match, Tier 2 stacktrace-similarity cluster hash (top-3 non-generic frames normalised + crash class -> SHA-256 first 8 hex chars), Tier 3 monthly operator merge review; multiple Issues.md entries for one root cause is a violation; (5) comprehensive root-cause analysis on every Firebase-sourced Issue carrying §11.4.4(a) systematic-debugging output (Phase 1 evidence, Phase 2 pattern, Phase 3 root-cause hypothesis UNCONFIRMED until a §11.4.43 RED test reproduces, Phase 4 fix direction); comment-only entries are PASS-bluff stubs and FAIL the Issue-xref gate.
  - Severity: Crashlytics FATAL impactedUsers >10 in last 7d -> Critical; 1-10 -> Major; 0 but historic -> Low. NON-FATAL >100/day -> Major; 10-100 -> Low; <10 -> Informational. ANR >1% sessions -> Major; 0.1-1% -> Low. Performance KPI regression >20% -> Major; 10-20% -> Low. Analytics funnel-drop >50% -> Major; 25-50% -> Low; feature_used regression >75% -> Major. Composes with §11.4.16 Type assignment.
  - A previously-Fixed Issue resurfacing in Firebase is positive evidence the fix did not hold; reopen attribution "AI: captured-evidence-contradicts" per §11.4.34. Never log the bearer token (§11.4.10). Clean `/tmp/firebase_review_*` work-dirs (§11.4.14). Firebase Status.md at `docs/firebase/status/Status.md` (§11.4.45). Operator MAY filter by minimum severity (`--severity-min major`) but the pass itself MUST execute.
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-47-PROPAGATION, CM-AF-FIREBASE-REVIEW-CADENCE (`scripts/firebase/review_round.sh` exists, executable, contains 7-stage pipeline literals + dedup algorithm + severity table), CM-AF-FIREBASE-ISSUE-XREF (every Issues.md entry with `**Source:**` of Firebase Crashlytics/Analytics/Performance carries `**Firebase Issue IDs:**` + `**Firebase URL:**` + `**Stacktrace Cluster Hash:**` for Crashlytics OR `**KPI:**` for Performance OR `**Funnel:**` for Analytics). Paired mutations strip the anchor / rename the review_round function / remove the Firebase-URL field from the template -> respective gate FAILs.
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-firebase-review, --no-issue-from-firebase, --firebase-review-not-applicable

#### §11.4.52 — Autonomous-Validation Mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:508-687
- **Rules:**
  - (1) Every user-facing feature MUST have at least one AUTONOMOUS validation path: runs end-to-end via `adb shell` + scripted automation, produces captured runtime evidence per §11.4.5, reaches PASS/FAIL WITHOUT a human present to drive UI, observe, or decide. Operator-attended tests are SUPPLEMENTARY, never PRIMARY; a feature whose only path is operator-attended is a violation regardless of evidence quality.
  - (2) Acceptable autonomous paths (any one or more, non-exhaustive): programmatic instrumentation APK (platform-signed app exercising the surface via SDK APIs, writing structured JSON result to a discoverable path); headless intent dispatch + state poll (`am start --es` / `am broadcast --es`, then poll `dumpsys`, `/proc/<pid>/maps`, `media.metrics`, `/sys/...`, sysfs, or network probe); ADB-driven uiautomator ONLY if the app exposes accessibility nodes (MUST verify `uiautomator dump | grep -c clickable=true` >= 1; a near-empty hierarchy is evidence UI automation is infeasible and test MUST fall back to instrumentation-APK or headless-intent); network-side sink probe (sink's own report counts as out-of-band evidence per §11.4.13); HelixQA autonomous QA session for projects with HelixQA incorporated per §11.4.27.
  - (3) Per-feature classification in the §11.4.25 coverage ledger, each feature in the closed set: `AUTONOMOUS_VERIFIED` (path exists + last-run-green per §11.4.46), `AUTONOMOUS_DESIGNED` (path exists but RED per §11.4.43), `OPERATOR_ATTENDED_ONLY` (release blocker until promoted), `NOT_APPLICABLE` (e.g. CLI with no UI, unit+integration already autonomous proof). `OPERATOR_ATTENDED_ONLY` rows MUST cite a tracked work item per §11.4.15 + §11.4.16 designing the autonomous migration; closing that item requires the migration to land, not an operator capture.
  - (4) Anti-bluff for autonomous paths: a path returning PASS without exercising user-visible behaviour is as severe as the original PASS-bluff; MUST produce positive captured evidence per §11.4.5 (audio: channel count + sample rate + glitch census; video: frame count + routing target + frame health + obstruction census); a grep on a non-behavioural metadata field is a metadata bluff. Paired §1.1 meta-test mutations MUST catch degradation to metadata-only or grep-only.
  - Autonomous path MUST exist in RED state BEFORE the fix lands, then go GREEN (§11.4.43); one authored after the fix is a PASS-bluff.
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17); each consumer adapts the path catalogue to its stack (Android: instrumentation APK + uiautomator + headless intent; Web: Playwright headless + API probe; CLI: subprocess + stdout/stderr assertion; mobile native: device farm headless runner).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-52-PROPAGATION (literal `§11.4.52` present in all 5 canonical files: constitution Constitution.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, plus the parent consumer's CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md, and full per-consumer propagation incl. owned/nested submodules and HelixQA dependencies, same scan as CM-COVENANT-114-51-PROPAGATION), CM-AF-AUTONOMOUS-PATH-PER-FEATURE (every §11.4.25 ledger entry has a non-empty autonomous-classification column in the closed set; OPERATOR_ATTENDED_ONLY rows cite a tracked migration item; project-side gate). Paired mutations: strip `§11.4.52` from Constitution.md -> propagation gate FAILs; inject an OPERATOR_ATTENDED_ONLY row with no tracked item -> CM-AF-AUTONOMOUS-PATH-PER-FEATURE FAILs.
- **No escape hatch:** --allow-operator-attended-only, --skip-autonomous-path, --manual-validation-suffices
- **Honest boundary:** none stated

#### §11.4.66 — Blocker-resolution interactive-clarification mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:691-783
- **Rules:**
  - When a task is blocked on input the agent cannot mechanically derive (operator decision, hardware access, external-service authorization, ambiguous scope), follow five steps before idling or asking free-form questions.
  - (1) In-depth research of agent-side options: identify the maximum scope landable unilaterally; surface every agent-actionable path even if it needs small operator confirmation.
  - (2) Calculate minimum-viable operator input: reduce to the smallest closed set of operator-only decisions; anything researchable MUST NOT be asked.
  - (3) Construct 2-4 mutually-exclusive options, each with (a) short label, (b) one-line trade-off, (c) explicit statement of what the agent does after that answer; one marked "Recommended" with rationale; options MUST genuinely differ (three close variants of one option is a violation).
  - (4) Present via the platform's interactive question mechanism (Claude Code `AskUserQuestion`: max 4 questions, each 2-4 options, multi-select for non-exclusive sets; equivalents on Copilot CLI, Codex, Gemini CLI). NEVER inline free-text "what would you like?" when interactive options would do.
  - (5) After the answer, resume work without additional round-trips; each option's promised action MUST suffice to unblock; needing a follow-up question means prior options were under-researched (violation). Contract: ask once, unblock, continue.
  - Protections: no silent waiting (if blocked, ask; if no input needed, do not ask); no bulk-text questions where options would do (free text only for truly open-ended ideation); operator should answer all questions in under 30 seconds total; recommended option highlighted explicitly; out-of-band channels (slack, voice, email) NEVER substitute.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-66-PROPAGATION (literal across the 42-file consumer fleet: parent CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md + 10 owned-submodule pairs + HelixQA-owned pairs; paired mutation strips the literal -> FAILs)
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-ask, --silent-wait, --free-form-only
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.7, §11.4.40, §11.4.41, §11.4.42, §11.4.52

#### §11.4.70 — Subagent-Driven Execution Is The Default
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:787-855
- **Rules:**
  - When executing plans authored via `superpowers:writing-plans` (or any task-decomposed flow), the default execution model is subagent-driven per `superpowers:subagent-driven-development`.
  - Inline execution via `superpowers:executing-plans` is permitted ONLY when (a) the task is trivial AND fits in a single sub-300-line edit, OR (b) the operator explicitly requests inline execution at brainstorm-handoff time per the writing-plans skill's explicit-execution-mode prompt.
  - Rationale: isolated context per task (avoids conductor bloat past ~100k tokens); two-stage review naturally enforced; subagents are the unit of parallelism in the §11.4.58 PWU pipeline; anti-bluff seam (conductor review structurally separated from the work, eliminating self-review blind spots); survives operator absence (subagents resume from on-disk plan + spec).
  - Skipping subagent-driven for non-trivial work without recorded operator authorisation is itself a PASS-bluff.
  - Default applies to every `superpowers:writing-plans` terminal handoff and every multi-task execution flow with independent subtasks.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-70-SUBAGENT-DEFAULT-PROPAGATION (anchor literal in every CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md across parent + 10 owned submodules + nested submodules + HelixQA dependencies, ~44-file fleet; paired §1.1 mutation strips literal -> FAILs)
- **No escape hatch:** --inline-execution-required, --no-subagents, --monolithic-execution
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.4, §11.4.6, §11.4.42, §11.4.43, §11.4.50, §11.4.51, §11.4.58, §11.4

#### §11.4.72 — Audio Top-Priority Mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:857-873
- **Rules:**
  - The conductor (main working stream: Claude Code session, AI agent, or human operator) MUST treat audio fixes as the highest-priority class on the serial dispatch queue.
  - Audio fixes include but are not limited to: section EU HDMI rejection, EM multichannel HDMI, ET Arvus integration, EV/EW/EX D3 audio defects, HiFi (Fix #74 pcm_config_deep, #76 HDMI/SPDIF resilience), AC3 (Fix #106 FFmpeg Codec2), ES8388 (Fix #103/#104/#105 mutual-output + DAPM), multichannel LPCM (Fix #112), and every future audio-stack improvement.
  - Per §11.4.42 the conductor selects in priority order; this anchor pins audio at the apex. Per §11.4.58, parallel BACKGROUND subagents (research, refactors, infrastructure docs) MAY run concurrently but do NOT preempt audio on the main-stream serial queue.
  - Operative rule: when choosing between an audio task and a non-audio task on the SAME serial resource (most commonly the `pre_build_verification.sh` + `meta_test_false_positive_proof.sh` edit-and-commit critical path), the audio task wins. No "non-audio is faster" or "research is more interesting" override.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named (prose: no override)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.42, §11.4.58

#### §11.4.82 — Iteration-speedup discipline mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:875-936
- **Rules:**
  - Every consuming project's build/test/commit/debug pipeline MUST adopt the following, each independently enforceable. (A) Phase 1 forensic before any speculative source patch: before any non-trivial patch (kernel, framework, native, HAL, ASoC) complete Phase 1 of `superpowers:systematic-debugging` (read error/log/call-chain end-to-end, identify a FACT-grade root cause); speculative patches are §11.4.6 and §11.4.82 violations regardless of time pressure.
  - (B) Live-ADB-First (or live-equivalent) before any rebuild (per §11.4.51, strengthened to release-blocker): ~70% of audio/UI/boot-script/config changes are LIVE_ADB_TESTABLE (push + `setprop` + `pm install -r` + ~30 s validation); only kernel / framework Java/AIDL / native C++-in-APEX / sepolicy / init.rc / ro.* / Android.bp / XML-resource-overlays / codec-XML-in-APEX changes truly REQUIRE rebuild; skipping the live probe for a LIVE_ADB_TESTABLE change is a violation.
  - (C) Pre-flight (~30 s) before any rebuild orchestrator (`nohup bash scripts/<rebuild>.sh &`): verify (i) target device(s) reachable via ADB, (ii) downstream sinks (Arvus AVR, HDMI sink, Bluetooth peers) reachable, (iii) host has memory and disk per §12.6, (iv) no stale lock files in `.git/` or build dirs, (v) no orphan git/build processes from prior killed iterations.
  - (D) Persistent build caches outside containers: containerized AOSP/kernel builds MUST persist `ccache` and equivalent caches (Soong cache, sccache, Gradle daemon state) on the host via bind-mount, not in the ephemeral container layer.
  - (E) Module-only rebuild: when a patch touches ONLY files in `kernel/.../drivers/*/foo.c` AND the drivers are loadable modules (`CONFIG_*=m`), rebuild MUST be `make -C kernel M=<driver-path> modules` (~2-5 min) not a full kernel rebuild (~25 min); a `flash_kernel_only.sh` or equivalent writes modules to the running device without re-flashing system.img. Built-in drivers (`CONFIG_*=y`) require full rebuild.
  - (F) Parallel multi-device testing: with more than one validation device (D3, D4, ...), the orchestrator MUST run autonomous validation cycles on EVERY device in parallel as background processes with separate `qa-results/<TS>/<device-tag>/` output directories.
  - (G) Subagent scope discipline + worktree isolation: subagents per `superpowers:subagent-driven-development` MUST be scope-bounded to <=30 min of focused work with incremental output (watchdog stalls at 600 s of no output); worktree-isolated by default via the Agent tool's `isolation: "worktree"` when supported; single-responsibility (one investigation OR one fix OR one doc draft; 2-3-task subagents complete reliably, 8-task ones stall).
  - (H) Lock-file + stale-process hygiene: detect and clean `.git/index.lock`, `.git/.commit_all.lock`, build-dir `.lock` files and orphan children (`git add -A`, `git pack-objects`, `git gc`) on session start or after a visible crash; never wait silently; auto git-gc MUST be disabled in repos with concurrent multi-agent work (`git config gc.auto 0`).
  - (I) Cycle telemetry per §11.4.24 build-resource stats: each cycle records (i) commit hash under test, (ii) wall-clock of build + flash + test phases separately, (iii) which of A-H applied, (iv) outcome (PASS / FAIL / partial / stall); §11.4.82 extends the §11.4.24 row schema with iteration-discipline columns.
  - Classify each speedup as universal (§11.4.17; belongs in this constitution submodule's helper inventory or a separate Containers submodule per §11.4.76) or project-specific (stays in the consuming repo). Universal overall.
- **Gates:** CM-ITERATION-SPEEDUP-DISCIPLINE (when implemented: audits last N cycles' telemetry for A-I flags; flags cycles with none active; paired §1.1 mutation: strip the speedup-flag column from a synthetic row -> gate FAILs)
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-phase1-forensic, --no-pre-flight, --rebuild-everything-always, --unlimited-subagent-scope, --ignore-locks, --no-telemetry
- **Honest boundary:** Speedups MUST stay within the §12.7 -j2 host-safety cap and memory budget; ccache config must not break determinism (§11.4.50).
- **Composes:** §11.4.4, §11.4.6, §11.4.9, §11.4.17, §11.4.20, §11.4.24, §11.4.42, §11.4.43, §11.4.50, §11.4.51, §11.4.52, §11.4.58, §11.4.70, §11.4.76, §12.6, §12.7, §107

#### §11.4.87 — Endless-loop autonomous work + zero-idle agent dispatch + anti-bluff testing mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:940-976
- **Rules:**
  - When the operator says continue "in endless loop fully autonomously" (or equivalent), it is a HARD-CONTRACT covenant with five obligations.
  - (A) Endless-loop continuation until ALL are simultaneously TRUE: `docs/Issues.md` Status column has zero `In progress` / `Ready for testing` / `In testing` / `Reopened` entries (§11.4.15); `docs/CONTINUATION.md` section 3 "Active work" is empty; no background subagent mid-execution (TaskList all `completed` or `pending` with pending items not prerequisite-blockers of anything actionable); no external dependency in flight (build, flash, push, sync). If any is FALSE, continue by claiming the next priority item, dispatching a subagent, or polling a background task. Scheduling a wake-up and ending the turn while actionable items, active CONTINUATION work, or productive subagents remain is a violation.
  - (B) Zero-idle agent dispatch: parallelisable work not contending on the same file-scope MUST be dispatched to a background subagent rather than serialised; "wait for results of something" is the ONLY acceptable idle reason (composes §11.4.20, §11.4.58, §11.4.70).
  - (C) Comprehensive test coverage with physical proofs: every item closed MUST land four-layer coverage per §11.4.4(b) (pre-build gate + on-device test + paired §1.1 meta-test mutation + HelixQA Challenge bank entry) and every PASS cites captured evidence per §11.4.5 + §11.4.69: captured audio (`tinycap` WAV with RMS + ffprobe channels), video (screen recording + ffprobe frames + recording-analyzer event match), network state (dumpsys + sink-side probe per §11.4.13), UI state (uiautomator dump per §11.4.48), sysfs state (`/sys/...`, `/proc/...` snapshots). Metadata-only, configuration-only, absence-of-error, grep-without-runtime PASS are critical defects.
  - (D) Anti-bluff end-to-end: every closure narrative cites captured evidence; every demotion cites same-conditions retest; every status transition cites the deterministic-consistency baseline; tests AND HelixQA Challenges bound equally.
  - (E) Termination ONLY when: (1) all conditions in (A) TRUE; OR (2) operator explicitly issues `STOP` / `END LOOP` / `pause autonomous work`; OR (3) host-session safety (§12, §12.6-§12.10) demands suspension; OR (4) agent has scheduled a wake-up against a known-future-actionable signal (CI completion, build completion, hardware-attended phase).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-87-PROPAGATION (anchor literal in every CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/QWEN.md across the canonical fleet; paired mutation strips `11.4.87` -> FAILs)
- **No escape hatch:** --idle-OK, --skip-endless-loop, --bluff-permitted-for-this-task, --metadata-only-test-suffices, --no-physical-proof-required
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.1, §11.4.2, §11.4.4, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.7, §11.4.13, §11.4.15, §11.4.20, §11.4.27, §11.4.42, §11.4.43, §11.4.48, §11.4.50, §11.4.52, §11.4.58, §11.4.68, §11.4.69, §11.4.70, §11.4.83, §11.4.85, §11.4.86, §12, §12.6, §12.7, §12.8, §12.9, §12.10

#### §11.4.89 — Background test execution mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:978-1008
- **Rules:**
  - (A) Any test cycle expected to exceed ~30 seconds (`pre_build_verification.sh`, `meta_test_false_positive_proof.sh`, `test_all_fixes.sh`, `recent_work_validate.sh`, HelixQA Challenge banks, on-device 4-phase cycles, full-suite retests per §11.4.40, `audio_loop_supervisor.sh`, `dual_display_record.sh`, `verify-all-constitution-rules.sh`) MUST be spawned detached via `nohup ... > <log> 2>&1 &` + `disown`, log under a known directory (e.g. `qa-results/<test_id>_<timestamp>.log`).
  - (B) Main stream proceeds on queued items: immediately return to the §11.4.42 priority queue; "wait for results" is the ONLY acceptable idle reason, and then check via short polling (`tail` / mtime / exit-status file), not blocking `wait`.
  - (C) Hard-dependency gating: a step genuinely requiring the test's exit code (e.g. commit_all.sh refuses if meta-test in flight per §11.4.84; release-tag gate per §11.4.40 step 4) MUST express it explicitly (poll exit-status file or `pgrep -af <test-name>`); if still running and needed, surface to operator per §11.4.66 with options.
  - (D) Failure surface + cleanup: backgrounded failures land in their `<log>`; next loop tick MUST check that directory; every long-running test mutating global state MUST `trap '<cleanup>' EXIT INT TERM` (per §11.4.14, §11.4.84).
  - (E) Do not invoke a long test synchronously when a backgrounded variant suffices; foreground only when the test completes in under 30 s OR the operator explicitly requests it; synchronous multi-minute execution without authorisation is a violation.
  - (F) Concurrency control: multiple backgrounded runs of the SAME script serialise via per-script flock (e.g. `.git/.pre_build.lock`, `.git/.meta_test.lock`); different tests run in parallel.
  - (G) Subagent long-op discipline + conductor-owns-inherently-long-ops (extension): (1) a SUBAGENT MUST NOT run any single synchronous operation expected to exceed the runtime's no-progress watchdog budget (conservatively ~5 min); it MUST background it per (A) and POLL with short frequent tool calls; (2) inherently-long ops a subagent cannot usefully background-and-poll (full artifact builds, full test suites, device flashes/deploys) are the CONDUCTOR's to run, dispatching subagents only for parallelisable slices around them; (3) a subagent killed by the stall watchdog is a CRASH per §11.4.147: registry entry flips to `crashed` and the unit is RESPAWNED until `complete`; a stall-kill absorbed as a completion is a §11.4.147 + §11.4 bluff.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker; no escape beyond explicit per-invocation operator authorisation.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-89-PROPAGATION, CM-BACKGROUND-TEST-EXECUTION-WIRED (long-running test invocations in helper scripts use `nohup ... &` + `disown` or equivalent). Paired §1.1 mutations strip load-bearing literals -> gates FAIL.
- **No escape hatch:** none named beyond explicit per-invocation operator authorisation
- **Honest boundary:** The watchdog budget is a RUNTIME property: read it from the runtime, never guess; when unknown treat any operation > ~5 min as long.
- **Composes:** §11.4.14, §11.4.40, §11.4.42, §11.4.66, §11.4.82, §11.4.84, §11.4.85, §11.4.87, §11.4.88, §11.4.147, §11.4

#### §11.4.94 — Zero-idle priority-first parallel-by-default operating mode
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1012-1051
- **Rules:**
  - Operating-mode reaffirmation binding §11.4.87, §11.4.20/.70, §11.4.42, §11.4.58, §11.4.72, §11.4.82, §11.4.88, §11.4.89 into one always-on contract; binds conductor, every subagent, every helper script.
  - (A) Idle-only-when-genuinely-blocked: the conductor MAY sleep/wait/idle ONLY when (i) every priority-queued item is genuinely blocked on external dependency (operator hardware action, network upstream, hardware-attended forensic, build/test completion it cannot accelerate), OR (ii) operator issued explicit STOP, OR (iii) host-session safety per §12 demands it. "I don't see what to do next" is NEVER valid; recheck the priority queue per §11.4.42 step 1 and §11.4.87(A).
  - (B) At every pause point (before any wake-up schedule, "waiting for X", or sleep): (1) survey the priority queue per §11.4.42 SCOPE LOCK + §11.4.72 + §11.4.87(B); (2) identify ALL items that can progress without contending with the in-flight blocker; (3) dispatch them in parallel per §11.4.20/§11.4.70 (subagent-driven if non-trivial), §11.4.58 (PWU disjoint scope), §11.4.89 (background long tests). Only after (3) returns no parallel work may the conductor schedule a wake/sleep.
  - (C) Priority order mandatory at every pick: per §11.4.42 and §11.4.72; highest-severity/priority item the conductor can autonomously progress; lower waits.
  - (D) Subagent-driven by default for non-trivial scope; conductor remains the integration + commit + push seam (§11.4.58, §11.4.84, §11.4.88); inline only for trivial (single-file, sub-300-line) or operator-requested.
  - (E) Background by default: any op over ~30 s wall-clock MUST run detached (nohup + disown) with log under `qa-results/<op-id>_<ts>.log` (§11.4.85, §11.4.89, §11.4.88); conductor returns to the queue immediately.
  - (F) Stability-preserving: parallel work MUST NOT compromise stability; every parallel branch's output passes 5-pass evaluation (§11.4.92) before integration; concurrent subagents in the same checkout coordinate via lockfile or git worktree (§11.4.84); respect §12.6 60% memory ceiling, §12.7, §12.8, §12.9 and -j2 AOSP cap.
  - (G) Status updates: conductor surfaces parallel-work catalogue + in-flight branches + recent closures in compact form when asked "how are we progressing" or at natural milestone boundaries (after each constitution-anchor landing, commit batch, subagent return).
  - Forbidden anti-patterns: scheduling a wake-up without first surveying the parallel-work queue; returning "nothing to do - sleeping" when progressable priority items remain; serialising work that could run in parallel without justification; picking lower-priority items while higher-priority remain progressable; doing foreground work that should run via subagent or background; letting parallel work introduce instability or regression.
  - Conductor idle without exhausting the parallel-work queue is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-94-PROPAGATION, CM-PARALLEL-WORK-AUDIT (when implemented: audits last N wake-up schedule decisions for surfaced parallel-work-queue evidence). Paired §1.1 mutations strip load-bearing literals -> gates FAIL.
- **No escape hatch:** none named (prose: none beyond the (A) genuinely-blocked / explicit-STOP / host-safety triad)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.20, §11.4.42, §11.4.58, §11.4.70, §11.4.72, §11.4.82, §11.4.84, §11.4.85, §11.4.87, §11.4.88, §11.4.89, §11.4.92, §12, §12.6, §12.7, §12.8, §12.9, §11.4

#### §11.4.97 — Maximum-use-of-idle-time mandate + progress-update cadence
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1055-1089
- **Rules:**
  - Strengthens §11.4.87, §11.4.94, §11.4.96 with a maximum-use-of-idle-time mandate and a progress-update cadence.
  - (A) Every minute of conductor idle time during which the conductor has work it could autonomously progress AND is NOT genuinely blocked (operator hardware action, network upstream, host-session safety, build/test completion) is a violation; the conductor MUST dispatch work continuously through the entire idle window, not just sample-check at scheduled wakes ("as much as possible, if not it all").
  - (B) The conductor MUST emit operator-facing progress updates (no operator prompt required), 1-3 lines each, at: every commit that lands (1-line "what just landed"); every subagent return ("subagent X returned, integrated"); every constitutional anchor landed ("§X.Y.Z propagated to 6 remotes"); every gathered physical proof ("captured evidence at qa-results/<path>"); every milestone closure (Issues->Fixed migration, Obsolete classification, etc.).
  - (C) Continuous physical-proof gathering: every autonomous-fixable item closed MUST gather positive captured evidence (ADB probes, dumpsys captures, screencaps, ALSA hw_params, sysfs reads, file-content hashes, runtime metric snapshots) committed with the closure narrative; per §11.4.93 SQLite SSoT the evidence path goes into `item_history.evidence_path` when DB integration lands.

  - (E) Idle only when genuinely blocked, same closed set as §11.4.94(A) (operator STOP, uncontrollable external dependency, host-safety); per §11.4.96 the safe-during-build catalogue (A-K) covers what is progressable and the conductor MUST exhaust it before sleeping.
  - Conductor idle when progressable work remains, or failing to emit milestone updates, is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-97-PROPAGATION, CM-IDLE-TIME-AUDIT (when implemented: audits wake/sleep schedule across recent sessions for unjustified idle). Paired §1.1 mutations strip load-bearing literals -> gates FAIL.
