#### §11.4.101 — Autonomous-decision-over-blocking mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1093-1122
- **Rules:**
  - In autonomous/endless-loop mode (§11.4.87) the agent MUST minimize operator-blocking and make the safe, reliable, reversible decision itself so work is not stalled (e.g. overnight).
  - The agent MAY proceed autonomously when ALL hold: (a) the action is reversible OR has a captured pre-op backup per §9.2 (hardlinked `.git` mirror, recorded refs/tags/submodule pointers); (b) the safe choice can be determined from captured evidence per §11.4.6 (`LIKELY` / `probably` / `seems` is NOT a determination); (c) a wrong choice's blast radius is bounded AND recoverable (local, undoable, no cascade); (d) it composes with existing covenants (anti-bluff §11.4, host-session-safety §12 incl. no suspend/log-out/overrun of §12.6 memory budget, data-safety §9 with no destructive op without the §9 protocol).
  - The agent MUST BLOCK (ask via §11.4.66) ONLY when ALL hold: the action is irreversible AND high-blast-radius AND the safe choice cannot be determined from evidence. Canonical block-required examples: external-account state the agent cannot inspect (registration, certification, billing portals), hardware it cannot physically access, destructive repository ops without a backup, force-push (independently requires §9.2 + §11.4.41 authorisation), spending money or sending messages/data to third parties. `Operator-blocked` per §11.4.21 is last resort, reached only after this rule fires AND the §11.4.21 self-resolution-exhaustion audit completes.
  - Maximize-progress-while-blocked: when a block is unavoidable, still maximize progress on every NON-blocked item in parallel per §11.4.87 + §11.4.94; the blocked decision parks one work unit, it does not pause the loop; posing the question and going idle is a §11.4.94 + §11.4.97 violation.
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-101-PROPAGATION (literal `11.4.101` across the consumer fleet; paired §1.1 mutation strips it -> FAILs; gate-code a separate work item)
- **No escape hatch:** --always-block-on-decision, --never-decide-autonomously, --skip-decision-rule, --block-without-self-resolution
- **Honest boundary:** Gate-code implementation is a separate work item; this anchor defines the contract.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.21, §11.4.40, §11.4.41, §11.4.66, §11.4.87, §11.4.94, §11.4.97, §9, §9.2, §12, §12.6, §11.4, §11.4.4(b), §11.4.17

#### §11.4.102 — Mandatory systematic-debugging activation + always-loaded skill-discovery + plugin-dependency availability
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1126-1152
- **Rules:**
  - (A) On ANY spotted issue, bug, test failure, gate failure, regression, misalignment, inconsistency, unexpected behaviour, or contradiction between evidence and expectation, the agent MUST activate the structured root-cause skill (`superpowers:systematic-debugging` on Claude Code, or platform-equivalent) BEFORE proposing, writing, or applying any fix. Iron Law: NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST. Run the full four-phase arc: (1) root-cause phase (read actual error/failing assertion/divergent evidence, reproduce deterministically, gather facts); (2) pattern phase (classify the defect, search for the same pattern elsewhere); (3) hypothesis phase (falsifiable hypothesis, prove or disprove with captured evidence, never LIKELY/probably/seems per §11.4.6); (4) implementation phase (design the fix only after the cause is a FACT).
  - Guess-and-retry, symptom-patching, "let me just try changing this", and re-running a failed test hoping it passes without a completed investigation are violations. Declaring a failure transient/flaky/intermittent/probably-timing without captured forensic evidence is simultaneously a §11.4.6 and §11.4.7 violation; the classification is forbidden until the arc has captured the proving evidence.
  - (B) The skill-discovery meta-skill (`superpowers:using-superpowers` on Claude Code, or platform-equivalent) MUST be loaded and applied at session start and consulted before any task; before acting on ANY request survey available skills; if ANY skill could apply, even at 1% chance, it MUST be invoked rather than improvising from memory. Skipping skill-discovery at session start, or improvising a task a loaded skill was built for, is a violation.
  - (C) Every skill plugin, marketplace package, or capability dependency the project relies on (Claude Code, its marketplaces, or other runtimes' equivalents) MUST be installed and loadable BEFORE dependent work proceeds. A missing plugin that blocks a mandated skill (e.g. `superpowers` absent so systematic-debugging cannot launch) is a release-blocker until installed and confirmed loadable. Install via the runtime's own path (Claude Code: in-session `/plugin` marketplace flow; others: npm/pip/cargo/editor extension manager). Availability MUST be confirmed by observing the skill in the live capability/loaded-skills list; install-command exit 0 is not proof (mirrors the §11.4.80 npm exit 0 != working binary lesson).
  - (D) AUTOMATIC activation, no operator prompt required (2026-07-13): the agent MUST auto-activate `superpowers:systematic-debugging` (or equivalent) on ANY spotted issue/bug/test failure/gate failure/regression/misalignment/inconsistency/unexpected behaviour WITHOUT waiting for an operator prompt, request, or per-issue confirmation, the MOMENT an issue is detected; the operator MUST NOT have to ask, request, or re-enable it per issue or session. Before the investigation, the `superpowers` plugin + `superpowers:systematic-debugging` AND `superpowers:using-superpowers` skills MUST be confirmed installed and loadable per (C), observed in the live capability list. "I did not activate it because the operator did not ask" is itself a violation. (D) strengthens (A); every (A) four-phase and Iron-Law requirement still applies in full.
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17); concrete skill names are the Claude Code instantiation, "or platform-equivalent" wording carries to other runtimes per §11.4.81.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-102-PROPAGATION (literal `11.4.102` across the consumer fleet; paired §1.1 mutation strips it -> FAILs; gate-code a separate work item)
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-systematic-debugging, --guess-and-retry-OK, --symptom-patch-permitted, --skip-skill-discovery, --plugin-optional, --missing-plugin-is-warning
- **Honest boundary:** Gate-code implementation is a separate work item; this anchor defines the contract.
- **Composes:** §11.4.4, §11.4.6, §11.4.7, §11.4.8, §11.4.17, §11.4.43, §11.4.70, §11.4.80, §11.4.81, §11.4.82(A), §11.4.92, §11.4.126

#### §11.4.122 — No-silent-removal-of-existing-components-without-operator-confirmation mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1156-1176
- **Rules:**
  - No application, system component, service, package, feature, driver, module, library, prebuilt asset, or any already-existing capability of the shipped System may be removed (deleted, dropped from the package set, disabled-into-non-shipping, un-bundled, de-listed, or otherwise made unavailable to the end user) WITHOUT FIRST interactively asking the operator and receiving an EXPLICIT keep-or-remove decision.
  - The question MUST be posed through the platform's interactive clarification mechanism per §11.4.66 (`AskUserQuestion` on Claude Code), NEVER free-text buried in narrative, NEVER a silent removal justified post-hoc, NEVER an autonomous removal decision. Silent removal is a release blocker regardless of rationale (deduplication, "it was broken anyway", "geo-restricted", "incompatible", "superseded").
  - Counts as removal (non-exhaustive): deleting an app/APK/binary from the build's package set (e.g. `PRODUCT_PACKAGES` / `device.mk` / equivalent manifest), removing a service from the init/boot/service-registry set, dropping a kernel module/driver/config from shipping configuration, un-bundling a prebuilt asset, deleting a submodule or its shipped output, removing a feature flag that gated a live capability, or any edit whose net effect is an end-user capability that shipped no longer ships. Adding, replacing with approved equivalent-or-better, or fixing is NOT a removal. When uncertain, treat it as a removal and ask.
  - Tracked drop path: ask the operator -> operator approves -> mark the item `Obsolete (-> Fixed.md)` with `Obsolete-Details` reason `feature-removed` AND an operator-approval citation (§11.4.90) -> then remove; the removal never precedes the operator's yes. Even a capability proven structurally impossible to keep (§11.4.112) is closed via §11.4.90 with operator awareness.
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies its capability-manifest paths per §11.4.35. Reason: two shipped capabilities (an Apple-TV-class app and a Huawei HMS component) were removed without asking and the operator reversed both.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-122-PROPAGATION (literal `11.4.122`), CM-NO-SILENT-COMPONENT-REMOVAL (recommended: diff-driven detector flagging deletion from the package/service/module manifest set without a matching operator-approval citation; a removal whose tracker item is `Obsolete (-> Fixed.md)` reason `feature-removed` with operator-approval citation passes; per §11.4.110 change-impact-clash pattern). Paired §1.1 mutations: strip the literal -> propagation gate FAILs; introduce a manifest removal with no citation -> CM-NO-SILENT-COMPONENT-REMOVAL FAILs. Gate-code is a separate follow-up.
- **No escape hatch:** --remove-without-asking, --silent-removal, --autonomous-removal-OK, --dedup-removal-exempt, --it-was-broken-anyway
- **Honest boundary:** Gate-code implementation lands as a separate follow-up work item; this anchor defines the contract.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.17, §11.4.35, §11.4.40, §11.4.42, §11.4.66, §11.4.90, §11.4.101, §11.4.110, §11.4.112, §11.4

#### §11.4.126 — Default autonomous-loop working mode from first prompt
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1178-1198
- **Rules:**
  - The endless fully-autonomous loop is the DEFAULT working mode, engaged automatically at the operator's FIRST request/prompt of a session; the operator MUST NOT have to ask for, restate, or re-enable it per session. It is the capstone promoting §11.4.87 from opt-in to always-on, with §11.4.94 zero-idle, §11.4.97 maximum-idle-use, §11.4.101 autonomous-decision-over-blocking, and §11.4.103 continuous-parallel-stream all engaged by default.
  - Continuation contract: the loop continues until ONE terminal condition holds: (A) release scope: a new fully-validated-and-verified version (tag) is created AND published across all owned submodules AND the main repo to all configured remotes (per §2.1 multi-upstream push, §11.4.40 full-suite-retest-before-tag, §11.4.113 no-force-push merge-onto-latest-main); (B) non-release main-stream scope: the main-stream goal is fully completed AND every side stream is done AND the queue holds nothing left for the current scope. Until then the agent keeps working (claims next priority item, dispatches next parallel stream, progresses every non-blocked item per §11.4.42/.72/.94/.103).
  - The loop STOPS ONLY on: (1) operator explicitly saying so (STOP / pause / end); (2) nothing left to do in the current working scope with the queue genuinely empty per (A)/(B); (3) a §12 host-session-safety demand (loop yields unconditionally). Idle-while-blocked parks one work unit, not the loop (§11.4.101 + §11.4.94 + §11.4.97).
  - Goal ABSOLUTE EFFICIENCY; applies to this project and every incorporating project.
  - Anti-bluff: mimicking/imitating the loop, narrating continuation without performing it, fabricating progress, or emitting false/bluff results of ANY kind is ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN (composes §11.4, .1, .2, .5, .6, .50, .69, .107); a report claiming the loop ran with no real work/evidence is a PASS-bluff at the operating-mode layer.
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies its release-tag/publish mechanism + queue source per §11.4.35. Terminal conditions are determined from captured queue/tracker state, never assumed (§11.4.6).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-126-PROPAGATION (literal `11.4.126` across the consumer fleet; paired §1.1 mutation strips it -> FAILs; gate-code a separate work item)
- **No escape hatch:** --ask-before-continuing, --single-turn-only, --not-default-loop, --mimic-OK
- **Honest boundary:** Gate-code is a separate work item.
- **Composes:** §11.4.87, §11.4.94, §11.4.97, §11.4.101, §11.4.103, §11.4.66, §11.4.6, §11.4.40, §11.4.42, §11.4.72, §11.4.113, §2.1, §12, §11.4, §11.4.1, §11.4.2, §11.4.5, §11.4.50, §11.4.69, §11.4.107, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.127 — Session-handoff resumption-prompt mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1200-1212
- **Rules:**
  - When a fresh session is needed (context limits, degradation) OR the operator asks about a new session / handoff, the agent MUST ALWAYS prepare and provide a ready-to-paste resumption prompt valid for that EXACT moment and project phase, enabling zero-loss resume; MUST proactively offer it the moment the need is recognised, not only when asked.
  - Two variants on demand: a SHORT first-sentence variant ("Read <handoff docs>, then continue <terminal goal> ...") AND a FULL detailed block.
  - (1) Point to the live handoff docs (`.remember/remember.md` if present + `docs/CONTINUATION.md` per §12.10), instruct reading them FIRST + `git fetch --all`.
  - (2) State current PHASE, immediate NEXT action, terminal goal.
  - (3) Embed exact live-state anchors: build IDs / artifact MD5, device/target serials, commit HEAD, in-flight PIDs + log paths, captured-evidence paths.
  - (4) Restate binding constraints: anti-bluff §11.4, no-force-push §11.4.113, exact version/naming, hardware/target gotchas.
  - (5) MOMENT-VALID, reflecting actual live state, NEVER a generic template.
  - Handoff docs MUST be brought current BEFORE the prompt is given (§12.10). Omitting the prompt, or giving a stale/generic one, is a violation.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies handoff-doc paths + state anchors per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-127-PROPAGATION, CM-HANDOFF-RESUMPTION-PROMPT-PRESENT
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-handoff-prompt, --generic-prompt-OK, --no-resumption-sentence, --handoff-without-state
- **Honest boundary:** none stated beyond the embedded state being captured fact, not assumed (§11.4.6).
- **Composes:** §12.10, §11.4.6, §11.4.66, §11.4.87, §11.4.103, §11.4.126, §11.4.113, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.129 — Huge-blocker release protocol
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1214-1224
- **Rules:**
  - A HUGE BLOCKER = release-blocking-severity defect (core user-facing capability broken, regression invalidating the in-flight validation cycle, or blast radius reaching the batch's other fixes) found during release validation. The agent MUST run this protocol in order with NO partial/spot-check shortcut.
  - (1) STOP all testing immediately on every device (§11.4.4 escalated to release granularity).
  - (2) Return to fixing ALL discovered issues, not only the blocker; root-cause each per §11.4.102; isolate regressions against the last known-good tag per §11.4.114.
  - (3) Process all recorded data from the last session (the §11.4.128 raw-corpus slice for the cycle, the §11.4.128(3) release-prep analyse trigger).
  - (4) Land rock-solid fixes per §11.4.123, §11.4.43/§11.4.115 (RED on broken artifact then GREEN), §11.4.9 batch-source-fixes-before-rebuild.
  - (5) Author NEW validation+verification tests of ALL supported test types per §11.4.27 (unit/integration/e2e/full-automation/security/stress/chaos/performance/UI/UX/Challenges/HelixQA) + §11.4.85, each anti-bluff with captured evidence + paired §1.1 mutation.
  - (6) Rebuild + reflash: full rebuild (NOT module-only), deploy to a CLEAN target per §11.4.108 (no stale-overlay shadow).
  - (7) RESTART full validation+verification from the last release tag to now (restart, NEVER resume; per §11.4.40), re-validating EVERY fix/change since the tag, on both/all owned devices IN PARALLEL per §11.4.103/§11.4.119, every run RECORDED per §11.4.128, with real physical captured proofs per §11.4.5/§11.4.69/§11.4.107, no bluff.
  - Adds the sequencing + "restart, never resume" rule; cites rather than duplicates the other anchors.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies device set, build/flash mechanism, last-known-good tag per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-129-PROPAGATION, CM-HUGE-BLOCKER-FULL-RESTART
- **No escape hatch:** --resume-after-blocker, --spot-validate-after-fix, --skip-recording-analysis, --skip-new-tests, --module-only-after-blocker, --single-device-restart
- **Honest boundary:** none stated beyond: a validation cycle continuing past a huge blocker yields "all green" on a known-broken build (a PASS-bluff).
- **Composes:** §11.4.4, §11.4.40, §11.4.42, §11.4.9, §11.4.27, §11.4.85, §11.4.102, §11.4.108, §11.4.114, §11.4.115, §11.4.123, §11.4.128, §11.4.103, §11.4.119, §11.4.5, §11.4.69, §11.4.107, §11.4.43, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.130 — Post-remediation validate-the-fix-FIRST-after-redeploy
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1226-1240
- **Rules:**
  - When a release-validation blocker is fixed, a new artifact is produced and the target is reflashed/redistributed/updated, the agent MUST follow this order with NO shortcut.
  - (1) Re-test the SPECIFIC last-failing features FIRST: targeted guard tests for exactly the defects the fix addressed, BEFORE any broader/full-suite validation.
  - (2) Validate+verify the just-incorporated fixes with real captured evidence: the RED test that reproduced the defect on the pre-fix artifact (§11.4.115) MUST flip GREEN at `RED_MODE=0` on the new artifact, AND the fix's declared runtime signature (§11.4.108) MUST verify on the CLEAN target the redeploy produced. Metadata-only/config-only/absence-of-error/grep-without-runtime PASS forbidden; proof captured per §11.4.5/§11.4.69/§11.4.107/§11.4.123.
  - (3) ONLY after the targeted fix is CONFIRMED on the new artifact proceed to the §11.4.40 full retest of every fix/change since the last release tag.
  - A targeted re-test that still FAILs is a finding: return to the §11.4.114/§11.4.115 isolate->RED->fix loop and produce another artifact; do NOT proceed to the full cycle on a still-broken fix.
  - Rationale: cheap-confirmation-first (§11.4.82) avoids discovering a fix-did-not-take at the end of a multi-hour cycle (then restart per §11.4.129). §11.4.129 step (7) full-restart MUST be preceded by this phase. Specialisation of §11.4.46.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies targeted-guard set, build/flash mechanism, clean-deployment/runtime-signature observables per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-130-PROPAGATION, CM-FIX-FIRST-AFTER-REDEPLOY
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-targeted-retest, --full-cycle-first, --assume-fix-took, --validate-fix-at-end, --skip-red-green-flip-on-new-artifact
- **Honest boundary:** "the fix probably took" is not "the fix took"; the targeted RED->GREEN flip + runtime-signature verification on the new artifact is the captured proof.
- **Composes:** §11.4.4, §11.4.40, §11.4.46, §11.4.108, §11.4.114, §11.4.115, §11.4.123, §11.4.129, §11.4.82, §11.4.5, §11.4.69, §11.4.107, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.131 — Standing session-resumption file mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1242-1262
- **Rules:**
  - Every project MUST maintain a SINGLE canonical, always-current session-resumption FILE at a fixed project-declared path (declared once per §11.4.35, never moved without a §11.4.66 operator decision). It is the out-of-the-box entry point: a new session needs ONLY to be pointed at this file. Promotes §11.4.127 into a standing, version-controlled artifact.
  - (A) Existence + fixed path: MUST exist at the declared path at all times; the path is a literal string in the project-layer instantiation, never silently moved.
  - (B) Always written + synced: (re)written whenever a fresh session is needed OR live state materially changes (new HEAD, build/artifact id, phase transition, device/target state, in-flight job, blocking decision), the §12.10 trigger set. A stale file is a violation of the same class as stale CONTINUATION.
  - (C) Content: carries both §11.4.127 SHORT and FULL variants; points to live handoff docs read FIRST (`.remember/remember.md` if present + `docs/CONTINUATION.md`) + `git fetch`; embeds exact live-state anchors (HEAD, build/artifact ids + checksums, device/target serials, in-flight PIDs + log paths, evidence paths); states PHASE + NEXT action + terminal goal; restates binding constraints (anti-bluff §11.4, no-force-push §11.4.113, version/naming, hardware gotchas). MOMENT-VALID, never a generic template.
  - (D) Export + freshness: in §11.4.65 scope, synchronized `.html`/`.pdf` siblings refreshed on every update; §11.4.44 revision header with monotonic revision + last-modified timestamp.
  - (E) Given ONLY this file's path a fresh session MUST fully resume with zero additional context.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-131-PROPAGATION, CM-SESSION-RESUMPTION-FILE-PRESENT

#### §11.4.132 — Risk-ordered validation priority mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1264-1286
- **Rules:**
  - Tests/validations/verifications MUST run in RISK-DESCENDING order: the highest-risk set FIRST; only AFTER it is fully GREEN with real physical captured evidence does the rest of the suite run.
  - Risk factors, highest first: (a) most-recently-worked; (b) historically most-problematic (longest defect history, most prior fixes/failures); (c) highest crash/break/regress likelihood (blast radius, complexity, dependency surface); (d) most-reopened per §11.4.55 reopen count.
  - Each item in the highest-risk set MUST pass with real captured evidence per §11.4.5/§11.4.69/§11.4.107; no metadata-only/config-only/absence-of-error/grep-without-runtime PASS; no false results or bluff.
  - Running the suite in arbitrary order, or lower-risk tests before the highest-risk set is GREEN, is a violation.
  - Refines/strengthens §11.4.130 (generalises "just-fixed first" to the full risk-ordered set), §11.4.46 (adds risk-ordering within the recent/high-risk set), §11.4.42 (priority discipline applied to validation ordering).
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies recency/problem-history/reopen-count sources (e.g. §11.4.93 DB `reopens_count` + `last_modified`) per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-132-PROPAGATION, CM-RISK-ORDERED-VALIDATION-PRIORITY
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-risk-ordering, --any-order-OK, --suite-order-fixed
- **Honest boundary:** none stated.
- **Composes:** §11.4.4, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.7, §11.4.40, §11.4.42, §11.4.46, §11.4.50, §11.4.55, §11.4.69, §11.4.107, §11.4.130, §11.4.72, §11.4.93, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.133 — Target-System + hardware safety mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1288-1312
- **Rules:**
  - Every change to the TARGET system (firmware, kernel, init/boot scripts, drivers, sysfs/devfreq/voltage/clock/thermal/regulator register writes, partition layout/bootloader/U-Boot, HAL, framework, prebuilts, device config, or non-Android equivalents) MUST ALWAYS be safe for (a) the target System (MUST NOT brick, boot-loop, corrupt user/system data, or render unrecoverable) AND (b) the hardware (MUST NOT drive any hardware-control surface beyond its safe electrical/thermal/voltage/clock envelope, MUST NOT damage panels, storage, radios, regulators, other components).
  - (1) Reversible-first: prefer reversible changes; for irreversible/high-blast-radius (bootloader/U-Boot/partition layout/fuse/OTP) verify against a known-good value (MD5/checksum/golden manifest) BEFORE applying and capture a pre-op backup of overwritten state (§9.2).
  - (2) No unverified hardware-control writes: NEVER write an unverified value to a sysfs node/register/firmware field governing voltage, clock frequency, regulator output, thermal-throttle threshold, current limit, or other physical-safety parameter; every value MUST be within datasheet/vendor-documented safe range established as FACT (cited per §11.4.8 + §11.4.99), never guessed. Pinning max OPP / disabling throttle / raising regulator output without proving cooling and electrical envelope tolerate it is forbidden.
  - (3) Thermal/performance changes (forcing performance governor, pinning top OPP, disabling idle/thermal management) MUST be validated against actual cooling capacity; captured thermal evidence (sustained-load temperature <= documented limit) is the proof; "it boots" is not proof.
  - (4) Flashing MUST use the project's sanctioned tool against a freshly-built, integrity-verified image; never an ad-hoc partition write, stale/unverified artifact, or tool/image of unestablished provenance.
  - (5) Unprovable safety => blocked: treat as UNSAFE and block; proceed only once the safe outcome is determined as FACT (§11.4.6), the change is reversible OR backed up (§11.4.101 + §9.2), and when still undeterminable the operator is asked via §11.4.66/§11.4.101. "Probably safe" is forbidden.
  - Distinct from §12 host-session safety (protects developer HOST); §11.4.133 protects the TARGET device; both apply, neither weakens the other.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies hardware-control surfaces, datasheet-safe ranges, known-good bootloader/image hashes, sanctioned flashing tool per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-133-PROPAGATION, CM-TARGET-HARDWARE-SAFETY
- **No escape hatch:** --unsafe-hardware-write, --skip-system-safety, --brick-risk-accepted
- **Honest boundary:** a build step can be host-safe yet ship a target-unsafe change; this gate covers the latter.
- **Composes:** §12, §12.6, §12.7, §12.8, §12.9, §12.10, §11.4.6, §11.4.8, §11.4.99, §11.4.101, §11.4.108, §11.4.123, §11.4.66, §9.2, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.150 — Mandatory deep multi-angle web research per change/issue, before declaring fixed or structural
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1316-1338
- **Rules:**
  - For EVERY fix/improvement/change/closure, however big/small/simple/complex, the agent MUST, in addition to systematic-debugging (§11.4.102), the fix, independent review (§11.4.125/§11.4.142) and multi-layer tests (§11.4.4(b)/§11.4.40), perform a DOCUMENTED deep multi-angle web research pass (articles, official/vendor docs, API references, standards, issue trackers, maintainer guidance, open-source code) to (i) find the best solution AND (ii) confirm there is not a more serious underlying problem.
  - (A) No closure as Fixed/Implemented/Completed (§11.4.33) OR as structurally-impossible won't-fix (§11.4.112) WITHOUT a documented deep-research pass. Unconditional for every workable item at the closure and structural-verdict gates (stronger than §11.4.8/§11.4.123).
  - (B) Multiple angles: >= 2 genuinely distinct angles (docs/standards/bug-trackers/alternative-approach/failure-mode/security/performance/platform-constraint/open-source-precedent; consumer picks subset) so single-source confirmation bias (§11.4.145) cannot pass; a one-link drive-by is NOT a pass.
  - (C) Confirm-no-bigger-problem: explicitly seek evidence the fix does not mask a deeper defect and the closure/structural verdict is safe; absence of a bigger problem is recorded as positive only when the search that would have surfaced it is enumerated (§11.4.118).
  - (D) Latest-source + cited per §11.4.99 (never memory): each source cited by URL + access date in the item's research artefact AND closure commit footer (`Deep-research <date>: <urls>` OR literal `NO external solution found — original work` per §11.4.8). Stale/memory-sourced research is a violation.
  - (E) Reopen-breaking is the purpose: a reopen (§11.4.34/§11.4.55) whose root cause a deep pass would have surfaced is a miss; a structural/won't-fix verdict without the pass is forbidden; structural-impossibility (§11.4.112) now REQUIRES the pass + cited authorities.
  - (F) ALWAYS in parallel with the main stream as a background subagent stream (§11.4.70/§11.4.20/§11.4.103/§11.4.89); never serialises the main stream; a blocked angle parks that angle, not the pipeline (§11.4.101).
  - (G) Applies retroactively and going forward to EVERY workable item (§11.4.93/§11.4.95); items closed without a documented pass are re-audited in the §11.4.40/§11.4.42 release-gate sweep.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies research corpora, angle set, tracker, closure-footer convention per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-150-PROPAGATION, CM-DEEP-RESEARCH-PER-ISSUE
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-deep-research, --single-source-suffices, --trivial-change-no-research, --close-without-research, --structural-without-research, --serialise-research, --research-from-memory-OK
- **Honest boundary:** research reduces unknown-unknowns but does not prove zero remaining defects (§11.4.118) and does not replace §11.4.108, §11.4.125/§11.4.142 review, or §11.4.40 retest; "probably no bigger problem" without the enumerated search is a guess.
- **Composes:** §11.4.8, §11.4.99, §11.4.123, §11.4.118, §11.4.145, §11.4.125, §11.4.142, §11.4.7, §11.4.112, §11.4.34, §11.4.55, §11.4.70, §11.4.20, §11.4.89, §11.4.103, §11.4.40, §11.4.42, §11.4.93, §11.4.95, §11.4.102, §11.4.33, §11.4.94, §11.4.97, §11.4.126, §11.4.101, §11.4.6

#### §11.4.151 — Project-prefixed release-tag/version-naming mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1340-1359
- **Rules:**
  - Every release tag AND version name on the main repo AND every owned submodule (§11.4.28) MUST be prefixed `<PREFIX>-<version>` (e.g. `myproject-1.0.0-dev-0.0.1`), so `git tag -l '<PREFIX>-*'` enumerates the release across all repos.
  - Prefix resolution, closed-set deterministic: (1) `HELIX_RELEASE_PREFIX` from the project's `.env`, authoritative when set; `.env` is git-ignored (§11.4.30) and the variable MUST be documented in the tracked `.env.example` (§11.4.77 regeneration discipline). (2) Fallback: lowercased snake_case project root directory name (no spaces, §11.4.29) when unset/empty.
  - The prefix MUST be IDENTICAL across the main repo and all owned submodules within one release; a differing/unprefixed submodule tag is a violation.
  - Version codes increment monotonically within the prefix (`<PREFIX>-...-0.0.1` -> `-0.0.2`), never reset, never skipped (append-only like §11.4.54).
  - Consumer supplies the prefix value and the env var per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-151-PROPAGATION, CM-RELEASE-PREFIX-NAMING
- **No escape hatch:** --no-release-prefix, --unprefixed-tag, --prefix-optional, --differing-submodule-prefix
- **Honest boundary:** the prefix guarantees identifiability + uniformity, NOT correct contents; the tag is created only after §11.4.40 full-suite retest GREEN and reaches every upstream via §11.4.113 merge-onto-latest-main (never force-push), fanned out per §2.1.
- **Composes:** §2.1, §11.4.29, §11.4.30, §11.4.40, §11.4.113, §11.4.126, §11.4.28, §11.4.77, §11.4.54, §11.4.6, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.152 — Crashlytics-recorded-data continuous monitoring + systematic-debug + regression-test-coverage mandate
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1361-1389
- **Rules:**
  - Every project with Firebase Crashlytics enabled/wired MUST treat the console as a first-class evidence channel and continuously process every recorded datum; an open Crashlytics issue with a green suite is a PASS-bluff at the field-telemetry layer. Strengthens/completes §11.4.47 (47 finds it, 152 fixes it and proves it stays fixed).
  - (1) Monitor ALL four surfaces: fatal crashes, ANRs, performance traces/regressions, AND non-fatals; skipping any is a bluff; non-fatals (catch/fallback/recovered-error paths) MUST be triaged.
  - (2) Systematic-debug each issue selected for fix per §11.4.102 (NO FIX WITHOUT ROOT-CAUSE INVESTIGATION): root-cause -> pattern -> falsifiable hypothesis -> fix. The §11.4.115 RED baseline reproduces the defect on the broken artifact (recorded stacktrace/ANR trace/non-fatal context is the captured evidence) BEFORE the fix; a fix without a prior reproducing test violates §11.4.43/§11.4.123. If unreproducible, deep research (§11.4.123/§11.4.150) is mandatory before any "cannot reproduce".
  - (3) A real fix/improvement for every confirmed issue (severity per §11.4.47 table), verified via §11.4.9/§11.4.43/§11.4.108 four-layer on a clean artifact; "acknowledged in the console" is not a fix; muting/ignoring a recurring issue without tracked rationale violates §11.4.6/§11.4.90.
  - (4) In the SAME commit as the fix (§11.4.43 DOCUMENT step), register a permanent §11.4.135 regression guard: a §11.4.115 polarity test with `RED_MODE=1` capturing the defect on the pre-fix artifact and `RED_MODE=0` as the standing GREEN guard; it MUST exercise the same user-reachable path the stacktrace/trace identifies, with captured evidence per §11.4.5/§11.4.69/§11.4.107/§11.4.123. A Crashlytics issue marked resolved WITHOUT a falsifiable regression test is FORBIDDEN. Each closure carries §11.4.34 demotion-evidence + a closure-log entry recording the console issue id/URL, root-cause analysis, fix commit, validation + verification test paths.
  - (5) Regular cadence: reuse the §11.4.47 five-trigger set (pre-build/pre-flash/pre-distribute/pre-tag blocking; daily + post-deployment-burn-in non-blocking); a one-time sweep is a violation.
  - (6) No false results: a "no new issues" claim requires enumerated monitored surfaces + queried window (§11.4.118); a "fixed" claim requires the RED->GREEN flip on the artifact (§11.4.115/§11.4.130); a guard whose paired §1.1 mutation does not make it FAIL is a bluff gate.
  - Classification universal (any equivalent crash/ANR/perf/non-fatal backend); consumer supplies Crashlytics project handle, console credential (§11.4.10, never logged), severity table, closure-log path per §11.4.35; reference instantiation is a consuming project's §6.O + §6.AC.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-152-PROPAGATION, CM-CRASHLYTICS-ISSUE-FULLY-COVERED
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-crashlytics-monitoring, --monitor-crashes-only, --skip-non-fatals, --resolve-without-regression-test, --console-mark-is-fixed, --monitor-once, --mute-without-rationale
- **Honest boundary:** reduces known-field-defect surface but does not prove zero remaining field defects and does not replace §11.4.108 or §11.4.40; an issue is closed only when its regression guard is GREEN on a clean artifact, not when the console mark is flipped.
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.1, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.9, §11.4.34, §11.4.40, §11.4.43, §11.4.47, §11.4.69, §11.4.90, §11.4.102, §11.4.107, §11.4.108, §11.4.115, §11.4.118, §11.4.123, §11.4.130, §11.4.135, §11.4.138, §11.4.150, §1.1, §11.4.10, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.172 — Mandatory production-readiness planning with realistic timeline projection
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1391-1391
- **Rules:**
  - Every project MUST maintain a living production-readiness planning document that: (a) gives REALISTIC timeline projections for all milestones (MVP, beta, production-ready) based on actual velocity data (items completed per week, reopening rate, blocking dependencies); (b) identifies ALL danger zones, weaknesses, risk areas with mitigations; (c) accounts for HW delivery timelines, licensing delays, external dependency risks; (d) defines the critical path and which items can slip without affecting MVP; (e) includes workstation/build-capacity analysis and optimisation recommendations; (f) is updated at least monthly or whenever item count changes by >= 10%; (g) is cross-referenced against the workable-items database.
  - The document MUST live at `docs/research/production_planning_<YYYYMMDD>/ANALYSIS.md` with HTML+PDF exports per §11.4.65.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-172-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** projections are estimates based on measured velocity; they guarantee the methodology is sound, NOT that dates will be met.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.40, §11.4.42, §11.4.93, §11.4.108, §11.4.65, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.185 — Manual QA-team testing as the mandatory FINAL confirmation of done
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1393-1395
- **Rules:**
  - No set of features / scope of work / release may be considered fully completed until it has received MANUAL TESTING confirmation by the project's QA team as the FINAL confirmation step, EVERYWHERE and ALWAYS (every feature, scope, release), never forgotten.
  - (1) Automation is necessary-but-not-sufficient: §11.4, §11.4.5/§11.4.69, §11.4.52, §11.4.40, §11.4.108 four-layer SOURCE->ARTIFACT->RUNTIME->USER-VISIBLE, §11.4.132 are automated confidence gates; QA manual test is the FINAL human sufficiency gate.
  - (2) Composition with §11.4.52: ADDS, does not weaken. A feature MUST have BOTH the autonomous path (§11.4.52, primary, always-on) AND manual-QA final confirmation. Validated only by manual QA with no autonomous path = §11.4.52 violation; validated only by automation with no manual-QA sign-off = §11.4.185 violation.
  - (3) Workflow: autonomous-validation-GREEN -> build -> flash/deploy -> autonomous on-device validation -> HAND OFF to QA team for manual testing -> ONLY after QA manual confirmation is the scope fully completed / eligible for closure or a release tag. The §11.4.126 terminal condition REQUIRES QA confirmation before the tag is cut; a scope marked done / migrated to Fixed.md without a recorded QA-team confirmation is a violation (definition-of-done bluff).
  - (4) The agent MAY drive autonomous-GREEN + build + flash + on-device validation, but MUST then hand off and WAIT; it MUST NOT self-certify, simulate, or infer the manual step from automated evidence. While waiting it keeps progressing every OTHER non-blocked item in parallel (§11.4.87/§11.4.94/§11.4.97/§11.4.101).
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies QA-team identity, hand-off mechanism, confirmation-recording location per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-185-PROPAGATION, CM-MANUAL-QA-FINAL-CONFIRMATION
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-manual-qa, --automation-suffices, --self-certify-manual-step, --assume-qa-confirmed, --autonomous-only-completion
- **Honest boundary:** the manual confirmation is a recorded FACT, never assumed (§11.4.6); the wait parks that one scope, not the loop.
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.40, §11.4.52, §11.4.69, §11.4.108, §11.4.126, §11.4.129, §11.4.130, §11.4.132, §11.4.87, §11.4.94, §11.4.97, §11.4.101, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.200 — Non-targetable deploy/flash tooling MUST isolate exactly ONE eligible target and VERIFY-AFTER-WRITE on the INTENDED target
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1397-1415
- **Rules:**
  - Whenever a deploy/flash/install/write tool CANNOT address a specific target (no selector, or one the procedure does not pass), the procedure MUST satisfy ALL of the following. Reason: an auto-selecting flasher wrote to a sibling board, printed SUCCESS, and the intended board kept its old build.
  - (1) Targetability is a PRECONDITION: EITHER the tool takes an explicit stable selector (serial/UUID/stable id per §11.4.111, never an enumeration ordinal) and it IS passed, OR the procedure GUARANTEES EXACTLY ONE eligible target is present at write time (siblings disconnected/powered down/excluded), with the enumerated eligible-target set captured as evidence (size == 1).
  - (2) The tool's own success message / exit 0 is NOT proof (proves only that bytes reached the device the TOOL selected); treating it as deployment evidence is a bluff.
  - (3) VERIFY-AFTER-WRITE: READ BACK the deployed artifact's IDENTITY (build id/version/checksum/fingerprint) from the INTENDED target itself and assert it EQUALS the artifact just written; a mismatch or the OLD identity is a FAIL, never a warning (§11.4.108 ARTIFACT->RUNTIME applied to deployment).
  - (4) No validation on an unverified target: any test run against a target whose deployed-artifact identity was NOT verified is INVALID and any PASS is a PASS-bluff.
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies deploy tool, identity read-back, eligible-target enumeration per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-200-PROPAGATION, CM-DEPLOY-TARGET-ISOLATED-AND-VERIFIED
- **No escape hatch:** --auto-select-target-OK, --trust-tool-success-message, --skip-post-write-verify, --validate-unverified-target, --multiple-targets-on-bus-OK
- **Honest boundary:** isolation + read-back prove the INTENDED target holds the INTENDED artifact, NOT that the artifact is correct (still §11.4.108/§11.4.40/§11.4.130).
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.46, §11.4.108, §11.4.111, §11.4.119, §11.4.130, §11.4.133, §11.4.139, §11.4.40, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.207 — Instant multi-stream resume engine: durable content-addressed snapshot resumed in O(changed) reads
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1417-1423
- **Rules:**
  - The continuation mechanism (§12.10/§11.4.127/§11.4.131/§11.4.205) is EXTENDED, never replaced, by a mechanical engine so a fresh session resumes ALL work (every Track, main stream, agent) at once, at token cost O(changed streams), reading ONE snapshot manifest + one blob per stream, never the full handoff history.
  - (1) Content-addressed Merkle store: each stream's canonical state bytes named by sha256 (unchanged streams share a hash); a snapshot is ONE manifest referencing every stream's content-hash (§11.4.205(4)).
  - (2) O(streams) resume, O(history) NEVER on the resume path: `RestoreAll` reads the manifest + one blob per stream; the append-only event ledger is audit + lost-update recovery only, never read to resume.
  - (3) Tamper-evident + deterministic: every blob integrity-checked on read (bytes MUST hash to their id), deterministic round-trip (re-serialize must byte-match), no wall-clock in hashed content, verified by a SELF-VALIDATING oracle: golden-good PASS + golden-bad detected FAIL + negative-control (legitimately-older-but-valid snapshot) PASS (distinguishes LAGGING from TAMPERED; §11.4.201/§11.4.107(10)/§11.4.206(3)).
  - (4) Durable + atomic + single-writer + crash-safe: atomic ref write (temp->fsync->rename->dir-fsync, §11.4.205(6)), append-only ledger, single-writer-per-stream refusal (§11.4.206), advisory lock with provably-stale reap (`kill -0` liveness, never steals a live lock, §11.4.180/§9.2).
  - (5) Project-agnostic engine, consumer-owned data: the engine (`github.com/vasic-digital/continuum`, GitLab mirror) carries ZERO project literals, fails closed rather than guess a store path (§11.4.6/§11.4.177), is inherited BY REFERENCE as a depth-1 submodule under the §11.4.28(C) carve-out (`constitution/submodules/continuum/`, `helix-deps.yaml`, zero own-org deps); consumer supplies store path / actor / stream naming as DATA.
  - Anti-bluff: four-layer coverage (unit + integration + e2e + stress + chaos §11.4.85, race-clean), measured resume Metric (`blobs_read == 1 + streams` is the O(streams) proof), self-validating oracle as captured evidence (§11.4.5/§11.4.69/§11.4.107).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-207-PROPAGATION, CM-CONTINUUM-RESUME-ENGINE-PRESENT
- **No escape hatch:** --resume-reads-history, --skip-integrity-check, --unvalidated-oracle-OK, --hand-typed-resume-state, --per-project-resume-reimpl
- **Honest boundary:** snapshots the state an agent REPORTS, not its execution image (not CRIU/durable-execution, §11.4.112); `est_tokens` is a `bytes/4` heuristic, not a tokenizer count.
- **Composes:** §12.10, §11.4.127, §11.4.131, §11.4.205, §11.4.116, §11.4.147, §11.4.180, §11.4.201, §11.4.206, §11.4.107(10), §11.4.28, §11.4.177, §11.4.85, §9.2, §11.4.17
- **Review addendum:** Gate CM-CONTINUUM-RESUME-ENGINE-PRESENT requires: the engine under `constitution/submodules/continuum/`; `go test -race ./...` green; `continuum selfcheck` good=PASS, bad=FAIL, negctrl=PASS; zero project literals.

#### §11.4.208 — Operator-request-history document: project-local always-in-sync ledger of every operator request/prompt
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1425-1435
- **Rules:**
  - Every governed project MUST maintain a single project-local, append-only, newest-first operator-request-history document of EVERY operator request/prompt at a fixed project-declared path (e.g. `docs/requests/history.md`; §11.4.35; never moved without §11.4.66 operator decision). The RULE is universal (constitution); the DOCUMENT is project-local and NEVER placed into the constitution (§11.4.35/§11.4.17).
  - Each entry MUST carry EXACTLY: (1) Request content (verbatim where archived else faithful complete summary, each entry marks which); (2) Accepted (when): date + time + TIMEZONE stated EXPLICITLY on every entry (consumer declares default zone; date-only => `time UNKNOWN`, never fabricated); (3) Track (§11.4.176/§11.4.178/§11.4.182); (4) Alias (§11.4.182/§11.4.196); (5) Model + effort.
  - (A) NO INVENTION (§11.4.6): an unrecoverable field is recorded literally `UNKNOWN` (one-line reason where useful), never guessed; a fabricated timestamp/alias/model is a bluff.
  - (B) HONEST RECONSTRUCTION BOUNDARY: pre-mandate sessions are best-effort reconstructed from the durable dated record (mandate provenance dates, session ledgers, handoff docs, VCS history), unrecoverable fields marked `UNKNOWN`, boundary stated explicitly (scope note), never implied complete.
  - (C) ALWAYS IN SYNC + EXPORTED: §11.4.44 revision header; §12.10 trigger set (every new operator prompt appends a row); exported per §11.4.65/§11.4.73 (`.md`+`.html`+`.pdf`+`.docx` where four-format applies, each non-`.md` sibling mtime >= the `.md`).
  - (D) KEEP-APPLYING MECHANISM: ship an append mechanism (helper script and/or `UserPromptSubmit`-class hook) appending a newest-first row per NEW prompt at capture time with exact timestamp + track + alias + model + effort (track/alias derived deterministically per §11.4.182, honest `?`/`UNKNOWN` when undeterminable); a helper without the auto-capture hook is honestly a partial mechanism (hook wiring a tracked §11.4.197/§12.10 follow-up, never claimed as automatic).
  - (E) COMPLEMENTS, NEVER REPLACES any per-session no-loss ledger (§11.4.197/§11.4.202), the workable-items DB SSoT (§11.4.93/§11.4.95), or §12.10/§11.4.131 resumption artefacts; loss of a requirement at intake is FORBIDDEN (§11.4.197).
  - (F) RULE-UNIVERSAL / DOCUMENT-PROJECT-LOCAL (§11.4.35); document, path and default timezone live ONLY in the consumer layer (§11.4.28 decoupling).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-208-PROPAGATION, CM-REQUEST-HISTORY-DOC-PRESENT
- **No escape hatch:** --request-history-optional, --skip-request-log, --no-timezone-stamp, --invent-missing-field, --request-history-in-constitution, --prompt-without-history-entry
- **Honest boundary:** reconstruction of pre-mandate prompts is best-effort with UNKNOWN fields; a helper without the auto-capture hook is a partial mechanism and not claimed otherwise.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.35, §11.4.44, §11.4.65, §11.4.73, §11.4.118, §11.4.131, §12.10, §11.4.176, §11.4.178, §11.4.182, §11.4.196, §11.4.197, §11.4.202, §11.4.93, §11.4.95, §11.4.66, §11.4.67, §11.4.28, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.210 — Zero-loss request/prompt intake: every operator request MUST be mechanically captured, tracked, and processed
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1437-1451
- **Rules:**
  - Every operator request/prompt MUST be (a) CAPTURED in the §11.4.208 request-history ledger MECHANICALLY at intake, never manual vigilance; (b) TRACKED, mapped to a tracked action/workable item (§11.4.202, §11.4.197) OR an explicit evidence-backed no-op-with-reason; (c) PROCESSED (respected, acted upon, executed, never skipped/ignored/avoided/dropped). Loss at ANY stage is a PASS-bluff at the requirements-intake layer (same class as §11.4.197). Strengthens §11.4.208(D): the auto-capture hook is PROMOTED from "tracked follow-up / partial" to MANDATORY, wired, verified. Reason: a session's prompts went unrecorded because the hook was left unwired.
  - (1) MECHANICAL CAPTURE (§11.4.205): the ledger's keep-applying mechanism MUST be a WIRED, VERIFIED-RUNTIME-STATE auto-capture hook (`UserPromptSubmit`-class appending every prompt at intake), NOT a tracked follow-up or manual conductor step. "Installed" = verified runtime state in the live hook path (§11.4.205(3)); the hook MUST be non-fatal (never blocks/fails a prompt) and honest (`UNKNOWN` fields never invented, §11.4.6).
  - (2) DOCS-CHAIN BOUND (§11.4.106): ledger + four-format exports (§11.4.65/§11.4.73) bound into the docs-chain; a stale export is a sync violation.
  - (3) GATED (§11.4.75, enforced-not-advisory): a pre-build gate FAILs if the hook is not wired in the live hook path (verified-installed per §11.4.205(3), content-matched to its tracked source) OR the ledger is stale relative to the durable prompt record; paired §1.1 mutation (un-wire hook / orphan ledger -> gate FAILs).
  - (4) AUDIT + NO SILENT DROP: any prompt found un-captured (`.remember/` logs, older CONTINUATION revisions, transcripts) MUST be back-filled, never silently dropped (§11.4.197); every captured request resolves to a tracked action/item (§11.4.202) OR an explicit evidence-backed no-op-with-reason; captured-then-ignored is forbidden.
  - (5) PROCESS EVERY CAPTURED REQUEST: the autonomous loop (§11.4.126/.87/.94/.97/.103) treats every open captured request as an actionable queue item; its done-condition MUST NOT read satisfied while any captured request is un-processed (mirrors §11.4.147(e)).
  - (6) Machine-derivable fields (timestamp/track/alias) captured verbatim; model/effort where undeterminable are `UNKNOWN`; a back-filled row honestly marks its reconstruction boundary (§11.4.208(B)), never a fabricated time.
  - Consumer supplies ledger path, hook path, docs-chain context per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-210-PROPAGATION, CM-REQUEST-CAPTURE-HOOK-WIRED
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-request-capture, --manual-ledger-OK, --hook-optional, --drop-unprocessed-request, --ledger-may-be-stale, --request-may-be-skipped
- **Honest boundary:** model/effort fields undeterminable stay `UNKNOWN`; back-filled rows carry an honest reconstruction boundary.
- **Composes:** §11.4.197, §11.4.202, §11.4.208, §11.4.205, §11.4.106, §11.4.126, §11.4.87, §11.4.94, §11.4.97, §11.4.103, §11.4.6, §11.4.75, §11.4.147(e), §11.4.65, §11.4.73, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.211 — Merge-conflict resolution during main->feature/product/flavor merges MUST run on Opus at xhigh effort as PRIMARY substrate, with a genuine-unavailability Sonnet fallback; no Fable (amended 2026-10-04)
- **Source:** Constitution.md (constitution tip a71b1767) lines 10610-10622 (groups/project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1453-1465 holds the pre-amendment text, see pin-upstream-findings.md)
- **Rules:**
  - Any merge-CONFLICT resolution while integrating the canonical trunk (`main`/`master`) into a feature/product/flavor branch (§11.4.188 cadence, §11.4.195 integration, §11.4.41 merge-first, §11.4.167(D) trunk-into-stream, §11.4.167(I) approval-gated back-merge) MUST be done on the Opus model at `xhigh` effort as PRIMARY substrate. Merge-resolution analogue of §11.4.209: pins model+effort for the DECISION-MAKING (which side to keep, union both sides without loss, marker removal, semantic reconciliation). The 2026-09-26 mandate superseded the model choice of the 2026-07-16 mandate (Fable-first); its scope and `xhigh` requirement stand. Amended 2026-10-04 by the same verbatim operator mandate as §11.4.209 (use Sonnet when Opus cannot be used; nothing blocked; maximal efficiency).
  - (A) PRIMARY substrate Opus-xhigh plus genuine-unavailability SONNET FALLBACK (amended 2026-10-04), no Fable: Fable is NOT permitted in any role; no lower effort for Opus itself. When Opus-xhigh is genuinely unavailable (not configured, rate-limited or unreachable, established as FACT per §11.4.6, never guessed) the resolution MUST be carried out on Sonnet (highest effort the path can set) rather than blocked; the Opus-unavailability FACT and the Sonnet substitution MUST both be recorded in the merge's captured evidence (§11.4.5/§11.4.69), never presenting a Sonnet-resolved merge as Opus-resolved. `xhigh` is REQUIRED on whichever substrate resolves the conflict where the dispatch path can set it (careless resolution drops a commit or commits a marker, §9/§11.4.41 step 3); where it cannot (§11.4.231(F.2) harness gap) the gap is recorded, never claimed as xhigh. ONLY when BOTH Opus and Sonnet are genuinely unavailable (each its own captured FACT) is the resolution BLOCKED and deferred: record the facts, do NOT complete the merge, leave the branch quiescent with no conflict marker committed (§11.4.84/§11.4.41 step 3).
  - (B) Scope: operator named tracks 2-4 (feature/product/flavor); GENERALISES per §11.4.17 to EVERY controlled main->(feature|product|flavor) merge on EVERY track that hits a conflict.
  - (C) Safety preserved: sets MODEL + EFFORT only; BOUNDED BY §11.4.113 (never force-push), §9/§9.2 (no commit lost, hardlinked pre-op backup before large/risky merge), §11.4.41 step 3 (ZERO conflict markers committed, ZERO file silently dropped, union of both sides preserved), §11.4.188(4) anti-bluff (post-merge smoke GREEN + conflict-marker scan empty + no-lost-commit, captured evidence §11.4.5/§11.4.69), §11.4.84 (quiescent-only), §11.4.37/§11.4.71 (fetch-first).
  - (D) A merge whose conflicts were resolved on Fable or any model other than Opus or the sanctioned Sonnet fallback, or below `xhigh`, or on Sonnet with no recorded Opus-unavailability fact, is a bluff at the substrate layer; the merge's captured evidence MUST record which model + effort resolved the conflicts (and, when blocked, the FACT that both Opus and Sonnet were unavailable); an effort the path cannot set is recorded as that gap.
  - Strict extension of §11.4.209 (review-side) to merge-side; the two are the review-side and merge-side halves of the same Opus-xhigh-primary-plus-Sonnet-fallback discipline; strengthens §11.4.188/§11.4.195/§11.4.41.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-211-PROPAGATION, CM-MERGE-CONFLICT-OPUS-XHIGH (a conflict-resolving merge records model=Opus + effort=xhigh or the honest §11.4.231(F.2) gap, OR model=Sonnet with a captured Opus-unavailability FACT; Fable/other model, xhigh claimed where unsettable, or Sonnet with no fact FAILs; BLOCKED with a captured fact that both were unavailable is honest and MUST NOT fire, the §11.4.201(1) guard; paired §1.1 mutations; gate-code is a separate work item)
- **No escape hatch:** beyond the sanctioned (A) Sonnet fallback (which requires a captured Opus-unavailability FACT): --merge-conflict-any-model, --skip-opus-merge-resolution, --non-xhigh-merge-conflict, --resolve-conflict-lower-effort-OK, --escalate-to-fable, --sonnet-fallback-without-recorded-fact, --leave-merge-blocked-while-sonnet-reachable
- **Honest boundary:** a merge recorded BLOCKED with a captured fact that both Opus and Sonnet were unavailable MUST NOT fire the gate (false-positive guard §11.4.201(1)).
- **Project note (Catalogizer, recorded 2026-10-06 in WP-07, corrected by the WF8 fix pass):** canon REQUIRES the (A) Sonnet fallback for merge-conflict resolution too (it is the merge-side half of §11.4.209). The project's earlier "blocked, never substituted" text digested the pre-amendment canon and was never an owner mandate. OPEN canon conflict, owner question OD-WP07-SONNET-FALLBACK (default: follow canon); interim practice, an agent's interim choice and not an owner decision: follow canon (Opus `xhigh` first, Sonnet fallback only on a captured Opus-unavailability fact, recorded with model and effort).
- **Composes:** §11.4.209, §11.4.188, §11.4.195, §11.4.41, §11.4.113, §9, §9.2, §11.4.6, §11.4.167(D)(I), §11.4.84, §11.4.37, §11.4.71, §11.4.196, §11.4.183, §11.4.231, §11.4.5, §11.4.69, §11.4.201, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.213 — FEATURE research-scheduling directive: SCHEDULES (never synchronously executes) a deep enterprise-grade research + planning effort as a tracked workable item
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1467-1487
- **Rules:**
  - Adds a fourth registered action `FEATURE` to the §11.4.202 reporting-directive family, recognised via ALL §11.4.140 forms: `FEATURE :: <desc>`, `DEFAULT::FEATURE :: <desc>`, `/FEATURE <desc>`, `/DEFAULT::FEATURE <desc>`, `FEATURE ---> <desc>`, and the single-colon `FEATURE: <desc>`; REGISTERED-ACTION-ONLY: the action token grammar is UPPERCASE-only (`[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*`), so lowercase prose "feature: ..." never expands and is never asked about (§11.4.6). `\FEATURE` escapes to a literal per §11.4.140.
  - (1) SCHEDULING, NOT SYNCHRONOUS EXECUTION: the directive's own execution is fast and bounded: create the tracked item (Type=Task, Status=Queued, §11.4.54 stable id), append it to a durable never-dropped feature-research queue, sync DB-derived documents, push to configured trackers, via the SAME §11.4.202 engine (never a duplicate implementation). The deep multi-day research is performed LATER by the standing autonomous loop (§11.4.87/.94/.97/.103/.126) when it claims the item and is driven to COMPLETED (implemented AND wired AND verified) or evidence-backed CLOSED under §11.4.197; never left un-wired in the backlog; "scheduled" is never reported as "done".
  - (2) The created item's comprehensive description (§11.4.148 D2/§11.4.171) embeds verbatim, as its acceptance-defining WORK PROGRAM: (a) deep web-research series (articles, guides, papers, open-source projects/codebases, examples) per §11.4.8/§11.4.99/§11.4.150; (b) systematic-debug (§11.4.102) of ALL data to enumerate EVERY weak spot/gap/danger-zone/inconsistency/imperfection, with a risk-free rock-solid solution for EACH, none unaddressed; (c) design ALWAYS enterprise-grade, bleeding-edge, innovative; (d) MANDATORY exhaustive documentation (technical docs, implementation plan down to lines-of-code + micro-PoCs, diagrams/schemes/graphs, illustrations, SQL definitions, templates), four-format-exported and revision-headed per §11.4.65/§11.4.73; (e) investigate + plan REUSE of existing `vasic-digital` + `HelixDevelopment` submodules BEFORE any rewrite, extending where needed, fully decoupled/project-not-aware per §11.4.28/§11.4.74/§11.4.177; (f) test planning from day one: every supported test type, Challenges submodule, full HelixQA bank coverage per §11.4.27/§11.4.169; (g) phases/tasks/subtasks nano-detailed, no vague placeholders; (h) enterprise scalability and maximal performance; (i) for UI/UX surfaces, full wireframes/diagrams/design files (Figma/PSD/PDF or project-mandated formats) via OpenDesign per §11.4.162/§11.4.190; (j) full CodeGraph integration with regular/real-time index sync per §11.4.78/§11.4.79/§11.4.80; (k) fully-detailed workable items (every detail + reference + attachment) synced in REAL TIME to the SQLite SSoT (§11.4.93/§11.4.95), every derived workable-items document, related project docs/components, and every connected external tracker (ClickUp, HelixTrack, JIRA, others per §11.4.148 D5), honestly SKIPPING any absent tracker with a machine-readable reason (`credentials_absent`/`tracker_client_absent`, §11.4.10/§11.4.6), NEVER faking a push.
  - (3) The item: Type=Task (§11.4.16; feature may later spawn its own Feature-typed items), Status=Queued (§11.4.15), stable id (§11.4.54), §11.4.148/§11.4.171 description embedding (i) the verbatim feature description, (ii) the full clause-(2) mandate verbatim, (iii) acceptance criteria: full research-doc tree produced under the item's recorded destination path, every gap has a designed solution, implementation plan down to lines-of-code exists, planned follow-on workable items created, whole effort validated per §11.4.197. Undetermined sections recorded as explicit `UNKNOWN:` gaps, never invented.
  - (4) Decoupled engine, reused machinery: the engine `constitution/scripts/feature/schedule_feature_research.sh` invokes the SAME §11.4.202 `report_item.sh` for item creation/doc sync/tracker push (not reimplemented). FEATURE-specific additions: research-doc-tree destination path and the durable `docs/requests/feature_queue.md` queue entry (mirroring `BACKGROUND`'s `docs/requests/background_queue.md`). Both engines inherited BY REFERENCE, ZERO project literals, fail closed with an actionable message when consumer config is absent (§11.4.6/§11.4.28/§11.4.177); project values (DB path, id prefix, research-doc root, sync command, tracker bindings) are consumer DATA in `feature.yaml`.
  - (5) Anti-bluff four-layer: pre-build gate `CM-FEATURE-DIRECTIVE` whose FUNCTIONAL invariant SOURCES and RUNS the §11.4.140 parser (never grep-only, §11.4.108) proving `FEATURE` expands via single-colon, `::`, arrow, slash forms while lowercase prose does NOT; paired §1.1 mutation test proving every invariant load-bearing (registry presence, engine parseability, decoupling, durable-queue append, delegation-not-reimplementation, scheduling-not-synchronous framing); captured evidence of a real feature-research item landing in a temp SQLite DB, derived docs regenerated FROM the DB, trackers SKIPping honestly.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-213-PROPAGATION, CM-FEATURE-DIRECTIVE
- **No escape hatch:** --feature-runs-synchronously, --skip-feature-queue, --feature-without-research-mandate, --reimplement-tracker-push, --hardcode-project-in-engine, --skip-item-creation
- **Honest boundary:** "scheduled" is never reported as "done"; undetermined sections are explicit `UNKNOWN:` gaps.
