#### §11.4.229 — Live in-session task/todo tracker MUST always be up to date and fully in sync with the real work state
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1489-1507
- **Rules:**
  - The agent's LIVE IN-SESSION TASK/TODO TRACKER (harness task list / `TodoWrite`-class tool / equivalent moment-to-moment execution-state surface) MUST ALWAYS be up to date and FULLY IN SYNC with real live work state: never stale, never showing completed work as pending, never showing pending/blocked/abandoned work as done or in-progress. Updated the MOMENT any task starts (in-progress), completes (done), is blocked, abandoned, split, re-scoped, or newly discovered; not batched, not reconstructed from memory at the end, not left on a superseded plan. A lagging tracker is a PASS-bluff at the execution-transparency layer.
  - (A) EVERY STATE-CHANGE UPDATES IT IMMEDIATELY: exactly one task in-progress where the surface models single-active-task; no completed task left pending; no pending task left done; no ghost task for dropped work (dropped work is closed with a reason); deferring the update is forbidden.
  - (B) NEVER STALE, NEVER INVERTED (§11.4.6): content is CAPTURED FACT, never a guess or aspirational plan; falsely-done = PASS-bluff, falsely-pending = FAIL-bluff (§11.4.1); drift is corrected the moment observed.
  - (C) DISTINCT ARTIFACT, COMPLEMENTS NEVER REPLACES: the ephemeral in-session tracker is different from §12.10 CONTINUATION, §11.4.131 session-resumption file, §11.4.97 progress cadence, §11.4.106(F) write-seam doc/DB sync, §11.4.202/§11.4.208 DB/ledgers; none of those binds the live tracker itself; a correct tracker is the truth they are materialised FROM; in-session analogue of §12.10.
  - (D) Where the runtime exposes NO such tracker, honestly N/A (§11.4.3 SKIP-with-reason; binds the moment such a surface exists, per §11.4.96 latent-binding); mandates that WHATEVER tracker exists is kept in sync, not that a tool must exist; "in sync" = reflects real work state as the agent knows it now, not omniscience.
  - Classification universal; consumer runtime supplies its concrete tracker surface per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-229-PROPAGATION, CM-LIVE-TASK-TRACKER-IN-SYNC
- **No escape hatch:** --tracker-may-lag, --batch-todo-updates, --stale-task-list-OK, --reconstruct-todos-at-end, --skip-task-tracker-sync, --pending-may-be-done, --completed-may-stay-pending
- **Honest boundary:** honestly N/A where the runtime exposes no live tracker; "in sync" means as known to the agent at that moment. Gate-code is a separate work item, not claimed shipped.
- **Composes:** §12.10, §11.4.131, §11.4.97, §11.4.106(F), §11.4.126, §11.4.116, §11.4.202, §11.4.208, §11.4.6, §11.4.1, §11.4.3, §11.4.96, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.235 — Build-and-deploy the moment source fixes are proven-correct (test-side hardening is a parallel stage, never a build gate) + post-deploy version increment
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1509-1521 for clauses (A)-(C); clause (D): Constitution.md (constitution tip a71b1767) lines 11113-11117 (groups/ at this tip does not carry clause (D), see pin-upstream-findings.md)
- **Rules:**
  - (A) The moment SOURCE fixes of a batch are done AND proven-correct (proven-correct = mandatory independent SOURCE-correctness review returned a clean GO: §11.4.125/§11.4.142/§11.4.194 on the source diff, on the §11.4.209 Opus-`xhigh` substrate, iterated to zero-finding/zero-warning GO per §11.4.134), the build MUST be triggered, pre-build + post-build tests EXECUTED (§11.4.108 layer-1 before, layer-2 after), and the artifact deployed. IN PARALLEL WITH the build AND manual-QA (§11.4.185), NEVER gating the build: (1) gate-instrumentation hardening + new-gate authoring (§11.4.110); (2) paired §1.1 mutations + four-layer §11.4.4(b) coverage + HelixQA Challenges; (3) "gates and checks of all kinds" (§11.4.96); (4) re-review of that test-instrumentation work. The build's GO-SIGNAL is source-correctness alone; test-guard hardening + its re-review are a deploy-independent parallel stage (§11.4.230(A)). Holding the build to wait for test-instrumentation buildout/re-review when source is proven-correct is a violation.
  - (B) POST-DEPLOY VERSION INCREMENT + MANUAL-QA-DEPLOY CYCLE BOUNDARY: the moment image(s)/artifact(s) deploy, the version code/version is INCREMENTED (next build targets next version; every deployed artifact has a distinct, monotonic, greppable id; §11.4.151/§11.4.108/§11.4.200); two deployments sharing one version id is a violation. EVERY deployment for manual QA testing (§11.4.185) is a DEVELOPMENT-CYCLE BOUNDARY: it CLOSES the outgoing cycle and STARTS a NEW one, with the version incremented AT THAT POINT, new-cycle work targeting the NEXT monotonic version (§11.4.151 prefix preserved), ALWAYS, as the STANDING working model. QA findings against the deployed artifact land in the NEW cycle on the NEW version id, never patched onto the already-QA-deployed id; new-cycle work still targeting the QA-deployed version id is a violation.
  - (C) STANDING DEFAULT (§11.4.126/§11.4.230/§11.4.103), never a per-request opt-in.
  - (D) FINDING-LAYER CLASSIFIER (added 2026-10-03, research-derived from the §11.4.230 four-agent audit of a consuming project's SpecKit-004 T048 remediation saga): the decidable split clause (A) relies on, mandatory at every §11.4.125/§11.4.142/§11.4.194 review verdict. Every finding a verdict records (§11.4.115(F) machine-written) MUST carry exactly one `finding_layer` from the closed set {source-defect | test-instrumentation | process-doc}, a field DISTINCT from any other per-finding classification the record carries (e.g. a pre-existing `class` field {mechanical | judgment | false-positive} is a different axis). `source-defect`: the finding shows the SHIPPED artifact's own behaviour wrong, unsafe or exploitable as it will run, OR invalidates the evidence that proves THIS batch's fixes correct (their §11.4.115 RED->GREEN guard, §11.4.108 runtime signature, or covering test per §11.4.125(6); a proving guard that cannot fail, or whose reviewer-authored mutation survives per §11.4.194(6)(d), means the source is NOT proven-correct). `test-instrumentation`: concerns only future-regression coverage, mutation-guard robustness or detection completeness of a guard/gate/meta-test whose protected behaviour was ALREADY proven, with no production decision path shown wrong and no proof-of-this-batch evidence invalidated. `process-doc`: labels, comments, citations or prose with no behavioural effect. The layer is recorded by the REVIEWER (§11.4.240/§11.4.249); the producer MAY contest it only via a fresh review round and MUST NOT lower it unilaterally. A finding that cannot be decidably classified defaults to `source-defect` (conservative-safe, §11.4.201(4), §11.4.101). §11.4.134 is NOT relaxed: every finding of every layer is still driven to zero-finding zero-warning GO in its own loop; (D) decides only which GO is the BUILD GO-signal: a batch/slice is BUILD-ELIGIBLE when its source-defect findings reach that GO, while outstanding test-instrumentation/process-doc findings continue as their own tracked §11.4.197 item on a §11.4.230(A)/§11.4.103 parallel stream. A BATCHED review spanning many slices/files MUST record its verdict PER SLICE/FILE, never one undifferentiated verdict. Applies prospectively; recorded verdicts are never rewritten or reclassified (§11.4.6/§11.4.268). Honest boundary: classification is a required, recorded, reviewer-owned decision, not made easy or infallible.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-235-PROPAGATION, CM-BUILD-ON-SOURCE-PROVEN-NOT-TEST-SIDE, CM-VERSION-INCREMENT-ON-DEPLOY, CM-REVIEW-FINDING-CLASS-RECORDED (clause (D): FAIL a batched-review verdict covering more than one slice/file with no per-slice verdict or no per-finding `finding_layer`; FAIL a slice marked build-eligible while any source-defect finding in it has not reached GO; FAIL a `finding_layer` lowered by the producer without a fresh review round; paired §1.1 mutation; gate-code is a separate work item, NOT claimed shipped, registered as a tracked deferral in scripts/gates/gate_ledger_deferrals.tsv; it binds additively by computing whether the existing `source_review_go` marker may be written). Upstream correction: CM-BUILD-ON-SOURCE-PROVEN-NOT-TEST-SIDE and CM-VERSION-INCREMENT-ON-DEPLOY ARE implemented (scripts/gates/cm_build_on_source_proven_not_test_side.sh, cm_version_increment_on_deploy.sh and their paired mutation tests); the earlier 'gate-code = separate work item' disclaimer for those two was stale.
- **No escape hatch:** --build-behind-test-hardening, --test-side-gates-the-build, --skip-source-correctness-review, --deploy-without-version-increment, --not-default-speed-mode, --serialise-build-and-validate
- **Honest boundary:** relocates the test-instrumentation re-review + gate hardening OFF the build critical path; does NOT weaken any substantive gate. The source-correctness review still precedes and gates the build; pre/post-build tests run at their seams; §11.4.185, §11.4.129, §11.4.40 un-weakened. Bounded to future-regression instrumentation: a check proving the SHIPPED artifact wrong is a §11.4.108 L1-2 gate and stays on the critical path. Clause (D) supplies the mandatory classification mechanism this boundary's own test presupposes: a review that never classifies its findings has not applied this boundary, it has merely stated it.
- **Composes:** §11.4.125, §11.4.142, §11.4.194, §11.4.209, §11.4.134, §11.4.108, §11.4.110, §11.4.4(b), §11.4.96, §11.4.230(A), §11.4.185, §11.4.151, §11.4.200, §11.4.126, §11.4.103, §11.4.129, §11.4.40, §11.4.201(1), §11.4.6, §11.4.227, §11.4.17
- **Review addendum:** FAIL conditions of the recommended gates: a build held past the source-correctness GO while test-side work is unfinished; a build started with NO source-review GO (the §11.4.201(1) dual-assertion guard); a new-artifact deploy sharing a version id; work of the cycle opened by a manual-QA deploy still targeting the QA-deployed version id.

#### §11.4.236 — QA-deploy-readiness gate: no manual-QA hand-off until the mandated validation produced a candidate-fingerprinted PASS verdict; a blocker MUST bind to a seam, never prose
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1523-1527
- **Rules:**
  - (1) DEPLOY-SEAM VERDICT-COVERAGE (§11.4.135 applied to the QA-deploy seam): a release artifact MUST NOT be deployed, published, or handed off for manual QA (§11.4.185) until the mandated autonomous validation(s) for that artifact produced a machine-written PASS verdict whose artifact fingerprint == the candidate (§11.4.115(F), fingerprint READ FROM THE TARGET at run time). ABSENCE of the verdict BLOCKS the deploy exactly as a FAIL does.
  - (2) MECHANICAL, NOT PROSE (§11.4.205/§11.4.226): the refusal lives in the deploy tool itself (the seam), never in prose an agent is trusted to honour; a source-gate asserting the validation harness merely EXISTS is necessary-not-sufficient.
  - (3) BLOCKER-BINDING RULE: any requirement an operator declares a blocker (a §11.4.140 CRITICAL, or explicit "release blocker"/"QA-ready blocker") MUST be bound to a mechanical seam at the point it gates, never satisfied by prose and never DOWNGRADED to a follow-up; when the blocker's own INSTRUMENT bugs, the response is §11.4.4/§11.4.120 (STOP, fix the instrument, complete the blocker), never route around it.
  - (4) EXPLICIT, RECORDED OVERRIDE ONLY: no silent bypass; an override is an explicit, logged, operator-set flag (the §11.4.234/§11.4.135 recorded-deferral pattern), never a follow-up downgrade or opaque skip.
  - (5) THE GATE IS SELF-VALIDATED (§11.4.107(10)/§11.4.201): ships golden-good (verdict present + PASS + fingerprint-match -> allow) + golden-bad (absent -> refuse / not-pass -> refuse / fingerprint-mismatch -> refuse) so it cannot false-allow; the verdict-emitter reads the fingerprint from the target at run time, never a hardcoded per-release value (§11.4.111; a version-pinned validator lets a stale verdict pass).
  - Classification universal; consumer supplies mandated-validation set, verdict path/schema, deploy tool per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-236-PROPAGATION, CM-QA-DEPLOY-READINESS-GATE
- **No escape hatch:** --deploy-without-verdict, --prose-blocker-suffices, --downgrade-blocker-to-followup, --skip-readiness-gate, --verdict-fingerprint-optional, --silent-override
- **Honest boundary:** the seam proves a candidate-matching PASS verdict EXISTS; it does NOT replace the §11.4.185 manual-QA sufficiency gate and is only as honest as the validation whose verdict it consumes (§11.4.5/§11.4.69/§11.4.107). Gate-code is a separate work item, not claimed shipped.
- **Composes:** §11.4.4, §11.4.107(10), §11.4.108, §11.4.111, §11.4.115(F), §11.4.120, §11.4.126, §11.4.135, §11.4.146(D3), §11.4.185, §11.4.201, §11.4.205, §11.4.226, §11.4.234, §11.4.140, §11.4.6, §11.4.227, §11.4.17, §11.4.35

#### §11.4.260 — Cutting-edge enterprise quality + production-deployment readiness (operator mandate 2026-08-15)
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1529-1551
- **Rules:**
  - Every work product MUST be built for cutting-edge enterprise quality targeted at production deployment, maximal stability and zero nasty surprises; standing default from the first prompt of a session for every batch, subagent, feature, fix and change; NEVER a per-request opt-in, NEVER downgraded to "good-enough", "will-do-for-now" or "MVP-first".
  - Every change MUST satisfy the closed production-readiness invariant set (B) before it is considered done; the project maintains docs/PRODUCTION_READINESS.md tracking readiness per component x invariant x evidence-source.
  - Strengthens §11.4.190 (web-only) into a universal discipline across all surfaces (web, service, CLI, container, library, docs, orchestration, tests, gates).
  - (A) "Cutting-edge" = current best-known engineering approach for the problem class, sourced via §11.4.99 latest-source verification (never memory), §11.4.150 deep multi-angle research, §11.4.8 external precedent, applied fully; NEVER a shortcut, stub, placeholder-with-TODO, "for now" (§11.4.124), duct-tape workaround or "will fix later" (§11.4.197). If the best-known approach is unavailable in the project's constraints, the gap MUST be honestly tracked (§11.4.197 item + [OPEN] marker per §11.4.223), never silently absorbed.
  - (B) Invariant set, ALL required: (1) functional completeness - every stated capability wired and verified on a clean target per §11.4.108, no unwired feature, no dead-code path (§11.4.124); (2) observability - health endpoint, structured logs, per-operation metrics, distributed-trace-ready surface, evidence-capture at every gate (§11.4.85, §11.4.128); (3) resilience - real failure-injection per §11.4.85 chaos (process death, network fault, resource exhaustion, state corruption), recovery verified never assumed; (4) security - SonarQube CLI installed and scanned (§11.4.184), no leaked credentials (§11.4.10 pre-store audit), supply-chain integrity at fleet minimum SLSA Build Level 2 (§11.4.246); (5) performance - measured under sustained load per §11.4.85, latency/throughput/resource footprint within declared SLOs; (6) maintainability - code review at Opus-xhigh (§11.4.209) with zero findings and zero warnings iterated to GO per §11.4.134; (7) deployability - rootless container (§11.4.161), deterministic build and reproducible artifact (§11.4.108 layer 2), deployment verified via §11.4.200 target-isolation and §11.4.108 layer 3 runtime signature; (8) documentability - §11.4.257, §11.4.258, §11.4.259 all GREEN; (9) testability - §11.4.27/§11.4.169 seven-type breadth plus §11.4.224 coverage floor, every gate paired with §1.1 mutation, every regression permanently guarded per §11.4.135; (10) operational runbook - documented remediation path for every non-trivial failure mode (§11.4.257 guide class).
  - (C) Zero nasty surprises: no known-broken behavior ships (§11.4.238); no failing gate silenced (§11.4.120, §11.4.201); no test disabled without a tracked follow-up (§11.4.197); no closed-with-workaround defect masquerading as fixed (§11.4.34); no "fails sometimes but rarely" tolerance (§11.4.50, §11.4.85); no try/catch/swallow silent-failure paths - a caught error either has a captured recovery path or re-raises to a bounded operator decision per §11.4.101/§11.4.66.
  - (D) Standing default: composes §11.4.126, §11.4.198, §11.4.183, §11.4.231; engaged from the first prompt, never negotiated, never opt-in.
  - (E) docs/PRODUCTION_READINESS.md: per-component x invariant x evidence-source table (§11.4.153 sibling); revision header per §11.4.44; auto-synced via §11.4.106; reachable from README per §11.4.212; source of truth for the §11.4.259 production-readiness gauge.
  - EXTENSION to (B)(2) observability mechanism (2026-08-20): (a) the three signals are distinct: structured logs (queryable key-value JSON events, not prose strings), metrics (numeric time series), traces (tree of timed spans), plus crash/ANR analytics (symbolicated stacks with breadcrumbs grouped by signature); do not attribute "observability triad" or "three pillars" labels to the corpus; (b) a correlation id (request_id/trace_id) MUST thread all signals and MUST survive async boundaries (queue, webhook, worker, scheduled sweep); pivot order metric -> trace -> log ("narrow before you theorize"); (c) crash-free users/sessions is a release gate (not raw crash count), and a crash signature new at a release boundary is a release blocker even at low volume (binds §11.4.152 and §11.4.265); thresholds are consumer DATA (§11.4.6/§11.4.35), no numeric value mandated.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-260-PROPAGATION, CM-PRODUCTION-READINESS-TRACKER-PRESENT, CM-CUTTING-EDGE-POSTURE-ALWAYS-ON, CM-ZERO-NASTY-SURPRISES-AUDIT, CM-CORRELATION-ID-THREADED-ACROSS-BOUNDARIES, CM-CRASH-FREE-RELEASE-GATE (paired §1.1 mutations; extension mutations: drop correlation id at the queue boundary -> first gate MUST FAIL; admit a release with a new crash signature at low volume -> second MUST FAIL; golden-FALSE: surface with no async hop and no crash channel, honest §11.4.3 SKIP-with-reason, MUST NOT fire; gate-code = separate work item, not claimed shipped)
- **No escape hatch:** --mvp-quality-OK, --good-enough, --will-fix-later, --skip-production-readiness-tracker, --production-readiness-optional, --acceptable-flakiness, --for-now-implementation
- **Honest boundary:** Mandates posture, invariant set and tracker; does NOT claim provably-bug-free (§11.4.118 remains; §11.4.238 escape triggers a coverage audit not a proof); unmet invariant is honestly red-badged (§11.4.259) and blocks release; a genuine research frontier is honestly marked and documented as original work (§11.4.8). Observability makes unreproducible defects diagnosable, it is not verification of correctness (that is §11.4.108/§11.4.185/§11.4.262); corpus does not assert "a system you cannot observe cannot be verified".
- **Composes:** §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.8, §11.4.10, §11.4.27, §11.4.34, §11.4.44, §11.4.50, §11.4.66, §11.4.69, §11.4.85, §11.4.99, §11.4.101, §11.4.106, §11.4.107, §11.4.108, §11.4.118, §11.4.120, §11.4.124, §11.4.126, §11.4.128, §11.4.134, §11.4.135, §11.4.150, §11.4.152, §11.4.153, §11.4.161, §11.4.169, §11.4.183, §11.4.184, §11.4.185, §11.4.190, §11.4.197, §11.4.198, §11.4.200, §11.4.201, §11.4.209, §11.4.212, §11.4.223, §11.4.224, §11.4.226, §11.4.231, §11.4.235, §11.4.236, §11.4.238, §11.4.246, §11.4.257, §11.4.258, §11.4.259, §11.4.261, §11.4.262, §11.4.265, §11.4.17, §11.4.227, §1.1

#### §11.4.261 — Zero shortcomings / gaps / weak spots / danger zones invariant with mechanical audit ratchet (operator mandate 2026-08-15)
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1555-1575
- **Rules:**
  - Every project MUST hold at ALL TIMES exactly ZERO shortcomings, gaps, weak spots and danger zones across every code path, service, component, gate, doc and configuration: a standing invariant, not a per-release checklist.
  - Enforced by a mechanical audit script inventorying a closed finding vocabulary, run at every pre-build, release and constitution-pull seam, producing a machine-readable ledger, bound to a MONOTONE-DECREASING ratchet (§11.4.135 pattern): the count of open findings only drops or the release refuses.
  - Every finding is either FULLY CLOSED with captured evidence (§11.4.5/§11.4.69/§11.4.107 plus §11.4.226 evidence-class-at-closure) or explicitly TRACKED as a §11.4.197 item with an honest §11.4.223 provenance marker and a §11.4.101 reversible-safe mitigation.
  - Generalises §11.4.124, §11.4.118 and §11.4.238 into a whole-project zero-finding invariant.
  - (A) Closed finding vocabulary, extensible via named consumer-owned additions (§11.4.35) but never subtractable: (1) shortcomings - implementation gaps behind a working contract; (2) gaps - missing capabilities the docs/schema/API promise; (3) weak spots - code paths without adequate guards/error handling/input validation; (4) danger zones - code/config/operational patterns known to cause serious harm under conditions; (5) TODOs/FIXMEs/"for now"/"temporary"/"will do later"/"placeholder"/NotImplementedError/stub-returns/dead code (§11.4.124); (6) skipped tests/disabled gates/commented-out assertions without a tracked "# SKIP-OK: <ticket>" per §11.4.3; (7) bluffs - any §11.4/§11.4.1 covenant violation surface (PASS-bluff, FAIL-bluff, echo-observable, source-green-closes-runtime); (8) unresolved §11.4.197 items past their stated completion window; (9) divergent/stale/orphan artifacts per §11.4.233; (10) un-catalogued anti-patterns identified in code review that lack a §1.1 mutation.
  - (B) Mechanical audit sweep: a single executable script (Lava binding scripts/audit/zero_findings_sweep.sh; consumers supply path as §11.4.35 DATA) iterating the closed vocabulary and emitting a machine-readable ledger {finding_id, class, file, line, description, status in {open|tracked|closed}, tracker_ref, mitigation_evidence}; persistent, append-only plus snapshot per §11.4.116, git-tracked (§11.4.95) so the ledger is the SSoT; runs at pre-build, release-tag and constitution-pull; each finding class ships golden-good/golden-bad fixtures per §11.4.107(10).
  - (C) Monotone-decreasing ratchet: snapshot records accepted open-finding count at brownfield adoption (per §11.4.135 pattern, per-class and total); every audit run's count MUST be <= snapshot for each class; an increase in any class REFUSES the seam (pre-build gate FAILs, release refuses, commit refuses); the ratchet may DECREASE (manual snapshot-lower after closure) and MUST NEVER INCREASE; release-tag path never silently absorbs new debt. Brownfield adoption per operator §11.4.66 decision (§11.4.224(E) adoption-fence pattern), never an invented ratchet.
  - (D) Every finding is CLOSED or TRACKED, never silently absorbed. CLOSED requires captured evidence at the defect layer per §11.4.226 (runtime > artifact > source), code/config genuinely repaired, finding gone from the sweep. TRACKED requires (i) a §11.4.197 workable item with §11.4.148 comprehensive structured description, (ii) an honest §11.4.223 provenance marker ([OPEN: ATM-NNN]) at the finding site, (iii) a reversible-safe mitigation per §11.4.101, (iv) the item's completion on the standing autonomous loop's queue (§11.4.87/.94/.97/.103/.126), (v) a §11.4.135 permanent regression guard where the exposure could cause harm before closure. Silent absorption ("we know this is broken but shipping anyway") is a violation of PASS-bluff severity; the ledger is the honesty seam.
  - (E) Honest "zero" means the closed-vocabulary audit finds zero unclosed-untracked entries; a project narrowing the vocabulary to declare "zero" is a §11.4.6 fabrication and a release blocker. A §11.4.238 escape triggers class-extension of the audit and a ratchet-snapshot bump-DOWN (never up) once the escaped class is added and cleared.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-261-PROPAGATION, CM-ZERO-FINDINGS-AUDIT-SWEEP, CM-ZERO-FINDINGS-MONOTONE-RATCHET, CM-EVERY-FINDING-CLOSED-OR-TRACKED (paired §1.1 mutations)
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-findings-audit, --allow-todo-without-tracker, --ratchet-may-increase, --silently-absorb-finding, --narrow-vocabulary-to-declare-zero, --for-now-in-production

Catches the CATALOGUED only; discovery (§11.4.118) still needed for the un-catalogued; composes with, never substitutes for §11.4.118, §11.4.238, §11.4.226, §11.4.135.
- **Composes:** §11.4.3, §11.4.6, §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.34, §11.4.44, §11.4.66, §11.4.87, §11.4.94, §11.4.95, §11.4.97, §11.4.101, §11.4.103, §11.4.107(10), §11.4.113, §11.4.115, §11.4.116, §11.4.118, §11.4.124, §11.4.126, §11.4.135, §11.4.148, §11.4.161, §11.4.197, §11.4.201, §11.4.223, §11.4.224(E), §11.4.226, §11.4.233, §11.4.238, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.264 — Build once, promote ONE immutable content-addressed artifact through every environment; never rebuild per stage (research-derived, 2026-08-20)
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1579-1608
- **Rules:**
  - Rationale: rebuilding per stage breaks the chain of evidence - every gate against the staging artifact measured a different binary than production runs, making each green verdict a PASS-bluff about the shipped artifact. Immutable artifact plus environment-specific config injected at deploy is the rule.
  - (A) BUILD ONCE: exactly ONE artifact per release candidate, by ONE build, under §11.4.246 (reproducible + hermetic + SLSA-L2 provenance); every later environment receives THAT artifact. A pipeline invoking its build step once per environment violates §11.4.264 however deterministic the build is claimed; determinism makes a rebuild detectably equivalent, never a licence to rebuild instead of promote.
  - (B) IDENTITY IS A CONTENT ADDRESS, not a tag: the artifact is identified by a content-addressed digest (sha256 or platform equivalent), never by a mutable tag, branch name or version string alone (defends against "same version, different bytes"). Composes §11.4.111 and §11.4.200 (deployed identity read back from the intended target and asserted equal to the promoted digest).
  - (C) PROMOTION IS A VERIFICATION, not a rebuild: verify this exact digest is authentic and approved for the next environment; the promotion gate checks identity and approval of a digest, not re-running a build. Signature, SBOM and provenance travel WITH the artifact (§11.4.246).
  - (D) ENVIRONMENT CONFIG IS INJECTED AT DEPLOY, NEVER BAKED AT BUILD: artifact is environment-agnostic; environment supplies secrets/endpoints/flags at run time. Build-time config baking re-creates the per-stage rebuild. Credentials remain governed by §11.4.10 - injection at deploy is never a licence to bake a secret into an artifact.
  - (E) ROLLBACK IS DETERMINISTIC BY CONSEQUENCE: point production at the previous known-good digest, not a rebuild-from-source scramble; precondition that makes §11.4.265 auto-abort a real undo.
  - (F) REBUILD-TO-DODGE IS GATE-EVASION, not a retry: re-running or rebuilding until a failing scan/flaky check turns green launders a real failure into a pass; retries MUST be counted and surfaced (composes §11.4.248 flaky-quarantine).
  - Environment ladder, digest scheme and config-injection mechanism are consumer DATA per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-264-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.264 as block-start, exactly-once per governance file, lockstep hash equality per §11.4.227(B)), CM-BUILD-ONCE-PROMOTE-DIGEST (build invoked at most once per release candidate; every post-build stage references a pinned digest; a stage re-invoking the build -> FAIL), CM-DEPLOY-CONFIG-INJECTED-NOT-BAKED (a per-environment build argument changing artifact bytes -> FAIL); paired §1.1 mutations: add a second per-environment build -> first MUST FAIL; replace a promoted digest with a mutable tag -> it MUST FAIL; bake an environment endpoint -> second MUST FAIL; golden-FALSE (§11.4.201(1)): one build + N digest-referencing promotions MUST NOT fire either; gate-code = separate work item, not claimed shipped
- **No escape hatch:** --rebuild-per-environment, --promote-by-tag, --bake-env-config-at-build, --rebuild-until-green, --skip-digest-pin, --deterministic-build-means-rebuild-is-safe
- **Honest boundary:** Guarantees the tested bytes are the shipped bytes; does NOT prove them correct (§11.4.108, §11.4.40, §11.4.185), does NOT prove the deploy reached the intended target (§11.4.200), does NOT prove injected config is right (§11.4.254). Closes only the artifact-identity link between test and production; §11.4.246 governs how the artifact is built, §11.4.264 that it is not built again.
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.1, §11.4.6, §11.4.10, §11.4.35, §11.4.108, §11.4.111, §11.4.151, §11.4.200, §11.4.235(B), §11.4.246, §11.4.248, §11.4.252, §11.4.265, §11.4.17, §11.4.227, §1.1
- **Review addendum:** Clause (F): a flaky test is quarantined with an owner and a deadline, never laundered by a rebuild; retries are counted and surfaced (§11.4.248).

#### §11.4.265 — Progressive delivery: traffic-shifted rollout gated by automated analysis on SLO AND business metrics, automatic abort to stable (research-derived, 2026-08-20)
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1611-1641
- **Rules:**
  - Progressive delivery is the first gate whose oracle is real user traffic; it exists to catch the defect the suite never encoded at a small blast radius.
  - (A) A release reaches users by a bounded-blast-radius strategy, NEVER an ungated cutover. The project declares its strategy per §11.4.35 from two named forms: CANARY (gradual traffic shift pausing at each step to evaluate; smallest blast radius; needs weight-based routing; old and new run concurrently so schema/compat must tolerate it) or BLUE-GREEN (stand up green alongside blue, switch all live traffic at once, keep blue for a rollback window; near-instant undo but all users hit the new version simultaneously). For a §11.4.239 critical-invariant surface the stated preference is canary paired with blue-green's instant-undo posture.
  - (B) The promote/abort decision is made by AUTOMATED analysis, not a human watching a dashboard: the controller compares canary against stable baseline across defined metrics over successive windows; within thresholds across required windows -> auto-promote; breach -> auto-abort and roll back all traffic to stable, no human needed. A manual approval click is rejected as the gate (rubber stamp with no receipt). Composes §11.4.240 (producer may not grade its own rollout) and §11.4.262 (controller's result is the machine-created evidence).
  - (C) LOAD-BEARING: the analysis MUST include business metrics, NOT ONLY infrastructure metrics (business KPIs, e.g. checkout-completion rate; "HTTP error rate is fine" can hide UI regressions that return 200 while failing the user). An infra-only canary is a PASS-bluff at the deploy layer. For a §11.4.239 critical-invariant surface the domain invariants ARE the steady-state hypothesis.
  - (D) Multiple consecutive analysis windows, never a single sample (a single noisy sample must not flip the decision); composes §11.4.50 and §11.4.107.
  - (E) Post-deploy smoke is a fail-closed precondition of traffic: runs against the freshly deployed instance before it takes real traffic or before promotion, proving wiring and configuration (bad secret, wrong endpoint, missing migration, environment drift); a failed smoke gate aborts promotion before any user is affected. Composes §11.4.254, §11.4.252.
  - (F) The deploy gate is independent of the merge gate: a merge MUST NOT be able to auto-deploy past the analysis gate ("got it merged" is not "got it shipped").
  - (G) Thresholds and window counts are consumer-supplied DATA, never constitutional literals (§11.4.6/§11.4.35); this anchor mandates no numeric value; a release gate quoting a stale requirement is itself a bluff.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-265-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.265 as block-start, exactly-once per file, lockstep hash equality per §11.4.227(B)), CM-PROGRESSIVE-DELIVERY-STRATEGY-DECLARED (release declares a bounded-blast-radius strategy with automated analysis or an honest §11.4.3 SKIP-with-reason naming the absent traffic surface; ungated full cutover with neither -> FAIL), CM-CANARY-ANALYSIS-INCLUDES-BUSINESS-METRIC (declared metric set contains at least one business/domain outcome metric; infra-only on a §11.4.239 surface -> FAIL); paired §1.1 mutations: strip every business metric -> second MUST FAIL; replace automated abort with manual approval -> first MUST FAIL; golden-FALSE (§11.4.201(1)): genuinely non-routable artifact with honest SKIP-with-reason MUST NOT fire either; gate-code = separate work item, not claimed shipped
- **No escape hatch:** --full-cutover-ok, --infra-metrics-suffice, --manual-approval-is-the-gate, --single-window-analysis, --skip-smoke-before-traffic, --merge-implies-deploy
- **Honest boundary:** Bounds blast radius and automates undo; does NOT prove the release correct (a defect invisible to declared metrics promotes cleanly), does NOT replace §11.4.185 manual QA, and does not apply where no traffic-shiftable surface exists (firmware, desktop binary, batch job): honest §11.4.3 SKIP-with-reason, never a fabricated canary. Corpus progressive delivery is exclusively traffic-shifting; feature flags, dark launch, kill switches, shadow traffic are not mandated.
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.1, §11.4.3, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.35, §11.4.50, §11.4.69, §11.4.107, §11.4.185, §11.4.201, §11.4.235, §11.4.238, §11.4.239, §11.4.240, §11.4.252, §11.4.254, §11.4.262, §11.4.264, §11.4.17, §11.4.227, §1.1

#### §11.4.266 — Claim-vs-reality ledger: every ADVERTISED capability is a row, typed from a closed bluff-type vocabulary; a capability with no passing challenge is a release blocker (research-derived, 2026-08-20)
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1645-1673
- **Rules:**
  - The ledger enumerates from the CLAIM side (what the project advertises), unlike §11.4.25/§11.4.52/§11.4.169 which are keyed on known features; a claim with no feature row is invisible to a feature-keyed ledger. It adds a keying, not a restatement (§11.4.227).
  - (A) ONE LEDGER PER REPOSITORY, claim-side: every advertised capability is a row. The project declares per §11.4.35 which surfaces are "advertised" (at minimum: README capability set reachable per §11.4.212, the §11.4.257 manual/guide/FAQ set, the §11.4.254 capability matrix, the §11.4.259 badge assertions).
  - (B) Each row carries a bluff type from the CLOSED seven-member vocabulary plus a severity: green-but-broken (passes CI, fails on device), coverage-theater (metric lives in prose or badge, not a failing gate), rubber-stamp-verified ("verified" set, never earned), stubbed-core (most-engineered code has no caller), doc-vs-code-drift (a countable claim in prose is wrong), config-present-but-unwired (flagship path silently no-ops while right code exists elsewhere), byte-identical-fork (name promises X, code is Y unchanged). Vocabulary closed for typing, extensible only by an explicit visible amendment; an un-typeable finding is an honest tracked GAP (§11.4.6/§11.4.197), never an invented type. Severity vocabulary is consumer DATA (§11.4.35); the corpus states no scale.
  - (C) The type is a routing key to a counter-gate (typing is mandatory): green-but-broken -> §11.4.108 (runtime on clean target) + §11.4.262; coverage-theater -> §1.1 paired mutation + §11.4.224(C); rubber-stamp-verified -> §11.4.146(D3) + §11.4.240 + §11.4.249; stubbed-core -> §11.4.27 + §11.4.254; doc-vs-code-drift -> §11.4.106 + §11.4.186 + §11.4.227; config-present-but-unwired -> §11.4.124 + §11.4.196(F); byte-identical-fork -> §11.4.251. §11.4.266 makes the ROUTING mandatory; it does not restate the counters.
  - (D) Release-blocking rule: a capability with no passing challenge is a release blocker; a row whose challenge is absent, never executed, or executed only against a stale artifact fingerprint blocks exactly as a FAILING challenge does (§11.4.135/§11.4.236 absence-blocks-as-FAIL applied to the claim side).
  - (E) Escape half is owned by §11.4.238 (any defect found out-of-band is a release blocker proving a gate hole; remediation includes the new check plus RED evidence); cited, not duplicated.
  - Provenance correction: no F-n, FP-n or L-n identifier exists in the corpus modules; those labels MUST NOT be cited as corpus wording; anchors cite the real structures (14-row failure-pattern table, 6-bullet portfolio-gate list, this 7-member vocabulary).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-266-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.266 as block-start, exactly-once per file, lockstep hash equality per §11.4.227(B)), CM-CLAIM-REALITY-LEDGER-COMPLETE (every advertised capability on every declared surface resolves to exactly one row; no row -> FAIL naming capability and surface), CM-UNCHALLENGED-CAPABILITY-BLOCKS-RELEASE (absent/never-executed/no verdict for candidate fingerprint blocks like a FAIL), CM-LEDGER-ROW-TYPED-FROM-CLOSED-VOCABULARY (ad-hoc type -> FAIL); paired §1.1 mutations: add a README capability with no row -> completeness gate MUST FAIL; blank a row's challenge ref -> blocking gate MUST FAIL; retype to an invented type -> vocabulary gate MUST FAIL; golden-FALSE (§11.4.201(1)): fully-populated ledger with fresh candidate-fingerprinted PASS verdicts MUST NOT fire any; gate-code = separate work item, not claimed shipped
- **No escape hatch:** --ledger-optional, --unchallenged-capability-ok, --untyped-ledger-row, --invent-bluff-type, --feature-ledger-suffices, --advertise-without-row
- **Honest boundary:** Proves every ADVERTISED capability has a passing challenge; does NOT prove the challenge strong (§11.4.245, §11.4.107(10), §1.1), the capability bug-free (§11.4.118), nor enumerate capabilities nobody advertised (claim-keyed and feature-keyed ledgers are complements; running one leaves an honestly stated blind side). Corpus supplies no worked row, severity scale or "reality" field; all are consumer DATA.
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.1, §11.4.6, §11.4.25, §11.4.27, §11.4.35, §11.4.52, §11.4.106, §11.4.108, §11.4.115(F), §11.4.118, §11.4.124, §11.4.135, §11.4.146(D3), §11.4.169, §11.4.186, §11.4.196(F), §11.4.197, §11.4.212, §11.4.224, §11.4.226, §11.4.227, §11.4.236, §11.4.238, §11.4.240, §11.4.245, §11.4.249, §11.4.251, §11.4.254, §11.4.257, §11.4.259, §11.4.262, §11.4.17, §1.1

#### §11.4.267 — Shared attempt record + converge-on-evidence / escalate-on-stall (research-derived, 2026-08-20)
- **Source:** project-lifecycle-and-release.md:1677-1707
- **Rules:**
  - Premise: the agent has no durable memory of prior attempts; the regime must externalise it; the record is externalised memory, not a convenience log.
  - Scope boundary: §11.4.147 governs a CRASHED agent, §11.4.232(C) a HUNG long-op, §11.4.21 the TERMINAL exhaustion audit; §11.4.267 governs the LIVE, healthy, progressing loop re-walking a dead end its predecessor already proved dead.
  - (A) SHARED DURABLE ATTEMPT RECORD: every multi-attempt effort (agent loop, producer-verifier cycle, fix-retry sequence, multi-agent hand-off) MUST write each attempt and its OUTCOME to a record shared across every actor that may take the next attempt (successor agent, §11.4.147 respawn, different track per §11.4.176). Project binds location as DATA (§11.4.35); §11.4.93 workable-items DB and §11.4.116 append-only event stream are the natural substrates and MUST be reused, not duplicated (§11.4.227). No schema mandated.
  - (B) CONSULTED BEFORE ACTING: the record MUST be READ before the next attempt is chosen; an approach recorded as failed MUST NOT be silently retried; a re-attempt is permitted only when it materially differs (changed precondition, corrected §11.4.199 reproduction sequence, new §11.4.115(F) RED) and the difference is recorded. A written-but-never-read record is the §11.4.196(F) configured-not-in-use failure and satisfies nothing.
  - (C) CONVERGE ON EVIDENCE: each loop must monotonically reduce uncertainty; preconditions: a single source of truth (spec + acceptance criteria is authority, verifier's captured failure is ground truth; disagreements adjudicated on the receipt, not on confidence) and concrete failure feedback (feed the exact captured error - argv, exit code, failing assertion, offending line - back as next input). Composes §11.4.240/§11.4.249 and §11.4.262.
  - (D) STALL IS A DETECTED SIGNAL WITH BOUNDED RETRY AND AN ESCALATION PATH: two named stall signatures ("the same criterion red after N tries", "oscillating diffs"); after N failed iterations stop and route to a human or a stronger model rather than burning cycles; stall itself is tracked and trended; forbidden shape: unbounded retry loop with no ground-truth feedback and no escalation. Escalation composes §11.4.231 (re-tier when complexity proven mid-flight), §11.4.101 (decide autonomously where safe/reversible; park only what is genuinely blocked), §11.4.66/§11.4.21 (operator path only after §11.4.21 self-resolution audit).
  - (E) N is consumer-supplied DATA, never a constitutional literal (§11.4.6/§11.4.35); the anchor mandates that a bound EXISTS and is DECLARED, no value; enforcing an invented number attributed to the corpus is a §11.4.6 violation.
  - (E) EXTENSION (2026-10-05): where the operator mandates a ceiling on N for a specific, named loop, that ceiling is recorded with its own verbatim mandate in its own anchor (§11.4.276 for the independent-review loop); this is the only form of N-bound literal this clause permits; the consumer's declared N within that ceiling remains consumer DATA, never the literal ceiling itself.
  - (F) Loop done-condition: a loop MUST NOT read satisfied while an attempt is recorded in-flight with no outcome; an escalation raised under (D) MUST reach a terminal disposition (resolved / re-tiered / operator-parked per §11.4.101), never silently dropped. Composes §11.4.87, §11.4.94, §11.4.97, §11.4.126, §11.4.147 (a parked escalation parks ONE work unit, never the loop), §11.4.197.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-267-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.267 as block-start, exactly-once per file, lockstep hash equality per §11.4.227(B)), CM-ATTEMPT-RECORD-SHARED-AND-CONSULTED (each attempt + outcome written to the declared record and read before the next dispatch; a second attempt duplicating a recorded-failed approach with no recorded material difference -> FAIL), CM-STALL-BOUNDED-AND-ESCALATED (declared retry bound exists; a loop exceeding it without recorded escalation to a terminal disposition -> FAIL); paired §1.1 mutations: strip the record-read step -> first MUST FAIL; remove the retry bound -> second MUST FAIL; record an escalation with no terminal disposition -> second MUST FAIL; golden-FALSE (§11.4.201(1)): loop converging on attempt 2 with both attempts recorded and no bound exceeded MUST NOT fire either; gate-code = separate work item, not claimed shipped
- **No escape hatch:** --no-attempt-record, --record-without-reading, --unbounded-retry-loop, --retry-same-failed-approach, --stall-without-escalation, --invent-N-and-cite-corpus
- **Honest boundary:** Makes loop history legible and prevents the RECORDED dead end being re-walked; does NOT guarantee convergence (escalation is an honest outcome), does NOT prove any attempt competent, does NOT substitute for §11.4.102 systematic debugging. Bounds waste and preserves knowledge across actors; does not manufacture insight.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.20, §11.4.21, §11.4.35, §11.4.66, §11.4.70, §11.4.87, §11.4.93, §11.4.94, §11.4.97, §11.4.101, §11.4.102, §11.4.115(F), §11.4.116, §11.4.126, §11.4.146, §11.4.147, §11.4.176, §11.4.187, §11.4.196(F), §11.4.197, §11.4.199, §11.4.231, §11.4.232(C), §11.4.240, §11.4.249, §11.4.262, §11.4.17, §11.4.227, §1.1


### Testing and TDD (39 anchors)

#### §11.4.14 — Test playback cleanup mandate
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:3-27
- **Rules:**
  - A test that completes (PASS, FAIL or SKIP) MUST leave the target quiescent: no orphan playback, recording, capture or background process after the last assertion; test side-effects on shared target state MUST NOT outlive the test.
  - Every test that issues a playback or capture command MUST issue the matching cleanup at test end (force-stop app, stop recorder, close fd, terminate helper).
  - Cleanup is mandatory on EVERY exit path (PASS, FAIL, SKIP, error, trap, signal, parent-killed); use shell `trap '<cleanup>' EXIT` or try/finally.
  - Tests MUST verify cleanup succeeded via positive evidence (§11.4.5).
  - The orchestrator MUST run a post-test sanity check between tests and FAIL the just-completed test if it left orphan state (blames the leaker, not the next test).
  - No grace period: "the next test will clean it up" is the PASS-bluff pattern; cleanup is the test's own responsibility, not the next test's nor the orchestrator's.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.5

#### §11.4.25 — Full-Automation-Coverage Mandate (User mandate, 2026-05-15)
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:28-106
- **Rules:**
  - No feature, functionality, flow, use case, edge case, service or application on any supported platform is DELIVERABLE until covered by automation tests collectively proving six invariants.
  - Invariant 1, anti-bluff posture (§7.1 + §11.4): every assertion carries captured runtime evidence; metadata-only, config-only, grep-based, absence-of-error PASSes are forbidden.
  - Invariant 2, proof of working capability: user-visible behaviour exercised end-to-end on the target platform topology (§11.4.3), not in a mock or in-memory facsimile.
  - Invariant 3, working implementation as expected: assertions match the documented promise (manual, README, specs), not an implementation-detail back-door.
  - Invariant 4, no issues/no bugs: the suite is the canonical seam for surfacing defects; passing without defect signals means defects do not exist or were previously surfaced, tracked (§11.4.15/§11.4.16) and closed.
  - Invariant 5, fully documented: user-facing doc entry exists (§11.4.18 for scripts, user-manual coverage otherwise), kept in sync with tests (§11.4.12).
  - Invariant 6, tests-covered (four-layer floor per §1): pre-build presence-of-change gate, post-build artifact-shipped gate, runtime/integration/on-device gate, AND meta-test paired mutation proving the runtime gate catches the break.
  - Universal reach: every consuming project, every feature surface (HTTP endpoints, CLI, slash commands, IPC, plugins, hooks, MCP servers, agents, providers, integrations, GUI/mobile flows, scheduled jobs) and every supported platform (Linux, macOS, Windows, iOS, Android, AuroraOS, HarmonyOS, embedded, containers, headless, kiosk, etc.).
  - Consuming projects MUST publish a coverage ledger (feature x platform x invariant 1..6 x status), regenerated in the release-gate sweep, documented (§11.4.18/§11.4.12) and committed via the §11.4.22 doc-sync wrapper.
  - Ledger gaps (`UNCONFIRMED:` / `PENDING:` / `BLOCKED:` cells) MUST cite a tracked work item (§11.4.15 + §11.4.16); rows that quietly omit a platform are violations.
  - Stacks on §1, §1.1, §7.1, §11.4.1, .2, .3, .6, .15/.16, .17, .18, .20, .22; does not supersede them.
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17); no escape hatch; severity-equivalent to a §11.4 PASS-bluff at release-gate layer.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated "No escape hatch")
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §1, §1.1, §7.1, §11.4, §11.4.1, §11.4.2, §11.4.3, §11.4.6, §11.4.12, §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.17, §11.4.18, §11.4.20, §11.4.22

#### §11.4.27 — No-Fakes-Beyond-Unit-Tests + 100%-Test-Type-Coverage Mandate (User mandate, 2026-05-15)
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:108-249
- **Rules:**
  - (A) Mocks, stubs, fakes, placeholders, in-memory facsimile implementations, TODO, FIXME, "for now", "in production this would", or any empty-implementation pattern are PERMITTED only inside unit-test sources (e.g. `*_test.go` without the integration build tag; `tests/unit/`; per-language equivalents).
  - (A) Every other test type (integration, E2E, full automation, security, DDoS, scaling, chaos, stress, performance, benchmarking, UI, UX, Challenges, HelixQA suites) MUST exercise the real, fully implemented system against real infrastructure (real databases, HTTP endpoints, containers, downstream services, captured devices). A non-unit test importing mocks, in-memory repositories, fabricated provider responses or placeholder structs is a violation (PASS-bluff severity).
  - (A) Production code MUST NOT make any mock import path reachable in production binaries. Pre-build gate scans non-unit test trees and production trees for forbidden patterns; paired mutation plants a fake and the gate FAILs.
  - (B) Every project MUST cover its entire codebase with every supported test type the domain warrants, 15 types: 1 Unit (isolated, mocks permitted per A); 2 Integration (multi-component, no mocks, real backing services); 3 E2E (full user-flow on target topology); 4 Full automation (orchestrated suites for every feature x platform, §11.4.25 ledger); 5 Security (authn/authz boundaries, secret-leak scans §11.4.10, input fuzzing, dependency-CVE scanning, threat-model verification); 6 DDoS (request-flood resilience at advertised tier with rate-limit and back-pressure assertions); 7 Scaling (horizontal+vertical under linear load growth incl. replica add/remove); 8 Chaos (network partition, process kill, disk full, clock skew; graceful degradation); 9 Stress (sustained load above tier, bounded resource exhaustion, clean recovery); 10 Performance (latency/throughput/tail-latency vs SLO baselines); 11 Benchmarking (micro+macro with historical p95-drift detection, §11.4.24); 12 UI (visual-regression + DOM-state + interaction-flow on every target platform); 13 UX (flow-correctness, accessibility, i18n, visual-cue ordering §11.4.23); 14 Challenges (`vasic-digital/Challenges` fully incorporated, per-feature Challenge scripts with captured runtime evidence); 15 HelixQA (`HelixDevelopment/HelixQA` fully incorporated, ALL written test banks executed, full autonomous QA sessions in release gates).
  - (B) Per-type 100% means: each feature x platform cell in the §11.4.25 ledger carries a verified PASS evidence pointer for EACH test type the cell warrants (CLI-only feature: unit+integration+E2E+full-automation+security+chaos+stress+performance+Challenges+HelixQA; UI feature adds UI+UX; network service adds DDoS+scaling+benchmarking). Gaps tracked per §11.4.15 with `UNCONFIRMED:` / `PENDING_FORENSICS:` / `OPERATOR-BLOCKED:` reasons.
  - (B.1) Seven-canonical-type floor (2026-08-15): (1) UNIT, (2) INTEGRATION, (3) E2E, (4) FULL AUTOMATION, (5) SECURITY, (6) PERFORMANCE AND BENCHMARK, (7) ANTI-BLUFF is the MINIMUM breadth; the broader set in (B) (DDoS, scaling, chaos, stress, UI, UX, Challenges, HelixQA sessions) is ADDED per domain, never subtracted. Applicability per type is consumer §11.4.35 DATA; a genuinely inapplicable type is §11.4.3 SKIP-with-reason in the type-breadth ledger, never silently omitted. §11.4.27 sets type BREADTH, §11.4.224 sets code-coverage FLOOR; both bind, satisfying one is never evidence for the other.
  - Required submodules (recursive, CONST-047): `Challenges` = `git@github.com:vasic-digital/Challenges.git`; `HelixQA` = `git@github.com:HelixDevelopment/HelixQA.git`; plus any additional functionality submodules under `vasic-digital/*` or `HelixDevelopment/*` the project depends on (do not duplicate their work). Vendored equivalents only if operator-authorised.
  - Submodule pointers MUST be bumped to upstream HEAD in the SAME commit as dependent cascade work (§11.4.26 step 7); pointer drift is a violation.
  - HelixQA autonomous session = orchestrator drives the running surface end-to-end, executes every registered test bank, captures wire evidence per check (status + body bytes + body-head + duration + screenshots for UI), and produces a session report committed via the §11.4.22 wrapper. A green session report without captured wire evidence is a PASS-bluff at the QA-orchestration layer.
  - Classification universal; no escape hatch; mocks reachable from non-unit paths OR missing required test-type coverage is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-NO-FAKES-BEYOND-UNIT-TESTS, CM-COVENANT-114-27-PROPAGATION, CM-TEST-TYPE-BREADTH-SEVEN-CANONICAL (new recommended: drop one type without SKIP-with-reason via paired §1.1 mutation -> FAILs)
- **No escape hatch:** none named as flags (stated "No escape hatch")
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §1, §7.1, §11.4.1, §11.4.2, §11.4.3, §11.4.6, §11.4.10, §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.17, §11.4.20, §11.4.22, §11.4.23, §11.4.24, §11.4.25, §11.4.26, §11.4.35, §11.4.224, CONST-047

#### §11.4.39 — Per-Feature On-Device End-User Validation Mandate (iter-76, 2026-05-17)
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:253-295
- **Rules:**
  - Every user-facing feature MUST have at least one HelixQA scenario exercising it from cold-launch with positive runtime evidence: a screenshot or screen recording at a named checkpoint; at least one assertion of type `screenshot`, `accessibility_count`, `accessibility_node`, `ocr_text`, `pixel_histogram` or `editor_state`; evidence files in a discoverable output directory so each PASS is cross-verifiable.
  - Scenarios MUST be RE-EXECUTED on every release candidate; a scenario authored but never re-run degrades to a metadata-only gate (PASS-bluff at the regression layer).
  - Authoring rule 1: scenarios live in a canonical bank directory designated by the consuming project (e.g. `<banks-root>/feature-coverage/`).
  - Authoring rule 2: each scenario YAML MUST include `name`, `version`, `metadata`, `platforms`, `test_cases`, and at least one step with `evidence_required: true` and a specific `evidence_type`.
  - Authoring rule 3: a coverage matrix document (feature x iteration x scenario) MUST exist; (a) each new iteration MUST add >= 1 scenario per new user-facing feature; (b) prior scenarios MUST NOT be deleted (mark `status: retired` if feature removed); (c) all non-retired scenarios MUST PASS for ship-ready.
  - Authoring rule 4: a static gate (challenge script) MUST assert scenario count >= N (N = user-facing features registered in the matrix) and that each YAML contains an `evidence_type:` assertion.
  - Authoring rule 5: evidence-validation scripts MUST use POSIX-portable file-size helpers (e.g. `wc -c < file`) not OS-specific ones (GNU `stat -c%s`) to avoid silent 0-byte reports on BSD/macOS; a regression challenge MUST verify the portable helper on the actual host.
  - Platform-deferred pattern (iOS etc.): scenarios written platform-agnostically with the platform in a comment deferral (e.g. `# iOS: deferred - tracker #X`) are valid; add to `platforms:` when tooling exists.
  - Classification universal; no escape hatch; a feature without an on-device scenario is NOT covered per §11.4.25 invariant 2.
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named as flags (stated "No escape hatch")
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §7.1, §11.4, §11.4.17, §11.4.25, §11.4.27, §11.4.38

#### §11.4.43 — TDD-Fix-Discipline Mandate (User mandate, 2026-05-18)
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:297-399
- **Rules:**
  - Every fix MUST follow the 5-step TDD-fix workflow.
  - Step 1 RED, failing test FIRST: before any code change author (or extend) a test exercising the user-visible path of the defect that FAILs for that defect specifically. Per §11.4.1 the FAIL MUST be a real product defect, not a script-bug FAIL. Per §11.4.2 the FAIL run MUST produce captured evidence (logcat/dumpsys/screenrecord/dmesg//sys snapshot/sink-side probe). The test identifier MUST cite the section letter or Fix-# under repair. A RED that "happens to pass because the probe lifecycle isn't wired" is itself a PASS-bluff.
  - Step 2 LIVE-ADB-PROBE: when feasible, try the fix on the running device first via `adb shell` for mutable surfaces (`setprop persist.*`, `settings put`, `pm clear`, `am force-stop`, `am start`, `cmd wifi`, `cmd media_session`, ad-hoc /sys writes, boot-script edits pushed to /vendor/bin/, test-fixture replacement). The live probe IS NOT the fix, it is the experiment proving the hypothesis before source investment (fast adb loop ~5 min vs build-flash-test ~6 h).
  - Step 2 exception: live probe is INFEASIBLE (must rebuild) for kernel changes, AOSP framework (frameworks/base/), hardware HAL, vendor/ partition contents, init.rc service definitions, sepolicy, ro.* build properties, AOSP-build-time XML/resource overlays, Android.bp/Android.mk, signed-system-app contents (LOCAL_CERTIFICATE := platform). Each exception MUST be cited in the commit message as `LIVE_PROBE_INFEASIBLE: <reason>`.
  - Step 3 GREEN, apply the fix to source: must achieve the same effect as the live probe; per §11.4.9 batched with other source-side fixes where appropriate; build via project containerized build (§12.9); flash via project flash script; bytes on the assembled image MUST land where the post-build gate expects (§11.4.4(b) four-layer).
  - Step 4 VERIFY, re-run the RED test, must now PASS: per §11.4.7 PASS MUST come from the SAME conditions that initially FAILed (same device, same firmware now carrying the fix, same load profile, same cycle position); per §11.4.5 PASS MUST carry positive captured evidence (presence + correctness: RMS amplitude, ffprobe channel count, frame count, OCR text, sink codec state, etc.); per §11.4.2 video tests MUST cross-check via the recording-analyzer; per §11.4.42 a reliability check at the iteration count (typically 10) MUST PASS all iterations; a single intermittent FAIL keeps the item `In progress` per §11.4.7.
  - Step 5 DOCUMENT, update every relevant doc in the SAME commit per §11.4.4(c): `docs/Issues.md` -> `docs/Fixed.md` migration with type-aware closure vocabulary §11.4.33 (Bug -> `Fixed`, Feature -> `Implemented`, Task -> `Completed`); project CLAUDE.md Applied Fixes Reference row; per-version `docs/changelogs/<tag>.md`; affected user guides under `docs/guides/`; HelixQA bank entry per §11.4.4(b); `docs/CONTINUATION.md` per §12.10; project memory file if non-obvious.
  - Classification universal; "I'll add the test after the fix" is the exact PASS-bluff pattern (test authored after the fix only shows it agrees with the fix).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-43-PROPAGATION (verifies anchor present in every CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md across the covenant file set; paired mutation strips the literal from one consumer file -> FAILs)
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-red-test, --no-live-probe, --skip-verify, --skip-document
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.1, §11.4.2, §11.4.3, §11.4.4, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.7, §11.4.8, §11.4.9, §11.4.17, §11.4.33, §11.4.40, §11.4.42, §12.9, §12.10
- **Review addendum:** Step 2 (LIVE-ADB-PROBE) force is MUST: the operator MUST attempt the fix on the running device via `adb shell` first, subject to the listed exceptions and the `LIVE_PROBE_INFEASIBLE:` footer.

#### §11.4.48 — UI-Driven Video Testing Mandate (User mandate, 2026-05-18)
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:401-535
- **Rules:**
  - Every video-playback test asserting secondary-display routing MUST traverse the user-equivalent UI path (Intent / MediaSession-only dispatch skips content-selection UI, player-surface allocation, MediaSession lifecycle and back-button cleanup, and cannot reproduce defects like routing-race §CL or frozen-frame mid-back-press §CM). Mandatory 5-surface coverage per video app.
  - Surface A, launch via launcher icon: `am start -n <launcher-pkg>/<launcher-activity>`, then `uiautomator dump` to locate the app icon tile, then `input tap X Y`. NOT `am start <video-pkg>/<MainActivity>`.
  - Surface B, navigate to content list: per-app driver knows home-tab to content-tab swipe/tap sequence; assert at least one content tile visible via `uiautomator dump` content-desc/text match.
  - Surface C, select + play: tap a specific content tile (driver records the tile's content-desc as captured evidence); wait for player surface visible.
  - Surface D, in-app control interaction: pause via in-app pause button (not `input keyevent KEYCODE_MEDIA_PAUSE`), resume via in-app play button, in-app rapid switch to a second video (covers §CL).
  - Surface E, stop via back button: `input keyevent KEYCODE_BACK`; assert §11.4.14 cleanup: VOM `activeDecoder == null`, secondary surface cleared, no orphan MediaSession.
  - App-coverage matrix: every video-capable app in PRODUCT_PACKAGES MUST have a UI-driven driver script set (Layer 2) AND at least one scenario using it (initial batch 15 apps; VK Video, MPV, Lampa fully implemented, 12 templated stubs; expansion to all 53 video-app entries queued under §O Issues.md).
  - Stream-type matrix: progressive HTTP / HLS / DASH / RTMP / file-local / DRM-protected; driver tags which stream types its content exercises; aggregator emits a per-cycle coverage matrix.
  - Codec matrix: video H.264 / H.265 / VP9 / AV1 / MPEG-2 / MP4V; audio AC-3 / E-AC-3 / TrueHD / DTS / DTS-HD / MLP / Opus / AAC. Per scenario assert the codec via `dumpsys media.metrics` (decoder name in event log) AND the Arvus codec-state probe (audio) per §11.4.13.
  - Secondary-display verification when HDMI-A-1 attached (detected via `dumpsys display | grep "Display 2"`): dual_display_record.sh ON for both displays (§11.4.5); assert `ffprobe -count_frames` on the secondary mp4 reports > N frames within 3 s of play-action timestamp; anti-assertion: `ffprobe -count_frames` on primary mp4 shows ONLY launcher/home pixels during playback; VOM cross-check: `dumpsys video_output_manager` shows `activeDecoder != null` during playback and `== null` within 3 s after stop.
  - Secondary absent (D2 default topology): SKIP per §11.4.3 with reason "topology: no secondary display attached"; NEVER FAIL on missing topology.
  - Arvus codec-state mandate (§11.4.13 + §CG), for any audio-codec assertion: call `arvus_probe_codec_state` >= 3 times at 1 s intervals during playback (transients fade by sample 2-3); call `arvus_screenshot_capture` per §CG for dashboard visual evidence; assert codec via `arvus_assert_codec_format <regex>`; ARVUS_HOST unreachable (ABK4 not joined / sink off) -> SKIP per §11.4.3, never FAIL.
  - Pre-build gates: anchor-literal propagation across parent + 10 owned submodules + HelixQA dependencies (42-file scan); `CM-AF-UI-DRIVEN-VIDEO-COVERAGE` asserts directory `device/rockchip/rk3588/tests/ui_driven/` exists with a `lib/ui_driver.sh` reference, a scenarios/ subdir, per-app driver subdirs for at least the 3 reference apps (vk_video, mpv, lampa), and `scripts/testing/run_ui_driven_video_suite.sh` executable.
  - Paired mutations: deleting `ui_driver.sh` -> CM-AF-UI-DRIVEN-VIDEO-COVERAGE FAILs; stripping the anchor literal -> CM-COVENANT-114-48-PROPAGATION FAILs.
  - Operators finding UI-driven tests "too slow" should land scenario-level parallelism (multi-device fan-out), not bypass.
  - Classification universal; applies to every project consuming the constitution AND shipping any video-capable Android app.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-48-PROPAGATION, CM-AF-UI-DRIVEN-VIDEO-COVERAGE
- **No escape hatch:** --use-intent-shortcut, --skip-ui-traverse, --legacy-intent-mode
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.3, §11.4.5, §11.4.13, §11.4.14, §11.4.17, §11.4.43, §11.4.44, §CG, §CL, §CM

#### §11.4.49 — Dual-Approach Testing Mandate (User mandate, 2026-05-18)
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:537-645
- **Rules:**
  - REFINES §11.4.48 (does not replace): every feature test ships in BOTH variants, UI-driven AND Intent-driven, over a shared assertion base; either alone is a PASS-bluff for the opposite half of the stack (UI catches app-side bugs; Intent catches framework/system-server bugs: Intent extras parsing, MediaCodec.configure hook MIME routing, IVideoOutputManager bind timing, broadcast permission gating, headless cron paths).
  - Element 1, both variants required: every feature test of a user-visible behaviour MUST ship `<feature>_ui.sh` (uiautomator-based, §11.4.48 surfaces A-E) AND `test_<feature>_intent.sh` (`am start --es` / `am broadcast`-based). Either alone is forbidden.
  - Element 2, shared assertion base: codec-state assertions, captured-evidence collection (screen-recording, ffprobe, RMS amplitude analysis), Arvus codec-state probe + dashboard screenshot, and §11.4.14 cleanup MUST be in a single POSIX-sh library `tests/lib/dual_approach_test_base.sh` reused by BOTH variants; code duplication in the shared layer is forbidden.
  - Element 3, specialised driver code: UI variant uses §11.4.48 per-app drivers under `tests/ui_driven/<app>/`; Intent variant uses `am start --es content_id <id> --es audio_track_id <track>` / `am broadcast -a <action>`. Each variant's specialised layer is responsible ONLY for how playback gets started; everything downstream routes through the shared base.
  - Element 4, comprehensive documentation per test: (a) §11.4.44 revision header in BOTH variant scripts; (b) per-feature contract `docs/dual_approach/<feature>.md` describing captured-evidence pairing and operator-side verification; (c) Issues.md / Fixed.md entry cross-linking both variant paths.
  - Element 5, Kinopoisk 5.1 EAC3 is the canonical first implementation (shared base + UI variant + Intent variant land together); later features (Netflix Dolby Atmos, MPV DTS-HD, Lampa+TorrServe HEVC, VLC FLAC) port to the same pattern; the §CN decoder-pipeline fix is the FIRST GREEN target; both variants are RED per §11.4.43 until §CN lands.
  - Captured-evidence directory contract: both variants write mirror-structured `qa-results/dual_approach/<F>/<run-ts>/{ui,intent}/` with identical filenames; the orchestrator diffs the two `result.json`; a status mismatch (UI=PASS/Intent=FAIL or vice-versa) is itself a finding pinpointing the buggy half.
  - Pre-build gates: anchor propagation across parent + 10 owned submodules + HelixQA dependencies (42-file scan); `CM-AF-DUAL-APPROACH-COVERAGE`: `tests/lib/dual_approach_test_base.sh` exists + sources anti_bluff / ui_driver / credentials + exports `dat_init` / `dat_start_capture` / `dat_assert_codec_state` / `dat_assert_video_frames` / `dat_assert_audio_channels` / `dat_arvus_dashboard_capture` / `dat_cleanup` / `dat_report_finding`; `CM-AF-KINOPOISK-5-1-DUAL-COVERAGE`: both `tests/ui_driven/kinopoisk/kinopoisk_5_1_play_movie_ui.sh` AND `tests/test_kinopoisk_5_1_play_movie_intent.sh` exist, both source the shared base, both reference EAC3 codec, both assert 5.1 / 6-channel.
  - Paired mutations (3): strip anchor -> propagation gate FAILs; delete UI variant -> coverage gate FAILs; delete Intent variant -> coverage gate FAILs.
  - Operators finding dual variants "too slow" should land scenario-level parallelism, not bypass.
  - Classification universal; applies to every project consuming the constitution AND shipping any Android app whose behaviour is triggerable via both UI and Intent/Broadcast.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-49-PROPAGATION, CM-AF-DUAL-APPROACH-COVERAGE, CM-AF-KINOPOISK-5-1-DUAL-COVERAGE
- **No escape hatch:** --ui-only, --intent-only, --skip-dual
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.3, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.10, §11.4.13, §11.4.14, §11.4.17, §11.4.43, §11.4.44, §11.4.48, §CG, §CB, §CN

#### §11.4.50 — Deterministic Consistency Mandate (User mandate, 2026-05-18)
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:647-765
- **Rules:**
  - Closes the gap left by §11.4.7's textual ban on `intermittent` / `transient` / `flake`: every PASS must come from N identical iterations, not a single observation.
  - Element 1, N-iteration deterministic outcome: every PASSing test MUST have been executed N times (default N=3; N=10 for cycle-validation suites) against the same firmware MD5 + same device + same topology with IDENTICAL PASS every iteration. A test whose outcome diverges across iterations is auto-FAIL; no "first PASSed therefore X was a flake" path.
  - Element 2, edge-case + flow + use-case coverage: every public API path (Activity / Service / Broadcast receiver / ContentProvider URI / IPC interface / JNI entry / sysprop write / sysfs node / init.rc trigger) MUST have >= 1 dedicated test. Untested paths surface in a feature-coverage-matrix audit and block release at the 99% threshold (ratchet 70 -> 85 -> 95 -> 99, mirroring the §11.4.18 docs-coverage ratchet).
  - Element 3, reliability check helper: project anti-bluff library ships `ab_run_n_times <test_name> <N> <fn> [args...]` which loops N times capturing exit code + evidence-hash per iteration, asserts all N exit codes identical AND all N evidence-hashes identical, on divergence calls `ab_fail` with a full N-iteration report; NO operator-facing escape path converts a divergent N-iter run into PASS.
  - Element 4, feature-coverage-matrix audit: project ships `scripts/testing/feature_coverage_audit.sh` that walks source layers (every public API surface) and test layers (test_*.sh references), emits `qa-results/feature_coverage/<ISO-UTC>/coverage.tsv`; the pre-build gate enforces a minimum threshold ratcheting 70 -> 85 -> 95 -> 99.
  - Element 5, composes with every prior anti-bluff anchor and does NOT replace §11.4.43 / §11.4.48 / §11.4.49: RED-first TDD still applies (every new test starts RED); UI-driven and dual-approach still apply, each variant passing N iterations identically.
  - Pre-build gates: `CM-COVENANT-114-50-PROPAGATION` (anchor literal `§11.4.50` in every CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md across parent + 10 owned submodules + HelixQA dependencies; >=42-file scan, phase 1 uses 5-canonical-file scan); `CM-AF-RELIABILITY-CHECK-WIRED` (`ab_run_n_times` literal present in `device/rockchip/rk3588/tests/lib/anti_bluff.sh` AND at least 3 on-device tests source-reference it; the 3-test floor ratchets up each phase); `CM-AF-FEATURE-COVERAGE-MATRIX` (`scripts/testing/feature_coverage_audit.sh` exists, executable, has run within the last 7 days, latest report meets the current threshold).
  - Paired mutations (3): `sed -i 's|11\.4\.50|11.4.MUTATED|g'` on constitution/CLAUDE.md -> propagation gate FAILs; rename `ab_run_n_times` to `ab_run_n_times_DISABLED` -> reliability gate FAILs; `mv` feature_coverage_audit.sh aside -> coverage-matrix gate FAILs.
  - Classification universal.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-50-PROPAGATION, CM-AF-RELIABILITY-CHECK-WIRED, CM-AF-FEATURE-COVERAGE-MATRIX
- **No escape hatch:** --allow-flake, --first-pass-suffices, --skip-n-iter, --skip-coverage-audit
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.1, §11.4.2, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.7, §11.4.17, §11.4.18, §11.4.43, §11.4.46, §11.4.48, §11.4.49

#### §11.4.51 — Live-ADB-First Maximization Mandate (User mandate, 2026-05-18)
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:769-889
- **Rules:**
  - REFINES §11.4.43 step 2 (LIVE-ADB-PROBE) with a per-file-class decision matrix, a classifier helper and a commit-message footer literal.
  - Element 1: classify every fix by rebuild-requirement using the project's per-file-class decision matrix; no guessing (§11.4.6); every file in the diff cites its matrix row.
  - Element 2, LIVE_ADB_TESTABLE: apply the fix to the running device via the appropriate `adb` channel first (`adb push` for scripts, `setprop persist.*` for runtime properties, `mount -o remount,rw /vendor` for boot scripts, `pm install -r` for locally gradle-built APKs); run the §11.4.43 RED test against the live-probed device, capture positive-evidence PASS, THEN commit source-side + rebuild + reflash as belt-and-suspenders re-validation. Commit footer MUST state `LIVE_ADB_VALIDATED: yes` plus a one-line live-probe sequence description.
  - Element 3, REQUIRES_REBUILD: go directly to source fix + rebuild + flash; footer MUST state `REQUIRES_REBUILD: <reason>` citing the matrix row. Categories: kernel, AOSP framework Java/AIDL, native C++ inside APEX, sepolicy, init.rc, `ro.*` build properties, `Android.bp` / `Android.mk` / `BoardConfig.mk`, XML resource overlays, codec XML inside APEX, ramdisk-bundled artifacts.
  - Element 4, mixed batch: footer states `LIVE_ADB_VALIDATED: partial` and enumerates per-file classification; per §11.4.9 batching preferred (live-probe testable files first, then batch with rebuild-required ones into one rebuild).
  - Element 5, helper enforces mechanically: project provides `classify_fix_rebuild_requirement.sh` walking `git diff --name-only`, looking up each file in the matrix and emitting the recommended footer; no override flag converts an unclassified path to LIVE_ADB_TESTABLE; unmatched paths classify as `REQUIRES_REBUILD: unmatched-path` (safe default per §11.4.6).
  - Canonical per-file-class matrix: `*test_*.sh` / `tests/lib/*.sh` (on-device) NO (adb push to /data/local/tmp/tests/); host-side test scripts NO; `atmosphere-*.sh` boot scripts DEPENDS (adb push to /vendor/bin/ after remount); Markdown docs/Constitution/plans/Issues/Fixed/CONTINUATION NO; forked-player Kotlin (Presenter, MPV, SmartTube, TorrServe, Lampa, VLC etc.) YES via gradle local build + `adb install -r` (no full firmware rebuild); framework Java (`frameworks/base/**/*.java`) YES (system_server needs reboot at minimum); AIDL (`*.aidl`) YES (stub generation); native C++ (`external/**/*.cpp`, `frameworks/native/**/*.cpp`) YES (APEX or system library); APEX libraries (`vendor/**/lib/**/*.so` inside APEX path) YES (squashfs read-only by Mainline integrity); kernel sources (`kernel-5.10/**`) YES (kernel rebuild + boot.img); sepolicy (`*.te`) YES; `init.rc` YES (parsed at boot only); `ro.*` properties YES (immutable post-boot); `persist.*` runtime properties NO (`setprop` mutable); XML resource overlays YES (RRO recompile); `media_codecs_*.xml` YES (APEX-bundled); `display_settings.xml` (userdata) DEPENDS (adb push if SELinux permits); `Android.bp` / `Android.mk` / `device.mk` / `BoardConfig.mk` YES; test fixture binary assets NO (adb push to /data/local/tmp/).
  - Pre-build gates: `CM-COVENANT-114-51-PROPAGATION`, `CM-AF-CLASSIFY-FIX-HELPER-EXISTS` (helper present + sentinel literals), `CM-AF-LIVE-ADB-FIRST-COMMIT-MARKER` (advisory WARN scanning recent commits for the footer literal); three paired meta-test mutations.
  - Classification universal; matrix MAY be project-specific (each consumer adapts the file-class list) but classify-before-commit, the LIVE_ADB_VALIDATED / REQUIRES_REBUILD footer literals, the classify-helper script and the three gates are universal.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-51-PROPAGATION, CM-AF-CLASSIFY-FIX-HELPER-EXISTS, CM-AF-LIVE-ADB-FIRST-COMMIT-MARKER
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-classify, --assume-rebuild, --no-footer-required
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.9, §11.4.17, §11.4.43, §11.4.46, §11.4.48, §11.4.49, §11.4.50

#### §11.4.67 — Shell-script target-shell-parseability mandate (User mandate, 2026-05-19)
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:893-1054
- **Rules:**
  - Every shell script that may be invoked under a target shell other than its shebang's MUST parse cleanly under that target shell (reason: Android `/system/bin/sh` is mksh, which parses the entire script before executing, so a runtime guard cannot save bash-only syntax like `exec > >(tee ...)`).
  - (1) Closed-set scope: every tracked `.sh` under `device/rockchip/rk3588/tests/`, `scripts/`, `scripts/testing/` (and equivalents in owned submodules). OUT of scope: `external/`, `prebuilts/`, `packages/modules/`, `kernel-5.10/`, `out/`, `build/`, `scripts/legacy/` (legacy quarantine), third-party vendored shell dirs.
  - (2) Every in-scope script MUST parse under POSIX `sh -n` on the developer host.
  - (3) Bash-only syntax (process substitution `>(...)`/`<(...)`, `[[ ]]`, `<<<`, indexed arrays `arr=()`, `declare -A`, `${var^^}`/`${var,,}`, bash-only `${var/pattern/replacement}`, `coproc`, `function name { ... }` instead of `name() { ... }`, any other bash-only construct) MUST EITHER be wrapped in `eval '...bash-only string...'` OR be guarded by sourcing the file only on bash-detected hosts (`[ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]` BEFORE the script loads; runtime guards inside a single mksh-parsed script do not work).
  - (4) Honest shebangs: a script with bash-only constructs without eval-deferral MUST declare `#!/bin/bash` (or equivalent) AND callers MUST invoke it as `bash script.sh` not `sh script.sh`; a script with `#!/system/bin/sh` or `#!/bin/sh` MUST be POSIX-clean (no bash-only syntax, no `local` without an mksh fallback, no `read -p`, no `echo -e` without portable equivalent).
  - (5) eval-deferral is the safe pattern: wrap in single-quoted eval, e.g. `eval 'exec > >(tee -a "$f") 2>&1'`, with a runtime guard around the eval.
  - (6) Sourced-function `exec` redirection-scoping (2026-07-23): in bash-family shells command-less `exec` applies EVERY redirection on the line to the CURRENT shell PERMANENTLY; in ANY sourced/library shell function an `exec` whose purpose is only to open/close/move fds MUST brace-scope its side redirections, `{ exec 9>>"$file"; } 2>/dev/null`, so error-suppression applies to the fd-operation alone; a command-less `exec` combining fd-manipulation operands with an additional unbraced redirection in sourced code is a REVIEW DEFECT (§11.4.142) and a greppable pre-build-gate class. Instrument-side twin catalogued in `docs/guides/shell_instrument_footguns.md` per §11.4.201(12).
  - Enforcement: pre-build gate `CM-SCRIPT-TARGET-SHELL-PARSEABLE` walks every in-scope `.sh`, runs `sh -n` on each with a 30-second per-file timeout, FAILs if any fails, citing the file + `sh -n` error message.
  - Propagation gate `CM-COVENANT-114-67-PROPAGATION` verifies the literal across the 44-file consumer fleet (parent CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md + Containers + 10 owned atmosphere submodules + nested SmartTube SharedModules/MediaServiceCore/MSC-SharedModules + 7 HelixQA submodules); constitution submodule files are canonical authority.
  - Paired mutations: (a) inject bash-only `exec > >(/bin/cat)` outside eval into a test script -> CM-SCRIPT-TARGET-SHELL-PARSEABLE FAILs; (b) strip `11.4.67` from one consumer file -> CM-COVENANT-114-67-PROPAGATION FAILs; for clause (6) unwrap one brace-scoped fd-open to bare form -> CM-SHELL-EXEC-REDIRECTION-SCOPED FAILs.
  - Mandatory protections: no `--skip-parseability-check` flag; no "this script only runs on bash" exception (almost all scripts can be invoked via `sh script.sh`); no "runtime guard catches it" exception; fix at source in the script itself (per §11.4.1), not defensively at callsites.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-SCRIPT-TARGET-SHELL-PARSEABLE, CM-COVENANT-114-67-PROPAGATION, CM-SHELL-EXEC-REDIRECTION-SCOPED (recommended: scans in-scope sourced/library shell for command-less `exec` lines combining fd operands with unbraced redirections -> FAIL citing file:line; brace-scoped forms and `exec` WITH a command exempt as §11.4.201(1) false-positive guard; gate-code = separate work item)
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-parseability-check
- **Honest boundary:** `sh -n` on the host is the closest portable parser to mksh and gives high confidence, not proof, of mksh parseability.
- **Composes:** §11.4.1, §11.4.4, §11.4.6, §11.4.50, §11.4.51, §11.4.142, §11.4.201

#### §11.4.81 — Cross-platform-parity mandate (User mandate, 2026-05-21)
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:1056-1093
- **Rules:**
  - Every consuming project whose `supported-platforms` manifest lists more than one OS MUST, for every feature/test/gate/challenge/mutation depending on platform-specific primitives, ship a per-OS-equivalent implementation chosen at runtime via `uname -s` (or equivalent detection). A Linux-only gate without macOS/Windows/BSD equivalents (when the kernel permits) is a PASS-bluff at the platform-coverage layer.
