  - Gates: propagation literal `11.4.243` + CM-CHARACTERIZATION-BEFORE-LEGACY-MODIFICATION + paired §1.1 mutation. Universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-243-PROPAGATION, CM-CHARACTERIZATION-BEFORE-LEGACY-MODIFICATION
- **No escape hatch:** --modify-untested-legacy-directly, --skip-characterization, --claim-tests-not-needed-because-obvious, --decorative-assertion-suffices, --refactor-without-safety-net
- **Honest boundary:**
  - Sampled input space = honest gaps (§11.4.118), not completeness; characterization captures current behaviour, not correctness.
- **Composes:** §11.4.115, §11.4.124, §11.4.118, §11.4.201, §11.4.224, §11.4.66, §11.4.17, §1.1

#### §11.4.244 — Cross-boundary contract tests + can-i-deploy gate
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:1568-1572
- **Rules:**
  - Changes modifying a boundary between independently-deployable components (service<->consumer, library<->dependents, DB schema<->readers/writers, message topic<->subscribers) MUST be covered by CONSUMER-DRIVEN CONTRACT TESTS on both sides AND a `can-i-deploy` gate MUST verify proposed provider version compatibility against every currently-deployed consumer version BEFORE shipping. The two are merged: useless in isolation.
  - CDC pattern: consumers publish assumptions about the provider (Pact / Spring Cloud Contract / gRPC schema-evolution rules); providers verify each consumer's contract against actual implementation; a provider change breaking a live consumer's contract fails the provider's build BEFORE shipping.
  - CAN-I-DEPLOY: at every deploy attempt the gate queries the contract broker for the compatibility matrix; a single red cell BLOCKS the deploy with a machine-readable verdict naming the incompatible pair, NEVER warning-with-continue.
  - A MISSING contract is a first-class refusal reason per §11.4.201 (false-positive refusal is a FAIL-bluff, false-negative allowance a PASS-bluff).
  - SemVer becomes MEASURABLE: a PATCH bump breaking a contract is mis-labelled.
  - Backward-compatibility window declared per §11.4.35.
  - Gates: propagation literal `11.4.244`, CM-CONTRACT-TESTS-BOTH-SIDES, CM-CAN-I-DEPLOY-GATE-WIRED, paired §1.1 mutations. Universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-244-PROPAGATION, CM-CONTRACT-TESTS-BOTH-SIDES, CM-CAN-I-DEPLOY-GATE-WIRED
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-contract-tests, --deploy-without-compatibility-check, --assume-compatible-when-broker-silent, --patch-may-break-contract, --contract-tests-optional-for-internal-boundaries
- **Honest boundary:**
  - Composed-system manual QA is still needed (§11.4.185); contract tests do not replace it.
- **Composes:** §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.35, §11.4.66, §11.4.108, §11.4.135, §11.4.185, §11.4.201, §11.4.17, §1.1

#### §11.4.245 — Oracle-problem-first test authoring
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:1576-1580
- **Rules:**
  - Every test MUST FIRST identify its ORACLE (the mechanism deciding PASS vs FAIL for the input it drives), and the oracle MUST be DIFFERENT from the code under test AND from the test's own assertion mechanism. Authoring without explicit oracle identification yields the "test agrees with the code" anti-pattern (a §11.4/§11.4.1 bluff at the test-authoring layer).
  - ORACLE STRATEGY CLOSED SET, each test's oracle NAMED explicitly in source: (1) SPECIFIED (spec/RFC/standard names expected output); (2) DERIVED (independent reference implementation); (3) METAMORPHIC (relations between related inputs, §11.4.107(8) generalised); (4) GOLDEN-MASTER/CHARACTERIZATION (past captured behaviour, §11.4.243); (5) INVARIANT (universal property, e.g. sort output sorted + permutation of input); (6) STATISTICAL (distribution properties for stochastic outputs, never a specific value); (7) HUMAN (§11.4.185 manual QA). NO other classes.
  - STRUCTURAL INDEPENDENCE: the oracle's SOURCE of expected value does not depend on the code being tested.
  - §11.4.107(10) self-validation generalised: the paired §1.1 mutation must produce a WRONG output and the oracle catches it.
  - Reviewer per §11.4.194 judges whether the identified oracle is genuinely independent.
  - Gates: propagation literal `11.4.245` + CM-ORACLE-STRATEGY-NAMED-AND-INDEPENDENT + paired §1.1 mutation. Universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-245-PROPAGATION, CM-ORACLE-STRATEGY-NAMED-AND-INDEPENDENT
- **No escape hatch:** --test-agrees-with-code, --skip-oracle-identification, --oracle-is-the-code, --assertion-is-oracle, --implicit-oracle-OK
- **Honest boundary:**
  - The oracle problem is the oldest unsolved problem in testing; §11.4.245 does not solve it, it mandates honestly identifying which strategy each test uses.
- **Composes:** §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.107(10), §11.4.115, §11.4.194, §11.4.201, §11.4.224, §11.4.243, §11.4.185, §11.4.17, §1.1

#### §11.4.246 — Reproducible + hermetic builds + supply-chain integrity at SLSA Build Level 2
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:1584-1588
- **Rules:**
  - Every consuming project's build pipeline MUST produce REPRODUCIBLE, HERMETIC artifacts and MUST meet SLSA Build Level 2 as the FLEET-WIDE MINIMUM (operator decision 2026-08-15; Level 3+ tracked as backlog per §11.4.197).
  - REPRODUCIBLE: same source at same time on any conformant host yields byte-identical artifacts (or a diff-set fully accounted for by declared non-determinisms pinned to canonical values).
  - HERMETIC: no undeclared inputs: every dependency version-pinned + lockfile-hashed, every tool version declared, no unpinned public-network reach at build, no host-env leakage.
  - SLSA-L2: signed provenance describing source URI + commit hash + builder identity + invocation + artifact hash, on a hosted tamper-resistant build platform.
  - Every consumer MAINTAINS `docs/security/SLSA_LEVEL.md` (or §11.4.35 equivalent) recording CURRENT level with cited evidence + TARGET level + tracked §11.4.197 upgrade items; CURRENT below L2 without a tracked item is a violation.
  - SUPPLY-CHAIN EXTENSION: dependencies either vendored (checked in hash-verified), from a provenance-attested source (npm/PyPI/crates.io as they add SLSA), OR mirrored through a hash-pinning local registry.
  - Gates: propagation literal `11.4.246`; CM-BUILD-REPRODUCIBILITY; CM-BUILD-HERMETICITY; CM-SLSA-L2-PROVENANCE-VERIFIED; CM-SUPPLY-CHAIN-DEPS-PROVENANCE-ATTESTED; paired §1.1 mutations. Universal (§11.4.17). Non-compliance is a release blocker.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-246-PROPAGATION, CM-BUILD-REPRODUCIBILITY, CM-BUILD-HERMETICITY, CM-SLSA-L2-PROVENANCE-VERIFIED, CM-SUPPLY-CHAIN-DEPS-PROVENANCE-ATTESTED
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-reproducibility, --allow-network-during-build, --no-provenance, --slsa-optional, --below-l2-OK, --unpinned-dependency-OK, --host-env-may-leak-into-build
- **Honest boundary:**
  - Threat model is NARROW: covers the source->artifact chain; does NOT cover a malicious commit landing in source (§11.4.142 review), a compromised dependency source, nor a bug-free artifact (§11.4.108 four-layer + §11.4.185 manual QA).
- **Composes:** §2.1, §11.4.6, §11.4.30, §11.4.35, §11.4.108, §11.4.113, §11.4.135, §11.4.142, §11.4.161, §11.4.184, §11.4.185, §11.4.197, §11.4.209, §11.4.77, §11.4.17, §1.1

#### §11.4.247 — Composite-output layer-move must move every layer
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:1592-1596
- **Rules:**
  - Changes MOVING a system-boundary layer (service migrates hosts, endpoint URL changes, API version bumps, DB schema shifts, message topic renames, ingress path re-routes, storage bucket moves) MUST move EVERY LAYER of the composite output atomically or via an explicit compatibility window; NEVER piecemeal.
  - Layer taxonomy (per §11.4.35 baseline): (i) server (handler + route + OpenAPI/proto/gRPC descriptor); (ii) client (call-sites + SDK stubs + integration tests); (iii) infrastructure (LB + ingress + API gateway + CDN + service-mesh + DNS); (iv) data stores (cached keys + DB URL rows + MQ subscriptions); (v) observability (metric labels + span names + log fields + dashboards + alerts + SLOs); (vi) documentation (user + dev + runbook + README + cookbook); (vii) tests (integration + e2e + contract per §11.4.244 + load + smoke).
  - Consumer provides `scripts/audit/layer_move_completeness.sh` reporting the residual-references delta; a change proposing a move MUST show ZERO residuals OR an explicit compatibility-window plan per residual with tracked §11.4.197 items.
  - COMPATIBILITY-WINDOW: old value keeps working alongside new until a stated date/version/event, with deprecation warnings named per caller, a tracked deadline, and clean removal at expiry; no "clean up later".
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-247-PROPAGATION, CM-LAYER-MOVE-COMPLETENESS-CHECK (plus paired §1.1 mutation)
- **No escape hatch:** --partial-layer-move-OK, --skip-completeness-check, --residuals-cleaned-up-later, --observability-layer-optional, --doc-move-can-lag
- **Honest boundary:** Phrases "composite-output", "surface-swap-not-recreate", "atomic move discipline" are this anchor's own paraphrase of the module-32 domain, NOT corpus quotations (zero occurrences in all nine modules); phrase-level attribution is UNVERIFIED, domain attribution plausible.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.35, §11.4.111, §11.4.118, §11.4.124, §11.4.135, §11.4.191, §11.4.197, §11.4.238, §11.4.244, §1.1

#### §11.4.248 — Flaky-test quarantine + protected-regression-spec gate ([PROTECTED-SPEC: ATM-NNN] + CODEOWNERS)
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:1600-1604
- **Rules:**
  - Flaky tests are the silent anti-bluff decay vector; two disciplines bound it.
  - (A) QUARANTINE: mechanical detection (test-history aggregator flags two-consecutive-run-different-verdict OR rerun-after-red pattern) moves the flaky test to `tests/quarantine/` (per §11.4.35), opens a tracked §11.4.197 stabilisation deadline, and the blocking suite runs WITHOUT the quarantined test so green means green; a deadline past = §11.4.66 extension or a violation.
  - (B) PROTECTED-REGRESSION-SPEC: regression tests codifying known-broken defect fixes (§11.4.135 permanent-guard suite) MAY be tagged `# [PROTECTED-SPEC: ATM-NNN]` (target-language comment equivalent) referencing the workable-item ATM-NNN (§11.4.54) they guard, marking the test load-bearing whose modification requires elevated review. The tag is applied deliberately per test, NOT blanket (blanket voids the discipline).
  - CODEOWNERS-REQUIRED-REVIEWER GATE: the consuming project's CODEOWNERS declares that modifications to `[PROTECTED-SPEC]`-tagged tests OR `regression/**/*` path scope require designated required-reviewer approval BEFORE merge; composes with §2.1 SSH + §11.4.113 no-force-push (gate cannot be silently bypassed); audit trail in PR review thread + commit history. The reviewer distinguishes STRENGTHEN (approve), FIX-DEFECT-IN-TEST (approve after verifying ATM-NNN's defect not re-introduced), WEAKEN/REMOVE (refuse or §11.4.66 escalate); the gate makes modification VISIBLE, not preventable.
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-248-PROPAGATION, CM-FLAKY-TEST-QUARANTINE-WIRED, CM-PROTECTED-REGRESSION-SPEC-GATE (plus paired §1.1 mutations)
- **No escape hatch:** --rerun-until-green, --quarantine-permanent, --protected-spec-review-optional, --codeowners-skip, --blanket-protect-everything, --tag-without-atm-id
- **Honest boundary:** The gate makes modification of protected tests visible/reviewed rather than preventable; ideal quarantine is empty (§11.4.50).
- **Composes:** §2.1, §11.4.6, §11.4.35, §11.4.50, §11.4.54, §11.4.66, §11.4.113, §11.4.115, §11.4.135, §11.4.197, §11.4.226, §1.1

#### §11.4.249 — Producer != oracle != gate != verifier + flight recorder
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:1608-1612
- **Rules:**
  - Every load-bearing quality mechanism has FOUR structurally separate roles: (1) PRODUCER (code computing/emitting/building output); (2) ORACLE (decides correctness per §11.4.245); (3) GATE (seam consuming the oracle verdict to allow/block/proceed); (4) VERIFIER (audits the gate's decision; paired §1.1 mutation proving the gate can refuse a bad output).
  - Collapse classes: producer=oracle (oracle-agrees-with-code, §11.4.245); oracle=gate (never says "cannot decide", defaults to allow: §11.4.201(6) FALSE-NULL); gate=verifier (self-auditing gate, §11.4.142 self-review anti-pattern).
  - FLIGHT RECORDER: a mechanism CAPTURING producer inputs + oracle verdict + gate decision + verifier audit as a durable replayable artifact (structured JSONL event stream per §11.4.116, content-addressed per §11.4.207), so post-hoc "why did this go through" has evidence. The recorder is NOT the gate; a gate reading its own recorder to decide collapses gate + verifier + recorder.
  - Detectable collapses the reviewer (§11.4.194) scans for: (1) producer=oracle (test's assertion calls the code under test); (2) oracle=gate (no "cannot decide" branch, defaults PASS); (3) gate=verifier (meta-test IS the gate: a mutation making the gate always-pass also makes the meta-test always-pass; meta-test MUST live OUTSIDE the gate); (4) recorder=decision-substrate (gate uses recorder contents as decision input; precedent-based gating not authorised).
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-249-PROPAGATION, CM-ROLE-SEPARATION-DECLARED, CM-FLIGHT-RECORDER-CAPTURED (plus paired §1.1 mutations)
- **No escape hatch:** --collapse-producer-oracle, --gate-self-audits, --skip-flight-recorder, --oracle-defaults-pass, --decision-without-recorded-rationale
- **Honest boundary:** Four-role taxonomy generalised from producer/verifier separation + oracle problem + gate mechanics (MATERIAL-THIN); flight recorder derived from clean-checkout re-run + attached receipts pattern per §11.4.17.
- **Composes:** §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.107, §11.4.116, §11.4.142, §11.4.194, §11.4.201, §11.4.207, §11.4.240, §11.4.245, §1.1

#### §11.4.250 — Heuristic-tower signals a primitive defect
- **Source:** testing-and-tdd.md:1616-1620
- **Rules:**
  - A codebase accumulating a TOWER of heuristics compensating for the same underlying issue (e.g. retry-with-backoff + connection-pool-warmup + DNS-cache-flush + health-check-with-startup-grace, all guarding one flaky DB connection) IS the diagnostic: the PRIMITIVE is defective; every layer papers over a manifestation.
  - Recognition signals: (i) each layer's justification is "we added because sometimes X happens" (reactive); (ii) removing any layer INCREASES failures but keeping all shows occasional residual; (iii) no single layer owns responsibility; (iv) layers added at different times by different authors per specific incidents; (v) monotone layer-count growth, a debugging session for the residual adds layer N+1 rather than fixing 1..N.
  - DISTINCT from defense-in-depth: defense-in-depth is deliberate, each layer targets a DIFFERENT failure class, designed together not accreted, and removing a layer produces a SPECIFIC different failure, not "same failure more often".
  - SYSTEMATIC-DEBUGGING RESPONSE on tower depth >= 2: (1) STOP adding layers; (2) INVOKE §11.4.102 systematic-debugging on the PRIMITIVE; (3) proceed root-cause/pattern/hypothesis/implementation phases; (4) fix the primitive; (5) REMOVE layers one at a time verifying with §11.4.5 evidence; (6) commit each removal per §11.4.124 with git-history evidence citing the primitive fix.
  - Classification universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-250-PROPAGATION, CM-HEURISTIC-TOWER-TRIGGERS-PRIMITIVE-DEBUG (plus paired §1.1 mutation)
- **No escape hatch:** --add-another-heuristic-layer, --skip-primitive-debug, --tower-is-defense-in-depth-without-justification, --reactive-mitigation-OK, --layer-per-incident
- **Honest boundary:** Source offset un-resolvable per §11.4.239 CITATION NOTE; resolves to module 35 taxonomy row 4 (module_35:99/102/104); the constant-offset mapping across §11.4.250/.251/.254 is an observed correlation, not asserted fact.
- **Composes:** §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.102, §11.4.124, §11.4.194, §11.4.201, §11.4.226, §1.1


### Translation and localization (3 anchors)

#### §11.4.237 — Mandatory exhaustive context-and-spirit-aware translation review
- **Source:** translation-and-localization.md:3-23
- **Rules:**
  - Reason: an accurate translation can still read stilted/foreign/register-wrong to a native speaker, and a pass that mangles a technical term or translates a non-translatable name ships a worse defect; accuracy is NECESSARY, not SUFFICIENT.
  - (A) Every translation and translated artifact (UI strings, pages, documents, PDFs, manuals, marketing copy, captions/subtitles, help text, any localized content) MUST undergo a HEAVY, EXHAUSTIVE independent review by a reviewer (agent or human) STRUCTURALLY SEPARATE from the translator (§11.4.70/§11.4.20). The translator's own pass (§11.4.92) PRECEDES this review and NEVER satisfies it (§11.4.142 no-self-review-substitution). An artifact accepted without it is a PASS-bluff at the localization layer.
  - (B) The reviewer MUST hold and apply three dimensions: (a) FULL CONTEXT of the source (original ideas, subject/domain, purpose, intended audience; reads MEANING, not just string, so intent, nuance, tone are carried across); (b) the SPIRIT of the target language (tradition, idiom, register, tone, cultural conventions) so the result reads NATIVE, natural, fluent, MAXIMALLY POLISHED, never literal/word-for-word/calqued; a construction correct in the source but foreign in the target is REWRITTEN into natural form; (c) CORRECT TECHNICAL VOCABULARY with established target-language equivalents, and NON-TRANSLATABLE tokens (product/brand names, proper nouns, technology/library/API names, code identifiers, trademarks) preserved VERBATIM, never translated, transliterated or localized away.
  - (C) Goal is maximally polished localization: fidelity is the FLOOR, not the ceiling; an accurate but stilted/foreign/register-wrong/idiom-broken rendering is a FINDING, not a pass.
  - (D) The review MUST emit captured machine-readable POSITIVE evidence per §11.4.5/§11.4.69 (`feature_class` = translation_review): a per-artifact verdict with PER-DIMENSION rationale across the closed set {fidelity, fluency/naturalness, spirit/register, terminology, completeness, non-translatable-preservation}; a PASS with no captured per-dimension rationale is a bluff. A FAIL on ANY dimension LOOPS BACK to re-translation/polish and re-review, iterating to zero-finding clean verdict per §11.4.134.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies language set, term glossary, non-translatable token list, reviewer substrate as DATA (§11.4.35).
  - Recommended gate behaviour: every localized artifact carries an independent per-dimension verdict with rationale, FAIL looping to re-review; paired mutations: accuracy-only acceptance, self-review by own translator, golden-bad mistranslated idiom or "translated" non-translatable product name -> gate FAILs; strip literal -> propagation gate FAILs; gate-code = separate work item, NOT claimed shipped.
  - Non-compliance is a release blocker regardless of context.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-237-PROPAGATION, CM-TRANSLATION-CONTEXT-SPIRIT-REVIEW
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-spirit-review, --accuracy-only-OK, --self-review-translation-OK, --literal-translation-OK, --translate-non-translatable-OK, --skip-per-dimension-rationale
- **Honest boundary:** REFINES localization discipline from PASS/FAIL accuracy to context-and-spirit native-polish review; does not replace the canonical translation pipeline (§11.4.255) nor independent per-language review (§11.4.256) but STRENGTHENS them. (Source text cites these as §11.4.140/§11.4.141 in their translation senses - a known operator-owned anchor-number collision; later re-minted as §11.4.255/§11.4.256.)
  - Does not make mistranslation impossible (a miscalibrated reviewer stays §11.4.107(10) golden territory); a target language with no established term for a concept is an honestly recorded finding (§11.4.3 SKIP-with-reason), never a silently invented word.
- **Composes:** §11.4.255, §11.4.256, §11.4.140, §11.4.141, §11.4.6, §11.4.69, §11.4.92, §11.4.134, §11.4.142, §11.4.209, §11.4.70, §11.4.20, §11.4.5, §11.4.3, §11.4.107(10), §11.4.17, §11.4.35, §11.4.227, §11.4.54, §1.1
- **Review addendum:** The mention that the §11.4.140/§11.4.141 translation numbering collision was later re-minted as §11.4.255/§11.4.256 is an annotation from the project status record, not text of this canon block; this block says the re-mint was still operator-owned.

#### §11.4.255 — Mandatory HelixTranslate canonical translation pipeline
- **Source:** translation-and-localization.md:25-51
- **Rules:**
  - Operator mandate (2026-06-25): every project inheriting this constitution MUST use HelixTranslate (`git@github.com:HelixDevelopment/HelixTranslate.git`) via a universal reusable pipeline to generate ANY translations; hard, non-negotiable.
  - ALL translations of ANY content (UI strings, documents, articles, CVs, READMEs, marketing copy, in-app messages, release notes, legal text, any human-language string in a non-source language) MUST be produced by HelixTranslate driven through the canonical pipeline at `scripts/translation/` (`translate-pipeline.sh` + `render-articles.sh`).
  - FORBIDDEN (a) Hand-translation: no human-authored, manually edited or "good enough" hand-written translation ever; the engine is the single source of every translated string.
  - FORBIDDEN (b) Other engines: no Google Translate, DeepL, raw ChatGPT/Claude prompting, OS translation APIs, library i18n auto-translators, or any engine other than HelixTranslate's `unified-translator`; exactly one engine.
  - FORBIDDEN (c) Silent fallback: no quiet substitution of the source string, no empty/partial output passed off as a translation, no swallowed engine error, no absence-of-error PASS (§11.4/§11.4.1). On exhaustion of all configured providers the pipeline MUST FAIL LOUD (non-zero exit, destination NOT written); a missing translation is a hard error, never a degraded-but-shipped string. Provider-to-provider failover WITHIN HelixTranslate (primary -> fallback, with logged evidenced retries) is NOT a silent fallback and is permitted; falling back to ANY non-HelixTranslate source is forbidden.
  - Mandatory validation: every generated translation MUST be validated for accuracy with real captured evidence per §11.4.5/§11.4.69/§11.4.107; no metadata-only/config-only/grep-without-runtime PASS, no false results, no bluff (§11.4.6). The per-file run log (provider used, byte counts, retries, success/failure) is the evidence artifact; an unvalidated or unevidenced translation is treated as ABSENT.
  - Explicit provider routing: provider + model routing MUST be explicit and recorded, never implicit. Canonical routing: provider `groq` / model `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`, documented failover to provider `mistral` / model `mistral-large-latest`; the provider that actually produced each output MUST be recorded in the per-file log; any deviation MUST be stated explicitly in configuration and logged.
  - Canonical pipeline location: `scripts/translation/translate-pipeline.sh` (universal Markdown/plain-text + article-frontmatter-preserving translator) and `scripts/translation/render-articles.sh` (article-source -> HTML fragment renderer); reusable verbatim; engine binary supplied by the consuming project via `HELIX_TRANSLATE_BIN`, built from the HelixTranslate repository.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies source files, target languages, HelixTranslate engine build per §11.4.35.
  - Rationale: single evidenced fail-loud engine gives known provenance, reproducible pipeline, captured accuracy proof (one engine, one pipeline, one evidence trail).
  - Canonical authority: Constitution.md §11.4.255; consumers restate and cite via §11.4.35 inheritance. Non-compliance is a release blocker regardless of context.
  - Recommended gate with paired §1.1 meta-test mutation; gate-code = separate work item.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-255-PROPAGATION, CM-MANDATORY-HELIXTRANSLATE-PIPELINE
- **No escape hatch:** --allow-hand-translation, --other-engine-OK, --skip-translation-validation, --silent-fallback
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.1, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.7, §11.4.69, §11.4.107, §11.4.17, §11.4.35, §1.1

#### §11.4.256 — Mandatory independent per-language translation review
- **Source:** translation-and-localization.md:55-81
- **Rules:**
  - Operator mandate (2026-06-25): translation quality for all supported languages MUST always be checked by independent specialized review agents performing full testing, review, validation and verification of all translated content.
  - Every translated artifact produced under §11.4.255 MUST, before it is shipped/committed/deployed, be INDEPENDENTLY REVIEWED by a per-language review agent; a hard non-negotiable gate that composes with and never replaces §11.4.255.
  - (a) Independence: the reviewer MUST be a different model/provider than the one that produced the translation (e.g. translator `mistral/mistral-large-latest` -> reviewer `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile`, or any distinct verified model); a model reviewing its own output is NOT independent and is forbidden.
  - (b) Per-language specialization: the reviewer MUST act as a NATIVE speaker/linguistic reviewer of the SPECIFIC target language, evaluating grammar, orthography and correct script (Cyrillic for ru/be/kk, Arabic for ar/fa, Han/Kana/Hangul/Devanagari for zh/ja/ko/hi, Latin for sr/de/es/fr/tr, etc.).
  - (c) Full criteria: each review MUST judge accuracy/fidelity, fluency/naturalness, completeness (nothing omitted or invented), correct script and orthography, and absence of untranslated source leftovers (proper nouns/URLs/code excepted).
  - (d) Strict machine-readable verdict + evidence: each review MUST emit a structured PASS/FAIL verdict with per-criterion scores and an issues list, persisted as a physical evidence artifact (§11.4.5/§11.4.69/§11.4.107). A FAIL, or an ERROR/unavailable-reviewer, BLOCKS the content; only a real PASS may ship. No metadata-only/absence-of-error PASS; no bluff (§11.4.6).
  - (e) Remediation loop: a FAIL routes the artifact back through the §11.4.255 pipeline (re-translate / multipass-polish) and is re-reviewed, iterating until PASS, never hand-patched to pass (hand-translation remains forbidden under §11.4.255).
  - Canonical tooling: `scripts/translation/review-translations.sh` (per-language review driver) + `scripts/translation/review_translation.py` (independent reviewer engine emitting strict JSON verdicts); reusable verbatim; consumer supplies source/translation file pairs and a reviewer provider DISTINCT from its translator.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); platform- and language-neutral QA discipline.
  - Rationale: §11.4.255 guarantees provenance and a fail-loud pipeline, not linguistic quality; an independent native-level per-language reviewer with a captured verdict makes quality an auditable fact.
  - Canonical authority: Constitution.md §11.4.256; consumers restate and cite via §11.4.35. Non-compliance is a release blocker regardless of context.
  - Recommended gate with paired §1.1 meta-test mutation; gate-code = separate work item.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-256-PROPAGATION, CM-MANDATORY-TRANSLATION-REVIEW
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-translation-review, --self-review-OK, --accept-unreviewed-translation
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.255, §11.4, §11.4.1, §11.4.5, §11.4.6, §11.4.69, §11.4.107, §11.4.134, §11.4.17, §11.4.35, §1.1


### Workable items and tracking (19 anchors)

#### §11.4.15 — Item-status tracking mandate
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:3-23
- **Rules:**
  - Every active item in the project's Issues file MUST carry a `**Status:**` line within five lines of its heading.
  - Status is drawn from a closed set: `Queued` (backlog, no work started; sub-state `Queued — BLOCKED on <reason>` permitted); `In progress`; `Ready for testing` (source-side fix landed, pre-build/meta-test gates green, awaiting next deploy cycle); `In testing` (deploy + cycle in flight, live captured evidence per §11.4.2 + §11.4.5 being collected); `Reopened` (failed runtime test cycle, back to active work, carries a reference to the failure-cycle artefact); `Fixed (→ Fixed file)` (closed: captured evidence per §11.4.5, runtime test PASS, paired meta-test mutation FAILs, item migrated to Fixed file).
  - Status MUST be updated as the item progresses; every commit that changes an item's lifecycle state MUST update its Status line in the same commit.
  - Issues, Issues_Summary and Fixed file types MUST be in sync at all times (Markdown + HTML + PDF).
- **Gates:** none named
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.2, §11.4.5

#### §11.4.16 — Item-type tracking mandate
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:25-58
- **Rules:**
  - Every active Issues item MUST carry a `**Type:**` line within eight non-blank lines of its heading (same window as the §11.4.15 Status audit).
  - Type is a CLOSED set of three: `Bug` (product defect/regression/user-visible broken behaviour that worked or was expected to work); `Feature` (new capability not previously offered to end users); `Task` (internal, not user-visible workstream: refactor, infrastructure, docs, audit, covenant clause, gate, mutation, propagation enforcement, host-safety hardening; largest class and the lowest-stakes default when ambiguous).
  - Only `Bug`, `Feature`, `Task` are valid; any other value is a violation; when ambiguous fall back to `Task`.
  - Type (what kind of work) is distinct from severity (how urgent) and status (where in lifecycle); the three axes drive ownership routing, testing strategy, release-note framing, changelog classification.
  - The Issues_Summary file MUST carry a Type column for every active item; Markdown + HTML + PDF stay in sync under `CM-DOCS-EXPORT-SYNC` (as §11.4.12 + §11.4.15).
  - Items that do not fit MUST be re-classified `INFORMATIONAL` and excluded from the active-item set rather than carry a fabricated Type.
- **Gates:** CM-ITEM-TYPE-TRACKING, CM-COVENANT-114-16-PROPAGATION, CM-DOCS-EXPORT-SYNC (paired mutations in the project meta-test required)
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated as: no escape hatch; re-classify as INFORMATIONAL instead)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.12, §11.4.15

#### §11.4.21 — Operator-blocked status + self-resolution exhaustion mandate
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:60-201
- **Rules:**
  - Operator dependency is a last-resort classification, earned only after documented exhaustion of self-resolution paths; routing an item to the operator without proving agent+tooling cannot unblock it is a planning-layer PASS-bluff.
  - (1) Status closed set is extended to seven values: Queued, In progress, Ready for testing, In testing, Reopened, `Operator-blocked` (cannot proceed without an operator action the agent and available tooling cannot perform), `Fixed (→ Fixed.md)`.
  - (2) BEFORE classifying Operator-blocked the agent MUST verifiably exhaust every applicable path: (a) CLI/ADB/SSH/API access already available; (b) subagent delegation per §11.4.20; (c) existing in-repo tooling/scripts/helpers; (d) captured fallback (synthetic event, stand-in fixture, mock, topology-aware SKIP per §11.4.3, downgrade to pre-build gate); (e) documentation + research per §11.4.8.
  - Only after each applicable path is attempted and documented as exhausted is Operator-blocked correct; "didn't try X because I assumed it wouldn't work" is a §11.4.6 AND §11.4.21 violation.
  - (3) Every Operator-blocked item MUST carry an `**Operator-Block-Details:**` line within 8 non-blank lines of its heading stating ALL of: WHAT (specific concrete operator action: verb+object+target system; generic "operator must investigate" forbidden); WHY (each exhausted path from (2) with a one-line statement of what was attempted and why it could not unblock); UNBLOCK CONDITION (observable signal the action is complete); WHO (handle/contact/pointer to operator-side details).
  - (4) The auto-generated Issues_Summary.md MUST include Operator-blocked as a first-class sortable Status value and the generator MUST emit a count of Operator-blocked items in any rollup line/header.
  - (5) Operator-blocked items MUST be re-evaluated every Nth tag-cycle (project-defined, recommended every 3rd), following the same (2) exhaustion checklist and documenting each re-attempt.
  - (6) A fake Operator-blocked is a covenant violation at the planning layer; the commit message introducing or maintaining the classification MUST contain evidence in the explicit form "Attempted: a — exhausted because X; b — exhausted because Y; c — exhausted because Z".
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-ITEM-OPERATOR-BLOCKED-DETAILS (every Operator-blocked heading has the details line within 8 non-blank lines; paired mutation strips it), CM-OPERATOR-BLOCKED-SELF-RESOLUTION-AUDIT (every NEW Operator-blocked item carries an "Attempted: ..." trail in Issues.md entry or commit message; paired mutation omits it), CM-COVENANT-114-21-PROPAGATION
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated: classification must be earned; an Operator-blocked heading without a self-resolution audit trail is a release blocker)
- **Honest boundary:** Legitimate operator interventions (hardware swaps, vendor contracts, physical-world inputs, account credentials, irreversible business decisions) are real and unavoidable, but must be earned via documented exhaustion.
- **Composes:** §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.19, §11.4.12, §11.4.20, §11.4.8, §11.4.6, §11.4.3, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.33 — Type-aware closure-status vocabulary
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:205-257
- **Rules:**
  - The closure terminal Status MUST agree with the item Type, from a 3-element closed map: `Bug` → `Fixed (→ Fixed.md)`; `Feature` → `Implemented (→ Fixed.md)`; `Task` → `Completed (→ Fixed.md)`.
  - The `(→ Fixed.md)` suffix is preserved across all three so the Issues.md → Fixed.md atomic-move tooling (§11.4.19) works without per-Type branching.
  - Generators (`generate_issues_summary.sh`, `generate_fixed_summary.sh`, status-counter helpers, the §11.4.23 colorizer) MUST treat the three terminal values as semantically equivalent (closed, positive evidence captured) while preserving the literal in emitted documents.
  - Closing a Feature with `Fixed` or a Task with `Implemented` is a §11.4.33 violation.
  - Type-mismatched closure vocabulary is a semantic-drift bluff at the documentation layer. Classification: universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-CLOSURE-VOCAB-TYPE-AWARE (recommended per consuming project: walks every Fixed.md heading and every Issues.md heading with a terminal Status and asserts the value matches the Type; paired mutation flips a Bug from Fixed to Implemented -> FAIL)
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated: no escape hatch)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.19, §11.4.23, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.34 — Reopened-source attribution mandate
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:261-326
- **Rules:**
  - Every tracker heading whose Status is `Reopened` MUST carry, within 8 non-blank lines, a `**Reopened-Details:**` line capturing four sub-facts.
  - **By:** `AI` (in-loop reopens: test failure, gate regression, captured-evidence retrospect) or `User` (operator-side: manual testing, end-user report, design reconsideration).
  - **On:** ISO date `YYYY-MM-DD`.
  - **Reason:** one-line cause from closed vocabulary `{ test-failed | manual-testing-detected | captured-evidence-contradicts | end-user-report | cycle-re-discovered | design-reconsidered }`; other values permitted only with explicit `Reason: <free text>` annotation, closed list tried first; no `likely/probably/maybe` causes (§11.4.6).
  - **Evidence:** path to or short description of the captured artefact justifying the reopen (log, recording, gate failure ID, operator quote); reopens without evidence are §11.4.6/§11.4.7 violations (a reopen is a demotion from Fixed requiring positive evidence captured under the conditions that re-exposed the defect).
  - The Issues_Summary.md Status column MUST distinguish Reopened sub-states by source so queries like "reopens by AI in last 30 days" are mechanical, e.g. `Reopened (AI: test-failed)` vs `Reopened (User: manual-testing)`.
  - A `Reopened` entry without `**Reopened-Details:**` is a violation. Classification: universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-ITEM-REOPENED-DETAILS (recommended per consuming project; mirrors CM-ITEM-OPERATOR-BLOCKED-DETAILS; missing details line WARN initially, hardens to FAIL once backlog populated)
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated: no escape hatch)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.7, §11.4.15, §11.4.21, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.54 — ATM-NNN ticket identifier mandate
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:330-451
- **Rules:**
  - Every workable item in `docs/Issues.md` AND `docs/Fixed.md` MUST carry a stable, unique, monotonic, append-only `[ATM-NNN]` identifier in its heading: `## §X.Y. [ATM-NNN] <title>` (or `### §X.Y.` for nested). NNN is a positive integer zero-padded to at least 3 digits.
  - Identifiers are allocated by the canonical helper `scripts/testing/assign_atm_ticket_ids.sh` maintaining an append-only state file `scripts/testing/.atm_ticket_state.json`.
  - Once assigned, an ATM-NNN MUST NEVER be: (1) renumbered; (2) reused for a different item even if the original is force-deleted; (3) decremented; (4) skipped intentionally (gaps indicate state-file corruption and FAIL the gate).
  - State file is JSON-lines, one record per ID with fields: atm_id, heading_hash (sha256 of normalized heading), type (Bug|Feature|Task), current_location (Issues|Fixed), current_status, reopens_count, created_at (ISO 8601 UTC), last_modified.
  - `heading_hash` is the canonical binding key: the helper looks up an existing ATM-NNN by hash before allocating; if heading text changes substantially, the hash is updated in place via an explicit migration command, NOT auto-rebound.
  - `docs/Issues_Summary.md` and `docs/Fixed_Summary.md` MUST carry a leftmost `ATM ID` column; generators (`generate_issues_summary.sh`, `generate_fixed_summary.sh`) MUST emit it as the first data column.
  - The helper MUST be invoked from `sync_issues_docs.sh` so new items get IDs before summary regeneration; per-item Reopens.md lives at `docs/issues/<ATM-NNN>/Reopens.md` (§11.4.55).
  - Applies to every consuming project with an Issues/Fixed split; projects without it are NOT_APPLICABLE. Classification: universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-ATM-TICKET-IDS-COMPLETE (every heading carries a token matching `\[ATM-[0-9]{3,}\]`), CM-ATM-TICKET-IDS-UNIQUE (state-file record count equals union of Issues.md + Fixed.md occurrences; no orphans/duplicates), CM-ATM-TICKET-IDS-MONOTONIC (max ATM-NNN equals record_count; no gaps), CM-COVENANT-114-54-PROPAGATION (literal `§11.4.54` in constitution/Constitution.md, constitution/CLAUDE.md, constitution/AGENTS.md, parent consumer CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md); paired mutations: remove an ID, duplicate an ID, delete ATM-NNN=2 from a 5-record file, strip the literal -> each gate FAILs
- **No escape hatch:** `--skip-atm-assignment`, `--renumber`, `--no-atm-id-required`
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.19, §11.4.33, §11.4.12, §11.4.53, §11.4.55, §11.4.57, §11.4.44, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.55 — Reopens-history tracking + per-item Reopens.md doc
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:455-564
- **Rules:**
  - Every workable item with `reopens_count > 0` MUST have a companion `docs/issues/ATM-NNN/Reopens.md` plus HTML + PDF exports (§11.4.44 + §11.4.53 sync).
  - The document MUST contain: (1) revision header per §11.4.44 (`Revision` integer + `Last modified` ISO 8601 UTC); (2) item identification: ATM ID, Title, Type, Current Status, Current Location (Issues.md/Fixed.md), link to live heading; (3) cycle counters: Total reopens, Total fixed cycles; (4) chronological timeline with one entry per state-change event, each with By (AI/User per §11.4.34), On (ISO date), Event (`Opened|Reopened|Fixed|Implemented|Completed`), Reason (the §11.4.34 closed-vocabulary value for reopens; captured-evidence summary for closures), Evidence (path/short description), Outcome (next state transition); (5) a reasoning chain for each closure (root-cause analysis link, captured evidence under same conditions per §11.4.7, gate/mutation pair defending against regression); (6) a most-recent state-change pointer to the current Issues.md/Fixed.md heading.
  - Issues_Summary.md and Fixed_Summary.md MUST carry a `Reopens` column with the integer count; when count > 0 the cell MUST hyperlink to `docs/issues/<ATM-NNN>/Reopens.md`. The §11.4.23 colorizer MAY apply a visual cue when reopens > 2.
  - §11.4.34 Reopened-Details (per-event) and §11.4.55 (per-item history) MUST stay in sync; the state-machine helper updates Reopens.md on every Reopened-Details parse. The Reopens column appears on BOTH summary tables.
  - Applies wherever §11.4.34 applies. Classification: universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-REOPENS-DOC-EXISTS-WHEN-COUNT-GT-ZERO, CM-REOPENS-DOC-REVISION-HEADER, CM-REOPENS-COL-IN-SUMMARIES, CM-COVENANT-114-55-PROPAGATION (paired mutations: delete a Reopens.md, strip revision header, remove Reopens column, strip `§11.4.55` literal)
- **No escape hatch:** `--skip-reopens-doc`, `--collapse-history`, `--reopens-not-applicable`
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.34, §11.4.54, §11.4.44, §11.4.45, §11.4.53, §11.4.23, §11.4.7, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.90 — Obsolete status + per-item obsolescence audit mandate
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:568-593
- **Rules:**
  - The §11.4.15 Status set gains a 4th terminal value `Obsolete (→ Fixed.md)`, applied regardless of Type when the item is no longer valid because: (a) superseded by a later operator mandate/design pivot, (b) the feature was removed, (c) duplicated and the canonical entry resolved it, (d) filed against an unsupported hardware/topology variant.
  - Every Obsolete heading MUST carry within 8 non-blank lines an `**Obsolete-Details:**` line with: Since (ISO date); Reason from closed vocabulary `{ superseded-by-design-change | superseded-by-later-mandate | feature-removed | duplicate-of | unsupported-topology | not-reproducible }` (`not-reproducible` = defect not reproducing on the canonical tree/baseline, an environment/isolated-worktree artifact; triple-check evidence MUST capture the canonical-tree non-reproduction); Superseding-item (§-letter reference or User-mandate verbatim quote anchor); Triple-check evidence (path to captured evidence: git log, code grep, runtime behaviour; bare assertion forbidden).
  - Visual treatment: the §11.4.23 colorizer MUST style Obsolete cells with class `cell-status-obsolete`: light-gray background `#E0E0E0` and strikethrough text on the row's description cell.
  - Audit cadence: at every release-gate sweep (§11.4.40) the conductor MUST re-evaluate every non-terminal Issues.md item AND every Fixed.md item for obsolescence; new findings produce atomic `Obsolete (→ Fixed.md)` migrations per §11.4.19. Each claim cites (i) the superseding mandate, (ii) code-state grep confirming the behaviour is gone, (iii) runtime/test evidence that no test still exercises the obsoleted path.
  - Marking a still-valid item Obsolete is a planning-layer PASS-bluff; leaving a genuinely obsolete item non-terminal is documentation drift.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-90-PROPAGATION, CM-ITEM-OBSOLETE-DETAILS, CM-OBSOLETE-COLORIZER-WIRED (paired §1.1 mutations: strip anchor literal, delete an Obsolete-Details line, strip the colorizer class)
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated: every obsolescence finding follows the triple-check evidence rule)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.19, §11.4.21, §11.4.23, §11.4.33, §11.4.34, §11.4.40, §11.4.42, §11.4.66, §11.4.71, §11.4.6, §11.4.7
- **Review addendum:** Gate CM-OBSOLETE-COLORIZER-WIRED checks two things: the colorizer emits the `cell-status-obsolete` class on the right cells, and the CSS file defines that class.

#### §11.4.91 — Summary-doc clarity mandate
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:597-632
- **Rules:**
  - Every short-form summary entry (Issues_Summary.md, Fixed_Summary.md, README.md doc-link section, Status_Summary.md pages 1+2, any one-liner derived from a long-form tracker entry) MUST have a self-contained, meaningfully informative description of WHAT the item is, not a fragment of the long-form body.
  - Forbidden one-liner anti-patterns: section labels as descriptions (`Composes with`, `Closure criteria`, `Fix direction`, `Forensic anchor`, `Reopened-Details`, `Operator-Block-Details`, `Obsolete-Details`, `Summary`, `Status`, `Type`, `Severity`, etc.); bare numeric/categorical fragments (`Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Bug`, `Feature`, `Task`, `Fixed`); generic restatements of Status (`In progress`, `Queued`, `Reopened`, `Operator-blocked`, `Fixed`); section-marker echoes matching `^[A-Z][a-z]+ (with|by|on|in|to|for):?$` with empty right-hand side; a §-letter alone (`§KB`, `§EU`).
  - Required shape: a complete clause of at least 6 words OR 40 characters (whichever is longer) that names the SUBJECT (component/app/behaviour/defect class) plus the PROBLEM or GOAL.
  - Generator enforcement: `generate_issues_summary.sh`, `generate_fixed_summary.sh`, `update_readme_doc_links.sh`, `generate_status_summary.sh` MUST extract the one-liner from the H1/H2 heading line of the source entry, NEVER from arbitrary downstream text, and MUST refuse to emit a row matching an anti-pattern, emitting the placeholder `(MISSING DESCRIPTION — fix source heading)` with the row visually highlighted.
  - Audit cadence: at every release-gate sweep (§11.4.40 + §11.4.42 step 4) re-evaluate every summary row; operator-facing HTML + PDF exports MUST never ship with an anti-pattern row.
- **Gates:** CM-SUMMARY-CLARITY-DESCRIPTIONS (scans every `*_Summary.md`; paired mutation injects "Composes with" -> FAIL)
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated: no escape hatch; non-compliance is a release blocker)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.12, §11.4.19, §11.4.23, §11.4.44, §11.4.53, §11.4.56, §11.4.57, §11.4.59, §11.4.60, §11.4.65, §11.4.74, §11.4.40, §11.4.42, §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.54

#### §11.4.92 — Multi-pass change-evaluation discipline
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:636-668
- **Rules:**
  - Every non-trivial change MUST pass a 5-pass evaluation (ALL passes must hold) BEFORE being accepted as commit-ready.
  - Pass 1 Main-task verification: captured evidence per §11.4.5/§11.4.69 shows the user-visible behaviour works as intended; no inferred/assumed/"should work".
  - Pass 2 Regression-blast-radius: enumerate every file touched and every file that imports/sources/references it; demonstrate via grep/dependency-graph/test run the existing contract is unbroken (signature change -> audit every caller; HAL config change -> every consuming test; gate addition -> every paired meta-test mutation); captured evidence.
  - Pass 3 Cross-feature interaction: evaluate against parallel features sharing state, timing, hardware or shell environment (audio HAL change -> video routing; WiFi roaming -> BT A2DP coex; test-script addition -> §11.4.84 quiescence + §11.4.89 background discipline); captured evidence.
  - Pass 4 Deep-research validation per §11.4.8: verify against external state of the art; cite an external precedent OR record the literal "NO external solution found — original work"; CodeGraph queries per §11.4.78 + §11.4.79 for intra-codebase precedents.
  - Pass 5 Anti-bluff confirmation per §11.4/.1/.6/.27/.50/.52/.69/.83: no new bluff surface (no metadata-only/config-only PASS, no script-bug FAIL-bluff, no "tests pass but feature doesn't work"); evidence directories reference exact passing paths.
  - Each Pass MUST produce written documentation (commit-message footers OR `docs/` entries OR `qa-results/` evidence); a change without all 5 passes documented is a process-layer PASS-bluff.
  - Only after all 5 passes may the change be committed via `commit_all.sh`, pushed via §11.4.88 background-push, tested via §11.4.89, released per §11.4.40.
  - Exemption for trivial changes (typo fixes, doc revision-header bumps, MD-export regeneration) ONLY when (i) zero source code touched AND (ii) the commit message explicitly cites the exemption.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-92-PROPAGATION, CM-MULTI-PASS-EVALUATION-EVIDENCE (audits recent commits for the 5-pass trail: commit footer, per-commit `qa-results/<commit-hash>/passes/`, or Issues.md/Fixed.md narrative); paired §1.1 mutations strip load-bearing literals

#### §11.4.93 — SQLite-backed single-source-of-truth for workable items
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:672-730
- **Rules:**
  - The DB is authoritative; all Markdown/HTML/PDF/Status/Summary surfaces (Issues.md, Fixed.md, Issues_Summary.md, Fixed_Summary.md, CONTINUATION.md, Status.md) are generator output. Regeneration always starts from the DB.
  - Canonical artefacts: (1) DB file at `docs/workable_items.db` (SQLite 3), TRACKED in git, NEVER gitignored; every commit mutating workable items MUST stage + push the DB with the Markdown regen output; exception to §11.4.30 (not a build artefact); WAL sidecars `*.db-wal` + `*.db-shm` ARE gitignored and checkpointed into the main `.db` by `workable-items sync` or `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`.
  - (2) Mandatory minimum schema tables: `items` (PK `atm_id` per §11.4.54; `type` §11.4.16; `status` §11.4.15 + §11.4.90 incl. Obsolete; `severity`, `title`, `description` >= 6 words / >= 40 chars per §11.4.91, `created_at`, `last_modified`, `current_location` Issues|Fixed, `forensic_anchor`, `closure_criteria`, `composes_with` JSON array); `item_history` (append-only: atm_id, event_type Opened|Updated|Reopened|Fixed|Implemented|Completed|Obsolete, by AI|User, on_date, reason, evidence_path); `obsolete_details` (atm_id, since, reason, superseding_item, triple_check_evidence); `operator_block_details` (atm_id, what, why_exhausted_alternatives, unblock_condition, who per §11.4.21); `firebase_metadata` (§11.4.47); `meta` (schema version, last_sync_direction, last_sync_timestamp, integrity_hash).
  - (3) Go binary at `cmd/workable-items/` (separate Go module, not part of the AOSP build), subcommands: `sync md-to-db` (idempotent upsert), `sync db-to-md` (idempotent regeneration of Issues/Fixed/Summaries/CONTINUATION.md §3/every Status.md), `diff` (DB vs MD divergence, used by pre-build gate), `validate` (schema sanity + §11.4.15/16/33/34/54/90/91 invariants per row, FAIL on violation), `add <type> <severity> --title --description` (mandatory fields enforced), `close <atm-id> --status <fixed|implemented|completed|obsolete> --evidence <path>` (mandatory evidence per §11.4.5/§11.4.90).
  - (4) Integration: `commit_all.sh` pre-commit runs `workable-items diff` and refuses on divergence; `sync_issues_docs.sh` invokes `workable-items sync db-to-md` (legacy generators become shims); `pre_build_verification.sh` runs `workable-items validate` as a gate (failure increments ERRORS).
  - (5) Anti-bluff coverage: unit tests for every CRUD op + schema invariant; integration MD->DB->MD round trip with byte-identical re-emission (closed-set cosmetic-whitespace tolerance); stress+chaos per §11.4.85 (1000-row insert, 10 concurrent writers, mid-write SIGKILL, corrupt-DB recovery, disk-full); paired §1.1 mutation (strip a CRUD function -> unit test FAILs); HelixQA Challenge `CME-WORKABLE-ITEMS-001` exercising end-to-end DB->MD->DB->MD.
  - Bidirectional regeneration: DB MUST be reconstructible from MD (disaster recovery/audit replay) and MD from DB (primary direction); both produce semantically equivalent output.
  - The Go binary lives in the constitution submodule (`constitution/scripts/workable-items/`) and consumers reference it per §11.4.74; never reimplement.
  - Migration path: Phase 1 file `§LA` Issues entry (scope-locked); Phase 2 Go binary scaffold + schema DDL; Phase 3 `sync md-to-db` + initial migration; Phase 4 `sync db-to-md` + byte-identical round-trip CI gate; Phase 5 legacy generators become Go shims; Phase 6 legacy text-direct edits prohibited (pre-commit hook).
  - A consuming project maintaining text trackers without the migration plan filed and actively progressing is a data-architecture-layer PASS-bluff.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-93-PROPAGATION, CM-WORKABLE-ITEMS-DB-PRESENT (DB regen mechanism per §11.4.77 + schema version current), CM-WORKABLE-ITEMS-MD-DB-IN-SYNC (diff empty); paired §1.1 mutations; CME-WORKABLE-ITEMS-001 (Challenge entry)
- **No escape hatch:** none named (stated: non-compliance is a release blocker)
- **Honest boundary:** none stated (the DB-tracking policy is amended by §11.4.95: DB is tracked, not gitignored)
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.12, §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.17, §11.4.19, §11.4.21, §11.4.27, §11.4.30, §11.4.33, §11.4.34, §11.4.42, §11.4.43, §11.4.44, §11.4.45, §11.4.47, §11.4.50, §11.4.51, §11.4.52, §11.4.53, §11.4.54, §11.4.55, §11.4.56, §11.4.57, §11.4.58, §11.4.60, §11.4.65, §11.4.74, §11.4.77, §11.4.83, §11.4.85, §11.4.86, §11.4.87, §11.4.89, §11.4.90, §11.4.91, §11.4.92

#### §11.4.95 — Workable-items SQLite DB is TRACKED in git, NEVER gitignored
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:734-758
- **Rules:**
  - The DB at `docs/workable_items.db` is the AUTHORITATIVE source of truth for every workable item in every consuming project and MUST be TRACKED in git; NEVER gitignored regardless of file size or build-artefact heuristics (it is authoritative source data, not a build artefact).

  - Pushed to every upstream per §2.1 so a fresh clone from any mirror reconstructs the full inventory.
  - WAL-checkpointed before commit: the `workable-items` binary MUST execute `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` before any commit-stage step; the transient `*.db-wal` + `*.db-shm` sidecars ARE gitignored (§11.4.30 transient classification).
  - NEVER force-rewritten without §9.2 hardlinked backup + operator authorization; DB commit history is the audit trail.
  - Explicit named exception to the §11.4.30 gitignore rule; §11.4.77 regeneration mechanism does NOT apply to this DB (the DB IS the source).
  - AMENDS §11.4.93: the earlier text describing the DB as gitignored with §11.4.77 regeneration is replaced; Markdown trackers remain tracked AND derived; the DB is tracked AND authoritative; both sync directions continue per §11.4.93.
