#### §11.4.104 — Participant identity, attribution & notification-tagging
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:762-801
- **Rules:**
  - Binds every consumer that ships a messenger/notification surface (Herald and flavor binaries are the reference implementation); detailed normative spec is Herald `docs/design/PARTICIPANT_ATTRIBUTION.md`; implementations code against the contract, not a paraphrase. Short tag: `participant-attribution-tagging`.
  - (A) Participant identity: every supported messenger MUST relate inbound+outbound messages to a Participant (logical Subscriber/User). Identity = logical subscriber (canonical messenger-neutral `handle`, `kind` in `{human, agent, service}`) PLUS per-channel aliases (`channel`, `channel_user_id`, per-channel `@username`). The canonical handle stored in attribution columns is from the closed set: `Claude` (reserved system-agent sentinel, kind=agent) OR a human's canonical handle (subscriber `@username`, resolved per-channel via the alias table).
  - (B) Operator designation: the Operator (human driving the system via the agent CLI) is designated by env var `HERALD_<CHANNEL>_OPERATOR_USERNAME` (e.g. `HERALD_TGRAM_OPERATOR_USERNAME`, `HERALD_SLACK_OPERATOR_USERNAME`) per messenger, NOT a DB flag; the Operator is a normal Participant whose canonical handle equals that env value.
  - (C) Every workable item MUST carry `created_by` and `assigned_to` canonical-handle columns: opened via agent CLI prompt -> `created_by = Operator`; opened by system/agent detection -> `created_by = "Claude"`; received as subscriber message -> `created_by =` sender's resolved canonical `@username`. `assigned_to` defaults to the Operator and MAY be overridden explicitly. Both columns are self-contained in the SSoT and its Markdown export. Legacy items carry empty `""` attribution and MUST still parse and validate.
  - (D) Notification @-tagging matrix on any workable-item event: mentions = {}; if assigned_to is a human handle AND != Operator -> add assigned_to; if created_by is a human handle AND != Operator AND != "Claude" -> add created_by; "Claude" is NEVER tagged; the Operator is NEVER tagged; de-duplicate; resolve each mention to the target channel's `@username`, skipping participants with no alias there.
  - (E) Anti-bluff: every layer ships unit + integration + E2E + full-automation tests with REAL captured evidence: real SQLite round-trip with the new columns (byte-identical, including legacy fixtures lacking the fields); the tagging matrix proven by a truth-table test with a mutation flipping one cell forcing FAIL; an E2E real-item-event -> real-dispatched-message asserting exact `@username`s AND a negative case proving the Operator is NOT tagged; evidence committed under `docs/qa/<run-id>/`.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); projects with no messenger surface inherit latently (binds when they ship one, per §11.4.96 pattern). 4-layer coverage per §11.4.4(b).
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-104-PROPAGATION (literal `11.4.104` across the consumer fleet CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/QWEN.md; paired §1.1 mutation strips the literal; gate-code is a separate work item)
- **No escape hatch:** `--skip-attribution`, `--no-participant-tagging`, `--tag-operator-anyway`, `--attribution-later`
- **Honest boundary:** Gate-code implementation lands as a separate work item; this anchor defines the contract.
- **Composes:** §11.4, §11.4.1..§11.4.16, §11.4.5, §11.4.69, §11.4.50, §11.4.91, §11.4.93, §11.4.95, §1.1, §11.4.17, §11.4.96, §11.4.35, §11.4.4

#### §11.4.112 — Structural-impossibility won't-fix classification mandate
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:805-827
- **Rules:**
  - When deep research per §11.4.8 PROVES (cited authoritative sources AND, where applicable, reproducible captured evidence) that a goal is structurally impossible on the target platform (forbidden by platform design / hardware-protocol constraint / documented kernel-or-API limitation, not merely unimplemented or hard), the goal MUST be: (1) classified `Won't-fix` and closed per §11.4.90 terminal-status discipline with closure reason `structurally-impossible` (a value in the §11.4.90 closed reason vocabulary); (2) documented with the impossibility evidence: cited authoritative source URLs (per §11.4.99 latest-source verification) PLUS reproducible probe/captured evidence, recorded in the tracker entry and the relevant `docs/` guide; (3) NOT re-attempted in future cycles: the closed entry is canonical; a re-open MUST cite NEW evidence that the platform constraint changed (per §11.4.34 and §11.4.7), never re-derive the same impossibility; (4) paired with the correct posture: the entry MUST state what the project DOES instead, so "impossible" is never confused with "broken/unhandled".
  - (5) Scope bounding (extension 2026-07-17): every `structurally-impossible` verdict MUST additionally (a) STATE ITS EXACT SCOPE as the narrowest claim the evidence supports (every load-bearing qualifier such as "without the application's cooperation", "while the UI stays put", "on this platform version" is part of the verdict; dropping one widens it); (b) ENUMERATE ADJACENT GOALS IT DOES NOT COVER, each marked NOT-COVERED-BY-THIS-VERDICT (a neighbour of unknown viability is recorded UNKNOWN with a tracked follow-up per §11.4.6, never silently absorbed); (c) BE CITATION-FENCED: the verdict MUST NOT be cited as the answer for any goal outside its stated scope, in planning/investigation/design/status, without that goal's OWN §11.4.150 deep-research pass and OWN proof (citing beyond the fence is a §11.4.6 violation and a verdict-layer bluff of the class §11.4.199 names).
  - Reserved for PROVEN impossibility only: "could not find a way", "very hard", "no time" are NOT structural impossibility (they are `Operator-blocked` §11.4.21 or open work); mislabelling to avoid work is a planning-layer bluff.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17).
  - Gate contract for clause (5): `CM-WONT-FIX-STRUCTURAL-IMPOSSIBILITY` is extended so every `structurally-impossible` entry carries (i) an explicit SCOPE statement and (ii) an adjacent-goals-NOT-covered enumeration (each not-covered or UNKNOWN+tracked); (iii) citing the verdict against a goal outside its scope without that goal's own §11.4.150 research + proof -> FAIL.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-112-PROPAGATION (literal `11.4.112`), CM-WONT-FIX-STRUCTURAL-IMPOSSIBILITY (recommended per family; entries carry cited authoritative-source evidence + stated correct-posture line + clause-5 scope and adjacent-goal enumeration); paired §1.1 mutations (strip literal; strip evidence citation; strip scope statement; strip adjacent-goal enumeration; cite an in-scope verdict against an enumerated not-covered neighbour -> FAIL)
- **No escape hatch:** `--wont-fix-without-proof`, `--reattempt-closed-impossible`, `--skip-impossibility-evidence`, `--impossible-equals-broken`, `--unscoped-impossibility-verdict`, `--skip-adjacent-goal-enumeration`, `--cite-verdict-beyond-scope`, `--neighbour-inherits-impossibility`
- **Honest boundary:** Gate-code is a separate work item (contract, not a claim of shipped code). The classification is durable but not eternal: a platform change can make the impossible possible, and reopening on NEW cited evidence is correct. An adjacent goal outside the fence is UNDECIDED, not viable, and earns its own verdict by its own evidence.
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.7, §11.4.8, §11.4.34, §11.4.90, §11.4.99, §11.4.150, §11.4.199, §11.4.21, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.148 — Workable-item integrity (status+type+id) + structured description + bidirectional external-tracker sync + BLOCKED unblock-choices
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:831-853
- **Rules:**
  - BINDS and STRENGTHENS §11.4.15/16/54/21/91/93/95/106 into one integrity contract across three surfaces: DB, docs, external tracker.
  - (D1) Every item, at every moment, MUST carry (i) a `**Status:**` from the §11.4.15/§11.4.21/§11.4.90 closed set, (ii) a `**Type:**` from `{Bug | Feature | Task}` (§11.4.16), (iii) a stable unique monotonic append-only `[<ID-NNN>]` identifier (§11.4.54). Missing any of the three in the DB, rendered docs, OR external tracker is a violation; validator FAILs (non-zero exit, release blocker). An id on one surface but absent on another is a sync-integrity failure.
  - (D2) Every item MUST carry a comprehensive self-contained structured description: at minimum WHAT it is (§11.4.91 >= 6 words / >= 40 chars), HOW it manifests, HOW to reproduce (deterministic steps, §11.4.115/§11.4.146), ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (captured-evidence verdict closing it per §11.4.123/§11.4.69). It lives in the DB `description` column AND renders into docs AND pushes to the external tracker; no one-liner stubs, no §11.4.91 anti-pattern fragments; a placeholder description is a planning-layer PASS-bluff.
  - (D3) BLOCKED items (tightens §11.4.21): every `Operator-blocked` item (any `Blocked`/`BLOCKED` input alias normalised to canonical `Operator-blocked`, a documented alias never a silent fork) MUST carry, beyond §11.4.21 WHAT/WHY/WHO, an enumerated set of UNBLOCK CHOICES (closed list of decisions/actions that would unblock, e.g. `[A] grant access X · [B] approve removal of Y · [C] provide credential Z`, mirroring §11.4.66 2-4 option shape). Validator FAILs a BLOCKED item whose unblock field is empty or has no enumerated choice marker.
  - (D4) The git-tracked SQLite DB (§11.4.93/§11.4.95) is the SSoT; rendered docs (Issues/Issues_Summary/Fixed/Fixed_Summary/per-item docs + §11.4.65/§11.4.106 exports) and the external tracker are DERIVED. A full sync MUST run regularly and on every state change: DB->docs (`db-to-md`), docs->DB (`md-to-db`, byte-identical round trip per §11.4.93), DB->external-tracker push, gated by a drift-proof §11.4.86 fingerprint (sha256 of the sorted item keyset, NOT mtime) so a forgotten sync FAILs a pre-build gate. The sync is bound into the §11.4.106 docs_chain engine as a registered consumer context, never an ad-hoc parallel script.
  - (D5) External-tracker push MUST carry each item's status (collapsed onto the tracker's native status set per §11.4.33 when fixed; the API-cannot-create-statuses case is a §11.4.112 structural constraint, precise value preserved in a description header), type, assignee (§11.4.104 participant handle `created_by`/`assigned_to`), and sub-tasks. An UNSET assignee defaults from a project-supplied env var (§11.4.104 operator-username pattern), never hardcoded, never logged (§11.4.10). IDEMPOTENT: dry-run-then-real, match-by-stable-key (`[<ID>]` name prefix / id custom field), present=UPDATE / absent=CREATE, rate-limited, credential-redacted, with captured sink-side `created=N updated=M failed=0` proof per §11.4.69. Machinery stays project-agnostic (§11.4.28); the consumer registers its tracker (service, list/board id, field map) at runtime; the constitution names the discipline, not the vendor.
  - Anti-bluff: every sync run and validator pass carries captured evidence per §11.4.5/§11.4.69 (round-trip diff, fingerprint match, tracker created/updated/failed line under `qa-results/`); a sync claimed with no growing evidence trail, a complete/Fixed item with no acceptance-criteria description, or a BLOCKED item with no unblock choices are PASS-bluffs.
  - EXTENSION SLICING (2026-08-20): (a) the slicing checklist is INVEST (Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable); the corpus defines only two letters, Small and Testable, which are linked (an item too big to test end-to-end is one whose "done" cannot be proven, so it closes on partial evidence and reopens on the untested part); no per-letter obligations beyond those two are invented, and no SMART obligation may be grounded on the corpus. (b) Items MUST be VERTICAL slices (thin end-to-end capability a user can observe), NEVER horizontal layers ("do all the database work", "do all the UI") which are never independently valuable or testable; example: "reconcile donations across nine gateways" is untestable as one unit and is sliced into e.g. "ingest and normalize gateway A's settlement file", "detect a provider-only ghost charge", "classify a fee/FX residual", each with its own Given/When/Then and evidence. (c) Under agents, a small testable item can be dispatched and verified against a clear oracle, while a big fuzzy item gets reported "done" with nothing to check it against (§11.4.240/§11.4.262 at the item-definition layer). (d) Ready-before-dispatch: three amigos (business, development, testing/QA views; the testing voice surfaces missing failure scenarios; output is a shared WRITTEN understanding) and specification by example (concrete real inputs and expected outputs, including awkward ones, become acceptance tests). MANDATE: an item MUST be sliced small enough that its own acceptance criteria are provable end-to-end from its own captured evidence and MUST be a vertical slice; an item that cannot be closed on its own evidence is not ready for dispatch and MUST be re-sliced before work begins.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies DB path, id prefix, tracker service + list/board id + field map + default-assignee env var, docs_chain context per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-148-PROPAGATION (literal `11.4.148`), CM-ITEM-INTEGRITY-STATUS-TYPE-ID, CM-ITEM-COMPREHENSIVE-DESCRIPTION, CM-BLOCKED-UNBLOCK-CHOICES, CM-TRACKER-SYNC-IDEMPOTENT, CM-ITEM-SLICED-SMALL-AND-TESTABLE (decidable-from-own-evidence criteria and vertical slice; horizontal-layer item or one whose criteria depend on a sibling landing -> FAIL naming the item); paired §1.1 mutations (strip literal; drop type/id/description-structure/unblock-choices; break tracker-sync idempotency key; re-shape one item into a horizontal layer -> gate MUST FAIL; golden-FALSE per §11.4.201(1): a legitimately-dependent item still independently testable once its dependency is met MUST NOT fire)
- **No escape hatch:** `--item-without-status`, `--item-without-type`, `--item-without-id`, `--stub-description-OK`, `--blocked-without-choices`, `--skip-tracker-sync`, `--one-way-sync-OK`, `--non-idempotent-tracker-push`, `--hardcode-assignee`
- **Honest boundary:** The contract guarantees every item is well-formed and the three surfaces agree, NOT that the underlying work is correct (that crosses §11.4.108/§11.4.40/§11.4.123). Slicing makes "done" provable, not the work correct (§11.4.108/§11.4.115/§11.4.185); "small" means testability-in-isolation, NOT a point/hour/line count. Gate-code is a separate work item, not claimed shipped.
- **Composes:** §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.21, §11.4.33, §11.4.34, §11.4.54, §11.4.66, §11.4.86, §11.4.91, §11.4.93, §11.4.95, §11.4.104, §11.4.106, §11.4.112, §11.4.123, §11.4.10, §11.4.28, §11.4.69, §11.4.6, §1.1, §11.4.5, §11.4.65, §11.4.115, §11.4.146, §11.4.239, §11.4.240, §11.4.262, §11.4.185, §11.4.201, §11.4.227

#### §11.4.149 — Per-workable-item testing-diary mandate
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:855-873
- **Rules:**
  - Every workable item MUST carry a TESTING DIARY: a chronological append-only record of every test run against it. It is distinct from §11.4.93 `item_history` (lifecycle state transitions) and §11.4.55 Reopens.md (reopen cycles): the diary records TEST EXECUTIONS, each of which may or may not cause a state transition.
  - (a) Append-only per-item `test_diary` table in the SQLite SSoT (additive to the §11.4.93/§11.4.95 schema, never a competing source): one row per test run, soft-keyed to the item's stable id, with at minimum: ISO-8601-UTC `date_time` (sortable, deterministic §11.4.50); `tested_by` from a closed set (e.g. `User | Operator | AI-agent | HelixQA`); `result` from the §11.4.45 closed verdict vocabulary `{PASS | FAIL | SKIP}` + short detail; in-depth `observations` (long markdown; facts or explicit `UNCONFIRMED:`/`PENDING_FORENSICS:` per §11.4.6, never "likely"); `action_taken` + a `status_changed` flag + from/to (did the run change status and WHY/why-not); and a §11.4.69 `evidence_path` + `feature_class`. A structural schema constraint makes a `PASS` row WITHOUT a non-empty evidence path impossible.
  - (b) Per item BOTH an in-depth diary document (one section per run, full observations + action + evidence link) AND a derived at-a-glance summary (rollup VIEW: total/pass/fail/skip runs, last verdict, last run, status-change count, distinct testers, distinct feature-classes), DERIVED never a duplicate source per §11.4.93; the summary feeds §11.4.132 risk-ordering inputs.
  - (c) Per-item `Diary` + `Diary_Summary` render to the project's full export-format set (§11.4.65 + any project-added format) with the freshness invariant (derived-format mtime >= source mtime), wired through the §11.4.106 docs_chain engine as a registered consumer context with a §11.4.86 drift-proof fingerprint (sha256 of sorted diary keyset, NOT mtime) so a diary row added but not exported/pushed FAILs a pre-build gate.
  - (d) External tracker: the workable-item task keeps its description = the item (§11.4.148 D2, NOT polluted with diary text); each diary run is a CHILD SUB-TASK (type `task`) with lifecycle `{TODO | In-progress | Completed}` (collapsed onto the tracker's native statuses per §11.4.33/§11.4.112 when fixed), carrying observations + action + an Evidence: line (the path, not the raw artefact, §11.4.10/§11.4.13) and a stable diary-entry idempotency key; the push reuses §11.4.148 D5 idempotent, rate-limited, credential-redacted, sink-side-proven discipline; mapper stays project-agnostic (§11.4.28).
  - (e) Minimal-LLM: tooling (add/export/tracker-sync/validate) is deterministic bash/Go with ZERO LLM in the data path; `observations` prose is authored by whoever ran the test. Covered per §11.4.27 by every applicable test type (unit + integration against the real tracker with an honest §11.4.3 SKIP-when-token-absent, never a faked PASS + export + HelixQA Challenge + paired §1.1 mutation).
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies DB path, diary doc layout, export formats, tracker sub-task field map, docs_chain context per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-149-PROPAGATION (literal `11.4.149`), CM-TEST-DIARY-SYNC (a diary row not exported/pushed FAILs), CM-DIARY-PASS-REQUIRES-EVIDENCE (a PASS row carries non-empty evidence path); paired §1.1 mutations (strip literal; strip the evidence-required constraint, sub-task lifecycle, or fingerprint); gate-code is a separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** `--skip-testing-diary`, `--diary-without-evidence`, `--no-diary-summary`, `--diary-without-tracker-subtask`, `--llm-in-diary-data-path`, `--diary-export-optional`
- **Honest boundary:** The diary guarantees a complete auditable test history per item, NOT that any single run's verdict is correct (that rests on the run's own captured evidence per §11.4.69/§11.4.107/§11.4.123).
- **Composes:** §11.4.6, §11.4.27, §11.4.45, §11.4.50, §11.4.55, §11.4.65, §11.4.69, §11.4.86, §11.4.93, §11.4.95, §11.4.106, §11.4.107, §11.4.123, §11.4.132, §11.4.148, §11.4.10, §11.4.13, §11.4.28, §11.4.33, §11.4.112, §11.4.3, §1.1

#### §11.4.171 — Mandatory comprehensive human-readable workable-item descriptions
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:875
- **Rules:**
  - Every workable item (ATM-NNN) in the workable-items DB, Issues.md, Fixed.md, Issues_Summary.md, Fixed_Summary.md and ALL derived documents MUST carry a comprehensive human-readable description in plain non-technical language suitable for non-developers (project managers, stakeholders, team leads, business partners).
  - The description MUST be 5-7 sentences minimum and explain: (a) WHAT the item is (feature/fix/task in simple terms); (b) WHY it matters (user/business value); (c) HOW it works (mechanism, without code references); (d) WHO benefits (end user or stakeholder); (e) WHAT the expected outcome is (measurable result).
  - The description is MANDATORY; an item without one is a §11.4 violation at the documentation layer.
  - Descriptions MUST NOT use jargon, unexpanded acronyms, code references, or technical implementation details as the primary explanation; technical details MAY appear as supplementary context AFTER the plain-language explanation.
  - The `description` column in the SQLite DB `docs/workable_items.db` is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH; all derived documents MUST carry the SAME description text.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17).
- **Gates:** CM-HUMAN-READABLE-DESCRIPTION (when implemented: walks every DB item and asserts `description` exists, non-empty, >= 50 characters; paired §1.1 mutation strips a description -> FAIL), CM-COVENANT-114-171-PROPAGATION (literal `11.4.171`)
- **No escape hatch:** none named
- **Honest boundary:** none stated
- **Composes:** §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.19, §11.4.91, §11.4.93, §11.4.148, §11.4.65, §11.4.17

#### §11.4.202 — Reporting directives: a report MUST auto-create a fully-populated, fully-synced workable item
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:877-881
- **Rules:**
  - Every governed project MUST expose REPORTING DIRECTIVES, the §11.4.140 registered actions `BUG` (Type=Bug), `TASK` (Type=Task) and `ISSUE` (generic report, CLASSIFIED into the §11.4.16 closed set), so a plain-language operator report becomes a real tracked fully-synced workable item automatically every time. A report discussed/acknowledged/answered in prose/"noted" WITHOUT landing a tracked item is a PASS-bluff at the requirements-intake layer (the §11.4.197 loss-of-requirements failure at its entry point).
  - (1) GRAMMAR: the directives are ordinary registry rows so every §11.4.140 form works (`BUG :: <text>`, `DEFAULT::BUG :: <text>`, `/DEFAULT::BUG <text>`, `BUG ---> <text>`) PLUS a SIXTH form added here: single-colon `NAME: <text>` (e.g. `ISSUE: subtitles are late`). The single-colon form is REGISTERED-ACTION-ONLY by construction: a single-colon token not a registered action is a NO-OP (ordinary prompt), NEVER an ASK and NEVER a sub-system shortcut (prose like `TODO:`, `WARNING:`, `FIXME:` shares the shape; `NOTE:` is a registered §11.4.140 severity marker); the other five forms keep ASK-on-unknown behaviour. Host-command collisions use the existing §11.4.140 mechanism (`slash_bare: auto` + `slash_conflicts: [..]`): a bare `/NAME` colliding with a built-in (e.g. Claude Code's `/bug`) is NOT honored, the namespaced `/DEFAULT::NAME` is always unambiguous, and `NAME:` / `NAME ::` / `NAME --->` forms are never affected by any host command.
  - (2) THE ITEM MUST carry on ALL surfaces: valid Status (§11.4.15, `Queued` at intake), Type from the closed set {Bug | Feature | Task} (`ISSUE` is a REPORTING CHANNEL, never a fourth type; inventing one is a violation), a stable auto-incremented id (§11.4.54), and a comprehensive structured description (§11.4.148 D2 / §11.4.171): what / affected-scope / reproduction / acceptance. An undetermined section is recorded as explicit `UNKNOWN:` gap, NEVER invented (§11.4.6). For `ISSUE` the type is classified from content and stated as FACT; if not determinable the operator is ASKED (§11.4.66/§11.4.105) BEFORE creation; ONLY when running autonomously where asking is impossible (§11.4.101) may the lowest-stakes default `Task` be used, and the defaulted classification MUST be recorded verbatim in the item and surfaced for reclassification.
  - (3) FULL SYNC in one shot: (a) item lands in the SQLite SSoT (§11.4.93/§11.4.95); (b) EVERY derived document regenerated FROM the DB (open + closed trackers, summaries, `.md`/`.html`/`.pdf`/`.docx` siblings per §11.4.12/§11.4.53/§11.4.65/§11.4.106); (c) item pushed to EVERY configured external tracker (§11.4.148 D5).
  - (4) NEVER A FAKED PUSH (§11.4.10/§11.4.6/§11.4.3): a tracker whose credentials or client are absent is SKIPPED with an honest machine-readable reason (`credentials_absent`: names of unset variables ONLY, never a value; `tracker_client_absent`: PENDING-OPERATOR-INPUT). A tracker PASS is recorded ONLY after a real push command really exited 0. Fabricating, assuming, or silently omitting a push is an integration-layer bluff; a missing tracker NEVER blocks the item from landing in DB + docs.
  - (5) DECOUPLED ENGINE, CONSUMER-OWNED DATA (§11.4.28/§11.4.177): the engine lives at `constitution/scripts/reporting/report_item.sh`, inherited BY REFERENCE (never copied), with ZERO project literals; DB path, id prefix, sync command, tracker commands and required env vars come from a CONSUMER-OWNED config file (DATA); the engine FAILS CLOSED with an actionable message when config is absent and never guesses a project's paths.
  - (6) ANTI-BLUFF (§11.4/§11.4.107(10)): four-layer coverage: a pre-build gate whose FUNCTIONAL invariant SOURCES and RUNS the parser (never grep-only, §11.4.108); a paired §1.1 mutation test proving each invariant is load-bearing; an end-to-end suite against a REAL SQLite DB with REAL binaries (no mocks, §11.4.27) asserting a real row lands with the right Type/Status/id, docs are regenerated FROM the DB, and an absent tracker SKIPs honestly; self-validated with golden-good + golden-bad + negative-control fixtures.
  - Classification: universal (§11.4.17); consumer supplies DB path, id prefix, sync command, tracker bindings per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-REPORTING-DIRECTIVES (registry declares ISSUE/BUG/TASK + single-colon registered-only; engine exists, parse-clean, project-literal-free; directives expand at runtime while prose does not; honest-skip reasons exist and a tracker PASS is gated on a real exit 0), CM-COVENANT-114-202-PROPAGATION (literal `11.4.202`); paired §1.1 mutations (strip an action row, flip single-colon to non-registered-only, strip the parser branch, remove the prose NO-OP branch, make the engine fake a tracker push, couple engine to one project -> gate FAILs; strip literal -> propagation gate FAILs)
- **No escape hatch:** `--report-without-item`, `--prose-acknowledgement-OK`, `--skip-item-creation`, `--skip-tracker-sync`, `--fake-tracker-push`, `--invent-a-fourth-type`, `--hardcode-project-in-engine`
- **Honest boundary:** The other five grammar forms keep ASK-on-unknown because their shapes do not occur in prose; non-compliance is a release blocker regardless of context.
- **Composes:** §11.4.140, §11.4.93, §11.4.95, §11.4.15, §11.4.16, §11.4.54, §11.4.148, §11.4.171, §11.4.106, §11.4.12, §11.4.53, §11.4.65, §11.4.10, §11.4.66, §11.4.105, §11.4.101, §11.4.197, §11.4.28, §11.4.177, §11.4.164, §11.4.107, §11.4.108, §11.4.27, §11.4.3, §11.4.6, §1.1

#### §11.4.214 — Recurrence-links-not-mints: a returning defect MUST reopen its existing item, never enter as a new id (research-derived, 2026-07-17)
- **Source:** workable-items-and-tracking.md:883-901
- **Rules:**
  - Reason: recurrences filed as new ids never increment the original's reopen counter, so the §11.4.55 reopens_count (the signal §11.4.132(d)/§11.4.189 use to rank the most-fragile work) stays quiet precisely on items that keep breaking; the recorded 52% reopen rate was a known undercount; duplicates inflate the queue and fork conflicting fixes.
  - Mandate: before minting a NEW id for any incoming defect from ANY intake path, check whether an existing item describes the SAME defect; if so LINK the report to it rather than mint, and REOPEN it if and only if it is currently in a terminal state (§11.4.33 Fixed/Implemented/Completed, or a §11.4.90 closure other than duplicate-of).
  - (0) Resolve to the CANONICAL CHAIN HEAD first: a duplicate-of closure is a pointer, not a destination. Every match MUST be resolved through its duplicate-of links to the chain head, and the link plus any reopen land on THAT head, never on an intermediate duplicate (reopening a duplicate-of closure would resurrect a non-canonical copy beside its live canonical item and credit the §11.4.55 signal to the wrong item). Multi-match: resolve every match to its head and act on the single surviving head; more than one distinct head -> UNDECIDED per (3) (ask, or mint-with-link; never guess, §11.4.6); resolved head OPEN -> prefer it and LINK ONLY. A chain whose head cannot be resolved (broken/circular duplicate-of) is UNDECIDED plus a tracked integrity defect (§11.4.186 orphan-ref class), never a silent pick.
  - Open-original case: when the resolved head is OPEN (any non-terminal §11.4.15 status: Queued / In progress / Ready for testing / In testing / already Reopened / Operator-blocked) the action is LINK ONLY; "reopen an open item" is undefined in the §11.4.15 status machine and §11.4.34 Reopened presupposes a prior closure (§11.4.7).
  - §11.4.202 precedence: §11.4.202 mandates no report is ever LOST; it is satisfied IN FULL by a same-defect report landing as a link plus (terminal-only) reopen; §11.4.214 refines WHICH item a report lands on, §11.4.202 owns THAT it lands. For DISTINCT or UNDECIDED verdicts, §11.4.202's mint path runs unchanged.
  - (1) EVERY intake path is bound, not only the reporting channel: §11.4.202 directives, AI-detected test/gate failures, regression-guard verdicts, cycle re-discovery, captured-evidence retrospect, operator manual testing (§11.4.34 reasons test-failed, cycle-re-discovered, manual-testing-detected, end-user-report).
  - (2) The key is structured, never a bare substring (§11.4.186): match on ticket reference where present, else a normalised (subject, scope).
  - (3) distinct-but-similar is a FIRST-CLASS verdict. Three outcomes: SAME-DEFECT (link + reopen), DISTINCT (mint a new id, correct and expected), UNDECIDED (do NOT guess: ask per §11.4.66/§11.4.105, or mint the new id WITH a recorded candidate-duplicate link for review; when autonomous per §11.4.101 prefer mint-with-link over merge, because a spurious id is recoverable and a wrongly merged defect is silently lost).
  - (4) The dedup oracle is self-validated (§11.4.107(10)/§11.4.186): golden-good (true recurrence MUST link+reopen), golden-bad (missed recurrence MUST be caught) and a negative-control (two genuinely DISTINCT items sharing a subject MUST NOT merge); an oracle without the negative control is a false-merge engine and a bluff.
  - (5) Id stability preserved (§11.4.54): linking never renumbers, reuses or retires an id; the original is reopened and its counter increments; an already-minted duplicate is LINKED (recorded duplicate-of per §11.4.90), never silently deleted or renumbered.
  - (6) The restored signal is the point: an undercounting reopen counter is a §11.4/§11.4.1 bluff at the prioritisation layer.
  - Consumer supplies tracker, id scheme, normalisation function and intake wiring per §11.4.35.
- **Gates:** CM-COVENANT-114-214-PROPAGATION (literal 11.4.214), CM-RECURRENCE-LINKS-NOT-MINTS (every intake path runs dedup before minting; oracle golden-good/golden-bad/negative-control wired into meta-test; every confirmed-duplicate link resolves to a canonical chain head; every link whose resolved head was TERMINAL at link time has a reopen event on that head). Gate scope is §11.4.201-bound: MUST NOT fire on a link whose head was OPEN, on an UNDECIDED candidate-duplicate link, nor demand a reopen on an intermediate duplicate-of closure; golden-FALSE set MUST include an open-head link, a candidate-duplicate link, and a link whose immediate target is a duplicate-of closure with the reopen correctly on the chain head; golden-TRUE MUST include a terminal-head link with no reopen (gate MUST fire). Paired mutations: file a known recurrence and let it mint a fresh id without a link -> gate FAILs; strip the negative control so two distinct same-subject items merge -> oracle self-check FAILs; strip the literal -> propagation gate FAILs; gate-code = separate work item
- **No escape hatch:** --skip-dedup-at-intake, --mint-every-report, --bare-substring-dedup, --merge-without-negative-control, --recurrence-as-new-id-OK, --reopen-counter-may-undercount
- **Honest boundary:** Dedup-at-intake makes the reopen signal TRUE; it does not make the item CORRECT nor prove the recurrence shares the original's root cause (§11.4.102 decides; the linked-and-reopened item is where that is recorded, not a reason to fork). Binds rather than re-authors: intake seam §11.4.202, keying/negative-control §11.4.186, reopen mechanics §11.4.34, counter §11.4.55, id stability §11.4.54, priority consumers §11.4.132/§11.4.189.
- **Composes:** §11.4.1, §11.4.6, §11.4.34, §11.4.54, §11.4.55, §11.4.66, §11.4.90, §11.4.93, §11.4.101, §11.4.102, §11.4.105, §11.4.107(10), §11.4.132, §11.4.148, §11.4.186, §11.4.189, §11.4.202, §11.4.7, §11.4.15, §11.4.33, §11.4.21, §11.4.17



## Part 2: Project and module override digests

Sources: each module's CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md (read in full). All three share two identical blocks (see "Shared blocks" at end).

### catalog-api
- **Identity/stack**
  - Go 1.25 REST API, Gin; backend for all clients (web, desktop, Android, Android TV). Media browsing, search, recognition, recommendations, deep linking, reading experience; multi-protocol storage (SMB, FTP, NFS, WebDAV, local).
  - Module path `catalogizer`; entrypoint `main.go`; sqlcipher/sqlite (dev) + PostgreSQL (prod) dual dialect; QUIC/HTTP3 via `quic-go/http3` (self-signed TLS certs generated at startup); Brotli via `andybalholm/brotli` middleware.
  - Depends on `digital.vasic.*` submodules via `replace` directives in go.mod.
  - DISCREPANCY: docs say "Go 1.25"; go.mod says `go 1.25.7`. go.mod replaces confirmed (challenges, assets, containers, concurrency, config, filesystem, auth, cache, entities, eventbus(event_bus), database, discovery, lazy, media, memory, middleware, observability, ratelimiter(rate_limiter), recovery, ... all `../submodules/<name>`).
  - Config precedence: env vars > `.env` > `config.json` > defaults (`config/`).
  - Dynamic port: server writes chosen port to `.service-port`; frontend reads it for API proxy.
  - Routes registered under `/api/v1` in `main.go`; Prometheus at `/metrics`.
- **Commands**
  - `go run main.go` (starts server, writes `.service-port`)
  - `go build -o catalog-api` (dev-only; release builds run in rootless container, §11.4.173)
  - `GOMAXPROCS=3 go test ./... -p 2 -parallel 2` (all tests)
  - `go test -v -run TestName ./path/to/pkg/` (single test)
  - `go vet ./...`
  - AGENTS validation: `go fmt ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `go build ./...`; `GOMAXPROCS=3 go test -race ./... -p 2 -parallel 2`
  - Single pkg: `GOMAXPROCS=3 go test -race ./services/ -count=1`
  - Race sweep: `../scripts/run-race-detector.sh --fast` (catalog-api only) / `--all` (+ all submodules)
  - Coverage: `go test -cover ./... -count=1`
- **Architecture & ownership boundaries**
  - Layering: Handler -> Service -> Repository -> Database (SQLite/PostgreSQL).
  - Dual-package layout: top-level (`handlers/ services/ repository/ middleware/ models/`) = domain logic (catalog browsing, media entities, search, downloads, storage ops); `internal/` (`handlers/ services/ middleware/`) = infra (auth, metrics, WebSocket, cache, media detection pipeline, SMB circuit breaker, lifecycle).
  - Top-level pkgs: `handlers/` (domain HTTP; do NOT mix auth/metrics/cache logic — lives in `internal/`); `services/` (domain logic; own the repo layer they mutate — do not reach into another service's repo); `repository/` (CRUD files/media items/collections; always via `database.DB` wrapper, never raw `*sql.DB`); `middleware/` (CORS, logging, rate limiting; factories MUST register cleanup goroutines with `middleware.StopAll()`); `models/` (shared structs; dependency-free, no imports from handlers/ or services/); `database/` (connection mgmt, dialect abstraction, migrations; dispatch in `migrations.go`, per-dialect in `migrations_postgres.go` / `migrations_sqlite.go`; SQL files in `database/migrations/` separate SQLite+PG variants); `filesystem/` (`interface.go` defines `UnifiedClient`, `factory.go` creates per-protocol clients; new protocols = implement `UnifiedClient`); `challenges/` (bank defs, registration, config; register groups in `RegisterAll()` in `register.go`); `config/`.
  - Internal pkgs: `internal/auth/` (JWT + role-based; don't duplicate JWT logic in top-level middleware); `internal/services/` (aggregation, title parsing, scanning, media detection pipeline); `internal/media/` (`detector/` -> `analyzer/` -> `providers/` (TMDB, IMDB, OMDB, MusicBrainz, OpenLibrary, IGDB, …)); `internal/media/providers/` (MUST degrade gracefully — missing API keys never block pipeline; register in `NewProviderManager()`); `internal/metrics/` (Prometheus; `GinMiddleware()` HTTP instrumentation, `StartRuntimeCollector()`; `snapshot.go` feeds `services/reporting_service.go`); `internal/lifecycle/` (`LazyServiceRegistry`, deferred init w/ dependency ordering — use for services depending on another's eventual construction); `internal/concurrency/` (semaphore-based; no hand-rolled buffered channels for limits); `internal/smb/` (circuit breaker, offline cache, exponential backoff retry; `net.DialTimeout` bounded 5 s, never raw `net.Dial`); `internal/httpclient/` (pooled client w/ reuse+retry; always use instead of `http.DefaultClient`).
  - Dependency graph: `main.go` -> handlers, services, repository, middleware, models, database, filesystem, challenges, internal/*. RULE: no package inside `internal/` may import top-level domain packages except `models/`; top-level may freely import `internal/`.
  - DB dialect abstraction (`database/dialect.go`): `RewritePlaceholders()` (`?`->`$1..`), `RewriteInsertOrIgnore()` (-> `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`), `BooleanLiterals()` (`=0/1` -> `FALSE/TRUE`), `database.DB` wraps `*sql.DB` with shadowed `Exec/Query/QueryRow` auto-rewrite; `InsertReturningID()` / `TxInsertReturningID()` replace `LastInsertId()` (PG `RETURNING id`).
  - File ownership: `main.go` (entry, routes, shutdown; touches ALL pkgs); `database/migrations.go` (dispatch); `database/dialect.go` (SQL rewriting, affects every SQL call); `filesystem/interface.go` (UnifiedClient); `challenges/register.go`; `internal/metrics/snapshot.go` (read by reporting_service.go).
- **Agent coordination rules**
  - 1 Database mutations: add new Version+Name entry in `migrations.go` `RunMigrations()`; add BOTH Postgres and SQLite impls (`migrations_postgres.go`, `migrations_sqlite.go`); wire dispatch `if db.dialect.IsPostgres() {...} else {...}` in `migrations.go`; add `.up.sql` + `.sqlite.up.sql` reference pair in `database/migrations/`; `TestRunMigrationsSQLite` in `database/migrations_parity_test.go` MUST stay green. Schemas: never modify a shipped migration (new version); use `INSERT OR IGNORE`; use `?` placeholders; use `InsertReturningID()` not `LastInsertId()`.
  - 2 Handler additions: register in `main.go` `setupRouter()` (or route-group helper); unit test in `handlers/` or `internal/handlers/` hitting route via `httptest.Server`; auth via existing `authMiddleware` (no hand-rolled auth in handler); rate limit via per-route config in `main.go` or `middleware.RedisRateLimit(...)`.
  - 3 Concurrency/goroutines: `wg.Add(1)` BEFORE `go func()`; `sync.Once` for cleanup (`Stop()`/`Close()`); expose shutdown method callable from `main.go`; tests `defer service.Close()` / `handler.Stop()` (else `go test -race` flags leak). Required shutdown order in `main.go`: (1) `metrics.StopRuntimeCollector()` (2) `wsHandler.Stop()` (3) `cacheService.Close()` (4) `mediaEntityHandler.Close()` (5) `logAdapter.Close()` (6) `root_middleware.StopAll()` (7) `srv.Shutdown(shutdownCtx)`.
  - 4 New metadata provider: implement `MetadataProvider` in `internal/media/providers/providers.go`; constructor `NewXProvider(client, logger)`; register in `NewProviderManager()` via `lazyProviders["x"] = NewLazyProvider(...)`; missing API key => empty result, no error.
  - 5 New challenge group: create `challenges/userflow_x.go`; challenge structs embed `challenge.BaseChallenge`; expose `RegisterUserFlowXChallenges(reg challenge.Registry) error`; call from `RegisterAll()` in `challenges/register.go`; NEVER "passes as stub" — return `challenge.StatusSkipped` with structured reason when infra unavailable.
  - 6 Testing standards: `GOMAXPROCS=3 go test -race ./path/... -p 2 -parallel 2` for concurrency changes; table-driven `t.Run`; test DB `database.WrapDB(sqlDB, DialectSQLite)` (helper `internal/tests/test_helper.go`, in-memory SQLite); `httptest.NewServer` for external mocks; coverage gate: package coverage must not drop below baseline (`go test -cover ./...`); `*_test.go` beside source; constructor injection `NewService(deps...)` with mocks.
  - 7 Error handling: wrap `fmt.Errorf("context: %w", err)`; never `_ = err` silently (log at Warn or return); no empty error check; typed errors (`errors.New`, `errors.Is/As`), no stringly-typed matching.
  - 8 Dependencies: `internal/httpclient` never `http.DefaultClient`; `database.DB` wrapper never raw `*sql.DB.Exec`; import submodules via `digital.vasic.*` paths wired by `replace` in go.mod.
- **Constraints**
  - Resource limits: `GOMAXPROCS=3`, `-p 2 -parallel 2`; never exceed 30-40% host CPU/RAM (host runs other critical processes).
  - Container builds: `podman build --network host`; `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`; fully qualified image names.
  - Zero-warning policy: no console errors, no failed network requests, no deprecation warnings.
  - Secrets: never commit `.env` or hardcode secrets; use `.env.example` placeholders.
  - Concurrency: `CacheService` and `WebSocketHandler` spawn goroutines — tests must `defer service.Close()` / `handler.Stop()`.
  - SQLite: explicit `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` after connect in `database/connection.go`; pool defaults MaxOpen=25, MaxIdle=10, MaxLifetime=5m, MaxIdleTime=3m.
  - NO SUDO/ROOT (see Shared blocks). Zero Unfinished Work (see Shared blocks; present in AGENTS.md only).
- **Commit conventions**
  - Conventional Commits: `feat(services): add sync rollup report`, `fix(smb): bound dial timeout`, `test(metrics): add snapshot coverage`, `refactor(handlers): extract search filter`, `docs(agents): clarify goroutine shutdown`.
  - Every commit: pass `go fmt`, `go vet`, `go build`; affected package tests under `-race`; end with Co-Authored-By trailer when AI-authored.

  - Package `catalog-web` (package.json version 2.4.0); React 18 (`^18.2.0`) / TypeScript strict / Vite 6 (`^6.2.0`) / React Router DOM v6; port 3000, proxies `/api` and `/ws` to catalog-api.

### catalogizer-api-client
- **Identity/stack**

  - Consumers: `catalog-web` (Auth, Media, SMB), `catalogizer-desktop` (Auth, Media), `installer-wizard` (Auth, SMB).
  - DISCREPANCY: catalog-web imports `@vasic-digital/catalogizer-api-client` (via `file:../submodules/catalogizer_api_client_ts`), while this module's package name is `@catalogizer/api-client`; docs don't reconcile (UNCONFIRMED relationship).
  - Structure: `src/index.ts` (`CatalogizerClient` extends `EventEmitter` w/ typed events; owns `auth`, `media`, `smb`; lifecycle `connect()`/`disconnect()`; re-exports); `src/services/AuthService.ts` (login, logout, register, token refresh, profile; `/auth/*`); `src/services/MediaService.ts` (CRUD, search, stats, playback progress; `/api/v1/media/*`); `src/services/SMBService.ts` (config, status, scanning; `/api/v1/smb/*`); `src/utils/http.ts` (`HttpClient`: Axios wrapper, token injection, retry, refresh); `src/utils/websocket.ts` (`WebSocketClient`: reconnecting, emits `download:progress`, `scan:progress`); `src/types/index.ts` (all types + errors: `ClientConfig`, `MediaItem`, `User`, `LoginRequest`, `SMBConfig`, `ClientEvents`).
  - Error hierarchy: `CatalogizerError` > `AuthenticationError` (401), `NetworkError` (connection), `ValidationError` (400).
- **Commands**
  - `npm install` | `npm run build` (`tsc`, to `dist/`) | `npm run dev` (`tsc --watch`) | `npm run test` (`vitest run`) | `npm run lint` (`eslint src --ext .ts`); `prepublishOnly` = build.
- **Architecture & ownership boundaries**
  - `src/index.ts` = single entry point, all public API surfaces here. `src/utils/http.ts` owns ALL HTTP transport (no parallel Axios instances). `src/utils/websocket.ts` owns WS lifecycle. Services own their endpoint prefixes. `src/types/index.ts` dependency-free.
  - Style: PascalCase classes, camelCase functions/vars; imports grouped: Node builtins, third-party, internal; tests Vitest Node env, co-located in `__tests__/`.
- **Agent coordination rules**
  - 1 New endpoint: add method to appropriate service class in `src/services/`; if none suits, create new service following pattern (constructor takes `HttpClient`); wire as property on `CatalogizerClient` (`src/index.ts`); add request/response types in `src/types/index.ts`; unit tests in `__tests__/`.
  - 2 Errors: map HTTP status to typed hierarchy in `HttpClient`; never throw raw `Error` or Axios errors.
  - 3 Auth token: `HttpClient` request interceptor injects bearer; response interceptor handles 401 by refresh then retry original; if refresh fails emit `auth:expired` via `EventEmitter`; don't duplicate token logic in consumers.
  - 4 Downstream: breaking changes to method signatures, error classes, or event names require coordinated updates in all consumers.
  - 5 Testing: Vitest Node env; co-located `__tests__/`; mock Axios — never real network calls in unit tests; test each HTTP status -> error subclass mapping.
- **Constraints**
  - API contract alignment: service methods must match catalog-api REST endpoints exactly; update in sync with backend.
  - No DOM access: pure HTTP/WebSocket, no React/browser APIs; must work in Node.js and browsers.
  - Consumers import from `@catalogizer/api-client` only — never individual service files.
  - DISCREPANCY: the module guide lists `catalogizer-desktop` as a consumer, but `catalogizer-desktop/package.json` has no `@catalogizer/api-client` dependency.
  - NO SUDO/ROOT (Shared blocks). Zero Unfinished Work (AGENTS only).
- **Commit conventions**

Code style: TS strict, PascalCase components, camelCase funcs; Rust edition 2021, snake_case fns, PascalCase structs, Serde; imports grouped React/framework, third-party, internal. Purpose: browse/manage Catalogizer media; Rust handles config persistence, HTTP proxying (SSRF protection), platform detection via IPC. Window 1200x800.
  - DISCREPANCY: docs omit extras in real files: package.json has `test:e2e`/`test:e2e:update` (Playwright ^1.48.0), `@tauri-apps/plugin-shell`; Cargo.toml has `directories 5.0`, `log`, `thiserror`, optional feature `vlc-player` (libvlc-sys 0.2), `src-tauri/src/vlc/` dir (docs say only main.rs), rust-version 1.60, version 2.4.0. package/Cargo/tauri.conf version = 2.4.0 (identifier/window 1200x800 match docs).

- **Architecture & ownership boundaries**:
  - Frontend: `src/pages/` (Home, Library, Login, MediaDetail, Search, Settings; one component per route, compose from components/); `src/components/` (Layout, LoadingScreen; reusable, do NOT import from pages/); `src/services/apiService.ts` (HTTP client, single source of truth for API calls, uses Tauri `make_http_request` IPC); `src/stores/` (Zustand `authStore`, `configStore`; client state only); `src/types/index.ts` (media/auth/playback/config types; keep dependency-free); `src/utils/cn.ts` (Tailwind merge, pure); `src/test-utils/` (helpers, mock data, custom render).
  - Backend: `src-tauri/src/main.rs` (ALL Tauri command handlers, config state, HTTP proxy); `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (window 1200x800, CSP, bundle, app identity/permissions); `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`.
  - IPC commands: `get_config`/`update_config` (full `AppConfig`: server_url, auth_token, theme, auto_start); `set_server_url`/`set_auth_token`/`clear_auth_token`; `make_http_request` (SSRF validation: URL must match configured server); `get_app_version`/`get_platform`/`get_arch`.

- **Agent coordination rules** (AGENTS.md):
  1. IPC command changes: (1) define Rust handler in main.rs with `#[tauri::command]`; (2) register in `.invoke_handler(tauri::generate_handler![...])`; (3) update TS bridge in `src/services/` via `@tauri-apps/api/core`; (4) add Rust unit tests in `#[cfg(test)]`; (5) add TS tests for bridge fn.
  2. HTTP proxy/SSRF: ALL frontend->catalog-api HTTP goes through `make_http_request`; it validates target URL matches configured server. Do NOT bypass with direct frontend HTTP.
  3. Config persistence: AppConfig managed by Rust backend; frontend reads/writes ONLY via get_config/update_config IPC; NO frontend persistence (no localStorage for auth tokens).

  5. Testing: Vitest+jsdom, RTL, mock Tauri IPC; Rust `#[test]` and `#[tokio::test]` for async commands; coverage via `npm run test:coverage`.

- **Identity/stack**: `digital.vasic.build` — generic reusable shell build framework: automatic versioning, change detection, multi-component build orchestration. Type: Shell (Bash 4.0+). Deps: Bash 4.0+ (associative arrays), Python 3 (JSON manipulation), sha256sum (coreutils), Git.

Key functions: `log_info/success/warn/error/step/header`; `detect_runtime/detect_compose`; `git_short_commit/git_branch/git_is_dirty`; `get_version/get_version_string/bump_version`; `compute_source_hash/needs_rebuild/show_hash_status`; `create_release_dir/generate_checksums/generate_build_info`; `build_main/parse_build_args`. Integration contract (projects MUST define): `BUILD_COMPONENTS` array; `BUILD_COMPONENT_PATTERNS` assoc array (component -> file patterns); `build_single_component()` function. (Dir also contains ARCHITECTURE.md, README.md — not in scope.)

### §11.4.173 — Containerized + distributed build mandate (User mandate, 2026-06-29) — FULL TEXT (identical in CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md; absent from CONSTITUTION.md)
EVERY build of EVERY component (source compile, artifact/package/installer/container-image production, codegen, asset render — for ANY language/platform: Go, Android/Gradle, desktop, web, native, firmware) MUST run INSIDE a specialized build container provisioned via the `digital.vasic.containers` submodule (§11.4.76) — NEVER on the bare host. The build containers MUST be DISTRIBUTED to the designated remote build host(s) (e.g. `thinker.local`) via the SAME containers-submodule distribution mechanism the infra uses (§11.4.76 Distributor / remote compose over SSH, §11.4.161 rootless), so the build EXECUTES on the remote build host (offloading the developer/main host); once the build completes the produced artifacts MUST be brought BACK to the originating main host (scp/rsync/volume copy) for use/flashing/distribution. Building outside a container, or on the bare host, is FORBIDDEN — a release blocker (the "works on my machine" / unreproducible-build class §11.4.76 exists to prevent). The build-host target + build-container definitions are config-injected (§11.4.28, never hardcoded in the submodule); a missing build-container capability is added by EXTENDING the containers submodule upstream (§11.4.74), never by an ad-hoc host build. Honest boundary (§11.4.6): the containerized+distributed build guarantees reproducibility + host-isolation + capacity offload — it does NOT replace the §11.4.40 full-suite retest, §11.4.108 four-layer artifact→runtime verification, or §11.4.38 installable-asset evidence (those still run against the brought-back artifact). Classification: universal (§11.4.17). Composes §11.4.76, §11.4.161, §11.4.74, §11.4.28, §11.4.24, §11.4.82, §11.4.121, §11.4.38, §11.4.108, §12.6. Propagation gate `CM-COVENANT-114-173-PROPAGATION` (literal `11.4.173`) + recommended gate `CM-CONTAINERIZED-DISTRIBUTED-BUILD` (every build runs via the containers submodule on the remote build host; a bare-host build is detected + FAILs) + paired §1.1 mutation. Canonical authority: constitution submodule `Constitution.md` §11.4.173. Non-compliance is a release blocker. No escape hatch — no `--build-on-host`, `--skip-container-build`, `--local-build-ok`, `--no-distributed-build`, `--bare-host-build` flag.
